summary: The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now supports non-ASCII filenames by encoding them according to RFC 2231. This prevents a `UnicodeEncodeError` that previously occurred when serving files with unicode characters in their names.

The Flask constructor now accepts host_matching and static_host arguments to ensure the static route is correctly configured during initialization. This fixes a bug where enabling host matching after instantiation left the static route in a broken state.

This commit removes the obsolete `zip_safe` setting from the installation documentation. It updates the `docs/tutorial/install.rst` file to reflect current packaging standards, ensuring the tutorial remains accurate for users setting up the project.

This commit refactors the Flask test suite by introducing a new base class, FlaskTestCase, to reduce code duplication. Several existing test classes, such as ContextTestCase and BasicFunctionalityTestCase, are updated to inherit from this new base class instead of directly from unittest.TestCase.
This commit adds a new method, `create_jinja_loader`, to the `Flask` class. It allows developers to customize the template loading process without modifying the entire Jinja environment setup.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to reflect current Python 3 support status. It replaces the outdated "Status of Python 3" section in the advanced foreword with a new "Python 3 Support in Flask" heading, removing previous warnings about migration difficulties.

This commit fixes a compatibility issue in the Flask test suite for Python 2.x by updating the PyStringIO helper class. It replaces a simple subclass with a wrapper that delegates attribute access to the underlying StringIO object, ensuring the send file tests run correctly.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the deprecation warning messages for the `_app_ctx_stack` and `_request_ctx_stack` attributes. The typo "remoevd" is changed to "removed" within the `__getattr__` function in `src/flask/globals.py`.

This commit corrects minor spelling errors in the documentation and test scripts. It fixes typos in the server documentation and a test script, improving the clarity of the text without altering any functional behavior.

This commit adds a `provide_automatic_options` keyword argument to the `Flask.add_url_rule` method. It allows developers to disable the automatic OPTIONS response for specific routes, even when using standard functions instead of view classes.

The Flask development server now binds to 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost by default to avoid browser connectivity issues. This change updates the Flask.run method and the quickstart documentation to reflect the new default host address.

This commit updates the documentation for error handlers in the errorpages module. It clarifies that an error handler is a function returning a response when a specific error is raised, similar to a view function. The text also notes that handlers for internal server errors may receive other uncaught exception instances.

This commit fixes a logic error in the `send_file` function within `flask/helpers.py` that prevented ETags from being generated when a file object was provided. It removes an unnecessary condition that made the check always false, ensuring proper cache headers are added.

This commit moves the `ensure_sync` method from the `Flask` app class to the `Scaffold` base class. This change allows extensions to override the method so that the custom synchronization logic applies consistently to all blueprints, preventing potential event-loop blocking issues.

This commit updates the server documentation to include `lsof` as an alternative command for identifying processes using a specific port on macOS. It also reorganizes the examples into separate tabs for `netstat` on Linux and `lsof` on macOS and Linux.

This commit switches the project's dependency management and CI workflows to use the uv package manager. It updates GitHub Actions to install uv instead of standard Python setup steps and adds a lock file for reproducible builds. The change affects the Flask application's build and testing infrastructure.

This commit updates the documentation for the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies that when a query argument value is set to `None`, the entire key-value pair is omitted from the generated URL.

This commit fixes a JSON import failure on Google AppEngine by falling back to Django's bundled simplejson module. The change modifies the import logic in flask/helpers.py to ensure JSON functionality remains available in that specific environment.

This commit removes obsolete Python 2 compatibility shims and unused helper functions from the Flask compatibility module. It cleans up the codebase by deleting legacy aliases and iterator utilities that are no longer needed for modern Python versions.

This commit changes the order of operations in the `RequestContext` class so that URL matching occurs before the session is opened. This allows custom session interfaces to access the request endpoint, preventing errors when that value is required.
This commit initializes the changelog for version 2.3.0 by adding a new entry to the CHANGES.rst file. It marks the release as unreleased, preparing the documentation for upcoming changes.

This commit adds Python 3.6 support to the test suite by updating the CI configuration and test environment definitions. It fixes test failures in `test_basic.py` and `test_ext.py` caused by Python 3.6-specific changes in regular expression syntax and exception hierarchy.

This commit updates the `find_best_app` function in `flask/cli.py` to use proper tuple syntax for iterating over attribute names. It also corrects a minor typo in the changelog, changing "0-argument" to "zero-argument" for consistency.

This commit updates the documentation in docs/config.rst to correct the section title to "Configuring from Environment Variables" and adjust line wrapping for improved readability. It clarifies the phrasing regarding how users can control configuration values directly from the environment.
This commit adds Edmond Burnett to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.
This commit moves package metadata from setup.py to setup.cfg for the main project and its examples. It also updates MANIFEST.in files to include the license file in source distributions.

This commit documents the new application context feature in Flask, which allows URL generation without an active request. It updates the API reference to include the `has_app_context` function and the `AppContext` class.

This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to include a concrete example of a secret key. It adds a sample byte string to the `docs/config.rst` file to illustrate the expected format for the `SECRET_KEY` setting.

This commit applies the Black code formatter to the entire Flask codebase, including the core library, examples, and tests. It standardizes the code style without changing any functional behavior or fixing bugs.

This commit removes simplejson from the test suite and configuration, reverting a previous addition. It deletes the specific test verifying that simplejson does not escape slashes and removes the dependency from the tox environment list.
This commit corrects a typo in the quickstart documentation. It updates the example code to use the correct parameter name, ensuring users see the accurate method for accessing URL query parameters.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to use proper Sphinx cross-references for the `flask` command and `--debug` option. It improves the accuracy of the CLI and installation guides by replacing plain text with structured references.

This commit updates the file upload documentation to include checks for missing file parts and empty filenames. It clarifies how to handle cases where a user submits a form without selecting a file, preventing errors during the upload process.

This commit updates the streaming documentation in the Flask patterns guide. It removes redundant source code directives, allowing code blocks to be defined directly within the text for cleaner formatting.

This commit adds a feature to the Flask application class that allows developers to register callbacks executed only once before the first request is processed. It introduces the `before_first_request` decorator and related logic to manage this one-time initialization behavior.

This commit removes an unused Ruff linting rule from the project configuration. It deletes the ignore directive for the UP038 rule, which previously suppressed warnings about using tuples in isinstance checks. The change affects the pyproject.toml file.

This commit adds documentation for the application factory pattern, explaining how to create multiple application instances for testing and running different versions. It updates the patterns index to include this new guide.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask blueprints to clarify their role in creating modular application components. It refines the explanation in the `docs/blueprints.rst` file to better describe how blueprints support common patterns within or across applications.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring for the ScriptInfo class in flask/cli.py. It changes the description from "Help object" to "Helper object" to accurately reflect the class's purpose. No functional behavior is altered.

This commit corrects several grammatical and spelling errors in the Flask configuration documentation. It improves the clarity of the text in the config.rst file by fixing typos such as "chose" to "choose" and adjusting sentence structure.
The quickstart documentation no longer includes a link to the ep.io deployment guide. This change removes an external reference from the Flask quickstart page.

This commit adds documentation for testing and response objects to the Flask API reference. It updates the main documentation index to include a testing section and refines the import of the Request class in the core module.

This commit removes obsolete test applications from the test suite, including configuration-based and site-package examples. It cleans up the test environment by deleting unused Flask app definitions and related directory structures.

This commit removes the apishowcase example from the repository, eliminating its associated Python module, templates, and static files. It also updates the minitwit example, likely to remove references to the deleted code.

This commit adds Python 3.4 to the list of environments used by the tox testing tool. It ensures the project's test suite runs against the new Python version, expanding coverage for developers and continuous integration systems.

This commit prevents Blueprint endpoints from containing dots, which previously caused routing conflicts. The `Blueprint.add_url_rule` method now raises an assertion error if a custom endpoint includes a dot. New tests verify that this restriction is enforced correctly.

This documentation update clarifies how to enable test mode in Flask applications. It replaces the older method of setting a configuration key with the direct use of the app's testing property. The changes appear in the testing guide.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the CHANGES.rst documentation file. It removes an extraneous "due" from the release notes for version 2013-06-13, ensuring the description of the `tojson` template filter is clear and accurate.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the request context documentation. It clarifies the explanation of error handling behavior when an exception is not caught and debug mode is disabled.
This commit updates the pip-tools dependency from version 5.3.0 to 5.3.1 in the development requirements. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the package management tool.

The `safe_join` function in `flask/helpers.py` now accepts multiple path components instead of just a single filename. This allows users to safely join several untrusted path segments to a base directory, similar to how `os.path.join` works.

This commit corrects a typo in the Python documentation for Unicode handling. It fixes a misspelling of "your" in the `docs/unicode.rst` file, ensuring the text accurately instructs users on how to specify their encoding to the interpreter.

This commit improves debugging for bad request errors by enabling the TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS setting by default in debug mode. It also updates the Flask class to include the specific missing key in the error description for BadRequestKeyError exceptions when debugging is active.

This commit adds tests to verify that the deprecated `static_path` argument in the Flask application class still functions correctly and triggers a deprecation warning. It also confirms that the `static_url_path` argument properly configures the URL for static files.

This commit updates the project's dependency management to use pip-compile instead of pip-compile-multi. It modifies GitHub Actions workflows and pre-commit configurations to reflect this change, ensuring consistent requirement generation across the build and test environments.

This commit removes deprecated code from the Flask library, including the `Flask.got_first_request` attribute and the `locked_cached_property` helper. It also eliminates the `_FakeStack` class and various module-level `__getattr__` functions that previously issued deprecation warnings.

This commit adds documentation for the endpoint parameter in the Flask.route method. It clarifies that users can explicitly specify an endpoint name, overriding the default behavior of generating one from the function name.

This commit updates the Blueprint documentation example to correctly demonstrate using the `template_folder` argument. It ensures users see the proper syntax for specifying a custom template directory when creating a Blueprint instance.

This commit reverts print statements in the `run_audit` class of `setup.py` to Python 2 syntax. It removes parentheses around the arguments to ensure the audit command runs correctly in Python 2 environments.

This commit updates the FlaskClient class in the testing module to support the new cookie interface introduced in Werkzeug 2.3. It replaces the old cookie jar attribute with a compatible storage mechanism and adjusts the error message for disabled cookies.

This commit adds a `teardown_request` decorator to the Flask class, allowing functions to run at the end of a request even if an exception occurs. It addresses the limitation where `after_request` handlers are skipped during errors in debug mode, ensuring reliable cleanup tasks like closing database connections.

This commit updates the security documentation to clarify that ECMAScript 5 changes to literal construction close a specific attack vector. It explains that literals now use the builtin constructor rather than the object's own constructor, preventing prototype pollution.
This commit updates the documentation theme submodule to a specific version. It ensures the project references the correct theme code for building the documentation site.

This commit updates the Blinker documentation to reflect the 1.1 release, replacing references to the removed `temporarily_connected_to` method with the new `connected_to` API. It also adds a note explaining this specific change in the signal module.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the configuration documentation. It fixes the misspelling of "instance" in the description of the `Flask.open_instance_resource` method within the `docs/config.rst` file.

This commit fixes inconsistent indentation in the import statements within the Flask application module. It corrects the alignment of continuation lines for imported symbols, ensuring the code follows standard formatting conventions without altering functionality.

This commit fixes a bug where Jinja2 template auto-reloading failed to activate when the Flask app was run with debugging enabled. It ensures that accessing the Jinja environment before starting the server does not prevent auto-reloading from turning on. The change modifies the `Flask.run` method to explicitly enable this feature when debug mode is active.

This commit clarifies the Flask tutorial documentation by explicitly stating where new code should be inserted. It specifies that imports belong in `flaskr.py` and the new function goes in `flask.py`, preventing user confusion.

The tutorial documentation and the Flaskr example application were updated to use the `g` object for managing database connections. This change replaces the previous approach of using `before_request` and `teardown_request` hooks with the `get_db` and `close_db` functions, simplifying how the application context handles database state.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the project's changelog file. It fixes the module name "werkzeug.execptions" to "werkzeug.exceptions" in the version 1.0 release notes.

This commit removes the `as_module` parameter from the `main` function in `src/flask/cli.py`. It allows the CLI to automatically detect the program name when Flask is executed as a Python module, simplifying the interface.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring for the `should_set_cookie` method within the `SessionInterface` class in `flask/sessions.py`. It corrects the word "weather" to "whether" to accurately describe the method's behavior regarding cookie setting.

This commit corrects a documentation example in the testing guide to use the proper application instance variable. It ensures the database configuration is set on the correct object, preventing confusion for users following the tutorial.

This commit updates the CLI help text in `flask/cli.py` to reflect the new method for enabling debug mode. It replaces references to the `FLASK_DEBUG` variable with instructions to set `FLASK_ENV` to 'development', ensuring users see the correct configuration syntax.

This documentation update corrects the description of gevent's underlying event loop, changing the reference from libevent to libev. It ensures the WSGI standalone deployment guide accurately reflects the current library used for the high-level synchronous API.

This commit fixes a crash in Flask's JSON serialization functions when no application context is active. It ensures that `dumps`, `dump`, `loads`, and `load` in `flask/json.py` only use the app's custom encoder or decoder if an application is currently on the stack.

This documentation update clarifies the concept of URL reversing in the Flask quickstart guide. It explicitly defines the process as using the `url_for()` function to build URLs, helping users understand why this method is preferred over hard-coding links in templates.

This commit adds documentation for integrating Celery with Flask, explaining how to set up background tasks after the removal of the official Flask integration. It introduces a new guide in the patterns section to help users configure Celery correctly.
This commit updates the project changelog to document the release of version 1.0. It specifically notes that the extension development guidelines have been updated.

This commit fixes the Flask tutorial documentation by adding missing closing tags to the HTML list items in the template examples. The change ensures the docs match the corrected example code, preventing users from copying invalid markup.

This commit corrects string literals across multiple Flask test suite modules, including basic, blueprints, and helpers. It ensures test assertions and expected values use the correct text, preventing false failures in the test cases.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to accurately describe the default URL converter. It clarifies that the `string` converter accepts any text without a slash, aligning the quickstart guide with the official API documentation.

This commit significantly enhances the project's documentation by updating the sidebar with useful links and refining the visual styling of the documentation theme. It also improves the docstrings for key methods within the Flask class, such as route and run, to provide clearer guidance for users.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to provide functional return statements in the code examples instead of placeholder pass statements. It clarifies how to handle variables within routing rules for the user.

This commit configures the repository to use a union merge strategy for the CHANGES file. This prevents merge conflicts when multiple contributors add entries to the changelog simultaneously, ensuring all updates are preserved.

This commit adds `appcontext_pushed` and `appcontext_popped` signals to the Flask application context lifecycle. These signals allow developers to monitor when an application context is pushed or popped, providing hooks for custom logic during context management.
This commit documents the new `get_namespace` method in the Flask changelog. It adds a version note to the `Config` class in `flask/config.py` to indicate the feature was introduced in version 1.0.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the contributing guide, changing "StackOverflow" to the proper name "Stack Overflow." It ensures the documentation accurately references the community resource for users seeking help.

This commit adds a new method, `get_static_file_options`, to the `_PackageBoundObject` class in Flask. It allows developers to customize the options used when serving static files, such as adjusting cache control headers, which were previously difficult to modify.

This commit adds documentation to the config module explaining how to set configuration values directly using environment variables. It provides examples for setting variables like SECRET_KEY and DEBUG on Linux, OS X, and Windows before starting the server.
This commit removes the DocVersion import and the versions list from the documentation configuration. It stops the docs from displaying a version selector for Flask 1.0, 0.12, and development builds.

This commit adds unit tests for the safe_join helper function to verify its path joining behavior. It covers valid path combinations, handling of relative segments, and edge cases like trailing slashes. The tests ensure the function correctly constructs and sanitizes file paths.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `copy_current_request_context` where concurrent workers shared the same request context copy, causing data interference. It now creates a fresh context copy for each call to ensure independent execution.
This commit updates the HTML FAQ documentation to remove outdated information. It clarifies that Mark Pilgrim's book is now published and removes a note about Internet Explorer's market share.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use version 2.11.0 of the tool. It ensures the project uses the latest available release for its automated code checks.

This commit updates the documentation for FastCGI, mod_wsgi, uWSGI, and other deployment patterns to use proper reStructuredText syntax for file paths and code snippets. It replaces plain text references with the :file: role and double backticks to improve rendering and clarity in the generated docs.

This commit updates the minimum version requirements for Flask's core dependencies in setup.py. It raises the required versions for Werkzeug, Jinja2, itsdangerous, and click to their latest release candidates, ensuring compatibility with newer library features.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the `open_resource` method of the `_PackageBoundObject` class in `flask.py`. It corrects the example path from `/template` to `/templates` to accurately reflect the standard directory structure for static resources.

This commit updates the `Config.from_pyfile` method in `flask/config.py` to ignore `ENOTDIR` errors when loading configuration files with `silent=True`. This prevents unnecessary error messages when a path component is not a directory, improving the robustness of silent config loading.

This commit fixes an issue in Flask's template JSON dumping where all forward slashes were unnecessarily escaped. The `_tojson_filter` function now only escapes forward slashes that immediately follow a closing angle bracket, preventing potential script tag injection while keeping other slashes unescaped.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the project's changelog file. It updates the description for version 1.0 to properly state that deprecated module functionality was removed.
This commit updates the Flask project version from 0.2 to 0.5 in the setup configuration. It also adds a new entry to the changelog file to document the upcoming 0.5 release.

This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the `open_resource` method within the `_PackageBoundObject` class in `flask/helpers.py`. It corrects a misspelled file path example from "schemal.sql" to "schema.sql" to ensure accurate documentation.

This commit updates the extension development documentation to reflect the new import system. It clarifies that extensions now use the `flask_something` package naming convention instead of the old `flaskext.something` namespace. The text also explains that users should import extensions via the `flask.ext` redirect package.
This commit removes two unused imports from the Flask module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating references to `cached_property` and `InternalServerError` that were not being used.

The `load_dotenv` function in `flask/cli.py` now uses `os.path.isfile` instead of `os.path.exists` to check for `.env` and `.flaskenv` files. This prevents the CLI from attempting to load environment variables if these paths point to directories rather than actual files.

Removes the obsolete run-simple.py script, which previously served as a standalone entry point for the Flask test suite. This change consolidates test execution under the main run-tests.py module, eliminating redundant code.

This commit updates Flask's response handling to allow view functions to return a tuple where the first element is already a Response instance. This enables developers to return objects like a JSON error message paired with a status code directly. The change modifies the Flask.make_response method to correctly process these tuples.
This commit adds Daniel Neuhäuser to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's attribution records to include his name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, and testing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revision to 3.9.1. These changes ensure the build environment uses current tools and libraries.

This commit adds tests to the BlueprintTestCase in flask/testsuite/blueprints.py to verify that user-defined exceptions are correctly handled within blueprints. It ensures that error handlers registered via decorators and functions properly catch and respond to specific custom exceptions.

This commit updates the documentation link for Flask-SQLAlchemy in the SQLAlchemy patterns guide. It replaces the outdated pythonhosted.org URL with the current pocoo.org domain to ensure users are directed to the correct project page.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.12.2-dev in the `flask/__init__.py` module. It marks the start of a new development cycle following the 0.12.1 release.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to use f-strings instead of percent-style string formatting. It modernizes code examples in modules like blueprints, views, and patterns to reflect current Python best practices.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.4.3 to v0.4.7. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the tool for code quality checks.

This commit updates the logging documentation to use the explicit two-argument form of the super() call. This ensures the example code remains compatible with Python 2, which does not support the zero-argument syntax. The change affects the RequestFormatter class example.

This commit corrects a typo in the installation documentation, changing the section title from "Leaving on the Edge" to "Living on the Edge." It updates the `docs/installation.rst` file to ensure the heading accurately reflects the intended meaning.

This commit corrects the syntax for setting the Python version environment variable in the CI test workflow. It ensures the variable is properly defined for subsequent steps by removing an incorrect prefix from the command.

This commit updates the Flask README to reflect the project's maturity, noting that the API is stable and unlikely to break. It also corrects the installation instructions to include pip as an alternative to easy_install.

This commit updates documentation in the Flask class to correct outdated references. It clarifies that the `after_request` hook is for closing database connections and updates the command-line tool reference from `runserver` to `run`.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use version 2.12.0 of the tool. It ensures the project uses the latest available release for its automated code checks.

This commit rewords the security documentation to improve clarity and flow. It simplifies the explanation of implicit state management in cookie-based authentication, removing informal language and redundant phrasing. The changes are limited to the `docs/security.rst` file.

This commit introduces the `after_this_request` decorator in the Flask module, allowing developers to register functions that execute after the current request is processed. It updates the `Flask` class and `RequestContext` to manage and invoke these specific post-request callbacks.

The `locate_app` function in `flask/cli.py` now distinguishes between a missing file and an import error within the module. If an `ImportError` occurs during the import process, it is re-raised instead of being masked by a `NoAppException`. This ensures users see the actual import failure rather than a misleading path error.

This commit improves how Flask handles and re-raises exceptions during request processing, ensuring errors are reported more accurately. It updates the `Flask.handle_exception` method in `flask/app.py` and adds documentation for extension developers regarding end-of-request behavior.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency in the development requirements from version 2.6.0 to 2.7.1. It ensures the project uses the newer version of the pre-commit framework for its development environment.

Adds a new method to the Config class that loads environment variables with a specific prefix into the application configuration. This allows users to easily manage settings via environment variables, with values automatically parsed as JSON when possible.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's Blueprint module where registering a route could result in double slashes in the URL path. It modifies the `add_url_rule` method in `BlueprintSetupState` to normalize the rule string, ensuring clean URL generation.

This commit adds documentation to the design guide explaining how Flask's routing system handles route ordering and URL uniqueness. It clarifies that routes are automatically sorted by complexity to support decorator-based routing and that ambiguous URLs are redirected to a canonical form.

This commit allows developers to customize the Jinja environment used by Flask applications by introducing a new `jinja_env_class` attribute. The `Flask.create_jinja_environment` method now instantiates this custom class instead of the default `Environment`, enabling the use of newer Jinja features.

The documentation build now uses the packaged flask_sphinx_themes module instead of a local git submodule. This removes the need to manage the docs/_themes directory and updates the Sphinx configuration to import the new theme package.

This commit removes the documentation section recommending the X-XSS-Protection header in the security guide. It eliminates outdated advice regarding browser-based XSS protection, as this header is deprecated and no longer recommended for modern web applications.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to a newer version and fixes type annotation syntax in the Flask context and helpers modules. It adds missing trailing commas to the type hints for the `after_this_request` and `stream_with_context` functions to satisfy linter requirements.

This commit fixes the documentation sidebar by adding the carbon ads template to the list of displayed sidebar components. The change is made in the `docs/conf.py` configuration file, ensuring the ad widget appears correctly in the generated documentation.

This commit adds a comprehensive test suite for the Flask framework, covering basic functionality, context handling, and templating. It introduces a Makefile to automate running these tests and cleaning up Python cache files.

This commit adds a helpful tip to the Flask CLI when environment files are detected but the required library is missing. The `load_dotenv` function in `flask/cli.py` now displays a yellow warning suggesting users install `python-dotenv` to utilize their `.env` or `.flaskenv` files.
This commit fixes minor typos in the lazy loading documentation. It corrects punctuation and grammar in the `docs/patterns/lazyloading.rst` file to improve clarity.

This commit corrects several spelling errors in the documentation style guide, including "brances," "arbitary," "singletones," and "functin." It also removes a stale submodule reference from the documentation themes directory.
This commit corrects the documentation for the `jsonify` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies how the `padded` argument handles JSONP requests and fixes grammatical errors in the description.

This commit updates the type hints for the `template_folder` parameter in the `Scaffold`, `Flask`, and `Blueprint` classes to accept `pathlib.Path` objects. This allows users to pass path objects directly without needing to convert them to strings first.

This commit introduces the `copy_current_request_context` function in the `flask.ctx` module to simplify working with greenlets by allowing request contexts to be copied. It also adds a `__repr__` method to the `Flask` class for better debugging output.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's context management where `has_app_context` and `has_request_context` were checking the wrong context variable. Previously, these functions returned incorrect results because they referenced the opposite context variable, leading to false positives or negatives. The fix ensures each function correctly checks its respective context variable.

This commit changes Flask's development server to respect the PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS configuration setting instead of always passing errors through. The Flask.run method and the CLI run_command function now use this setting to determine error handling behavior.

This commit fixes the FastCGI lighttpd documentation by adding a trailing slash to the static file path. Omitting this slash previously caused unintended behavior in the server configuration. The change updates the example in the deploying/fastcgi.rst file.

This commit fixes the alignment of the logo in the Flask documentation. It removes the right-alignment setting from the image directive in the main documentation index file, ensuring the logo displays correctly.

This commit updates a broken documentation link in the SQLAlchemy patterns guide. It corrects the URL for the declarative extension in the `docs/patterns/sqlalchemy.rst` file to point to the current documentation location.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now accepts filenames encoded in latin-1 instead of restricting them to ASCII. It removes unnecessary Unicode normalization and encodes the filename directly as latin-1 when a UTF-8 header is required.

This commit updates the Flask security documentation to reorder sections by semantic importance and corrects a broken link to the flask-talisman package. It also rewords several security concepts for clarity, including renaming the Content Security Policy section to HTTP Strict Transport Security.
This commit removes an unused import from the Flask helpers module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a reference to a Python 2 compatibility constant that is no longer needed.

This commit adds a new section to the upgrading documentation for Flask version 0.5. It explains that the framework is now distributed as a Python package and that autoescaping is restricted to specific file extensions. Users with custom template extensions must override the select_jinja_autoescape method to maintain previous behavior.
This documentation update removes the recommendation for dropzone.js from the file upload patterns guide. It also corrects the jQuery reference to use a proper reStructuredText link.

This commit clarifies the `url_rule` attribute in the `Request` class documentation. It explains that when a request triggers a 405 error, the rule is not bound, so users must check `routing_exception.valid_methods` to find allowed HTTP methods.

This commit improves the error message shown when accessing form files without the correct multipart encoding. It updates the `attach_enctype_error_multidict` function in `debughelpers.py` to provide a clearer explanation of the issue.

This commit updates the session handling in Flask by making the `SessionMixin` class inherit from `MutableMapping` and converting the `permanent` attribute into a property. It also adds a test to verify that session attributes work correctly.

This commit updates the test suite to use the modern `tmp_path` fixture instead of the deprecated `tmpdir` fixture. It renames the `modules_tmpdir` and `modules_tmpdir_prefix` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` to `modules_tmp_path` and `modules_tmp_path_prefix`, respectively, and updates all dependent tests to use the new names.

This documentation update corrects the outdated Google Developer libraries URL and bumps the referenced jQuery version from 1.6.1 to 1.9.1. It ensures users following the `jquery.rst` guide use the current, minified library source.

This commit fixes a template lookup error in Flask's `_DispatchingJinjaLoader` class. It ensures that a `ValueError` is raised when a template loader cannot be found, preventing incorrect behavior when loading templates from directories within modules.

This commit updates the CLI documentation to use consistent formatting for command references. It changes the text in the `docs/cli.rst` file to properly style the `flask` command, aligning it with the conventions used elsewhere in the documentation.

This commit corrects a typo in the deprecation warning message for the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It changes the wording from "is not deprecated" to "is now deprecated" to accurately reflect the status of the parameter.

This commit corrects typos in the Pluggable Views documentation by replacing the non-existent `add_url_view` method with the correct `add_url_rule` method. It ensures the code examples in `docs/views.rst` accurately reflect the proper API usage for registering views.

This commit adds a new documentation environment to the tox configuration. It runs a Sphinx link check to verify that all URLs in the project documentation are valid, ensuring broken links are caught during testing.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It changes the word "catched" to "caught" in the description of the handle_exception method to improve clarity.

This commit ensures the `flask.json` package is included when installing Flask. It fixes a potential issue where the JSON module might be missing from the installed distribution. The change updates the package list in `setup.py`.

This commit corrects the indentation of the changelog entries in the CHANGES.rst file. It ensures the release notes are properly formatted for consistent display.

This commit updates development dependencies and GitHub Actions versions for the Flask project. It bumps the setup-python and upload-artifact actions in CI workflows and updates requirements files. This commit fixes the execution order of request callbacks for nested blueprints in the Flask application. It ensures that pre-request handlers run from the app down to the specific blueprint, while post-request handlers run in the reverse order.

This commit updates the WTForms documentation to include a hyperlink to the project's website. It adds a reference link in the text and defines the corresponding URL target in the documentation file.

This commit updates the Flask project version from 0.6 to 0.7 in the setup configuration. It also adds a new entry to the changelog for the upcoming 0.7 release, noting that the release date and codename are still to be determined.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the Flask templating documentation. It clarifies that Flask provides specific Jinja2 filters in addition to the standard ones, improving the clarity of the "Standard Filters" section.

This commit cleans up the Flask documentation by removing unused reference labels and replacing legacy page references with modern doc directives. It updates cross-references in files like `api.rst` and `quickstart.rst` to improve link accuracy and consistency across the project.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.0.2 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It also marks the release as complete in the changelog, removing the unreleased status.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.4.3 to 3.5.1. It modifies the dependency specifications in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the newer release.

This commit resolves static type checking errors in Flask's helper and JSON modules. It adds type overloads to `stream_with_context` to correctly handle both generator and callable inputs. Additionally, it suppresses a specific type error in the JSON provider's `_default` function.

This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the `dispatch_request` method within the `View` class in `flask/views.py`. It fixes a missing space in the text "function code," ensuring the documentation is readable and accurate for users.

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the HTML FAQ documentation by correcting the syntax of the reference label. The change ensures the link to the "Dive into HTML5" resource resolves correctly for users.

This commit improves the wording of the error message displayed by the DebugFilesKeyError class in Flask's debug helpers. It clarifies that file contents, rather than just files, were not transmitted and adjusts the explanation of what the browser submitted.

The upgrade script now correctly rewrites references to `application.modules` in addition to `app.modules` when migrating to Flask 0.7. This ensures the script handles both common variable names for the application object.

This commit corrects the import path for the secure filename utility in the quickstart documentation. It updates the example to import from the utils module, ensuring users copy the correct code for their projects.

This commit restructures the Flaskr example application to use a standard Python package layout with a setup.py file. This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the `make_response` method within the `Flask` class. It clarifies that the `headers` argument can be a list or a dictionary, improving documentation accuracy for users.

This commit updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 4.6.1 to 4.7.0 in the GitHub Actions workflows. It ensures the CI environment uses the latest minor release for Python setup, potentially incorporating bug fixes or improvements.

This commit adds a new documentation chapter explaining how to handle application configuration in Flask. It details the use of the Config class and its methods for loading settings from environment variables or Python files.

This commit adds a devcontainer configuration to the Flask project, enabling developers to use a standardized, pre-configured development environment. It includes a setup script that automatically creates a virtual environment and installs necessary dependencies upon container creation.

This commit adds documentation for a middleware that allows clients to override HTTP methods, such as using POST to simulate PATCH, when proxies restrict specific verbs. The new guide is integrated into the Flask patterns index.

This commit fixes a broken link in the documentation that pointed to the wrong target for the detailed contributing guide. The change updates the reference in the `docs/contributing.rst` file to ensure users are directed to the correct Pallets documentation page.

This commit adds support for pulling macros from templates via the new `get_template_attribute` function. It also documents key design decisions in the Flask framework, including the rationale for the explicit application object.

The TaggedJSONSerializer in flask/sessions.py now supports serializing and deserializing UUID objects within session data. This change allows users to store UUIDs in their Flask sessions without manual conversion, and the new functionality is documented in the API reference.

This commit enables translation support for the documentation by adding gettext configuration options to the Sphinx setup. It sets flags to generate unique identifiers for translatable strings and disables compact mode, allowing the docs to be localized.

This commit cleans up code formatting in several documentation files and fixes warnings generated during the documentation build process. It also updates references in the Flask CLI module to use proper attribute syntax for the FlaskGroup class.

This commit removes the deprecated BaseRequest and BaseResponse classes from the Flask wrappers module. It updates internal imports in the app and testing modules to use the standard Response class directly, ensuring compatibility with newer Werkzeug versions.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.12.5 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.
This commit corrects a typo in the CLI documentation where "lated later" was changed to "added later." It clarifies the explanation of when application context behavior is unavailable for commands.

This commit removes the `tests` package initialization file, treating the test suite as a namespace package instead. This change ensures the test directory is not recognized as a standard Python package, which affects how modules are loaded during testing.

This commit moves the `flask.g` object from the request context to the application context, making it available whenever the app context is active, not just during a request. It also renames the `request_globals_class` attribute to `app_ctx_globals_class` in the `Flask` class to better reflect this change.

This commit updates the CHANGES.rst file to replace placeholder text with actual pull request links. It adds reference definitions to ensure readers can easily navigate to the specific code changes mentioned in the release notes.

This documentation update clarifies how to pass command-line arguments to the test runner. It corrects the example in the testing guide to show that arguments should be provided as a keyword argument rather than a positional list.

The `Flask.run` method now accepts `None` for the host and port arguments, allowing the application to use configured defaults instead of hardcoded values. This change clarifies the default behavior for users running the development server.

This commit updates the Flask application context documentation to clarify that code execution occurs in at least two distinct states. It restructures the text to explicitly list the application setup state and corrects awkward phrasing in the description.

This commit updates the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py` to pass the `_scheme` argument to the `handle_build_error` callback. This ensures that custom error handlers receive the requested URL scheme when a build error occurs.

This commit pins the operating system and Python version for the Read the Docs build environment. It ensures documentation builds use Ubuntu 20.04 and Python 3.10, preventing unexpected failures from uncontrolled dependency updates.

This commit fixes a crash in the Request class when handling JSON loading failures outside of an active application context. It now safely checks if the request context exists before accessing app configuration, preventing errors when current_app is unavailable.

This commit finalizes the 0.8.1 release of Flask by updating the version string from a development build to the stable release. It modifies the version identifiers in the package initialization and setup files, and updates the changelog to record the official release date.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the Flask tutorial where the `teardown_request` method was incorrectly listed twice. It replaces the duplicate entry with the correct `after_request` method to accurately describe the available request lifecycle hooks.

This commit corrects grammatical errors in the Flask documentation for application and request contexts. It fixes phrasing in the appcontext, reqcontext, and shell modules to improve clarity and consistency.

This commit updates the `_called_with_wrong_args` function in `flask/cli.py` to correctly identify argument errors in Python 3. It expands the error message check to include "missing" alongside "takes," ensuring the CLI properly detects when functions are called with incorrect arguments.

This commit updates the project changelog to include a new entry for Flask version 0.8. It adds a placeholder section for the upcoming release, noting that the release date and codename are still to be determined.

This commit updates the documentation for the appdispatch module to use modern Python 3 class syntax. It removes unnecessary explicit inheritance from the object base class in the SubdomainDispatcher and PathDispatcher examples.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.1.2 to 3.2.0. It modifies the pinned dependency versions in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the newer release.

This commit updates the CHANGES file to add a placeholder section for the upcoming Flask 1.0 release. It includes a header and a note indicating that the release date and codename are still to be determined.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the Config class in flask/config.py. It fixes the wording for the silent parameter in the from_envvar and from_pyfile methods to accurately describe the behavior for missing files.

This commit removes the `flaskext_migrate` script and its tests from the Flask repository, as the tool has moved to a separate project. It updates the upgrading documentation to point to the new repository location for the migration utility.

This commit updates the wording in the installation documentation to improve clarity and flow. It modifies the text in the `docs/installation.rst` file, specifically adjusting sentences regarding virtualenv and Python version requirements.
This commit removes unused imports from the Flask application module to resolve lint warnings. It cleans up the codebase by deleting references to `Mapping` and `iterkeys` that were no longer needed.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.12.3 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.

The changes primarily affect the `RequestContext` class and the `Flask` application's teardown logic.

This commit fixes an error in the Flask CLI when using the `--extra-files` or `--exclude-patterns` options. The issue was caused by an invalid super call within a list comprehension in the `SeparatedPathType` class. The fix ensures these command-line arguments are processed correctly.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.1.0 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It also marks the release date in the changelog, transitioning the status from unreleased to officially released.

This commit updates the Flask tutorial documentation to clarify the purpose of the templates directory. It replaces a generic instruction to drop templates there with a specific note that templates created later in the tutorial will be stored in this location.

This commit adds documentation to the testing guide explaining how to mock resources and application context. It demonstrates how to override user authorization data stored on the Flask `g` object during tests.
This commit removes the Dependabot configuration for Python dependencies to reduce notification noise. It stops automated monthly updates for the requirements directory on the 2.0.x branch.

This commit updates the SLSA GitHub generator dependency in the publish workflow from version 1.6.0 to 1.7.0. It ensures the build process uses the latest minor release of the supply chain security tool.

This commit rewrites the Flask installation documentation to explicitly recommend Python 3 and list all required dependencies. It clarifies the supported Python versions, including Python 3.3 and newer, Python 2.6 and newer, and PyPy.

This commit fixes a missing newline at the end of the `flask/signals.py` file. It also updates the `test_before_render_template` test in `tests/test_signals.py` to use a context manager for signal connection instead of manual try/finally blocks.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to include a missing return statement in the login example. It clarifies that the code following the conditional check executes when the request method is GET or credentials are invalid, ensuring the login template is properly rendered.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `Config.from_file` method in the Flask `Config` class. It updates the version added note from 1.2 to 2.0 to accurately reflect when the feature was introduced.

This commit moves URL matching in Flask's `RequestContext` from initialization to the push phase. This ensures the application context is fully available before matching, allowing custom URL converters to access resources like the database.

This commit updates the documentation configuration to handle missing package metadata gracefully. If the Flask distribution is not found, it now displays a helpful message instructing users to run the development setup command instead of failing silently.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the Python 3 documentation by adding the missing word "be" to a sentence about library stability. The change is located in the docs/python3.rst file.

This commit fixes a minor grammatical error in the documentation for the Flask class. It corrects the description of the first parameter to properly state that it gives Flask an idea of what the application is.

This commit fixes a bug where setting a static URL path with a trailing slash caused incorrect route generation. It updates the Flask and Blueprint classes to strip the ending slash before constructing the static file route.

The Flask application now supports a list of functions for handling URL build errors instead of a single handler. This change modifies the `Flask` class to allow multiple error handlers to be registered and executed when `url_for` fails.

This commit fixes a documentation display bug by correcting font family typos and adjusting padding in the Flasky theme CSS. It also updates the deployment guide to properly reference the LighttpdCGIRootFix class and includes a setup.py workaround for development versions.

This commit corrects a misplaced parenthesis in the documentation for the `has_request_context` function in `flask/ctx.py`. The fix clarifies the sentence structure regarding how to check for the presence of request objects like `request` or `g`.

This commit updates the Flask deployment documentation to improve clarity and consistency across various server configurations. It refines the descriptions for CGI, FastCGI, and other deployment methods in the docs/deploying module.

This commit updates the upgrade documentation to help Windows users who lack the `patch` command-line utility. It suggests using Unix runtime environments like Cygwin or version control systems with built-in diff support to apply changes.

This commit updates the WTForms documentation to correct HTML syntax in the form helper examples. It fixes the rendering of error lists and form attributes to ensure the code snippets are valid and properly formatted.

This commit updates the documentation for the request context module to clarify the teardown behavior. It renames the example function from `after_request` to `teardown_request` and adjusts the output text to prevent confusion with other request hooks.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring for the `create_url_adapter` method within the `Flask` class. It corrects the misspelled word "UR" to "URL" to ensure accurate documentation for the application context.

This commit updates outdated documentation links for Jinja2 and Werkzeug in the Flask project. It corrects the URLs in several documentation files to point to the current, valid locations for these libraries.

This commit updates documentation examples in the Flask testing guide and template attribute docs to use alcohol-themed placeholder names instead of generic terms. It modifies the Flask class documentation and the get_template_attribute function to reflect these changes.

This commit corrects a parameter name typo in the `apprunner` function within the `test_exception_propagation` test. It changes the argument from `configkey` to `config_key` to match the intended naming convention, ensuring the test code is accurate despite previously working by accident.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.2.3. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

This commit renames the changelog file to use the RST extension and updates the version header to 1.0. It also corrects the minimum Werkzeug version requirement and adds new entries for recent bug fixes and features.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the packages module. It changes the text to properly use the plural form "modules" when describing how to split views in larger applications.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the Flask API documentation regarding proxies. It corrects a missing word in the description of how proxies are shared between threads, improving clarity for users reading the notes on proxies.

This commit updates the documentation for the Request class in flask/wrappers.py to clarify how JSON requests are identified. It explicitly mentions the JSON mimetype and references the is_json method in the descriptions for the json property and get_json function.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the copyright header of the `flask/debughelpers.py` module. It removes an extraneous "1" character that appeared before the copyright notice, ensuring the file metadata displays correctly.

This commit removes the deprecated `encoding` parameter from Flask's JSON serialization functions, including `dump`, `dumps`, `load`, and `loads`. Users will no longer see deprecation warnings when calling these functions, and the parameter is no longer accepted.

This commit updates the Flask documentation and example READMEs to include a shell prompt prefix before command-line examples. This change clarifies that the text represents commands to be executed in a terminal, improving readability for users following the guides.

This commit updates the pinned versions of several development and typing dependencies, including filelock, pip-tools, mypy, and various type stubs. These changes ensure the project uses the latest compatible releases of these tools for development and static analysis.

The release script previously failed to correctly parse changelog entries because its date-matching pattern required the text to start at the beginning of the line. This fix updates the regular expression in the parse_changelog function to allow for leading whitespace, ensuring the script accurately identifies release dates.
This commit updates the project's changelog to reflect version 0.11 instead of 1.0. It corrects the version header in the CHANGES file to match the current release.

This commit fixes a Python 3 import error in the Flask command-line entry point. It changes the main module to use a relative import for the CLI, ensuring the application starts correctly when run as a script.

This commit simplifies the file-based database configuration example in the documentation. It removes the dynamic path calculation logic and replaces it with a static temporary file path for the SQLite database URI.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to fix broken external links and redirects. It corrects URLs in various deployment and configuration guides, ensuring users can access the correct resources for tools like BIND, Fabric, and Google App Engine.

This commit updates documentation examples in the sqlite3 and signals modules to use Python 3 print function syntax. It corrects outdated code snippets that would cause syntax errors if copied and run in a modern Python environment.

This commit updates the Python dependencies in the requirements files to newer versions. It bumps sphinx to 7.3.7, pyright to 1.1.359, and pallets-sphinx-themes to 2.1.2. These changes ensure the project uses the latest stable releases for documentation and type checking tools.

Fixes a syntax error in the documentation example for generating a secret key. The corrected command in the configuration guide now properly prints the generated token without an extra closing parenthesis.

This commit removes Python 2.5 from the supported versions in the project's CI configuration. It also eliminates the specific pre-install step for the simplejson library, which was required for that older Python version.

This commit prevents the template memory leak test from running on Python versions other than CPython 2.7. It adds a version check to the MemoryTestCase class in the Flask regression test suite to ensure the test only executes in the specific environment where it is valid.

This commit removes the separate `requirements-skip` directory and moves its test dependency files into the main `requirements` folder. It updates `tox.ini` to reference the new file locations and adds a configuration to skip installation for the update environment.

This commit updates the donation link in the documentation configuration to include a reset parameter, ensuring the contribution form loads correctly. The change modifies the URL in the `html_context` setting within `docs/conf.py`.

This commit fixes a typo in the JavaScript documentation where "is is" was corrected to "it is." The change improves the clarity of the explanation regarding how JavaScript interacts with Jinja template rendering.

This commit removes outdated documentation from the testing guide that incorrectly stated database connections were closed before after-request functions ran. It clarifies the testing documentation by deleting this misleading sentence.

This commit fixes an issue where the session cookie was not properly removed because the `samesite` and `secure` attributes were missing during deletion. The `SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session` method in `flask/sessions.py` now includes these options when calling `delete_cookie`.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `test_client_class` attribute in the `Flask` class. It clarifies that this attribute defines the class used to create test client instances, replacing a vague description with a precise reference to the default `FlaskClient` class.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 3.1.3 by updating the version string in the project configuration and lock files. It also marks the release as complete in the changelog, removing the unreleased status.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.12.4.dev in the `__init__.py` file. It marks the start of the next development cycle following the 0.12.3 release.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to replace gendered pronouns with the gender-neutral "they." It improves the readability and inclusivity of the user guide and API reference without changing any application behavior.

This commit removes legacy fallback imports for `url_quote`, `wrap_file`, and `url_parse` in `flask/helpers.py` and `flask/testing.py`. It standardizes the codebase to rely exclusively on the current Werkzeug module locations, eliminating unnecessary compatibility checks.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for the error handling module. It fixes the typo "exceptinos" to "exceptions" in the description of the debug option, ensuring the text is accurate for users.

The `flask run` CLI command now supports an `extra_files` option, allowing users to specify additional files for the reloader to watch. This change is implemented in the `run_command` function within `flask/cli.py`.

This commit adds a test to verify that the CLI correctly re-raises specific exceptions when lazy loading fails. It ensures that `DispatchingApp` properly propagates errors from background loading tasks. The change also removes an outdated test for background loading.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to reflect that signal handlers must now accept extra keyword arguments. It modifies the example function signatures in the signals guide to include the required parameter, ensuring users implement handlers correctly.
This commit removes an unused system import from the Flask configuration module. It cleans up the codebase without altering any application behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.

The project's continuous integration setup is migrated from Azure Pipelines to GitHub Actions. This change removes the legacy Azure configuration and introduces a new workflow file to run tests on pull requests and pushes.

This update documents that the `flask.Flask.run` method now accepts `None` for `host` and `port` arguments. It allows developers to pass configuration values directly, ensuring the method uses default values when `None` is provided.

This commit fixes the Read the Docs build by explicitly specifying the Sphinx configuration file path. It ensures the documentation builds correctly by pointing to `docs/conf.py` in the `.readthedocs.yaml` configuration.

This commit updates the CONTRIBUTING.rst file to include a new section on submitting patches. It provides contributors with step-by-step instructions for setting up their git environment, forking the repository, and creating branches for their changes.

This commit removes outdated references to a mailing list from the project's documentation and configuration files. It updates the contributing guide and extension development docs to direct users to GitHub Discussions and Discord instead.

This commit updates the documentation theme submodule and adds a tabular columns directive to the HTML FAQ. It ensures the documentation renders with the correct table layout for the specified content.

This commit adds explicit documentation for inherited attributes in the Flask and Blueprint classes to improve API reference clarity. It defines the import_name, template_folder, and root_path attributes directly on these classes to ensure they appear in generated documentation.

This commit replaces the deprecated assert_ method with assert_true across the Flask test suite to eliminate annoying deprecation warnings. The change affects the FlaskTestCase class and various test modules, ensuring cleaner test output without altering the actual test behavior.

This commit removes the static RST files used to list approved, listed, and unlisted extensions. It replaces this manual documentation with a dynamic website listing, ensuring the extension status is always up to date.

This commit updates the Flask Persona example to display a specific site name during the login process. It modifies the persona.js script to pass the site name to the browser's identity request and updates the layout template title to match.

This commit updates the Flask contribution guide to fix a setup error. It adds a missing directory change command before the editable install step, ensuring users correctly navigate to the project root before installing the package.

In the Flask class, the `preprocess_request` and `do_teardown_request` methods now access the current request's blueprint via the `_request_ctx_stack` instead of the global `request` proxy. This change ensures consistency with other parts of the application that use the context stack to retrieve request data.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the error message displayed by the DebugFilesKeyError class in the Flask debug helpers module. It ensures the message accurately states that the browser transmitted file names, improving clarity for developers debugging file upload issues.

This commit removes the redundant `cache` parameter from the `_get_data` helper and `JSONMixin.get_json` method in `flask/wrappers.py`. It also adds a new section to the testing documentation describing how to test JSON APIs.

This commit corrects grammatical errors and punctuation in the Flask documentation, specifically within the Foreword and Tutorial sections. It improves the clarity of the user guide by fixing sentence structure in files covering setup, templates, and database configuration.

This commit corrects the formatting of extension review metadata in the extreview documentation files. It ensures that fields like approval dates and versions use the proper RST field list syntax, preventing rendering errors in the generated documentation.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `tojson` filter in Flask's API and templating guides. It corrects outdated instructions regarding escaping within script tags, noting that automatic handling began in Flask 0.10.

This commit adds a test to verify that enabling debug mode via the app run method correctly triggers template auto-reloading. It ensures the Jinja environment updates its auto-reload setting when the debug flag is passed directly to the run function.

The `make_test_environ_builder` function in `flask/testing.py` now correctly extracts the URL scheme from the provided path. This ensures that test requests using HTTPS paths generate the correct scheme in the environment, rather than defaulting to the application's preferred scheme.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask's application and request contexts, clarifying how the `g` object stores data during an application context. It also refines the `Flask` class and `ctx` module to better describe context management and teardown processes.

This commit changes the `flask run` command to immediately exit with a traceback if errors occur during the initial server startup, rather than deferring them. It modifies the `DispatchingApp` class to automatically determine eager loading based on the Werkzeug environment, ensuring errors are only deferred when the server is reloading.
This commit updates the version history documentation for the Flask application, Blueprint, and Request classes. It corrects the recorded introduction version for specific features from 0.11 to 1.0.

This commit introduces environment support to Flask, allowing users to set the app's mode via the FLASK_ENV variable. It automatically enables debug mode when the environment is set to development, changing how the Flask class and CLI handle configuration.

This commit corrects minor grammatical errors and punctuation in the Flask configuration documentation. It improves the readability of the text in the docs/config.rst file without altering any application behavior.

This commit updates the SQLAlchemy documentation to clarify how to properly register models. It explains that importing model modules is required before initializing the database to ensure they are registered on the metadata. The changes focus on the `init_db` function usage.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.1.6 to v0.1.9. It ensures the project uses the latest available version of the tool for code quality checks.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.8.8 to 1.8.10. This patch-level update ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for deploying packages.

This commit standardizes project metadata by updating the release script and build configuration files. It refactors the make-release.py script to handle versioning and packaging tasks more consistently. The changes also clean up the MANIFEST.in and Makefile to ensure proper file inclusion during distribution.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to include an installation step. It ensures the project is installed in editable mode before running tests, allowing the build to use the current codebase.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to include the `run --debug` command syntax, which was previously hidden because it was not yet available in the 2.2.x release. It clarifies that the debug flag can be passed to the top-level command or the run subcommand. The changes affect multiple documentation files, including `cli.rst` and `config.rst`.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `send_file` function where ETags were not correctly generated for file streams that had a name. Users relying on conditional requests might have experienced incorrect cache validation. The change ensures the ETag is properly set for these file objects.
This commit updates the Python setup action in the test workflow from version 3 to version 4. It ensures the CI environment uses the latest major release of the setup tool.

This commit fixes type annotation errors that occurred in Python 3.6.0 by replacing unavailable typing imports with the typing_extensions library. It updates the Flask, NullSession, and Request classes to ensure compatibility with older Python versions.
This commit approves the Flask-CouchDB extension for version 0.2.1 under the MIT license. It adds the new entry to the approved list and removes the pending Flask-mail entry from the listed file.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to improve readability and accuracy. It wraps long lines, tightens the wording for the routing section, and removes a converter reference. The changes also correct the reStructuredText code syntax in the `docs/quickstart.rst` file.

This commit corrects a typo in the application factory documentation. It clarifies the explanation for creating multiple instances of the app by adding the missing word to the sentence in the appfactories module.

This commit removes an outdated compatibility note in the Flask application class. The note previously advised users to handle a missing attribute on internal server errors for older Werkzeug versions, which is no longer necessary.

The CLI now displays a clear error message to stderr when the application fails to load, instead of showing a full traceback or a generic "command not found" error. This improves the user experience for commands like --help by making loading failures more obvious. The change also fixes a test fixture issue where imported apps remained accessible after tests completed.
This commit adds a new changelog file and restructures the documentation index. It renames the "Textual Documentation" section to "User's Guide" and includes the changelog in the docs.

This commit adds support for PathLike objects to Flask's static file helpers, allowing users to pass pathlib.Path instances directly to send_file and send_from_directory. It introduces a compatibility function in flask/_compat.py to handle the conversion, ensuring these functions work with any object implementing the __fspath__ protocol.

This commit adds a Python 3.7 classifier to the project's setup configuration. It ensures the package metadata correctly indicates compatibility with that specific Python version for users and package managers.

This commit updates the documentation to explain that new sessions restrict data to JSON with limited extensions. It also notes that users can maintain compatibility with the old session system by installing the Flask-OldSessions extension.
This commit updates the project's setup.py file to include brief instructions for saving and running a sample script. It adds simple text guidance to help users quickly test the application setup.

This commit adds a minimal blueprint example to the Flask documentation. It demonstrates how to create a simple blueprint that renders static templates and handles missing pages with a 404 error. The changes are located in the blueprints documentation file.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency in the development requirements from version 2.8.2 to 2.9.3. It ensures the project uses the newer version of the pre-commit framework for its development environment.
This commit removes the manual style check job from the GitHub Actions test workflow. The project now relies on pre-commit.ci to handle code style validation automatically.

This commit updates the flake8 configuration to use the new extend-select and extend-ignore syntax, replacing the deprecated select and ignore options. It also fixes a bugbear lint error in the test suite by changing a generic exception to a specific ValueError in the app context teardown test.

This commit adds documentation for creating custom error pages in Flask. It introduces a new pattern guide explaining how to replace the default plain-text error responses with custom HTML pages for common HTTP status codes.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, and testing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions to ensure the build environment uses the most recent tooling.

This commit refactors the `test_jsonify_basic_types` method in the `TestJSON` class to use pytest's parametrize decorator. It replaces a manual loop over a hardcoded tuple of values with a parameterized test, allowing each basic type to be tested individually.

This commit adds a test to ensure that creating a Flask application does not trigger an import of the application name. It introduces a new test case in the helpers module that verifies this behavior using a dummy module designed to raise an error if imported.

This commit updates the Azure Pipelines configuration to correct the display name of the test job. The job label is changed from "Flask" to "Tests" in the .azure-pipelines.yml file, ensuring the pipeline interface accurately reflects the job's purpose.

This commit updates the license link on the Flask website homepage to point to the local documentation page instead of the GitHub repository. This ensures the license information remains accessible even if the external source changes or becomes unavailable.
