Flask now supports Click 7 to improve compatibility with other libraries, though it triggers a deprecation warning. The main function in the CLI module checks the Click version to issue this warning. This change relaxes the dependency requirement in the setup configuration.
This commit removes trailing whitespace from the configuration documentation. It cleans up the formatting in the config.rst file to improve code hygiene.

This commit cleans up the CLI documentation by removing incorrect text regarding filename-based configuration. It corrects the description of the FLASK_DEBUG environment variable in the docs/cli.rst file.

This commit restructures the Flask documentation by adding a new "Textual Documentation" section to the index. It also includes links to the external Jinja2 and Werkzeug documentation, clarifying that these dependencies are not covered in the main Flask docs.

This commit ensures the `SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT` configuration and `get_send_file_max_age` hook apply consistently to all file serving operations, not just static files. Previously, calling `send_file` directly ignored these settings, but now it respects them. The changes primarily affect the `Flask` and `Blueprint` classes in `flask/app.py` and `flask/helpers.py`.

This commit enables Flask's View and MethodView classes to handle asynchronous request handlers. Previously, class-based views did not support async functions, but now they correctly dispatch to coroutine-based methods.
This commit corrects a typo in the Flask quickstart documentation. It removes a duplicated word in the description of the URL routing module, ensuring the text reads clearly for users.

This commit updates the Python version classifiers in the project's setup configuration to align with Werkzeug's standards. It removes support for Python 2.6 and 2.7, replacing them with a general Python 3 specification.

This commit updates the Travis CI build matrix to test the project against both the lowest supported and development versions of dependencies. It introduces new requirements files for these specific versions and excludes Python 3.3 from the lowest-requirements test to avoid compatibility issues.

This commit updates six Python dependencies in the requirements directory to their latest versions. It includes minor and patch upgrades for packages such as cryptography, mypy, pytest, and tox. These changes ensure the project uses current, supported versions of its development and testing tools.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.1.3 by updating the version number in the project configuration and lock files. It also adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes for this release.

This commit updates the documentation for the `as_view` method in the `View` class within `flask/views.py`. It clarifies the explanation of how the method generates a view function and adjusts line wrapping to fit the file's character limit.

This commit removes a redundant call to the URL builder in the `url_for` function within `flask/helpers.py`. Previously, if the initial build attempt succeeded, the code would unnecessarily execute the same build operation a second time. This change ensures the URL is constructed only once, improving efficiency.
This commit updates the extension development documentation to include a new approval requirement. It specifies that extensions must now support Python versions 2.5, 2.6, and 2.7 to be approved.

This commit restores the `Session` class to the public API in the `flask` module. It ensures that existing code importing `Session` directly from the top-level package continues to work without errors.
This commit fixes a minor documentation typo in the testing guide by removing an unnecessary period before a code block. The change is located in the `docs/testing.rst` file.

The deployment documentation now includes a direct link to PythonAnywhere's Flask hosting instructions. This addition helps users find specific guidance for deploying their applications on that platform.

This commit simplifies the Travis CI configuration by removing the explicit version constraint for the tox package. It also streamlines the test execution command by using a standard environment variable format instead of complex shell string manipulation.

This commit fixes a race condition in the Flask application class where the first request flag could be set incorrectly under concurrent load. It ensures that before-first-request functions execute exactly once by moving the flag update to the correct location. A new test verifies this behavior using concurrent threads.

This commit updates the documentation for the SessionInterface class in Flask's sessions module. It clarifies that concurrent requests may access the same session simultaneously, warning developers to synchronize reads and writes to the backing store. The text also notes that session opening and saving occur in the order requests begin and end processing.

This commit updates the urllib3 dependency from version 1.26.3 to 1.26.4 in the development and documentation requirements files. The upgrade addresses a security vulnerability in the library, ensuring the project uses a patched version.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.1.0. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

This commit updates Flask to use explicit imports for Werkzeug utilities, such as `abort` and `redirect`, instead of importing them from the top-level package. This change affects the `Flask` class and related modules to ensure compatibility with newer Werkzeug versions.

This commit updates the documentation configuration to point to the current Blinker documentation site. It fixes broken cross-reference links in the generated docs by replacing the outdated PythonHosted URL with the new Read the Docs address.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to ensure compatibility with Python 3 by replacing the deprecated built-in reload function with six's reload_module. The change specifically affects the ExtImportHookTestCase setup method, allowing extension import tests to run correctly across different Python versions.

This commit removes the standalone async helper function from Flask's helpers module to prevent user code from bypassing app-level configuration. It introduces a new async_to_sync method on the Flask class, ensuring that any custom extensions modifying synchronization behavior are respected throughout the application.

This commit updates the distribution documentation to remove references to the deprecated easy_install tool. It clarifies that pip is the standard installation manager and notes that modern Python versions include pip and setuptools by default.

This commit adds an optional encoding parameter to the open_resource methods in the Flask and Blueprint classes. It allows users to specify the text encoding when opening resource files, defaulting to UTF-8.

This commit updates the deployment documentation to include Google Cloud Run as a new hosted option for Flask. It adds a link to the official quickstart guide, allowing users to find instructions for building and deploying their applications on that platform.

This commit updates the documentation configuration and static assets for the Flask project. It removes legacy Python 2 compatibility code from the Sphinx configuration and cleans up the build scripts. Additionally, it renames and updates the project's logo and favicon files.

This commit fixes a truncated docstring in the `explain_template_loading_attempts` function within `flask/debughelpers.py`. It completes the sentence to clarify that the function helps developers understand what failed during template loading.

This commit removes support for Python 2.6 and 3.3 by deleting their test configurations and updating documentation. It modifies the Travis CI setup and tox configuration to exclude these versions from the build matrix. The changes also update the changelog and installation guides to reflect the new minimum version requirements.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the Flask documentation for URL processors. It fixes a typo in the description of the `url_defaults` function within the `urlprocessors.rst` file.

This commit updates the error handling documentation to clarify that error handlers display custom error pages. It also corrects a grammatical error in the description of how these handlers are registered for exceptions.

This commit adds Flask-Testing and Flask-WTF to the approved extensions list in the extreview module. It also removes Flask-CouchDB from the listed extensions, resolving a previous issue where its test suite was missing from the distribution package.

This commit corrects minor grammar and spelling errors in the Flask documentation and source code. It fixes a typo in the docstring for the `safe_join` function and improves sentence structure in the template inheritance guide.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to standardize error messages for JSON parsing failures. It replaces dynamic exception details with a fixed string to ensure compatibility with Python 3's JSON loading exception format.

This commit adds a blank line to the `flask/signals.py` module. It improves code readability by adjusting whitespace after an import exception block. No functional behavior or user-facing logic is changed.

This commit updates the Flask package version from a development build to the stable 1.0 release. It modifies the `__version__` variable in the `flask/__init__.py` module to reflect the final release status.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.2.0 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the changelog as released. It changes the package version from a development build to the stable release.

This commit configures Dependabot to automatically check for updates to GitHub Actions workflows. It schedules these checks to run monthly on Mondays at 16:00 UTC, ensuring the project's CI/CD infrastructure stays current.

This commit deprecates the `__version__` attribute in the Flask package, advising users to use `importlib.metadata` for version checks instead. Accessing the attribute now triggers a warning via a new `__getattr__` function in `src/flask/__init__.py`.

Updates the TestJSON class in tests/test_helpers.py to verify error messages without relying on specific HTML formatting. This change ensures the tests remain compatible with both older and newer response formats by checking for the plain text content instead of the full paragraph tag.

This commit introduces a new .editorconfig file to standardize code formatting across the project. It enforces consistent indentation, line endings, and whitespace rules for all supported file types, ensuring a uniform development environment.

This commit updates the test suite for the sendfile helper to explicitly verify that specific deprecation warnings are raised. By specifying the warning category when clearing the record, the tests now ensure the correct warning types are triggered rather than just checking the total count.

This commit updates the jinja2 dependency from version 2.11.2 to 2.11.3 in the development and documentation requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the Jinja2 templating engine.

This commit fixes a typo in the shell documentation by correcting the phrase "firstly import" to "star import." The change clarifies the intended behavior for users setting up interactive sessions in the shell module.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.6.4 to 1.8.4. This dependency upgrade ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release for deploying packages to PyPI.
This commit updates the Flask package version from 0.11-dev to 0.10.1. It modifies the version string in the main module and the setup configuration to reflect the new release.

This commit updates the documentation for the `APPLICATION_ROOT` configuration value in Flask. It clarifies that this setting defines the session cookie path only when `SESSION_COOKIE_PATH` is not explicitly configured.
This commit adds a link to the project's official Discord chat server in the README. It provides users with a direct way to access the community chat for support and discussion.

This commit updates the pinned versions of development dependencies and GitHub Actions workflows. It refreshes the configuration files for testing, building, and publishing to ensure the project uses the latest stable tooling.

The `BetterLoader` class in `run-tests.py` now identifies test cases more accurately by matching names that appear as distinct segments within the full path, not just at the end. This prevents valid tests from being missed during discovery.
This commit updates the jQuery documentation to remove the obsolete type attribute from script tag examples. It clarifies that modern browsers do not require this attribute to execute JavaScript.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the testing documentation. It changes the phrasing in the description of the TESTING config flag to improve clarity for users reading the guide.
This commit updates the Read the Docs build environment configuration. It changes the operating system from Ubuntu 20.04 to 22.04 and upgrades the Python version from 3.10 to 3.12.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation example for the signals module. It updates the code snippet in docs/signals.rst to accurately reflect the expected output, ensuring users see the correct variable name.

This commit updates Flask documentation to clarify that extensions should store data on the `flask.g` object rather than the application context stack. It replaces outdated examples using the internal `_app_ctx_stack` with modern patterns using `flask.g` in the application context, SQLite3, and database connection tutorials.

This commit updates the documentation for the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` to remove outdated security advice. It replaces a manual filename validation example with a recommendation to use `send_from_directory` for handling user-provided file paths safely.

This commit allows developers to customize the URL routing map class used by the Flask application. It introduces a new `url_map_class` attribute to the `Flask` class, defaulting to Werkzeug's standard Map, and updates the initialization process to instantiate this configurable class instead of hardcoding the default.

The `got_first_request` property on the `Flask` class is now deprecated and will be removed in version 2.4. Accessing this property triggers a `DeprecationWarning` to alert developers that the feature is no longer supported.

This commit adds the `app_template_filter` method to the `Blueprint` class in `flask/blueprints.py`. It allows developers to register custom Jinja2 template filters that are available across the entire application, not just within the specific blueprint.

This commit updates the development dependency tox from version 3.18.0 to 3.18.1. The change is recorded in the requirements/dev.txt file to ensure the project uses the latest patch release of the testing tool.
This update documents a change in how automatic JSON request data unpacking works. The system now considers the charset mimetype parameter when processing requests.

The `safe_join` function in `flask/helpers.py` now uses `posixpath` to construct paths, ensuring consistent behavior on Windows. This change prevents potential path traversal issues by standardizing how directory components are joined.

This commit adds a test case to verify that static files are correctly served when a Flask module is registered with a specific subdomain. The new test in `SubdomainTestCase` ensures that accessing a static file via the subdomain URL returns the expected content.
This commit adds support for the "query" HTTP method in Flask's MethodView class. Users can now define a query method to handle requests using this specific verb.

This commit adds documentation to the `_called_with_wrong_args` function in `flask/cli.py`. It explains that the traceback variable is explicitly deleted to prevent circular references, referencing the Python standard library documentation.

This commit fixes the GitHub link generator in the documentation configuration to correctly identify development releases. It replaces a simple string check with a robust version parsing method, ensuring links work properly for all development version formats.
The CI workflow now tests Python 3.11 as a stable release and adds support for Python 3.12 development builds. This update also configures the test environment to use the latest version of tox.

This commit updates the Config class in Flask to accept PathLike objects for file paths, not just strings. This change aligns the configuration methods with standard Python practices, allowing users to pass path objects directly to functions like from_file and from_pyfile.

This commit removes the `register_error_handler` method from the `Blueprint` class in Flask. It also deletes the associated test case for blueprint-specific user error handling. This reverts a previous feature addition, restoring the prior behavior where blueprints could not register custom error handlers.

This commit removes the documentation section for HTTP Public Key Pinning from the web security guide. The feature is considered obsolete and unsupported by major browsers, making the previous advice and external links outdated.

This commit fixes several typos in the documentation for the Flask class and the send_file helper function. It corrects misspellings in the docstrings to improve clarity for users reading the API reference.

This commit makes the request, session, and g objects available in imported Jinja templates by adding them as proxies to the template context. The change is implemented in the Flask class's create_jinja_environment method to ensure these variables are accessible outside of standard context processors.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the signals module regarding the use of the captured_templates context manager. It clarifies that the list of recorded templates must be passed as an argument rather than being returned, and updates the example code to reflect this correct usage.

This commit updates the Celery integration pattern in the documentation to prevent the loss of the current context. It corrects the task execution method to ensure proper context handling within the Flask application.

This commit modernizes the Flask codebase by replacing string formatting with f-strings across the source, tests, and documentation. It affects core modules like the Flask app, blueprints, and CLI, as well as various helper functions and test suites.
This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class, specifically within the finalize_request method. It also adds a missing comma to improve the readability of the text.

This commit corrects a misleading error message in the `url_for` function within `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies that URL generation requires an active application context, fixing a confusing description of the failure condition.
This commit corrects a typo in the extension development documentation. It clarifies that the extension itself, rather than the license, must be BSD, MIT, or WTFPL licensed.

This commit cleans up the SVG files used for the Flask documentation branding. It updates the horizontal, vertical, and icon assets to improve their structure or rendering. No functional code changes are included.

This commit corrects the suggested command for initializing submodules in the documentation build configuration. It updates the error message in `docs/conf.py` to recommend the proper `git submodule update --init` command instead of the incomplete `git submodule init`.

This commit adds documentation for serving Single-Page Applications with Flask. It introduces a new guide explaining how to configure static folders and catch-all routes, and updates the patterns index to link to this new section.

The test target in the Makefile now invokes the dedicated test runner script instead of the setup module. This change ensures the project uses its preferred testing infrastructure for executing the test suite.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Flask tutorial's setup guide. It clarifies that the application module should be placed in the `flaskr` folder rather than the `flask` folder, ensuring users follow the correct directory structure.

This commit improves error reporting in Flask's session system when non-ASCII byte strings are encountered. It introduces a new UnexpectedUnicodeError class in flask/debughelpers.py and updates the TaggedJSONSerializer in flask/sessions.py to raise this specific error with a helpful message instead of a generic failure.

This documentation update clarifies that the `flaskext_compat` module must be activated rather than simply imported to enable the `flask.ext` namespace. It corrects the usage instructions in the extensions guide to reflect the proper initialization step.

This commit updates the table of contents in the deployment documentation to reorganize the self-hosted options. It moves the mod_wsgi entry to appear under the uwsgi section, clarifying the hierarchy for users navigating the guide.

This commit corrects indentation errors in the reStructuredText documentation for the Flask class. It ensures that code examples and text descriptions for the `template_global` method are properly formatted, preventing rendering issues in the generated documentation.
This commit corrects a syntax error in the WTForms documentation example. It ensures the code snippet properly returns the redirect response, preventing users from copying invalid Python code.
Removes the deprecated `from_json` method from the `Config` class in Flask. Users should now use `from_file` with a JSON loader instead to load configuration from JSON files.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `g` object in `flask.globals` to use `_AppCtxGlobals` instead of `AppContext`. It also reformats the `session` annotation for clarity. This ensures static type checkers report the correct type for the application context object.

This commit updates the method override documentation to clarify that the HTTP method is replaced with the header value before being passed to Flask. It also corrects the encoding of quotation marks in the text.

This commit updates the changelog to document a bug fix in Flask version 0.11.1. It resolves an issue where setting the FLASK_APP environment variable to a package's __init__.py file failed to work correctly.

This commit removes the "Share your Local Server with a Friend" section from the quickstart documentation. It eliminates instructions for using the localtunnel tool to expose a local Flask server, simplifying the guide for users.

The `flask run` command now supports HTTPS by accepting `--cert` and `--key` options. This allows developers to run the development server over a secure connection using ad-hoc certificates, imported objects, or file paths.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 3.1.2 by updating the version number in the project configuration and lock files. It also marks the release date in the changelog and restricts the zipp dependency to Python versions below 3.10.

This commit changes how Flask CLI handles environment files so that a path specified with the `-e` flag takes precedence over default `.env` and `.flaskenv` files. The `load_dotenv` function now loads default files in addition to the specified path unless `load_defaults=False` is passed.

This commit adds a new configuration variable, `JSONIFY_MIMETYPE`, to allow developers to customize the MIME type returned by `jsonify` responses. Previously, the content type was hardcoded to `application/json` within the `jsonify` function in `flask/json.py`. This change enables users to specify alternative MIME types through the Flask application configuration.

This commit corrects a broken documentation reference in the database connection tutorial. It updates the link in the dbcon.rst file to point to the correct sqlite3 section instead of the invalid slite3 target.

This commit removes an unused configuration option from the project's pyproject.toml file. It cleans up the project settings by deleting a redundant flag that had no effect on the build or linting process.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the MethodView example within the views module. It corrects a missing assignment so that the model attribute is properly set, ensuring the example code is accurate for users.

Adds a Travis CI configuration file to automate testing for the project. It sets up Python environments for versions 2.5 through 2.7 and PyPy, installs the simplejson dependency, and runs the test suite via setup.py.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation file `becomingbig.rst`. It changes the possessive form from "it's" to "its" to properly refer to the documentation.

This commit corrects minor spelling and grammar errors in the FastCGI deployment documentation. It fixes articles and capitalization in the `docs/deploying/fastcgi.rst` file to improve clarity and accuracy.

This documentation update clarifies that Python's default logging level is typically set to 'warning' when no specific configuration is provided. It explains that log messages below this threshold will not be visible to the user.

This commit improves the reliability of detecting incorrect function arguments in the Flask CLI by using traceback inspection instead of parsing error message strings. The `_called_with_wrong_args` function in `flask/cli.py` now distinguishes between a factory failing due to bad arguments and a factory that internally raises a TypeError.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the extension development documentation. It fixes a typo in the description of request context validity within the docs/extensiondev.rst file.

This commit corrects grammatical errors in the extension development documentation. It clarifies the instructions for specifying test dependencies within the setup file, improving readability for users following the guidelines.

This commit removes the Dependabot configuration file, disabling automated dependency updates for GitHub Actions and Python packages. Users will no longer receive automatic pull requests for security patches or version upgrades in these ecosystems.

This commit corrects the SQLite3 documentation to accurately describe how to access the database connection. It clarifies that users should call `get_db()` rather than accessing an incorrect `g.db` attribute, ensuring the pattern guide reflects the actual implementation.
Updates the Pallets Development Versions test job in the GitHub Actions workflow to use Python 3.8 instead of 3.7. This ensures the development environment tests run against the newer Python version.

This commit adds a new `send_file` function to the Flask module, allowing developers to efficiently serve file contents to clients. It includes support for various file types and attachment options, with corresponding tests and documentation updates.

This commit allows the Flask application to run even when the pkg_resources module is unavailable. It modifies the Flask class to fall back to the current working directory for locating resources if pkg_resources cannot be imported.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the Flask tutorial's schema file where the SQL column name "text" was missing required quotes. Without proper escaping, the database engine would fail to parse the schema definition. The change updates the example in docs/tutorial/schema.rst to correctly quote the reserved keyword.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for handling application errors. It rewrites the section on external debuggers to clarify how they interact with the built-in debug mode and improve the explanation of using IDEs for stepping through code.

In debug mode, Flask now detects when a form submission is missing the required enctype attribute. This change adds a helpful error message to the `Request` class to guide developers, preventing confusing generic errors.

This commit adds documentation explaining the "address already in use" error that occurs when starting a Flask server on a port already occupied by another program. It guides users to a new section in the server documentation for handling this specific OSError.

This commit refactors how Flask logs internal server errors by introducing a new `log_exception` method on the `Flask` class. It allows developers to customize the logging behavior for unhandled exceptions, replacing the previous hardcoded logging logic within `handle_exception`.

This commit replaces the deprecated `imp` module with `types.ModuleType` to ensure compatibility with Python 3.5 and later. It updates the `Config` class in `flask/config.py` and the `activate` function in `scripts/flaskext_compat.py` to use the new standard library approach for creating module objects.

This commit updates the documentation build dependencies to install a development version of Sphinx from the source repository. This change fixes broken documentation builds by resolving compatibility issues with the previous stable release. The update also bumps the versions of Jinja2 and MarkupSafe to support the new Sphinx version.

This commit ensures that the `test_extended_flashing` test in `flask/testsuite/basic.py` correctly propagates assertion errors instead of silently failing. It sets `app.testing = True` so that exceptions in view functions are raised rather than converted into 500 responses, preventing false positives in the test suite.

This commit rewrites the Flask deployment documentation to improve clarity and accuracy. It updates references in the async-await guide and adds a new section for Apache httpd, while refreshing content across various WSGI and ASGI server guides.

This commit removes support for Python 3.7 from the Flask project, updating the minimum required version to 3.8. It adjusts the test matrix, configuration files, and documentation to reflect this change, ensuring the codebase targets only Python 3.8 and later.

This commit reorganizes the test suite in tests/test_reqctx.py by moving the greenlet context copying tests into a new class named GreenletContextCopying. This change improves code structure and organization without altering the actual test behavior or fixing any bugs.

The documentation for testing the Flaskr tutorial now instructs users to install the application in editable mode using pip to ensure the module imports correctly. It also corrects the test setup example to use the `create_app` factory function instead of importing the application object directly.

This commit adds a donation section to the project documentation, encouraging users to support the Pallets organization. It also updates the donation link in the documentation configuration to include a reset parameter for a cleaner user experience.

This commit fixes minor typos in the documentation comments within the `flask/signals.py` module. It corrects the phrasing of the introductory text for the signal namespace and the core signals section.

The Flask development server now runs with threading enabled by default, allowing it to handle multiple requests concurrently. This change modifies the `run_command` function in `flask/cli.py` to update the default behavior for the `--with-threads` option.
The `Module` class in `flask.py` no longer accepts or stores a `package_name` argument. This removes an unused attribute from the module initialization process.
This commit adds a new testing guide to the documentation and corrects typos in the Minitwit example. It updates the Minitwit application code and templates to improve clarity and accuracy.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to clarify that the session cookie's cryptographic signature is validated against a maximum age. It explains that if the signature is older than the configured permanent session lifetime, the session is considered invalid. The changes are made in the configuration and security documentation files.

This commit prevents Blueprint view functions from having names that include dots, which previously caused routing errors. The `Blueprint.add_url_rule` method now raises an assertion error if the function name contains a dot.

This commit removes the custom `__init__` method from the `AppGroup` class in `flask/cli.py`. The change simplifies the class by relying on the default constructor from its parent class, `click.Group`, rather than explicitly calling it.

This commit updates the documentation to replace references to jQuery with modern JavaScript and the fetch API. It renames the relevant documentation file and updates the index to reflect this change, guiding users toward current web development standards.

This commit adds static type checking tests for Flask application decorators. It verifies that the `after_request`, `before_request`, and `teardown_appcontext` decorators correctly handle both synchronous and asynchronous functions. This ensures the type hints for these hooks are accurate for users.

This commit adds documentation to the file uploads guide explaining that the local development server may return a connection reset error instead of a 413 status code for large files. It clarifies that using a production WSGI server resolves this behavior.
This commit corrects a typo in the Flask configuration documentation. It removes a stray word from the description of the internal configuration values in the config.rst file.

This commit fixes broken documentation links in the docstrings for the `dump`, `dumps`, and `load` functions in Flask's JSON module. It corrects the Sphinx directive syntax so that references to the standard library's JSON functions render properly in the generated documentation.

This commit fixes a typo in the jQuery documentation where a hash symbol was incorrectly used instead of a dollar sign in the selector syntax. The change corrects the example in the `docs/patterns/jquery.rst` file to accurately reflect standard jQuery usage.
This commit standardizes the encoding name used in the `send_file` function within `flask/helpers.py`. It changes the string literal from 'utf8' to 'utf-8' to ensure consistent naming conventions.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify how Flask handles trailing slashes in URL rules. It explains that accessing an endpoint without a trailing slash triggers a redirect to the canonical URL, improving the clarity of the unique URLs section.

This commit adds a GitHub Actions workflow to run pre-commit checks on the repository. It introduces a new configuration file that triggers the pre-commit lite workflow, ensuring code style and linting standards are enforced automatically.

This commit cleans up the AppVeyor CI configuration by removing unnecessary quotes from environment variables and deleting a redundant Python version check command. It also streamlines the test matrix to include only Python 2.7 and 3.6, removing the Python 3.5 entry.

This commit removes references to the deprecated FLASK_ENV variable from the Flask documentation. It updates the CLI, configuration, and debugging guides to reflect current best practices, such as using the --app flag instead of environment variables.
This commit updates the project changelog to mark version 0.10 as officially released. It sets the release date to June 13, 2013, and assigns the codename Limoncello to this specific release.

The example tests for Flaskr and MiniTwit now pass on Windows by using a more compatible method to create and clean up temporary database files. This change updates the setUp and tearDown methods in the test case classes to properly manage file handles and remove files after tests.

This commit fixes a grammatical ambiguity in the Flask documentation's advanced foreword. It clarifies that the framework has "a few" design choices that may seem unorthodox, rather than implying it has few such choices. The change is located in the docs/advanced_foreword.rst file.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to replace generic assertion methods with more specific ones. It affects test classes in modules like basic, blueprints, and helpers to improve error reporting clarity.

The `Flask.add_url_rule` method now accepts an optional `view_func` parameter, allowing developers to register a view function directly when adding a URL rule. This simplifies the process of associating a rule, endpoint, and view function in a single step.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the CONTRIBUTING.rst file where the project was incorrectly referred to as Werkzeug. It updates the text to properly identify the project as Flask, ensuring contributors receive accurate information about the codebase they are working on.
This commit fixes a grammatical typo in the application context documentation. It corrects the phrase "On the contrast" to "In the contrast" within the appcontext.rst file.

This commit enables the `url_for` helper to generate URLs without an active request context by creating a URL adapter for the application context. It modifies the `Flask` class to support this new behavior and adds tests to verify basic URL generation works correctly.

This documentation update clarifies the error responses for Flask's `Request.json` property. It distinguishes between a 400 Bad Request error for invalid JSON bodies and a 415 Unsupported Media Type error for missing or incorrect Content-Type headers.

This commit removes a broken external link to the Sentry quickstart guide from the error handling documentation. The change updates the "See also" section in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file to prevent users from encountering a dead link.
This commit adds Python 3.15 to the project's test matrix and environment list. It ensures the codebase is verified against the new Python version in the CI workflow and local testing configurations.
This commit adds Flask-Login to the list of approved extensions in the extreview module. It records the initial approval date, version, and license for the package.

This commit standardizes SQL query casing in the tutorial documentation and test examples. It updates the `test_register` function in `test_auth.py` and the corresponding documentation to use uppercase keywords for consistency.

This commit adds copyright headers to numerous source files and reverts the copyright year to the project's start date. It also updates the documentation configuration to filter out copyright and license metadata from the generated API documentation.

This commit prevents users from nesting test client invocations in Flask. It raises a runtime error in the FlaskClient class when entering a context while one is already active, avoiding unexpected behavior.

This documentation update clarifies that the `zip_safe` flag in the setup script must be set to `False` for extension approval. It ensures developers understand this requirement applies even if the extension is technically safe for zipping.

This commit updates the pinned versions of several development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies. It ensures the project uses the latest stable releases of tools like pytest, pre-commit, and cryptography.

This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to clarify how the instance folder path is determined. It explains that users can either explicitly set the `instance_path` parameter or allow Flask to autodetect the location, noting that explicit paths must be absolute.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flask quickstart documentation. It fixes the `methods` parameter spelling in the login route example, ensuring the code snippet is accurate for users following the guide.
This commit adds a README file to the Flask sansio module. It explains that this code is designed for alternative implementations like Quart and must avoid input/output operations or Flask globals.

This commit resolves build warnings in the documentation configuration by updating the print statements in `docs/conf.py` to use Python 3 syntax. It also reformats the extension list for clarity and simplifies the error message displayed when Flask is not installed.

This commit adds type stub packages to the project's development and typing requirements. It includes types-dataclasses, types-setuptools, and cryptography to improve static type checking capabilities.

This commit standardizes the terminology in documentation and code comments by replacing the single-word "sourcecode" with the grammatically correct "source code." The changes affect the license, tutorial, and pattern documentation, as well as the `flask/signals.py` and `flask/templating.py` modules.

This commit updates the extension development guidelines to remove the requirement for Python 2.6 support. Extensions now only need to support Python 2.7, reflecting the end of security updates for the older version. The change is made in the `docs/extensiondev.rst` file.

This commit updates the changelog to document a bug fix in the Flask development server. It prevents `flask run` from displaying a NoAppException when an ImportError occurs within the imported application module.
This commit corrects several spelling errors in the Unicode documentation. It fixes typos in the unicode.rst file, including "pleasent" and "UTF08," to improve the clarity of the user guide.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.0.4 to 3.1.0. It modifies the pinned dependency versions in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the newer release.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.3.3 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the changelog entry as released. It removes the development suffix to indicate the stable release status.
This commit fixes a typo in the Waitress deployment documentation. It corrects the spelling of "reverse" in the section describing how to bind to external IPs.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.0.2. It updates the project version in the configuration file to a development release and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

The `shell_command` function in `src/flask/cli.py` now invokes the system's interactive hook to enable readline features. This change allows the Flask shell to provide tab and history completion by default when the readline module is available.

This commit introduces a tox configuration file to standardize the project's testing environment. It defines test environments for Python 2.6, 2.7, PyPy, and 3.3, ensuring the test suite runs consistently across these versions.
This commit updates the minimum required version of the Werkzeug dependency to 3.0.0. It modifies the project configuration and test requirements to ensure compatibility with the new major release.

This commit fixes a bug where renaming a Flask blueprint during registration did not update the endpoint names. The BlueprintSetupState class now correctly uses the renamed identifier when constructing URL rules.

This commit updates the packages documentation example to clarify how modules are registered with the application. It adds a `url_prefix` argument to the `register_module` call and explains that this prevents endpoints from defaulting to the root path.

This commit adds a placeholder note to the Azure Pipelines configuration file, indicating that a nightly build step is still pending. It does not change any current behavior or fix a bug, but documents a future task for the CI/CD pipeline.

This commit removes the static website files and the associated upload target from the main branch. It cleans up the repository by deleting the HTML pages, images, and the Makefile rule used to deploy the site.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.5.0 to v0.5.6. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the tool for code quality checks.

This commit updates the Flask application class to remove the use of ImmutableDict for default configuration values. It also adjusts the testing module to verify that the environment base defaults and modifications behave correctly.

This commit increases the base font size in the documentation and website to improve readability. It updates the Flasky theme's CSS to use a fixed pixel size for the body text and slightly larger sizes for the sidebar. The main project website's HTML is also adjusted to include a character set declaration and updated styling.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use the renamed repository URL for the reorder-python-imports hook. It ensures the tooling continues to function correctly by pointing to the new location of the project.

This commit updates the MethodView class in the flask.views module to automatically dispatch HEAD requests to the get method when a specific head handler is not defined. This change ensures that HEAD requests behave consistently with GET requests for method views, simplifying implementation for developers.

This commit adds documentation to the extension development guide, showing how to access the database connection outside of a request context. It explains that Flask 0.9 or later allows using the app context to execute database queries, with teardown handlers running automatically.

This documentation update corrects the Celery configuration example in the Flask patterns guide. It replaces the incorrect backend setting with the proper result backend configuration, ensuring users implement the right integration.

This commit updates the Fabric documentation to explain how to use a `setup.cfg` file for configuring development builds. It details how to set build tags so that `sdist` commands apply them correctly while release builds ignore them.

This commit adds pre-commit to the development dependencies in setup.py, ensuring it installs with the dev extras. It updates CONTRIBUTING.rst to instruct developers to use Black for code formatting via the pre-commit hook, replacing the previous general PEP8 guidelines.

The `load_dotenv` function in `flask.cli` now explicitly uses UTF-8 encoding when reading environment files. This ensures that non-ASCII characters, such as Chinese text, are loaded correctly instead of causing errors or garbled output.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2014 to 2015 across the Flask project. It modifies the license file, documentation configuration, and various example and test files to reflect the new year.

The `is_ip` function in `flask/helpers.py` now handles Python 2 on Windows, which lacks the `inet_pton` utility. It falls back to checking only IPv4 addresses using `inet_aton` in that specific environment to prevent errors.

This commit updates the type annotations for the errorhandler decorators in the Scaffold and Blueprint classes to use the new ErrorHandlerDecorator type. It also adds tests to verify that these type checks work correctly for various error handling scenarios.
Corrects a typo in the API error patterns documentation. The example code now properly imports the `jsonify` function from Flask instead of the misspelled `jsonfiy`.

This commit clarifies the navigation flow in the Flask installation documentation. It updates the text to guide users to the quickstart or documentation overview after installation, and corrects a reference to return to the previous section on Windows.

This documentation update fixes an AttributeError that occurred when Celery was instantiated without a backend argument. It instructs users to include the backend configuration in the Celery constructor to prevent runtime errors.

This commit adds a new security documentation page to the Flask project. It details security considerations such as Cross-Site Scripting and updates the documentation index to include the new section.

This commit introduces the initial version of the Flask web framework, including the core Flask class and helper functions. It also adds two example applications, apishowcase and minitwit, to demonstrate basic usage patterns.

This commit updates the documentation for the application context to improve clarity. It corrects the wording in the description of URL generation behavior when no request context is active. The change is limited to the `docs/appcontext.rst` file.

This commit updates the error handling documentation to remove outdated code examples for capturing custom exceptions with Sentry. It replaces the removed content with a brief reference to additional reading materials regarding worker queue error handling.

This commit adds a `request_globals_class` attribute to the `Flask` class, allowing developers to specify a custom class for the `g` object. This enables users to define custom attributes or behaviors for request-scoped data instead of using the default plain object.
This commit adds official support for Python 3.8 to the project. It updates the package metadata in setup.py and configures the test environment in tox.ini to include Python 3.8 in the test matrix.

This commit updates the Dependabot configuration to group all GitHub Actions and Python dependency updates into single pull requests. This reduces the number of individual update notifications and simplifies the review process for maintainers.

The test fixture for resetting logging now only re-registers the logging plugin if it was originally active. This prevents the test suite from incorrectly enabling the plugin when it was not part of the initial configuration.

The contributing guide for Flask has been updated to direct users to the #questions Discord channel and GitHub Discussions for support. It also corrects a command example in the setup instructions to include the shell prompt.

This commit prevents test failures in the Flask test suite when the pytz library is not installed. It adds a conditional import check and skips the aware datetime tests in the TestJSON class if pytz is unavailable.

This commit ensures that `after_request` handlers are executed even when an exception occurs during request processing. This change allows resources like database connections to be properly closed after errors. The update modifies the `Flask` class in `flask.py` and adds tests to verify this behavior.

This commit adds documentation for configuring Apache httpd to use FastCGI with a web application. It explains how to use the ScriptAlias directive or a custom WSGI middleware to hide the .fcgi file extension from user-facing URLs.

This commit fixes an issue in the `Request` class where form data was incorrectly loaded for multipart requests that contained no files. It ensures the monkeypatch is only applied when all files are missing, preventing unnecessary processing.

This commit adds a changelog entry for Flask version 0.7.2, documenting a bugfix release. It notes that URL processors now work correctly on blueprints, resolving a previous issue where they did not function as expected.
This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the Flask class's errorhandler method. It fixes a malformed cross-reference to the HTTPException class, ensuring documentation links render correctly.

This commit removes the installation and contributing sections from the Flask project's README. It aims to prevent users from installing the package directly into their system environment and relies on the GitHub interface for contribution links.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.3.1. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

This documentation update clarifies the installation process for Windows users by specifying that the `sudo` command should be omitted. It ensures users know to run the standard installation commands without elevated privileges on Windows systems.

This commit updates documentation links to use HTTPS instead of HTTP for PyPI resources. It ensures users are directed to the secure version of the site, avoiding unnecessary redirects. The changes affect multiple documentation files, including the changelog and API references.

This commit updates the development dependency tox from version 3.15.1 to 3.15.2. It modifies the requirements/dev.txt file to reflect this version bump, ensuring the project uses the latest patch release of the testing tool.

This commit documents the addition of a silent flag to the `Config.from_pyfile` method in the `flask/config.py` module. It updates the changelog and adds version notes to clarify that this parameter was introduced in version 0.7.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's error handling where raising an unhandled exception after registering a custom handler caused an uninformative IndexError instead of preserving the original error. The fix modifies the Flask._find_error_handler method to stop searching when the class hierarchy is exhausted, ensuring the correct exception is propagated.

This commit updates the `get_send_file_options` method in the `_PackageBoundObject` class within `flask/helpers.py`. It now returns a dictionary containing the `cache_timeout` setting from the application configuration instead of an empty dictionary.

The documentation build now uses an external reusable theme instead of the bundled flasky theme. This change removes the local theme files and updates the Sphinx configuration to reference the new external source.

This commit adds a new documentation chapter on fabric-based deployments to the project's patterns section. It also updates the configuration guide to link to the new deployment pattern and adds a reference label to the mod_wsgi deployment documentation.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the database initialization tutorial documentation. It corrects the verb "require" to "requires" in the `dbinit.rst` file to ensure the text is properly conjugated.

This update documents a change in Flask's behavior where the session is no longer modified when retrieving flashed messages if none exist. This prevents unnecessary session updates and potential side effects for users. The change affects the `flask.get_flashed_messages` function.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the `run_audit` command within `setup.py` by removing unnecessary triple quotes from a print statement. This ensures the script runs correctly when PyFlakes is not installed, preventing a crash during the audit process.

This commit corrects typos in the docstring for the `create_logger` function in Flask's logging module. It fixes grammatical errors in the description of how the application logger is retrieved and configured.

This commit relocates the test suite from the `flask/testsuite` directory to a top-level `tests` directory. It updates `setup.py` and `MANIFEST.in` to reflect this structural change, removing references to the old location.

This commit improves the readability of a sentence in the project's foreword documentation. It clarifies the description of Flask's foundation and adaptability for large applications. The change is limited to the docs/foreword.rst file.

This commit corrects grammatical errors and clarifies the description of the reloader feature in the error handling documentation. It updates the text to accurately state that the reloader restarts the process when modules change, rather than when an exception occurs.

This commit updates the changelog to document a fix for parsing IPv6 addresses with ports. The correction applies to the `run` command and the test client, ensuring these components handle such addresses correctly.

This commit updates the testing documentation to use direct imports for Flask components instead of accessing them through the main module. It clarifies the recommended import style for users writing tests by replacing `flask.xxx` references with `from flask import` statements.

This commit refactors the Flask command-line interface to improve the integration with the Click library. It restructures the `FlaskGroup` and `ScriptInfo` classes in `flask/cli.py` to better manage application loading and context. The changes also add detailed API documentation for these CLI components.

The `flash` function in `flask.py` now accepts an optional category parameter, allowing developers to tag messages as errors, warnings, or information. This change enables `get_flashed_messages` to filter and display messages based on their specific type.

This commit adds documentation to the deployment guide showing how to integrate Flask with the Tornado and gevent web servers. It provides code examples for users who want to run their Flask application using these specific non-blocking frameworks.

The Config class in flask.py now accepts any object, not just modules, for loading configuration values. The from_module method is renamed to from_object to reflect this broader capability, allowing users to pass classes or other objects directly.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask class's `inject_url_defaults` method where blueprint names containing dots were incorrectly parsed. It changes the string splitting logic to use the last dot as the delimiter, ensuring the correct blueprint is identified for URL generation.
This commit updates the contributing guide to include Python 3.7 in the list of required versions for running tests. It also corrects a missing comma in the documentation text.

This commit removes duplicate documentation text from the Flask class in flask/app.py. It cleans up the docstring for the static_folder parameter, which previously contained redundant lines describing the default value.
This commit updates the changelog to document the removal of the `create_jinja_loader` function. It notes that this feature is no longer used in version 0.5 due to improved module support.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the CLI guide where the `@click.command` decorator was missing parentheses. Without them, the example code fails with an AttributeError because the function object lacks the required name attribute. The change updates the example in `docs/cli.rst` to use `@click.command()` correctly.

This commit corrects two minor grammatical errors in the API documentation. It fixes a missing verb in the converter examples section and a subject-verb agreement error in the routing rules description within the docs/api.rst file.

This commit updates the main documentation page to include a brief description of Flask as a lightweight WSGI web application framework. It clarifies the project's purpose for new users before directing them to the installation guide.

This commit fixes an issue where calling `Request.get_json` with `cache=False` incorrectly returned previously cached data instead of re-parsing the request body. The `Request` class now respects the cache flag, ensuring fresh parsing when caching is disabled.

This commit updates the CHANGES.rst file to remove Sphinx cross-reference directives from the changelog entries. It replaces structured links with plain text names for methods and functions, such as SessionInterface.get_cookie_name and Config.from_file, to simplify the documentation format.

This commit updates the changelog to document that the `send_file` helper now supports `PathLike` objects, such as `pathlib` paths, in Python 3. It also includes minor formatting corrections to existing changelog entries.

This commit adds support for long-running sessions in the Flask application. It introduces a new `Session` class that allows developers to set a session as permanent, extending its lifetime beyond the browser session. The `Flask` class is updated to handle these permanent sessions via `open_session` and `save_session` methods.

This commit corrects a typo in the CLI documentation by adding a missing space in the Python module invocation command. It also fixes a grammatical error in the explanation of the script integration design.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude venv/ and .venv/ directories from version control. This prevents Python virtual environment folders from being accidentally committed to the repository.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.3.3. It updates the version string in the `flask` module to a development release and adds a new entry to the changelog.

This commit adds a test to the Flask test suite to verify that subdomain matching works correctly when the server name includes a port number. The new test case ensures that requests to a URL with a specific port are properly routed to the correct subdomain handler.

This change modifies the Flask application's response handling to prevent lists from being treated as response tuples. Previously, passing a list to the view function would incorrectly trigger tuple unpacking logic in the make_response method. Now, only tuples are processed for unpacking, allowing lists to be passed directly to the response class initializer.

This commit corrects the signal handler examples in the documentation to include the required sender argument. It ensures the code snippets for the template_rendered signal accurately reflect the expected function signature.

This commit finalizes the 1.0 release by updating the changelog to mark the version as released on April 26, 2018. It removes the "unreleased" status from the version header and adds a blank line to the unreleased section.

The migration script in `scripts/flaskext_migrate.py` previously failed to properly process source files. It now correctly reads the input, applies import fixes, and writes the updated code back to the file.

This commit updates the `CertParamType` class in `src/flask/cli.py` to accept any type instead of restricting it to specific string, path, or SSL context types. This change allows the CLI to handle a broader range of certificate parameter inputs without type errors.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency in the development requirements from version 2.12.0 to 2.12.1. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the pre-commit tool for running git hooks.

This commit updates the installation documentation to replace the `source` command with the POSIX-standard dot command for activating virtual environments. This change ensures the instructions work across different shell types, including those that do not support the `source` keyword.

This commit automates the generation of .mobi ebook files for the Flask documentation. It adds a Makefile target that uses Calibre to convert the existing .epub file and updates the sidebar template to include a direct download link for the new format.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use the new ruff-check hook and removes obsolete noqa comments from the Flask application and session modules. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating unnecessary suppression directives in the Flask class and NullSession class.

This commit aligns the behavior of `Flask.run` with the CLI `run_command` by enabling threaded mode by default and displaying additional server information. It also ensures that environment variables modified by `load_dotenv` correctly override the application's `env` and `debug` settings.
This commit updates the project's development and testing dependencies to newer versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions to ensure the latest linting and formatting tools are used.
This commit updates the Flask version number from 0.8 to 0.9-dev in the package initialization and setup files. It also adds a placeholder entry for the upcoming 0.9 release in the changelog.

This commit corrects a duplicated word in the Flask documentation for the request context. It clarifies the description of when teardown functions are executed, removing a redundant "are" from the text.

This commit updates the changelog to document a new behavior in the session module. It notes that the session cookie now sets the Vary: Cookie header whenever the session is accessed, modified, cleared, or refreshed.

This commit adds the `with_statement` future import to the Flask testing module and its test suite files. This change ensures the codebase remains compatible with Python 2.5, which requires this import to support the `with` statement syntax.
Updates the Flaskr test example to use the modern yield-based fixture syntax for the client fixture. This replaces the previous approach of manually adding a teardown function to the request context.

This commit standardizes the spelling of "URLs" in documentation and comments to match the prevailing style in the codebase. It updates the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py` and a template in the blueprint example to use the capitalized form.

This commit adds a test application structure that registers Flask blueprints to verify template and static file handling. It introduces a new test case in the Flask test suite to ensure that blueprint-based apps correctly serve resources, mirroring the behavior of legacy module apps.

This commit fixes minor typos and grammatical errors in the SQLite 3 documentation for Flask. It corrects phrasing in the `docs/patterns/sqlite3.rst` file to improve clarity regarding database connection handling and application context requirements.

This commit corrects an incorrect import path in the error handling documentation. It updates the reference to the file logging handler to use the correct module location, ensuring users copy the right import statement.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the API documentation for the session object. It corrects the phrasing regarding session lifetime in the docs/api.rst file to improve clarity for users.

This commit corrects a confusing sentence and removes a duplicated word in the application context documentation. It also fixes a typo in the quickstart guide where "the" was repeated before a link to the Jinja2 documentation.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE` configuration option in Flask. It updates the description in `docs/config.rst` to recommend the 'Lax' value and adds a version note. The changes also refine related security documentation and session interface tests.

This commit updates the approved version of Flask-SQLAlchemy in the extreview module from 0.9 to 0.9.1. It reflects a minor version bump in the project's documentation, ensuring the recorded approval matches the latest release.

This commit updates the documentation configuration to use the Alabaster theme by default. It removes the previous logic that attempted to load the Flask Sphinx theme and fall back to the default if unavailable.

This commit adds a new documentation chapter explaining how Flask handles Unicode text. It introduces a dedicated guide for developers to understand character encoding basics within the framework. The changes update the documentation index and create a new file detailing Unicode support.

This commit updates the project metadata in pyproject.toml by removing the authors field. It retains the maintainers entry, ensuring the package configuration reflects the current project ownership structure.

This commit adds a test to verify that the simplejson library no longer escapes forward slashes by default. It also updates the tox configuration to include a new test environment specifically for running tests with simplejson installed.

This commit fixes incorrect indentation in the project description string within setup.py. It ensures the text displays correctly in package metadata by removing extra leading spaces from the example output lines.

This commit renames the internal helper function in the Flask CLI module from `check_factory_for_script_info_and_call` to `call_factory`. The change simplifies the codebase by using a shorter, clearer name for the function that invokes application factories.

This commit removes outdated documentation in the Flask class constructor regarding backward compatibility for extension registration. It clarifies that extensions no longer need to check for the existence of the app.extensions attribute, as support for very old versions is no longer required.
This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the distribute pattern. It updates the example MANIFEST.in instructions to properly include all files in the templates and static directories.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the Flask configuration documentation. It clarifies that setting the host to "localhost" does not help with the described issue, improving the accuracy of the user guide.

This commit updates the changelog and setup.py to reflect new minimum version requirements for Werkzeug and Click. It also clarifies that running a Flask app from the command line development server will now be a no-op to prevent unexpected behavior.

This commit simplifies the MANIFEST.in file by replacing verbose recursive include and exclude commands with more concise graft and global-exclude directives. This change streamlines the source distribution packaging process for the project.

This commit updates development dependencies and GitHub Actions versions to their latest releases. It refreshes the pre-commit and publish workflows, along with related configuration files, to ensure compatibility with newer tooling.

This commit moves the `url_for` implementation from the helpers module to the `Flask` class, making it a method that handles missing application contexts. It updates the function signature to use keyword-only arguments and improves error messages for server name configuration.

This commit adds tests to the TestJSON class in tests/test_helpers.py, verifying that exception details are included in the response body only when the application's DEBUG setting is enabled. It ensures that users see specific error messages during development but receive generic responses in production environments.

This commit consolidates the project's code coverage configuration by moving settings from the dedicated .coveragerc file into setup.cfg. This change standardizes the configuration location, ensuring coverage tools read the same settings as other project metadata without altering the actual coverage behavior.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to include an AUTHORS file and license text, while fixing a typo in the main flask.py module. It clarifies contributor credits and ensures the license notice is properly displayed in the docs.

This commit updates the minimum version requirements for Werkzeug, Jinja2, and itsdangerous in the project setup. It also removes dependencies on development master branches from the test configuration, ensuring tests run against stable releases.

This commit removes the global suppression of the E402 linting rule in the project configuration. It updates the JavaScript example and blueprint test application to explicitly ignore this rule for specific imports, ensuring code style checks are enforced elsewhere.

This commit improves the automatic extension testing script by adding a new Makefile target to run tests with a browse option. It updates the test module to handle temporary directories more robustly across different operating systems and refactors imports for better organization.

This commit improves the documentation for the Flask class constructor. It clarifies that the first argument should be the application's module name, explaining why `__name__` is used to distinguish between running as a script or being imported.

This commit updates the test environment configuration to automatically install the argparse package when running tests on Python 2.6. It ensures the dependency is available for older Python versions that do not include it in the standard library.

This commit updates the documentation for the WTForms pattern to fix a broken link to the Flask-WTF project. It corrects the URL in the `docs/patterns/wtforms.rst` file to point to the current stable documentation, ensuring users can successfully access the referenced resources.

This commit improves the visual quality of the generated PDF documentation for Flask. It updates the Sphinx configuration in `docs/conf.py` to use a custom LaTeX style and a new index file, resulting in a more professional layout.

This commit updates the Flask extension development documentation to describe the approval process. It explains that approved extensions are tested with Flask releases and outlines requirements, such as using the flaskext namespace and providing a test suite.

This commit hardens the `safe_join` function in `flask/helpers.py` to explicitly reject filenames that are exactly `..`, preventing potential path traversal issues. It adds a regression test to verify that attempting to join a directory with `..` correctly raises a `NotFound` error.

This commit fixes a compatibility issue where Flask failed on Python versions below 3.6 due to the use of os.fspath. It replaces this call with the internal _compat.fspath function within the _PackageBoundObject class to restore support for older Python versions.
This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the FlaskGroup class in the Flask CLI module. It corrects the spelling of "wil" to "will" in a description regarding shell commands.

This commit adds documentation notes explaining that certain Flask objects are proxies. It updates the API and signals documentation to clarify this behavior for users. The changes primarily affect the docs/api.rst and docs/signals.rst files.

This commit adds a context manager for request binding to the Flask application class, simplifying how developers manage request contexts in tests or scripts. It also updates the API documentation to clarify the application object structure and incoming request data handling.

This commit allows view functions to disable the automatic OPTIONS request handling in Flask. By checking a specific attribute on the view function, the `Flask.add_url_rule` method now respects explicit opt-outs, preventing unwanted default behavior.
This commit updates the pytest dependency from version 6.1.1 to 6.1.2 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the testing framework.

This commit corrects grammatical errors and improves clarity in the Flask application context documentation. It updates the docs/appcontext.rst file to fix phrasing such as "in lack of" and "pillar's," ensuring the text reads more professionally.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.10 by updating the version string from a development build to the stable release. It modifies the version identifiers in the main package initialization and the project setup configuration.

This commit adds the `template_global` method to the Flask application and `app_template_global` to Blueprints, allowing developers to register custom functions available in all templates. It mirrors the existing template filter functionality, providing a new way to expose application logic to the view layer.

This commit updates the API documentation to include the `full_path` attribute in the Request object description. It clarifies that this attribute represents the complete request path, including any query string parameters.

This documentation update clarifies that request properties refer to IRIs rather than standard URLs. It updates examples in the API documentation to include extended characters, such as Japanese text, to better reflect internationalized resource identifiers.

This commit fixes test failures for uninstalled packages by ensuring path comparisons use consistent pathlib objects. It introduces a helper function to check if a path is relative to a base directory, improving compatibility across Python versions. The changes primarily affect the scaffold module's package discovery logic.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now explicitly sets the `Content-Length` header when using the `x-sendfile` mechanism. This ensures the client receives the correct file size information, preventing potential connection issues or incomplete downloads.

This commit integrates the Click library into Flask, replacing the previous command-line interface with a new `flask/cli.py` module. It introduces a `FlaskClickGroup` to manage commands and updates the `Flask` application class to support shell context processors and custom CLI commands.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to improve the quickstart deployment section. It adds a cross-reference in the general deployment guide pointing users to the quickstart for hosted options and removes outdated Heroku-specific instructions from the quickstart.

This commit removes the development build tag from the project configuration. It ensures the package is no longer identified as a development version in its metadata. The change affects the setup.cfg file.

This commit updates the pinned versions of several development, documentation, and testing dependencies in the requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest compatible releases of libraries such as attrs, babel, and requests.

This commit updates the Sentry error handling documentation to reflect the transition from the legacy raven client to the modern sentry-sdk. It replaces outdated links and removes the app factory pattern example, while adding a new example for custom exception handling.

This commit updates HTML templates in various Flask examples to use double quotes for attribute values. It standardizes the syntax for class and link attributes across files like layout.html and login.html. This change ensures consistent formatting in the example applications.

This commit updates development resources by fixing the tox configuration to test examples and adding a new environment for faster testing. It also cleans up the Makefile, expands the issue template, and adds a pull request template to improve the contribution workflow.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the templating documentation by adding a missing closing quote to a string example. The correction ensures the code snippet in the docs/templating.rst file is valid and no longer causes a parsing error.
This commit updates the changelog to document the addition of the `safe_join` function. It informs users that this new utility is now available in the upcoming release.
This commit corrects minor typos in the documentation and removes an unused import from the Flask module. It improves the clarity of the API and pattern guides without altering application behavior.

This commit updates the SLSA GitHub generator dependency in the publish workflow from version 1.4.0 to 1.5.0. It ensures the build process uses the latest minor release of the supply chain security tool.

This commit updates the project's external links in the README, documentation configuration, and setup files. It redirects the donation link to the Pallets Projects site and adds new references for WSGI, Werkzeug, Jinja, and pip.

This commit introduces a new automated release script to handle versioning and packaging tasks. It replaces the previous manual release process in the Makefile with a call to the new script, which manages git tags and version updates.

The `create_app` function in the Flaskr tutorial now aborts if the instance folder cannot be created, rather than silently ignoring permission errors. This change ensures the directory exists as expected and updates the documentation to reflect the removal of unnecessary exception handling.
