This commit adds documentation to the installation guide explaining how to run the latest development version of Flask. It instructs users to clone the repository and use a virtual environment to install the package in development mode.

This commit rewrites the deployment documentation to clarify that Flask's built-in server is unsuitable for production environments. It updates the main deployment guide and quickstart to provide clearer guidance on selecting appropriate WSGI servers for running applications.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.4.7 to v0.5.0. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the tool for code quality checks.

This commit fixes a test isolation issue in Flask's test suite where a detected request context leak would leave the stack dirty, affecting subsequent test cases. The `ensure_clean_request_context` method in `FlaskTestCase` now properly cleans up leaked contexts before asserting that no leaks exist.

This commit adds documentation assets and templates to the project. It also fixes bugs in the Flask class, specifically within the route and add_url_rule methods, that were introduced in the previous update.

This commit updates the documentation for the Blueprint class in the Flask blueprints module. It replaces outdated references to "module" with "blueprint" in the docstrings for methods like route and add_url_rule. This clarifies the terminology for users reading the API documentation.

This documentation update clarifies how to start a Celery worker when the application instance is named `celery` rather than the default `app`. It corrects the command in the Celery pattern guide to explicitly reference the instance, preventing startup errors for users following the example.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the extension development documentation. It fixes the typo "scrip" to "script" within the guidelines for the `zip_safe` flag.

This commit updates the Flask application's exception handling to prioritize error handlers registered for specific exception classes over generic HTTP status code handlers. This allows developers to create custom exceptions that subclass standard HTTP errors, enabling extensions to provide default error pages while still permitting users to define specific handlers for those subclasses.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to clarify the difference between client-side and server-side sessions. It adds a note mentioning that several Flask extensions are available for handling sessions on the server side, improving the overall reading flow.

This commit adds a new configuration option, `JSONIFY_PRETTYPRINT_REGULAR`, to the Flask application. When enabled, the `jsonify` function will format JSON responses with indentation for standard browser requests, while keeping them compact for AJAX calls.
This commit updates the copyright year in the project's license file from 2013 to 2014. It ensures the legal documentation reflects the current year of contribution.

This commit ensures the Flask documentation builds reproducibly by preventing the inclusion of absolute build paths in the output. It modifies the API documentation configuration to exclude the `json_module` attribute, which previously caused non-deterministic build results.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for package patterns to clarify how to avoid circular imports. It specifies that view modules should be imported after the application object is created, rather than at the bottom of the file.

This commit modifies the Blueprint class in Flask to ensure that blueprint extensions are only applied during the initial registration. This prevents duplicate or conflicting configurations when a blueprint is registered multiple times.
This commit updates the documentation to correct the capitalization of the book title "Dive Into HTML5" in the HTML FAQ. It ensures the reference link and text match the proper title casing.

This commit updates the installation instructions in the project's setup file to recommend using pip instead of the deprecated easy_install tool. Users will now see the modern pip command when reading the setup documentation.

This commit approves the Flask-Themes and Flask-Uploads extensions for the Flask ecosystem. It moves these packages from the pending review list to the approved list, resolving previous issues regarding missing test suites in their distribution packages.

This commit adds a new TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD configuration option to the Flask application. It allows developers to disable automatic template reloading for improved performance, ensuring templates are only reloaded when the application is running in debug mode. The change modifies the Flask class and its create_jinja_environment method.

This commit fixes a test failure in the Flask test suite that occurred on Python 3.x. It updates the `test_session_cookie_setting` method in `BasicFunctionalityTestCase` to correctly compare response data as bytes instead of strings.

This commit fixes a documentation build error where the system could not find a theme named 'flask'. It resolves the issue by adding the 'pallets_sphinx_themes' extension to the configuration in docs/conf.py.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the documentation file `becomingbig.rst`. It corrects the phrasing to clarify that the documentation is published, improving the readability of the text for users.

This commit updates the pyupgrade pre-commit hook from version 3.2.2 to 3.3.0. It modifies the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to ensure the project uses the latest version of this code modernization tool.

This commit updates the python-dotenv dependency from version 0.18.0 to 0.19.0 in the development and test requirements files. It is a minor version bump that does not change application behavior but ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the library.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `get_json` method in the `Request` class. It clarifies that setting the `silent` parameter to `True` causes the method to return `None` instead of `False` when parsing fails.

This commit updates the error handling documentation to recommend Sentry as a tool for managing application errors. It explains how Sentry aggregates duplicates and captures stack traces to prevent overwhelming users with error emails. The changes are located in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file.

This commit clarifies misleading comments in the `RequestContext` class within `flask/ctx.py`. It updates the documentation for the `push` method to accurately describe how database information is accessed via the `g` object rather than the app context.

This commit changes the internal storage of flash messages from a list to a tuple within the `flask` module. It simplifies the `Request` class by defining `endpoint` and `view_args` as class attributes instead of initializing them in the constructor.
Adds a test for the `from_mapping` method in the Flask configuration module. It verifies that keys not in uppercase are ignored during the configuration update process.

This commit updates the changelog to document a fix in the OPTIONS method handling. It clarifies that the automatically provided OPTIONS method is now correctly disabled when a user registers an overriding rule using the lowercase options name.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the quickstart documentation. It changes the phrase "want to one of the" to "want to use one of the" in the WSGI middleware section.

This commit adds a new example project demonstrating how to integrate Celery with Flask for handling background tasks. It includes a Flask application with views for submitting tasks and polling results, along with documentation updates linking to this new example.

This commit adds two unit tests to the test suite for the Flask application's run method. It verifies that the default execution path and the custom server port configuration correctly invoke the underlying Werkzeug serving function.

This commit updates the Flask JSON module to import the standard `json` library from `itsdangerous` instead of the deprecated `simplejson` alias. This change ensures compatibility with newer versions of the dependency that have removed the legacy import path.

This commit refactors the Flask application class to use a consistent pattern for applying callback functions, removing unnecessary nested iterables and avoiding unnecessary defaultdict lookups. It streamlines methods like preprocess_request and process_response to apply functions immediately upon lookup.

This commit allows template context processors in Flask to be asynchronous, enabling them to perform IO operations like database queries. The `Flask.update_template_context` method now handles both sync and async functions, and the `TemplateContextProcessorCallable` type is updated to reflect this support.

This commit fixes the documentation sidebar by adding the carbon ads template to the list of displayed sidebar components. The change is made in the `docs/conf.py` configuration file, ensuring the ad widget appears correctly in the generated documentation.

This commit prepares the Flask 0.6 release by updating the version number in the setup configuration and adding a placeholder entry to the changelog. It does not alter application behavior but establishes the version metadata for the upcoming release.

This commit updates the test suite to handle differences in how Python 3 formats import error messages. It modifies the `ExtImportHookTestCase` to expect the module name to be quoted in the error string on Python 3, ensuring the test passes across versions.

This commit replaces the previous secure cookie implementation with the itsdangerous library to handle session signing and serialization. It updates the SecureCookieSession and related classes in flask/sessions.py to use URLSafeTimedSerializer, removing dependencies on cPickle and older Werkzeug utilities.

This commit updates the pip-tools dependency from version 5.2.1 to 5.3.0 in the development requirements. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the package management tool for generating lock files.

This commit documents the new `config_class` attribute on the `Flask` class in the version 1.0 changelog. It also adds a version-added note to the attribute's docstring in `flask/app.py` to indicate its introduction.

This commit adds test coverage for the Blueprint class, specifically verifying the behavior of app-wide URL processing methods. It ensures that URL defaults and preprocessors registered on a blueprint correctly apply to routes defined at the application level.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the WSGI standalone deployment guide. It fixes a copy-paste mistake that incorrectly identified uWSGI as the server for running Flask applications, where Gunicorn was intended.

The `get_version` function in `flask/cli.py` now includes the Werkzeug version in the output of the `flask --version` command. This change ensures users can see the specific Werkzeug version installed alongside Flask and Python versions.

This commit standardizes the documentation for HTTP method names like GET and POST by using double backticks for consistent formatting. It updates the Flask class documentation and various guide files to ensure these terms are displayed correctly in the rendered output.

This commit updates the FlaskClient class in the testing module to maintain compatibility with Werkzeug 2.3.3. It adjusts the session_transaction method to handle a new path argument required for cookie updates, ensuring the test client works correctly across different Werkzeug versions.

This commit fixes a bug in the `get_debug_flag` function within `flask/helpers.py` where the debug flag was not disabled if the `FLASK_DEBUG` environment variable was set to uppercase values like "FALSE". It now correctly converts the value to lowercase before checking against the list of falsy strings.

This commit corrects the project URLs in the setup.py file, which previously incorrectly pointed to the Pallets Sphinx themes repository. It updates the code and issue tracker links to reference the correct Flask repository.

This commit adds a test to verify that the `routes` command in the Flask CLI correctly handles applications with no registered routes. It ensures the command exits successfully and displays a specific message indicating that no routes were found.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the linters. It bumps the revision for the main linter from v2.9.0 to v2.10.0 and another tool from v2.3.6 to v2.4.0.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now decodes byte-string attachment filenames to text using UTF-8. This prevents a `UnicodeDecodeError` when processing non-ASCII filenames, ensuring the file is sent correctly.

This commit fixes a bug where blueprint URL prefixes with multiple trailing slashes were incorrectly collapsed. It modifies the BlueprintSetupState class to strip only a single trailing slash during registration, ensuring consistent URL routing behavior.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the quickstart documentation by correcting the plural form of "revision control system." The change ensures the text accurately reflects that multiple systems use HTTP, improving the clarity of the user guide.

This commit updates the deprecation warnings for the Flask class methods open_session, save_session, and make_null_session, as well as the make_test_environ_builder function. It changes the scheduled removal version from 1.1 to 2.0, giving users more time to migrate to the recommended session interface methods.

This commit removes outdated documentation regarding Python 2.4 support for CGI deployment, as the version is no longer supported. It also updates the Werkzeug documentation link in the Sphinx configuration to point to the current stable URL.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to include a link to the Werkzeug debugger guide. It helps users find more detailed information on using the debugger by referencing the external Werkzeug documentation.

This commit ensures that the `get_flashed_messages` function in `flask/helpers.py` always returns a list, even when a category filter is applied. Previously, filtering could result in a filter object being returned instead of a list, which might cause unexpected behavior for users expecting a standard list type.
This commit corrects minor wording and grammar errors in the design documentation. It clarifies the description of how the Werkzeug routing system handles unique URLs and canonical redirects.

This commit fixes broken cross-references in the file upload documentation by correcting the module paths for the FileStorage class and secure_filename function. Users viewing the fileuploads page will now see working links to the correct API documentation.

This commit updates the changelog to document the refactoring of URL adapter creation, which is now customizable via the Flask.create_url_adapter method. It also corrects a documentation reference in the Flask class, changing the mention of create_jinja_loader to select_jinja_autoescape.

This commit updates the `Config.from_pyfile` method in `flask/config.py` to use the `imp` module for creating dynamic modules instead of the `type` function. This change ensures that the temporary module object is properly recognized by Python's import machinery during configuration loading.

This commit restores the ability to run Flask directly from the shell by adding a helper function to resolve package paths. It also updates the quickstart documentation to include a screenshot of the debugger in action.

This commit updates the project's pinned dependencies to support Python 3.8, the minimum version required for the build process. It adjusts the requirements files and configuration to ensure compatibility with older Python environments.

This commit updates the SLSA GitHub generator dependency in the publish workflow from version 1.5.0 to 1.6.0. It ensures the build process uses the latest minor release of the supply chain security tool.

The installation documentation now clarifies that the virtualenv workaround applies specifically to Python 2 users. It updates the command to explicitly invoke the Python 2 module, ensuring the correct interpreter is used for environment creation.

This commit removes the "Becoming Big" documentation page from the Flask project. It updates the documentation index and related pages to reflect the removal of this specific guide on scaling applications.

This commit updates the Flask documentation and configuration to reflect a new minimum requirement of Python 2.6, removing all references to Python 2.5. It adjusts the installation guide, extension development guidelines, and the Travis CI build matrix to align with this change.

This commit corrects the type hint for the `path_or_file` argument in the `send_file` function within `flask.helpers`. It ensures the type annotation accurately reflects that the path can be any string or bytes-like object, improving static type checking accuracy for users.

This commit updates the Flask typing module to accept AsyncIterable types for response values. This change improves type compatibility for Quart, allowing it to handle views that return asynchronous iterables without requiring generic application classes.

This commit updates the project's metadata in setup.py to declare support for Python 3.3. It adds the appropriate classifier so that the package is correctly identified as compatible with this version on package indexes.

This commit introduces a new "future" test environment in the tox configuration to run tests against the tutorial and JavaScript examples. It updates the Azure Pipelines workflow to use this specific environment and expands the list of environment variables passed to the test runner.
Adds a "Donate to Pallets" link to the documentation navigation. This change modifies the `html_context` configuration in `docs/conf.py` to include the new external link for users.

This commit removes the test_click_7_deprecated function from the Flask CLI test suite. It eliminates a check that verified a deprecation warning was raised when using older versions of the Click library.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to explicitly introduce the `escape` function from `markupsafe` and explain why it is omitted in examples. It also cleans up imports and adjusts the installation reference in the `docs/quickstart.rst` file.

This commit updates the AppVeyor CI configuration to support both Python 3.5 and 3.6 environments. It adds an initialization step to set the correct Python path and prints the version, while simplifying command execution by using the `python` command directly instead of full paths.

This commit adds a git submodule for the Flask Sphinx themes to the documentation directory. It configures the repository to pull in the external theme package, enabling custom styling for the project's documentation.

This commit fixes broken cross-reference links in the API documentation by updating class references to their correct module paths. It ensures that links to Werkzeug request and data structure classes resolve properly for users viewing the docs.
This commit updates the deployment documentation to include a link to an article about deploying on Azure using IIS. The change adds a new hosted option to the list of available deployment guides.

This commit fixes broken cross-reference links in the documentation by correcting the base URL for the WTForms intersphinx mapping. The change ensures that references to WTForms documentation resolve correctly instead of pointing to a non-existent stable version path.

This documentation update removes the obsolete `-R` flag from the `egg_info` command example in the distribute patterns guide. It corrects the build instructions to reflect the current command syntax for creating release builds.
Removes the unused `_json_loads` helper function from the `flask.config` module. This cleanup eliminates dead code left over from a previous feature, with no impact on user-facing behavior.
This commit corrects a broken hyperlink in the project's changelog. It updates the documentation to ensure the link to the Python version support notice functions correctly for users.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.2.3 by updating the version string in the `flask` module. It also clarifies the changelog to state that autoescaping is enabled by default for SVG template files.

This commit updates the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to respect the charset specified in the request's mimetype parameters. It ensures that the `json` property correctly decodes the request body using the provided encoding, preventing potential parsing errors for non-UTF-8 data.

This commit updates the changelog to document a new feature in Flask version 0.12. It notes that the command-line interface now correctly responds to the version flag, allowing users to check the installed version.

This commit removes test fixtures and cases that relied on the deprecated pkgutil.get_loader function. It cleans up the test suite by eliminating the limit_loader fixture and associated path tests in test_instance_config.py.

This commit adds two new static image assets, "no.png" and "yes.png," to the documentation directory. These files are likely intended for use in the project's documentation to visually represent boolean states or choices.

This commit removes an unused reference label from the favicon documentation page. It cleans up the docs/patterns/favicon.rst file by deleting the label definition, which does not affect user-facing behavior.

This commit fixes a logic error in the `prepare_exec_for_file` function within `flask/cli.py` where an `__init__.py` file was incorrectly stripped of its extension. The change ensures the filename is only modified if it is not an `__init__.py` file, and adds a test to verify this behavior.

This commit updates the test suite to suppress specific Werkzeug warnings using the standard warnings module instead of the deprecated pytest.warns(None) syntax. It resolves compatibility issues with pytest 7 in the test_basic and test_reqctx modules.

This commit deprecates the `locked_cached_property` helper in Flask, replacing it with Werkzeug's standard `cached_property` for attributes like `Flask.jinja_env` and `Flask.logger`. This change removes internal locking mechanisms that could briefly block concurrent requests, improving application concurrency.

The development environment configuration in the tox.ini file was updated to target Python 3.8 instead of Python 3.7. This change ensures that the development test suite runs against the newer Python version.

This commit fixes broken navigation links on the project's homepage. It updates the URLs in the index.html file to correctly point to the documentation pages, ensuring users can access the quickstart, testing, and session guides.

This commit corrects the formatting of a command-line example in the package patterns documentation. It adds a text code block directive to the `docs/patterns/packages.rst` file to ensure the terminal output renders correctly.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Flask package's initialization file that prevented the module from loading correctly. The change corrects the indentation of the imported helper functions in `flask/__init__.py`.

This commit updates the error handling documentation to incorporate suggested wording changes. It corrects minor grammatical and spelling errors in the description of Sentry, a tool recommended for managing application errors.

This commit ensures that Flask's error handler omits detailed key error descriptions when trapping bad request errors, not just in debug mode. The change modifies the `Flask.handle_user_exception` method to check the `TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS` configuration. A new test verifies that sensitive key names are not exposed in the response body when this setting is active.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies to newer versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions for black and isort to ensure consistent code formatting and import sorting.

This commit removes the unused `g` object from the Flaskr example application. It updates the import statement in `flaskr.py` to exclude `g`, cleaning up the code without changing any user-facing behavior.

This commit corrects a documentation example in the templates tutorial to use the proper "or" operator for conditional logic. It clarifies how to display either a log out link or registration links, fixing a misleading syntax in the Jinja2 template description.

This commit updates the title of the 404 error page in the website module. It replaces the generic "Awwww" message with the specific text "Chapter 404: The Lost Page" to improve the user experience when a page is not found.

This commit adds tests and a changelog entry for the feature where `app.run` uses the `SERVER_NAME` configuration as the default host and port. It verifies that the application correctly falls back to these config values when explicit arguments are not provided to the run method.

This commit adds a pre-commit hook to automatically reorder Python imports across the codebase, excluding the examples directory. It updates the import order in the main Flask source files and test suites to comply with the new style.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for view decorators to clarify how to handle the `next` parameter during login. It explains that developers must manually pass this value from the GET request to the POST request using a hidden input field.

This commit documents the new `message_flashed` signal in the Flask API and signals reference. It explains that the signal is emitted when a message is flashed, providing the message and category as keyword arguments to simplify testing.

This commit fixes a crash in Flask's JSON serialization helpers when no request context is active. It ensures the app's JSON coder is used as a fallback if a blueprint's coder is not set, preventing errors in `_dump_arg_defaults` and `_load_arg_defaults`.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the reorder_python_imports and black tools. It ensures the project's automated code formatting and import sorting checks run with the latest stable releases.

This commit corrects minor grammatical and typographical errors in the Flask quickstart documentation. It fixes phrasing in the introduction and clarifies the explanation of the Flask class and run method.

Adds tests to the TemplatingTestCase in tests/flask_tests.py to verify that the template_filter decorator works correctly with actual HTML templates. These tests ensure that custom filters, such as reversing a string, are properly applied when rendering templates via Flask.
This commit refines the documentation for the application dispatch pattern. It clarifies the explanation of how this approach differs from the module approach in the appdispatch.rst file.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `url_for` function where passing a value named `self` caused an error. By making the `self` parameter positional-only, users can now use `self` as a regular argument name in URL generation.

This commit corrects a documentation comment in the `RequestContext` class within `flask/ctx.py`. It clarifies that specific teardown functions are executed before the standard "after_request" handlers, rather than implying they run even during errors.

This commit fixes a resource leak in the Config class where the configuration file was not explicitly closed after being read. By using a context manager in the from_pyfile method, the file is now closed immediately, preventing potential file descriptor exhaustion.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions for flake8 and black to ensure consistent code formatting and linting standards.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.2.2 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the release date in the changelog. It transitions the package from a development state to a stable release.

This commit updates the testing documentation to correct an inconsistency in the example login credentials. It replaces a generic username with an email field in the `docs/testing.rst` file to better reflect standard authentication practices.
This commit corrects a variable name in the documentation for the views module. It updates the example code to use a consistent variable name, improving clarity for users reading the guide.

This commit updates the Flask extension development documentation to remove the requirement for using the `==dev` version specifier. It clarifies that this installation method no longer works because pip no longer processes links found in project descriptions. The change affects the `docs/extensiondev.rst` file.
Corrects a spelling error in the URL processors documentation. The word "reptition" is changed to "repetition" in the explanatory text. This improves the readability of the guide for developers.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflows for publishing and testing to use newer versions of the checkout, setup-python, upload-artifact, and cache actions. This ensures the CI/CD pipeline runs with the latest stable releases of these dependencies.
Updated the docstring in the `flaskext_compat` module to include an example of activating the compatibility layer. This clarifies how users should enable the feature.

This commit streamlines the introductory text in the error handling documentation, removing verbose examples to focus on the core concept of displaying error pages. It also corrects a minor punctuation error in the upgrading guide regarding the ValueError exception.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to remove references to the deprecated `flask.ext` import pattern. It clarifies how to import extensions in the API and extension development guides, ensuring users follow current best practices.

This commit updates the Flask subclassing documentation to replace a Jinja2 example with a more practical use case. It now demonstrates how to override request parameter handling to preserve order by subclassing the Request class.

This commit extends URL generation in the Flask module by automatically prefixing endpoint names with the current blueprint when a dot is not present. It also updates the request context to capture routing exceptions during URL matching, allowing for more robust error handling.
This commit adds a README file to the MiniTwit example directory. It provides a brief description of the application and instructions for initializing the database and running the Flask server.

This commit cleans up the documentation for the Flask CLI, fixing minor formatting and spacing issues in the user guide. It also refines the `ScriptInfo` class and related helper functions in the `flask.cli` module to improve code consistency.

The `jsonify` function in `flask/helpers.py` now correctly handles the `padded` keyword argument by extracting it before processing other parameters. This prevents the argument from being passed to the JSON serializer, which previously caused a content-type assertion error in tests.

This commit corrects a typo in the help text for the `run_command` function in `flask/cli.py`. It changes the phrase "is active is debug is enabled" to "is active if debug is enabled," ensuring the documentation is grammatically correct.

This commit adds documentation to the `Flask.test_client` method in `flask/app.py`. It explains how to pass optional keyword arguments to a custom test client class constructor, allowing users to configure specific client behaviors.
Adds a "Donate to Pallets" link to the documentation navigation. This change modifies the `html_context` configuration in `docs/conf.py` to include the new external link for users.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask class where class-based views failed to register correctly due to an incorrect identity check. The change modifies the `add_url_rule` method to use value comparison instead of identity comparison when checking for existing view functions.

This commit updates the Request class in flask/wrappers.py to ensure JSON error messages are compatible with Python 2.6. It changes the string formatting syntax in the on_json_loading_failed method to use positional arguments instead of keyword arguments.

This commit replaces the custom metaclass for Flask's MethodView with the standard __init_subclass__ hook. This simplifies the class creation process and updates the type hint for the methods attribute to accept any collection of strings.

This commit adds future annotations imports across the Flask codebase to enable modern type hinting syntax. It updates core modules like the Flask app, blueprints, and context managers to support deferred evaluation of type hints.

This commit clarifies the documentation for Flask's `got_request_exception` signal. It specifies that the signal is only triggered by unhandled exceptions, excluding those with registered error handlers like HTTP exceptions.
This commit updates the Ruff pre-commit hook from version 0.1.5 to 0.1.6. It modifies the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to ensure the project uses the latest stable release of the linter.

This commit refactors the `DispatchingApp` class in `flask/cli.py` to accept a loader function instead of a static app ID. This change enables more advanced application loading patterns by delegating the app resolution process to the provided loader.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `static_folder` parameter in the `Flask` class. It explicitly states that the path is relative to the application's `root_path` or can be an absolute path, improving clarity for users configuring static file serving.

This commit removes a reference cycle in the TaggedJSONSerializer class within flask/sessions.py. The change prevents memory leaks by ensuring the internal _tag function does not retain a reference to the serializer instance during the dumps process.

This commit updates the Travis-CI configuration to use the new container-based infrastructure. It adds the `sudo: false` directive to the `.travis.yml` file, which enables faster build times by running tests in a lightweight container environment.

This commit adds documentation for caching strategies and view decorators in the Flask patterns guide. It explains how to use Werkzeug's cache support to speed up applications by storing function results. The changes update the caching and view decorator documentation files.

This commit updates the logging documentation to prevent errors when accessing request data outside of an active request context. It demonstrates using the `has_request_context` function to safely check for a request before setting URL and remote address attributes on log records.

This commit moves the JUnit XML report generation from the Azure Pipelines configuration into the tox test runner. It updates the test command to output a fixed filename, ensuring the CI pipeline correctly locates the results file.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask extensions to clarify import methods for versions prior to 0.8. It modifies the `docs/extensions.rst` file to reword the section title and simplify the guidance on using the `flaskext` namespace for older applications.

This commit corrects the version history documentation for the session interface in the Flask class. It updates the versionadded directive from 0.7 to 0.8 to accurately reflect when the feature was introduced.
This commit updates the CHANGES file to record the release of version 0.12. It specifies the release date as December 21st, 2016, and assigns the codename Punsch to this version.

This commit adds initial documentation for the application dispatching pattern. It explains how to manage multiple application instances with different configurations, specifically focusing on dispatching requests by subdomain. The changes are located in the `docs/patterns` module.

This commit adds a security warning section to the documentation foreword and includes a footnote regarding the `g` variable. It also updates the Flasky theme CSS to style footnote tables with borders and padding.

This commit corrects a typo and clarifies the documentation for the `has_request_context` function in `flask/ctx.py`. It improves the readability of the docstring by fixing grammatical errors and restructuring the example sentence.

This commit adds `stream_template` and `stream_template_string` functions to the Flask templating module, allowing templates to be rendered as a stream of pieces. It updates the documentation and changelog to reflect these new capabilities for efficient data streaming.

This commit updates the python-dotenv dependency from version 0.17.0 to 0.17.1 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the library for environment variable management.

This commit standardizes the secret key used in documentation, examples, and tests to ensure consistency across the project. It updates the Flask application factory and test configuration to use a unified key, preventing discrepancies between documented examples and actual test behavior.
This commit fixes a typo in the Flask documentation for the request context. It removes a duplicated word in the description of the teardown functions executed before the context is popped.

This commit updates the Flask package version from a development build to the stable 1.0 release. It modifies the `__version__` variable in the `flask/__init__.py` module to reflect the final release status.

This commit updates the build configuration for the Celery, JavaScript, and Tutorial examples to use flit instead of setuptools. It removes the now-unnecessary MANIFEST.in files and adjusts license definitions to point directly to the license file.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use version 3.9.0 of the tool. It ensures the project uses the latest available release for its automated code checks.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `errorhandler` decorator in Flask. It replaces a complex protocol definition with a simpler callable type in the `typing` module, ensuring static type checkers accurately recognize the expected function signature.

This commit updates the documentation for the Flask class to remove references to the deprecated flaskext namespace. It clarifies that extension module keys should now match the new naming convention, such as flask_foo instead of flaskext.foo.

This commit removes an unused request parameter from the client fixture in the largerapp test module. It simplifies the test setup without changing any application behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.

This commit fixes the `before_first_request` method in the `Flask` class so it functions as a proper decorator. Previously, the method did not return the wrapped function, preventing it from working as intended for registering handlers.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for blueprints to clarify that the static folder path is exposed without a prefix. It corrects the description of how the `static_folder` argument works, specifying that the path is relative to the blueprint's location.

This commit updates the documentation for the Flask.run method to clarify that the host defaults to the SERVER_NAME configuration variable if it is set. This change ensures users are aware of the fallback behavior when starting the development server.

This commit updates the Flask.run method to explicitly set the host to 127.0.0.1 and the port to 5000 when these arguments are not provided. This ensures the development server uses consistent default values instead of relying on implicit behavior.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now automatically sets the `Content-Length` header for file responses. This ensures clients receive accurate file size information when downloading static files.
This commit corrects a typo in the Flask configuration documentation. It fixes the misspelled function name "jsonfiy" to "jsonify" in the description of internal configuration values.
This commit raises the minimum required version of the Blinker dependency from 1.8 to 1.9. It updates the project configuration and test requirements to ensure compatibility with the newer version.

This commit adds `json_encoder` and `json_decoder` attributes to the `Blueprint` class, allowing developers to override the application's default JSON serialization settings. It also cleans up related helper functions in `flask/json.py` and updates the changelog to document this new feature.

This commit introduces a distinct application context to Flask, allowing the application to be bound to the current context independently of a request. It adds the AppContext class and a new app_context method to the Flask class, enabling developers to manage application state outside of request handling.
This commit standardizes the capitalization of "GitHub" in the documentation. It updates the sidebar introduction, extensions guide, and jQuery patterns page to ensure consistent branding.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the installation documentation. It fixes the word "familar" to "familiar" in the shell prompt description within the docs/installation.rst file.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.8.6 to 1.8.7. This patch-level dependency update ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for publishing packages.

The `rewrite_blueprint_imports` function in the Flask upgrade script no longer performs direct rewrites of `flask.Module` references. Instead, it relies on constructor calls to handle the transition to `flask.Blueprint`, simplifying the migration logic.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.2.5 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the release date in the changelog. It transitions the package from a development state to a stable release.

This commit corrects two typos in the docstring for the FlaskGroup class in flask/cli.py. It removes a duplicated word and fixes the spacing in "use cases," improving the clarity of the documentation without changing any functional behavior.

This commit updates the `flask/_compat.py` module to use feature detection instead of version checks for Python 2 and 3 compatibility. It resolves linter errors for undefined names like `unicode` and `long` by wrapping these definitions in a try-except block, allowing the code to pass static analysis without special directives.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the CLI guide where the `@click.command` decorator was missing parentheses. Without them, the example code fails with an AttributeError because the function object lacks the required name attribute. This commit updates six Python dependencies in the requirements files, including major version bumps for sphinx-issues, cryptography, and pytest. These changes ensure the project uses the latest stable releases of these libraries for development, documentation, and testing.

This commit relocates the test for test client context binding from the ContextTestCase to the TestToolsTestCase in the Flask test suite. It ensures the test is grouped with other test tooling checks, improving code organization without altering the tested behavior.

This commit refactors the `Config.from_json` method in `flask/config.py` to delegate its logic to the `from_mapping` method. This change simplifies the code by removing redundant key iteration and ensures consistent behavior when loading configuration from JSON data.

This commit updates the mypy configuration in setup.cfg to include the tests/typing directory in the type-checking scope. This ensures that type annotations within the typing tests are validated alongside the main Flask source code.

This commit updates the test suite for the application context module to use the identity operator instead of equality when checking for None. It aligns the code with PEP8 style guidelines, ensuring that assertions in the test functions correctly verify the absence of an application context.

This commit refactors the Flask CLI's app factory invocation logic to better handle function arguments. It updates the `call_factory` function in `flask/cli.py` to accept an optional tuple of arguments, allowing for more flexible and natural splitting of the code.

This commit optimizes the error handler lookup in the Flask application class. It prevents unnecessary iteration when no specific error code is provided, improving the efficiency of the `_find_error_handler` method.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to clarify how signals interact with the request context. It explains that context-local variables, such as those in `flask.g`, remain accessible between the `request_started` and `request_finished` signals.

This commit updates the API documentation to inherit descriptions for request data attributes from the Werkzeug library instead of duplicating them. It removes redundant manual definitions for form, args, values, and cookies attributes in the docs/api.rst file.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the Flask documentation and source code, such as changing "existance" to "existence" and "generaly" to "generally." It updates the Flask class, ExtensionImporter, and Request wrapper to ensure accurate terminology in docstrings and comments.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions workflows to use the correct hyphenated parameter names for the PyPI publishing step, ensuring the build process runs without configuration errors. It also removes the redundant step that manually updates pip, wheel, and setuptools in the test workflow.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.2.2. It updates the version string in the `flask` module to a development release and adds a new entry to the changelog.

This commit fixes an issue in the Flask application where setting `SERVER_NAME` incorrectly restricted requests to that specific domain when `subdomain_matching` was disabled. The change ensures that `SERVER_NAME` no longer limits request handling in these configurations.
This commit updates the project's author list to include Matt Campell. It acknowledges his contributions to patches and suggestions within the AUTHORS file.

This commit updates the documentation build to use the theme provided by pallets-sphinx-themes. It modifies the Sphinx configuration and related files to integrate the new theme, replacing previous custom styling.

This commit fixes malformed Sphinx documentation directives in the Flask class. It corrects the versionadded syntax for the handle_exception and handle_http_exception methods, ensuring the documentation builds correctly.

This commit adds a warning to the Flask configuration documentation regarding the SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN setting. It explains that changing this value can cause browsers to send multiple competing session cookies in an undefined order, potentially leading to unpredictable session behavior.

This commit corrects documentation for the file upload pattern and the `get_flashed_messages` helper. It clarifies how file extensions are controlled in uploads and explains that the category filter restricts returned messages to specific categories.
This commit adds a new templating section to the Flask documentation. It updates the quickstart guide to reference this new section and begins documenting cross-site scripting security measures.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the pyupgrade and black tools. It ensures the project's automated code checks run with the latest available releases of these linters.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It changes the phrase "to sent" to "to send," improving the clarity of the docstring for users reading the API reference.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the .cache directory from version control. This prevents developers from accidentally committing local cache data, such as test failure records, to the project repository.

This commit updates the Flask installation documentation to replace references to the deprecated `easy_install` command with `pip`. It clarifies the recommended methods for installing the standard and development versions of the package.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flask documentation tutorial. It fixes a missing word in the setup guide to ensure the text accurately describes how the application initializes variables from a module.

This commit updates the deployment documentation to include a link to the AWS Elastic Beanstalk tutorial for Flask applications. It helps users find official guidance for hosting their Flask apps on AWS.

This commit changes the default value of the `APPLICATION_ROOT` configuration to a forward slash instead of `None`. It updates the `Flask` class and `SessionInterface` to use this new default, ensuring consistent URL and cookie path handling without requiring explicit configuration.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the Jinja2 templating documentation. It changes the verb "generate" to "generates" in the `docs/templating.rst` file to improve the accuracy of the text describing secure HTML injection.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the CHANGES file, changing "instane" to "instance." It ensures the release notes accurately describe the designated location for instance paths.

This update makes the endpoint parameter optional for the `flask.Module.add_url_rule` method. This change ensures consistency with the application object's equivalent function, allowing developers to omit the endpoint when defining routes for modules.

This commit adds Flask-Genshi to the list of approved extensions in the extreview documentation. It records the review details for version 0.3.1 and notes that it is the first template engine extension, suggesting a future common interface for similar tools.

The `fix` function in `scripts/flaskext_migrate.py` is now exposed as a callable wrapper instead of running directly on import. This change allows other modules to import and test the import-fixing logic without executing the script's main entry point.

This commit standardizes the spelling of "class-based" by adding a hyphen across the documentation and source code. It improves readability for users referencing the View and MethodView classes in Flask.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to describe the `g` object for sharing request-specific data and adds details about the WSGI environment. It also refines the API reference and quickstart guide to improve clarity for developers using the `Flask` class.

Adds a test to verify that Flask's URL generation correctly encodes spaces in route parameters as percent-encoded characters. This ensures the `url_for` function produces valid URLs for routes with special characters.

This commit fixes a bug in the `send_file` function within `flask/helpers.py` where a cache timeout of zero was incorrectly ignored. It changes the validation to check if the value is not `None`, allowing users to explicitly disable caching by setting the timeout to zero.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for error pages, renaming the section to "Returning API errors as JSON." It clarifies how to use the abort function with a description parameter to generate JSON responses for API errors.

The `flask run` command now accepts a `--debug` flag to explicitly enable or disable debug mode. This change modifies the `run_command` function in `src/flask/cli.py` to prioritize the command-line argument over the default environment-based detection.

This commit allows developers to customize the test client used by the Flask application. It introduces a new `test_client_class` attribute on the `Flask` class and adds a `use_cookies` parameter to the `test_client` method, enabling more flexible testing configurations.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's debug helpers where the DebugFilesKeyError exception returned a byte string instead of a text string on Python 3. It ensures the error message displays correctly by storing the message as a standard string and applying the implements_to_string decorator.

This commit removes the flawed custom JSON HTTP exception subclasses from the Flask exceptions module. Users relying on these specific error types will need to implement their own replacements, as the previous interface was considered broken.

This commit updates the PyCharm integration documentation in the CLI guide. It clarifies that PyCharm Professional offers a dedicated Flask run configuration for the development server, while other editions require manual setup.

This commit updates the `ResponseValue` type in `src/flask/typing.py` to accept `TypedDict` objects as valid return values from view functions. It resolves a type-checking limitation where `TypedDict` was previously rejected, allowing developers to use them for structured JSON responses.
This commit updates the docstring for the `teardown_request` method in the `Flask` class. It breaks a long line into two to improve readability. No functional behavior is changed.
This commit updates the changelog to mark version 0.6.1 as officially released on December 31st, 2010. It clarifies the release status for users checking the project's history.

This commit updates the project changelog to finalize the release details for version 0.5. It replaces the placeholder text with the official release date of July 6th, 2010, and assigns the codename Calvados.

This commit renames the documentation file for the extension review process from "rejected" to "unlisted." It updates the terminology to reflect that extensions are unlisted rather than rejected, improving clarity for users reviewing the process.
Bumps the package version from 0.3 to 0.4 in the setup.py file. This update reflects a new release of the software.

The `flaskext_migrate` script now supports fixing function calls during import migration, not just import statements. This change refactors the `fix` function to modularize the code and adds a new `fix_function_calls` method to handle these updates.

The test suite for the Flask extension now uses a dedicated configuration file instead of overwriting the project's main tox file. This prevents the test from deleting the original configuration, preserving the repository state. The changes affect the create_tox_ini and test_extension functions in tests/flaskext_test.py.

This commit restructures the Flask test suite by moving it from the top-level tests directory into a new flask.testsuite package. It splits the monolithic test file into multiple modules covering specific features like basic functionality, blueprints, and templating. This change organizes the test code for better maintainability and modularity.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's Blueprint module where URL rules could end up with double slashes when combining a prefix and a route. The `BlueprintSetupState` class now normalizes the prefix and rule to ensure a single slash separates them.

This commit introduces a new Config class to Flask, allowing users to load application settings from Python files or modules. It updates the Flask application initialization to support this new configuration mechanism and adds corresponding documentation and tests.

This commit updates the test for template auto-reload behavior when running in debug mode. It modifies the test to use the standard app fixture and verifies the new templates_auto_reload property instead of checking internal configuration values.

This commit fixes a rendering error in the Flask configuration documentation where environment variable references were displayed incorrectly. It corrects the reStructuredText syntax in the `docs/config.rst` file to ensure the `YOURAPPLICATION_SETTINGS` variable displays properly.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to use the `env` command for setting the `FLASK_APP` variable. This change ensures the example command works correctly across different shell environments, including Fish, where the previous syntax failed.
This commit updates the changelog to document a fix for registering partials without a name as view functions. It adds a reference link to the specific issue in the CHANGES.rst file.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the API documentation for the Flask module. It clarifies that simplejson is provided by both the standard library and an extension, improving the readability of the text.

This commit adds documentation for streaming large amounts of data in Flask applications. It introduces a new guide explaining how to use generators to send data directly to clients without storing it in memory. The changes update the patterns index to include this new streaming section.

This commit adds tests to verify that accessing deprecated properties on the Flask request object triggers the expected deprecation warnings. It specifically checks the behavior of the `request.json` property and the `request` module attribute within the `TestRequestDeprecation` class.

This commit reverts documentation changes to correct the placement of the `--debug` flag in Flask CLI examples. It ensures the flag is shown before the `run` command in guides like `cli.rst` and `config.rst`, preventing user confusion about proper syntax.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's testing client where session data was not correctly loaded during transactions. The change modifies the `FlaskClient` class to ensure environment overrides are properly initialized, allowing `session_transaction` to access existing session data.

This commit adds support for injecting default values into URL generation. It introduces the `inject_url_defaults` method to the `Flask` class and calls it within the `url_for` helper. This allows developers to automatically add parameters to URLs based on the endpoint.

This commit fixes the `assert_true` method in the `FlaskTestCase` class to accept an optional message argument. Previously, the method ignored any custom failure messages, but it now correctly passes them to the underlying assertion, allowing for more descriptive test error reports.
This commit updates the quickstart documentation to include an example of setting the application's secret key. It clarifies how to configure this essential security setting for session management.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the testing documentation that would have caused a rendering failure. It corrects the example code in `docs/testing.rst` to use valid dictionary syntax instead of invalid keyword arguments.

This commit corrects a typo in the URL defaults example within the API documentation. It updates the route definition in the `docs/api.rst` file to properly specify the integer type for the `id` parameter, ensuring the example code is accurate.
This commit finalizes the release notes for version 1.0.2, documenting fixes for backward compatibility issues with URL merging and an error in the `flask routes` command when no routes exist.

This commit changes the default session serialization format from pickle to JSON to reduce security risks if the secret key is leaked. It introduces the `TaggedJSONSerializer` and `UpgradeSecureCookieSession` classes in `flask/sessions.py` to handle the new format and automatically upgrade existing pickle-based sessions.

This commit refactors several test cases in the test suite to use pytest's raises context manager instead of manual try/except blocks. This change improves code readability and allows tests to utilize pytest's exception information features, such as checking exception types directly.

The publish workflow now correctly handles build artifacts by capturing the artifact ID from the upload step and using it to download files in subsequent jobs. This ensures the release step accesses the correct distribution files, preventing failures when creating draft releases.

The Flask documentation now guides users to use MongoEngine instead of the unmaintained MongoKit library for MongoDB integration. This change updates the "Patterns for Flask" section to ensure compatibility with recent PyMongo versions.

This commit adds CI jobs to test the project against the minimum and development versions of Pallets dependencies. It introduces new requirement files for these specific versions and updates the GitHub Actions workflow to run the corresponding tests.
This commit corrects the indentation of the `test_login_logout` example in the testing documentation. It ensures the code snippet displays with proper formatting for users reading the guide.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to clarify that HTTP is the protocol used by web applications. It also corrects the description of how the `Flask.route` decorator handles `HEAD` requests, noting that they are processed according to RFC standards.

This commit corrects minor spelling and formatting errors in several Flask documentation files. It updates terms like "mailinglist" to "mailing list" and "life cycle" to "lifecycle" for consistency. The changes improve the readability of the project's documentation without altering any functional code.
This commit updates the Ruff linter version in the pre-commit configuration from v0.3.5 to v0.4.3. It ensures the project uses the latest available version of the tool for code quality checks.
This commit removes the `add_to_path` helper function from the test suite's initialization module. The function was used to manage the Python path for tests but is no longer needed.

The `Config.from_prefixed_env` method in Flask's configuration module now supports nested dictionary access using double underscores as separators. It also removes the requirement to specify a separator in the prefix and improves error handling for JSON parsing.
This commit updates the Flask documentation to adopt a new visual theme. It replaces static image assets and modifies the Sphinx configuration in `docs/conf.py` to support the updated styling.
This commit corrects minor grammatical errors in the SQLite 3 documentation for Flask. It improves the clarity of the text in the `docs/patterns/sqlite3.rst` file by fixing phrasing and punctuation.

This commit introduces the initial Sphinx documentation structure for the Flask project, including configuration files and API references. It also updates the root .gitignore to exclude egg-info directories and adds a .gitignore for the documentation build output.

This commit replaces placeholder text in the installation documentation with detailed instructions for setting up Flask. It explains the framework's dependencies on Werkzeug and Jinja2, as well as the role of WSGI in Python web applications.

This commit corrects a minor typo in the changelog for the 2022-07-13 release. It removes an extra trailing space from the description regarding imported submodules.
This commit initializes the changelog for version 1.0.2 by adding a new section to the CHANGES.rst file. It marks the release as unreleased, preparing the documentation for upcoming changes.

This commit updates CLI messages in Flask to improve clarity and formatting. It changes the `app.run` warning to use `click.secho` and ensures the dev server banner displays all lines in grey. The changes affect the `Flask` class, `DispatchingApp`, and `FlaskGroup` modules.

This commit corrects the indentation of the `permanent` attribute documentation in the Flask API reference. The fix ensures the description renders correctly within the `session` object section, resolving a formatting error in the generated documentation.

The `make_test_environ_builder` function in `flask/testing.py` now correctly handles full URLs by using `urlparse` to extract the host and path. This fixes an issue where subdomain-based requests were not processed properly during testing.

This commit fixes a bug in the `locate_app` function within `flask/cli.py` where the error message for a missing file path failed to substitute the actual module name. Users previously saw the literal text "%s" instead of the specific path they provided, making it difficult to identify the error.
This commit corrects a typo in the deferred callbacks documentation. It removes a redundant word from the explanation of moving logic to the after_request callback in the Flask patterns guide.

This documentation update clarifies that while blueprint endpoint names are automatically prefixed with the blueprint name, the URL path is not. It corrects a minor formatting error in the Flask blueprints guide to prevent user confusion about URL routing behavior.

This commit fixes an issue in the Flask CLI where the `call_factory` function failed to correctly handle app factories with a single argument that has a default value. This commit adds missing documentation comments to several Flask modules and corrects the package setup file. It also resolves import errors by renaming the configuration module, ensuring the test suite passes successfully.

This commit adds support for the `TRUSTED_HOSTS` configuration in the Flask application. It validates the request host during routing to prevent security issues, raising a 400 error if the host is not trusted. The `Flask` class handles this check within its URL adapter creation process.
This commit removes the `run_audit` command from the `setup.py` module. Users can no longer execute the `audit` command to check source code for undefined or redefined names using PyFlakes.

This commit adds support for generic HTTPException handlers in Flask, allowing developers to define catch-all error handlers for both the application and blueprints. The `Flask._find_error_handler` method now resolves handlers in a specific priority order, checking for specific status codes before falling back to generic exception handlers.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflows to use the latest patch versions of the setup-python, upload-artifact, and download-artifact actions. This ensures the CI/CD pipelines run with the most recent stable releases of these tools.

This commit ensures that template auto-reloading respects the debug flag from the run command, even if the Jinja environment was previously accessed. It introduces a property for the Flask class to manage this setting and updates the CLI to reconfigure the app during execution.

This commit updates the sidebar introduction in the documentation to remove a warning that the software is unstable. It also deletes a request for user feedback via email, simplifying the message for readers of the development version.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.2.0. It updates the project version in pyproject.toml to a development release and adds a new entry to the changelog.

This commit fixes a bug where file modification times were incorrectly interpreted as local time instead of UTC. The change updates the `TestSendfile` test to use `utcfromtimestamp` when calculating the last modified date.

This commit updates the documentation for the `before_request` attribute in the `Flask` class. It clarifies that the registered functions are called at the beginning of each request and improves the wording regarding blueprint scope.

This commit updates the HTML form example in the WTForms documentation to use lowercase "post" for the method attribute. It corrects the syntax in the `docs/patterns/wtforms.rst` file to align with standard HTML conventions.

This commit fixes an issue where the `flask run` command failed if the `--key` option was provided before `--cert`. By marking the certificate parameter as eager in the `run_command` function, the CLI now accepts these options in any order.

This commit adds a `set_debug_flag` option to the `ScriptInfo` class in `flask/cli.py`. It prevents the CLI from overwriting the debug setting based on environment variables, allowing custom CLIs to preserve debug flags defined in their own configuration files.

This commit updates the testing documentation to fix a TypeError in Python 3.4.2, where string literals no longer support the buffer API. It changes example assertions in the docs/testing.rst file to use byte strings instead of regular strings.

This commit corrects minor grammatical errors and punctuation in the testing documentation. It improves the clarity of sentences in the docs/testing.rst file without altering any functional code or behavior.

The release script previously failed to correctly parse dates containing ordinal suffixes like "1st" or "2nd". This commit updates the `parse_date` function in `scripts/make-release.py` to use a regular expression for more robust date cleaning.
This commit updates the setup.py script to use Python 3-compatible print statements. It modifies the run_audit function to ensure the audit tool runs correctly in modern Python environments.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Flaskr example README where the FLASK_APP environment variable was missing quotes. It ensures the application factory path is correctly parsed by the Flask CLI.

This commit corrects a typo in the WTForms documentation example. It fixes a misspelled keyword argument in the password validation code snippet, ensuring the example is syntactically correct for users.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of several code quality tools, including pyupgrade, reorder_python_imports, black, and pip-compile-multi. It ensures the project's automated checks run with the latest available releases.

This commit improves the clarity of the Flaskr tutorial documentation. It updates several pages, including database connection and initialization guides, to use more precise language and add helpful navigation notes.

This commit adds a comment to the lock workflow configuration to clarify its behavior. It explains that the system locks closed issues after two weeks of inactivity rather than automatically closing stale ones, encouraging users to open new issues for related problems.

This commit updates the Flask package version from 0.8-dev to 0.7.1-dev in the `flask/__init__.py` and `setup.py` files. It ensures the software reports the correct version number for this specific branch.

This commit updates the pytest dependency from version 6.2.1 to 6.2.2 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the testing framework, incorporating recent bug fixes and improvements.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to prevent a TypeError when registering views that handle multiple HTTP methods. It instructs users to split GET and POST requests into separate `add_url_rule` calls instead of combining them in a single method list.

This commit removes the Flask-Creole entry from the extreview/listed.rst file. The package was previously listed as pending review due to test suite issues, but it has since been approved. This change cleans up the list by removing the redundant entry.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now URL-quotes colons and slashes in UTF-8 filenames. This change improves compatibility with certain browsers that previously failed to handle these characters correctly in attachment filenames.

This commit updates the file upload documentation to recommend using the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH configuration key instead of subclassing the request object. It clarifies how to limit upload sizes in Flask and adds a link to the Flask-Uploads extension.

This commit corrects a typo in the HTML FAQ documentation, changing "Flask" to "Flash" to accurately list video add-ons. The fix ensures the documentation correctly references the Flash plugin instead of the unrelated Flask framework.

This commit corrects the return type hint for the `invoke` method in the `FlaskCliRunner` class. It changes the annotation from a generic type to the specific `Result` class, improving type checking accuracy for users of Flask's testing utilities.

This commit replaces the flake8 linter with ruff for both linting and formatting across the Flask codebase. It updates configuration files and applies ruff's style rules to source code, examples, and tests, including modules like Flask and DefaultJSONProvider.

This commit updates the project's contributor list by adding Adam Zapletal and Christopher Grebs to the AUTHORS file. It acknowledges their contributions to patches and suggestions without altering any functional code or behavior.

In debug mode, the Flask application now raises an assertion error if views or other setup functions are registered after the first request has been handled. This change helps developers catch import order mistakes earlier by providing immediate feedback in the `Flask` class.

This commit replaces the flake8 linter with ruff for both linting and formatting across the Flask codebase. It updates configuration files and applies ruff's style rules to source code, examples, and tests, including modules like Flask and DefaultJSONProvider.

This commit corrects invalid JavaScript syntax in the Flask documentation examples. It updates the `data.append` calls in `docs/patterns/javascript.rst` to use commas instead of colons, ensuring the code snippets are valid.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the documentation for the `pop` method of the `_AppCtxGlobals` class in Flask. It changes the phrasing to properly describe the behavior when a key is missing, improving the clarity of the docstring.

This commit modifies the `add_url_rule` method in the `Flask` class to accept `provide_automatic_options` as an explicit keyword argument. It clarifies the behavior for automatically providing OPTIONS responses by adding documentation to the method's docstring.

This commit removes the initialization of the `view_functions` dictionary in the `Blueprint` class constructor. It likely fixes an issue where the attribute was incorrectly defined or shadowed, ensuring the blueprint's view function storage is handled correctly.

This commit re-introduces a mechanism to prevent `app.run` from blocking the CLI when invoked outside a main guard. It sets an environment flag in `FlaskGroup.make_context` to signal that the app is running from the command line. This ensures the development server does not start prematurely during imports.

This commit fixes documentation build warnings by correcting invalid RST syntax in the Flask-RESTful documentation. It updates file and command references in the installation and extension guides to use proper inline literal markup.

This documentation update repositions a note about Flask's debug mode behavior within the error pages guide. It clarifies that the 500 Internal Server Error handler is not triggered in debug mode, placing this warning before the code examples for better visibility.

This documentation update in the testing guide clarifies best practices for handling JSON responses. It advises storing the result of the JSON getter in a variable to avoid redundant calls when accessing multiple fields.
This commit removes an unused import from the Flask context module. It cleans up the codebase without altering any application behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.1.1. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a placeholder entry to the changelog for the upcoming release.

This commit updates the database initialization tutorial to use Python 3 syntax. It changes the print statement in the `flaskr.py` example to use parentheses, ensuring the code is compliant with modern Python versions.

This commit updates the security documentation to warn developers about the risks of unquoted HTML attributes in Jinja2 templates. It explains that unquoted attributes can lead to XSS via attribute injection, a vulnerability that standard HTML escaping does not prevent. The changes are located in the security and foreword documentation files.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the documentation for error pages. It corrects the phrasing in the `docs/patterns/errorpages.rst` file to improve clarity for users reading the guide.

This commit updates the development dependencies for the project's CI/CD workflows. It bumps the versions of the checkout, setup-uv, and cache actions in the pre-commit, publish, and tests workflow files.

This commit refactors the Flask, RequestContext, and _PackageBoundObject classes to use Python decorator syntax for properties instead of manual property assignments. It updates the debug, templates_auto_reload, g, and static_folder attributes to improve code readability and maintainability.

This commit updates the installation documentation to point to the new, official location for the get-pip.py script. Users following the installation guide will now be directed to the bootstrap.pypa.io URL instead of the previous GitHub raw link.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the deferred callbacks pattern where a required import was missing. It updates the code example in the `deferredcallbacks` documentation to correctly include the `after_this_request` function alongside `request`.

The CI test workflow now runs against Python 3.12 instead of the 3.12 development version. This update ensures the project is tested against the stable release of Python 3.12 across Linux, Windows, and macOS environments.

This commit adds the zizmor security scanner to the repository's CI workflows. It also refines GitHub Actions permissions by moving them to the job level and adds concurrency controls to prevent duplicate runs.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask test client explaining that setting the app's testing flag to true is required for exceptions to propagate. Without this setting, users would only see a generic 500 error instead of the actual assertion or exception details.
This commit corrects the indentation of a code example in the WTForms documentation. It ensures the template snippet in the patterns guide displays with consistent spacing for better readability.

This commit updates the pre-commit CI configuration to target the 2.1.x branch for automatic updates. It changes the autoupdate_branch setting in the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to ensure the tooling tracks the correct release line.

This commit updates the documentation in the foreword to clarify that Flask allows entire applications to fit in a single Python file. It also refines the description of the target audience to better define the scope of suitable projects.

This commit deprecates the `as_tuple` parameter in the `FlaskClient` and `FlaskCliRunner` classes within the `flask.testing` module. Users should now access request data via `response.request.environ` instead, as the parameter will be removed in future versions.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the request context documentation. It changes the phrase "at different point" to "a different point" in the description of teardown callbacks.

This commit updates the Flask project's documentation and configuration files to reflect its move to the Pallets organization. It changes GitHub repository links in the docs, contributing guide, and sidebar to point to the new Pallets location.
