This commit updates the Flask documentation for error handling and blueprints. It renames the blueprint error handler section to improve clarity and adds a new section recommending Sentry for error logging.
This commit removes unused imports from the test_deprecations.py file. It cleans up the test module by deleting references to flask, unittest, and the catch_warnings helper that were not being used.

This commit adds a test to the Flask test suite to verify that the routing system correctly handles non-ASCII characters in URL paths. It ensures that requests to routes containing international characters return the expected response without error.

The `Config` class in `flask/config.py` now supports a `trim_namespace` parameter in the `get_namespace` method. This allows users to load configuration options while retaining the original namespace prefix in the resulting keys, rather than always stripping it.

This commit fixes a bug where extension tests would fail if the extensions were already installed in the environment. It modifies the `add_to_path` function in the Flask test suite to prioritize the test directory in the Python path, ensuring the correct modules are loaded.

This documentation update moves the HTML escaping example from the Minimal Application section to the Variable Rules section in the Flask quickstart guide. It removes the markupsafe escape demonstration from the minimal example, which does not process user input, to better align the tutorial with actual security requirements.
This commit corrects a typo in the release notes for version 0.8.1. It changes the date notation from "July 1th" to the proper "July 1st" in the CHANGES file.

This commit updates the docstring for the Blueprint class in the Flask module. It clarifies that a blueprint is a collection of routes and functions that can be registered on an application later, without requiring an application object upfront.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.12.2 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.

This commit restructures the project's GitHub issue and pull request templates by replacing a single legacy file with a dedicated directory containing separate templates for bug reports and feature requests. It also updates the configuration to support this new layout, improving the organization of user submissions.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to import the escape function from markupsafe instead of Flask. It also corrects references to the Markup class to point to the markupsafe module, ensuring users follow the current import conventions.

This commit fixes a packaging error in setup.py by correcting the module declaration for the Flask package. It also updates the quickstart documentation to warn users against naming their application file flask.py to avoid import conflicts.
This commit fixes broken cross-references on the jQuery patterns documentation page. It updates the link to the `MultiDict.get` method to point to the correct `werkzeug.datastructures` module path.

This commit disables memory-related tests in the Flask test suite by default to prevent them from running during standard test executions. The `suite` function in `flask/testsuite/regression.py` now only includes `MemoryTestCase` if a specific environment variable is set, and a new Makefile target allows users to explicitly run these tests.
This commit updates the mod_wsgi deployment documentation to reflect current package names. It corrects the installation commands for Debian and FreeBSD systems to use the Python 3 specific packages.

This commit adds a future import to the Flask helpers module to enable the use of the `with` statement. This ensures compatibility with older Python versions that require this explicit import for context manager support.

This commit removes legacy Python 2 compatibility code from Flask's CLI, context, and helper modules. It simplifies SSL context handling in CertParamType and eliminates obsolete exception clearing calls in AppContext and RequestContext.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the blueprint nesting example within the documentation. It fixes a missing closing quote in the child blueprint's URL prefix, ensuring the code snippet is valid and copy-paste ready for users.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `test_request_context` method in the `Flask` class. It clarifies that the method creates a `RequestContext` object rather than a WSGI environment, ensuring the docstring accurately reflects the function's behavior.

This change prevents `get_flashed_messages` from modifying the session when no flash messages are present. It avoids unnecessary session updates by only popping the data if it actually exists, ensuring the session remains unchanged in empty cases.
This commit fixes a broken internal link in the advanced foreword documentation. It corrects the reference to the Python 3 support page so that users can successfully navigate to the correct section.

This commit adds a dedicated section to the Flask quickstart documentation explaining how to manually escape user-provided data to prevent injection attacks. It introduces the `markupsafe.escape` function as a tool for sanitizing values in HTML responses, noting that Jinja templates handle this automatically.
This commit initializes the changelog for the upcoming Flask 0.13 release. It adds a new section to the CHANGES file to track updates for this major version.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the quickstart guide that caused incorrect HTML list nesting. It adjusts indentation in the reStructuredText source to ensure the description list renders correctly within the ordered list.
This commit updates the project's changelog to finalize the release details for version 0.8. It sets the release date to September 29, 2011, and assigns the codename "Rakija" to the release.

This commit updates the Flask installation documentation to correct minor grammatical errors and improve sentence clarity. It refines the descriptions of Werkzeug and Jinja2 roles within the docs/installation.rst file.

This commit initiates the 0.10.1 maintenance branch for a pending bugfix release. It updates the version string to 0.10.1-dev in the Flask package initialization and setup configuration, and adds a placeholder entry to the changelog.

This commit refines the session saving logic in the SecureCookieSessionInterface class within the Flask sessions module. It ensures that an empty session is handled by returning early, preventing unnecessary cookie operations. This improves the efficiency and clarity of how session data is persisted or cleared.

This commit updates the test configuration to replace the deprecated `pytest.yield_fixture` with `pytest.fixture`. This change ensures compatibility with modern pytest versions and removes unnecessary deprecation warnings from the test suite.
This commit adds a maintenance note to the memory leak tests in the test_regression.py module. It flags that the tests require revision because they broke during the project's port to Python 3.
Updates the PyCharm run configuration screenshot in the documentation to include a highlighted area. This clarifies the specific settings users need to adjust when configuring their project.

This commit restores the ability to store binary data in Flask sessions, fixing a regression that broke token verification workflows. The `TaggedJSONSerializer` class now encodes byte strings using base64 and decodes them upon retrieval.

This commit fixes a documentation rendering issue in the CLI guide where Windows file paths were displayed incorrectly. It corrects the path syntax in the `docs/cli.rst` file to ensure the backslashes are properly escaped for the documentation build.

This commit updates Flask documentation to recommend using the secrets module instead of os.urandom for generating secret keys. It clarifies that the SECRET_KEY configuration value should be a hex string rather than a byte string, improving clarity for users setting up secure applications.

This commit updates the changelog entry for the 2021-05-21 release to clarify that a previous modification to URL matching order was reverted. It corrects the wording in the CHANGES.rst file to accurately reflect the restoration of the original behavior.
This commit removes an unused pickle import from the test_basic module. It cleans up the test file without altering any functional behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.

This commit adds the missing documentation file for file uploads to the project's patterns directory. It provides a guide on handling file uploads, explaining the basic process and introducing a simple application example.

This commit improves the error message shown when `render_template` or `render_template_string` is called without an active application context. It replaces a generic failure with a clear `RuntimeError` explaining that an application context is required.

This commit updates the documentation for package patterns to clarify the distinction between directories and files in the project structure. It also recommends using a setup.py file instead of runserver.py for larger applications to follow standard project conventions.

This commit changes the `jinja_loader` property in the `_PackageBoundObject` class to use a thread-safe locking mechanism instead of a standard cached property. This prevents potential race conditions during concurrent access to the Jinja2 loader.

This commit adds a documentation note to the Flask tutorial views, warning against storing passwords in plain text. It explains that while hashing is recommended for security, the tutorial uses plain text for simplicity.

This commit updates the installation documentation to clarify that the shell prompt indicates the active environment rather than specifically a virtualenv. The change improves the accuracy of the user-facing instructions in the installation guide.

This commit adds tests to the Flask test suite to verify that the `Vary: Cookie` header is correctly included in responses when sessions are accessed. It ensures the header is present for session reads and writes, but absent for routes that do not interact with the session.
This commit updates the project changelog to document version 0.5.1, a bugfix release. It notes that this version resolves an issue with template loading for modules.

This commit adds a failing test to verify that streaming responses correctly preserve the session context. It ensures that accessing session data within a generator function works as expected, preventing potential data loss during streaming.

This commit updates test fixtures in the minitwit example and core test suite to use the modern yield syntax instead of manual finalizers. It simplifies the client, leak_detector, and disable_extwarnings fixtures by removing explicit teardown functions and request parameters.
This commit corrects grammatical errors in the file upload documentation. It improves sentence structure and word choice in the fileuploads.rst file to enhance clarity for users.

This commit renames the environment variable used to skip dotenv loading to FLASK_SKIP_DOTENV and adds documentation for this feature. It updates the FlaskGroup class in flask/cli.py and the get_load_dotenv helper in flask/helpers.py to support the new name, ensuring users can prevent automatic dotenv loading when using external runners.

The FlaskClient.open method now accepts an existing EnvironBuilder or dictionary as an argument. This allows developers to pass custom environment data directly when making requests with the test client.

This commit updates the blueprint documentation to correct a template path example and adds a detailed explanation of how route decorators register functions and prefix endpoints. The changes clarify the behavior of the Blueprint class for users implementing static page rendering.

This commit consolidates Flask documentation by merging the separate API errors and error pages guides into the main error handling document. It updates cross-references in the blueprints guide to point to the unified resource, improving the organization of error management information.

This commit updates the HTML5 FAQ documentation in the docs module to improve clarity and correct minor grammatical errors. It also adds Matthew Frazier to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file.

This commit updates the templating documentation to clarify how to use custom filters after they are registered. It adds an example showing that registered filters work in templates just like built-in Jinja2 filters.

This commit updates the project's dependency management to use pip-compile instead of pip-compile-multi. It modifies the GitHub Actions workflows and various requirements files to reflect this change, ensuring consistent dependency resolution across the build and test environments.

This commit moves the test discovery and loading logic from the standalone runner script into the Flask testsuite package. It introduces a custom test loader and helper functions to recursively find and name all test cases, improving the organization of the testing infrastructure.

The `locked_cached_property` class in `flask.helpers` now inherits from Werkzeug's `cached_property` instead of implementing its own logic. This change simplifies the codebase by reusing the existing implementation while maintaining thread-safe access.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the static file tutorial where the localhost URL was missing the default port number. Users following the guide would have been unable to access the login page correctly. The change updates the URL in the static.rst file to include port 5000.

This commit fixes a broken link in the error handling documentation that previously pointed to a non-existent relative path. It updates the URL in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file to include the proper HTTPS protocol, ensuring users can successfully access the project's GitHub repository.

This commit adds a changelog entry for Flask version 0.7.1, documenting it as a bugfix release. It specifically notes the addition of a missing future import that previously broke Python 2.5 compatibility.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.1.2 by updating the version number in the project configuration and lock files. It also adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes for this release.

This commit corrects a typo in a comment within the `flash` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies the documentation regarding session synchronization, ensuring the text accurately describes the behavior without changing any functional code.

The `Flask.route` decorator in `flask.py` was refactored to delegate to the new `add_url_rule` method. This change simplifies the internal logic for registering routes and marks `add_url_rule` as available since version 0.2.

This documentation update clarifies how Flask handles multiple configuration imports, noting that the last imported setting takes precedence. It explains that the `from_envvar` method in the `flask.Config` class helps achieve this robust setup by loading environment-specific files.

This commit expands the Flask quickstart documentation by adding a new section titled "About Responses." It explains how the framework automatically converts various return values from view functions into proper response objects, detailing the default status codes and content types applied.

The release script previously failed to upload the package because it used an invalid command sequence. This fix updates the `build_and_upload` function in `scripts/make-release.py` to correctly invoke the setup tool for building and uploading the distribution.

This commit configures the project to automatically run the Black code formatter using pre-commit. It adds a new style check environment to the tox configuration that executes pre-commit on all files, ensuring consistent code formatting is enforced during testing.

This commit refactors the Flask test suite to use pytest fixtures, reducing code duplication across multiple test files. It introduces shared fixtures in conftest.py and updates tests to utilize them, improving maintainability. Additionally, it standardizes docstrings and applies parameterization to specific tests.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flask documentation for the signals module. It updates the example import statement to reference the correct signal name, ensuring users see the accurate function name in the docs.

This commit fixes broken Markdown link syntax in the README file by removing unnecessary empty brackets from several references. It ensures that links to WSGI, Werkzeug, Jinja, and the donation page render correctly for users reading the documentation.

This commit updates Flask's test suite to expect response data as bytes instead of strings. It modifies assertions in test cases across basic, blueprints, helpers, subclassing, templating, and testing modules to reflect this data type change.

This commit updates the Flask CLI to print a full stack trace when an error occurs during command execution. Previously, errors might have been handled silently or with limited information, which could confuse users. The change modifies the `FlaskGroup` class in `flask/cli.py` to ensure detailed error reporting.

This commit ensures the documentation PDF uses the Flasky code highlighting style. It explicitly sets the pygments style in the Sphinx configuration to prevent inconsistent syntax coloring in generated PDFs.

This commit updates the minimum required Werkzeug version to 2.3.7. It modifies the `get_version` function in `flask.cli` and the `FlaskClient` class in `flask.testing` to use `importlib.metadata` for retrieving version information.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the FastCGI deployment guide by correcting the indentation of a code example. The change ensures the Python snippet in the `fastcgi.rst` file displays with proper formatting for users.

This commit updates the Flask debugging documentation to clarify that the application must remain in debug mode when using an external debugger. It explains that disabling debug mode causes unhandled errors to display as generic 500 pages, while the built-in debugger and reloader should still be turned off to prevent interference.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.12.4 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.

The `request.json` property in Flask's `JSONMixin` is no longer deprecated, removing the warning previously issued when accessing it. This change restores the property as a standard feature without requiring users to switch to `get_json()`.

This commit fixes a grammatical typo in the help text for the Flask shell command. It corrects the possessive pronoun in the description of the shell's namespace configuration within the `shell_command` function in `src/flask/cli.py`.

This documentation update adds a direct hyperlink to the Flask extensions page within the "Hook. Extend." section of the becomingbig guide. It improves user navigation by allowing readers to easily access the community extension list.

This commit adds a test to verify the correct precedence of error handlers when an exception inherits from multiple registered exception types. It ensures that the most specific handler is selected over a generic one. The test is located in the test_basic.py module.

This commit reverts a previous change to the `register_blueprint` method in the `Flask` class. It restores the original docstring and parameter documentation for registering blueprints, ensuring accurate help text is displayed to users.

This commit removes the redundant `_get_data_for_json` method from the `Response` class in `flask/wrappers.py`. The method was unnecessary because the class already inherits the required functionality from its parent classes, simplifying the code without changing behavior.

This commit introduces module-based request and response processing to the Flask application. It updates the Flask class to correctly register modules and handle after-request hooks, ensuring that response processing functions are applied appropriately.

This commit corrects minor typos in the Flask sessions module. It fixes a capitalization error in the error message raised by the NullSession class and corrects a spelling mistake in a comment within the SessionInterface class.

This commit fixes an error that occurred when applying multiple route decorators to a single async function. It modifies the Flask class and run_async helper to track wrapped functions, allowing the app to correctly compare and update routes without raising exceptions.

This commit fixes a broken documentation link in the quickstart guide. It updates the reference in the `docs/quickstart.rst` file to point to the correct `application-errors` section instead of the invalid `errorhandling` target.

This commit adds a Makefile target to generate test coverage reports and updates the contributing documentation to clarify available build commands. It also configures the repository to ignore coverage output files.

This commit updates the project metadata in setup.py to ensure project URLs appear in a specific, consistent order. It replaces the standard dictionary with an OrderedDict to preserve the sequence of Documentation, Code, and Issue Tracker links.

This commit updates the project changelog to finalize the release details for version 0.6. It replaces the placeholder text with the specific release date and assigns the codename Whisky to this version.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the SQLite3 documentation example by adding a missing colon to the context manager statement. The change ensures the code snippet in the `docs/patterns/sqlite3.rst` file is valid Python.

The `template_filter` method in the `Flask` class now requires parentheses when used as a decorator. This change removes support for the previous usage without parentheses, ensuring consistent behavior for registering custom Jinja filters.

This commit updates the changelog to document a fix in the session system. It notes that empty session cookies are now automatically deleted, resolving a potential issue where stale cookies might persist.

The `from_pyfile` method in Flask's `Config` class now accepts a `silent` parameter. This allows the method to ignore missing files or directories without raising an error, matching the behavior of `from_envvar`.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for the message flashing pattern by providing a complete, runnable code example. It adds the necessary application setup, including the Flask instance and secret key, to the existing snippet in the flashing guide.

This commit fixes a documentation build failure by ensuring the `html_theme_options` variable is always defined. It adds a fallback assignment in `docs/conf.py` to prevent errors when the theme import fails.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency in the development requirements from version 2.12.1 to 2.13.0. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the pre-commit framework for managing git hooks.

This commit corrects the testing documentation for the EnvironBuilder class. It replaces the incorrect keyword argument name "query" with the valid "query_string" to prevent users from encountering errors when setting request query parameters.

This commit expands the documentation for the API module to clarify how default URL parameters trigger 301 redirects to simpler forms. It warns developers that if a route handles POST requests, the default route must be restricted to GET to prevent loss of form data during the redirect.

This commit updates the test suite to stop relying on the private `monkeypatch` fixture API from the `_pytest` module. It modifies the `_reset_os_environ` and `_standard_os_environ` helpers in `tests/conftest.py` and adjusts related tests in `tests/test_cli.py` to use supported methods instead.

This commit updates the `url_for` function in `flask.helpers` to use Python 3 syntax for raising exceptions with tracebacks. It replaces the deprecated Python 2-style raise statement with the modern `with_traceback` method, ensuring compatibility with Python 3.

This change updates the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to include the specific error message when JSON loading fails. Previously, the `on_json_loading_failed` method raised a generic `BadRequest` exception, but it now passes the underlying exception details to the response.

This commit removes the `--eager-loading` and `--lazy-loading` options from the `flask run` command, eliminating the `DispatchingApp` middleware. The application now always loads eagerly on the first run and lazily in the reloader, which immediately prints tracebacks for loading errors while continuing to serve requests.
This commit fixes minor grammatical and stylistic errors in the SQLite3 documentation. It corrects punctuation and capitalization in the Flask patterns guide to improve readability.

This commit introduces URL value preprocessors to the Flask application and Blueprint classes. It adds new attributes and methods that allow developers to register functions for modifying URL values during the building process.

This commit ensures that calling setdefault on a Flask session marks the session as accessed, preventing the Vary: Cookie header from being omitted. The change adds a setdefault method to the SecureCookieSession class to explicitly set the accessed flag before delegating to the parent implementation.

This commit modernizes the test suite by replacing custom assertion methods in the TestFlask class with standard unittest assertions. It updates test files across the project to use these standard methods, removing the need for the previously defined helper functions.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the docstring for the `setdefault` method within the `_AppCtxGlobals` class in `src/flask/ctx.py`. It also removes redundant parentheses from an assertion in the `test_routing_redirect_debugging` test.

This commit corrects a typo in the Fabric documentation example. It updates the file path in the `put` command to explicitly name the target archive, ensuring the example accurately reflects the intended deployment behavior.

This commit fixes an UnboundLocalError in Flask's handle_url_build_error method, which occurred when a custom error handler re-raised the exception. The issue stemmed from Python 3 clearing the exception variable upon exiting the except block. A test case was added to verify that re-raising the error works correctly.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to clarify that the 500 error handler is not triggered when the application runs in debug mode. It adds a note to the error pages guide to prevent user confusion regarding error handling behavior.

This commit corrects inconsistent double spacing in the Flask API documentation. It standardizes the text in docs/api.rst to use single spaces after periods, improving the visual consistency of the rendered documentation.

This commit corrects punctuation and grammatical errors in the WTForms documentation to improve readability. It updates the text in the `docs/patterns/wtforms.rst` file, specifically fixing phrasing in the introduction and the description of the Flask-WTF extension.

This commit updates the pinned versions of GitHub Actions in the lock, publish, and tests workflows. It ensures the repository uses the latest stable releases of actions like checkout and setup-python, improving security and compatibility.

This commit updates the mod_wsgi deployment documentation to clarify how to handle factory functions defined in an application's `__init__.py` file. It instructs users to explicitly import and call the factory function to create the application instance.

The `_render` function in `flask/templating.py` no longer checks the return values of `before_render_template` signal receivers. This change removes the previous behavior where a single non-None return value would override the standard template rendering process.

Flask now automatically handles HTTP OPTIONS requests for all routes, allowing clients to discover supported methods without manual implementation. This behavior is managed within the Flask application class and request context, unless a developer explicitly defines an OPTIONS handler for a specific URL rule.
This commit removes the deprecated `flask.session` module alias to prevent confusion with the session proxy object. Users should now import session classes directly from `flask.sessions` instead.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to replace outdated IRC links with the current Discord server address. It clarifies that Discord is the preferred communication channel while noting the IRC bridge remains available. The change also removes a note about rejecting style-related patches.

This commit updates domain matching tests in `tests/test_basic.py` to accommodate changes in Werkzeug 3.2. It introduces a version check to adjust expected subdomain and host matching behavior, ensuring tests pass with the newer library version.

This commit corrects typos and outdated terminology in the installation documentation. It updates references from "setuptools" to "distribute" and fixes the spelling of "privileges" in the installation guide.

This commit refactors the session serializer into a new `flask.json.tag` module to make it extensible. It allows developers to register custom tags for storing additional data types in session cookies. The `TaggedJSONSerializer` class now supports serializing single-item dictionaries where the key is a tag.
The pre-commit workflow now triggers on the stable branch instead of all versioned branches. This change ensures that automated checks run specifically for the stable release line.

This commit adds a unit test for the `find_default_import_path` function in the Flask CLI module. It verifies that the function correctly returns the value of the `FLASK_APP` environment variable or `None` if the variable is not set.

Adds test coverage for the `trim_namespace` argument in the `get_namespace` method of the application configuration module. These tests verify that disabling namespace trimming preserves the original key prefixes in the returned dictionary.

This commit updates the greenlet dependency from version 0.4.17 to 1.0.0 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the greenlet library for its testing environment.

The test_json_key_sorting method in flask/testsuite/helpers.py now handles differences in JSON key sorting between standard library and simplejson. It first checks for integer-based sorting and falls back to string-based sorting if that fails, preventing test failures caused by simplejson version changes.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Blueprint class within the flask.blueprints module. It fixes an incorrect reference to the BlueprintSetupState class, ensuring the module name is spelled correctly in the docstring.

This commit updates the documentation for the `JSONMixin` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to clarify that `get_json` handles both request and response data. It also refines the API reference in `docs/api.rst` to explicitly list the `is_json` and `get_json` members for request and response objects.

This commit updates the Flask 0.7 upgrade script to handle the transition from modules to blueprints. It adds logic to rewrite import statements and replace module-specific function calls with their blueprint equivalents. The changes primarily affect the `rewrite_for_blueprints` and `rewrite_from_imports` functions.
This commit updates the changelog to document the removal of deprecated module functionality in version 1.0. It clarifies that the module system no longer supports the previously deprecated features.
This commit corrects minor grammatical errors in the Django tutorial documentation. It updates the setup and views guides to improve clarity and accuracy for users following the instructions.
This commit corrects several spelling errors in the Flask documentation for blueprints. It fixes typos in the description of how the Blueprint class determines its resource folder.

This commit updates the build configuration to use the modern bdist_wheel command instead of the deprecated wheel command. This change ensures the project correctly generates universal wheels according to current Python packaging standards. The modification is made in the setup.cfg file.

The test suite now creates the Flask application with an explicit name and root path instead of relying on the module name. This ensures the application context teardown event consistently reports the correct name, fixing an assertion failure in the test_clean_pop test.

This commit restructures the minitwit and flaskr examples to be installed as editable packages, allowing them to be run via standard Flask commands. It updates the test suites to follow pytest standards, ensuring tests execute correctly without manual path adjustments.

This commit adds a new example application demonstrating how to integrate Persona authentication into a Flask project. It includes the necessary Python backend logic for handling login and logout, along with the required JavaScript, CSS, and HTML templates for the user interface.

This commit updates the documentation in the `flaskext_migrate.py` script to accurately reflect its current capabilities. It clarifies that the tool now handles function calls in the source code, not just import statements, removing outdated limitations from the comments.

This commit fixes a Windows installation failure introduced by a previous change. It modifies the setup.py file to use include_package_data instead of explicitly defining package_data, ensuring the package installs correctly on all platforms.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.1.1 to 3.1.2. It modifies the pinned dependency versions in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the latest patch release.

This commit adds a new section to the Quickstart documentation explaining how to use Flask extensions. It introduces the concept of extensions as packages for common tasks, using Flask-SQLAlchemy as an example, and directs readers to the dedicated extensions reference.

This commit adds a test case to verify that returning a value from a before_request hook correctly short-circuits the request, preventing the view function from executing. The test ensures the response matches the hook's return value and that the view function is never called.

This commit fixes the release creation workflow to correctly include build artifacts in the generated release. It updates the publish workflow to reference the dist directory instead of a non-existent artifact path, ensuring the release action succeeds.

This commit corrects the documentation for the Flask templating system to accurately reference the configuration object. It updates the symbol reference in the templating module documentation to point to the Flask instance's config attribute instead of the deprecated global config.

This commit moves the initialization of the `cli` attribute from the shared `Scaffold` class to the `Flask` class. This change ensures that the Flask-specific Click command group is not incorrectly set in the framework-agnostic sansio code.

This documentation update clarifies that Flask does not include a database abstraction layer. It corrects the foreword to accurately reflect the framework's design philosophy of keeping the core simple and extensible.

This commit updates the Flask codebase to resolve type checking errors reported by mypy in strict mode. It adds precise type annotations across core modules like the Flask app, blueprints, and CLI tools to improve static analysis accuracy.

This commit updates the CLI documentation to reflect changes in PyCharm 2017.3. It explains that users can now run the Flask module directly by name instead of locating the executable file in the virtual environment.

This documentation update clarifies that Flask's `register_error_handler` function is an alternative to the `errorhandler` decorator, particularly useful within application factories. It helps users understand the different ways to register error handlers in the `flask` module.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask's built-in server in the deploying guide. It removes the claim that the server serves only one request at a time, clarifying that its main limitation is poor scalability.
This commit updates the changelog to document a new feature in version 1.0. It notes that view functions can now return tuples containing a response and headers.

The `reset_logging` fixture in `tests/test_logging.py` now uses the `pytestconfig` fixture to manage the logging plugin. This updates the test setup to use the modern pytest API for unregistering and re-registering the plugin, replacing the deprecated global `pytest.config` access.

This commit updates the documentation in the quickstart guide to improve the wording of the Heroku deployment section. It clarifies that Heroku is a suitable option for hosting small Flask applications for free.

The CI test workflow now runs standard and free-threaded Python environments as separate jobs instead of combining them. This change affects the test configuration in the GitHub Actions workflow file.

The main function in the Flask upgrade script now displays a custom usage message when the command-line options are requested. This change clarifies the expected command syntax for users running the script.

This commit resolves a build warning by renaming the documentation table of contents file to avoid a naming conflict. It updates the Makefile to include the HTML build step and adds commands to package and upload the documentation. The documentation index files are updated to reference the new filename.

This commit removes per-project contribution files to prevent synchronization issues, relying instead on a global guide. It updates the README to include a section linking to this guide, as GitHub's interface does not automatically display it.

This commit adds documentation for the application dispatching pattern in the Flask project. It explains how to combine multiple Flask or WSGI applications at the WSGI level, allowing them to run side by side with isolated configurations.

This commit removes support for Python 2.6 and 3.3 from the project's documentation and configuration. It updates the contributing guide and FastCGI deployment instructions to reflect the new minimum version requirements.

This commit updates the changelog to document a change in session cookie behavior. It clarifies that the `SERVER_NAME` configuration key now also sets the session cookie domain to be valid across subdomains.

This commit updates the `ResponseValue` type in `src/flask/typing.py` to explicitly include lists and dictionaries, ensuring type checkers accept these return types. It also adds new test routes in `tests/typing/typing_route.py` to verify that returning JSON strings, dictionaries, and lists is correctly typed.

This commit updates the installation documentation to use "venv" instead of "env" for the virtual environment directory name. It also replaces the deprecated "easy_install" command with "pip install" and simplifies the activation instructions by using "source" directly.

This documentation update clarifies that deprecation warnings are disabled by default in Python 2.7. It instructs users to explicitly enable these warnings using the warnings module to see potential deprecation messages during upgrades.

This commit restructures the Flask configuration documentation by replacing a static table with linkable sections. This change improves navigation and readability for users referencing specific configuration keys in the docs/config.rst file.
This commit removes the `docs-html` environment from the test suite in `tox.ini`. It resolves an issue where the `detox` tool was breaking the documentation test environment.
This commit deprecates the `json` property on the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py`. Accessing this property now triggers a warning, guiding users to use the `get_json()` method instead.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the release date for version 0.10 within the CHANGES file. It updates the ordinal suffix from "13nd" to "13th" to ensure the documentation is accurate.

Flask's JSONEncoder now supports serializing datetime.date objects, allowing them to be converted to HTTP date strings. This change ensures that date values are handled correctly when using the jsonify function.

This commit clarifies the documentation for testing code that uses sessions. It explicitly states that the test client should be called after the session transaction completes, rather than during it. The changes are located in the testing documentation file.

This commit updates the documentation in the becomingbig module to clarify URL initialization issues. It suggests using a single module to explicitly define and import target functions as a better solution for managing application scale.

This commit fixes an issue in Flask's logging module where the debug log level was incorrectly applied even when a specific log level was explicitly set. The `create_logger` function now only defaults to debug mode if no explicit level is configured, ensuring user-defined settings are respected.
This commit fixes broken HTML in the Flask example templates by removing unnecessary end-tags and correcting formatting. It ensures the blueprint example pages render correctly without syntax errors.

This commit fixes an issue in the Flask application where proxy exceptions without error codes were incorrectly handled. It ensures these exceptions are returned unchanged in the `handle_http_exception` method and adds a regression test to verify the behavior.

This commit removes a stray debug print statement from the `fix_imports` function in `scripts/flaskext_migrate.py`. It also updates `scripts/test.py` to use a standard import statement instead of a multi-line import, improving code consistency.
This commit prevents test failures when the asgiref package is missing. It adds a check to the test_async.py module that skips async tests if the dependency is not installed.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to prevent the pytest cache directory from being tracked by version control. It also standardizes other ignore patterns by adding trailing slashes to directory entries like env, dist, and build.

This commit expands the Flask documentation's quickstart guide by adding a new section on URL building. It explains how to use the `url_for` function to generate URLs for specific routes, providing practical examples for users.
Adds a test suite for the Blueprint example application. The new BlueprintExampleTestCase verifies that the root, hello, and world routes return successful responses.

This commit updates the Flask application, blueprint, and view modules to access type definitions through a new namespace alias. It replaces direct imports of specific callable types with references to the `ft` module, simplifying the codebase's type management.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to reference Flask instead of Jinja. It clarifies guidance for users unfamiliar with the Flask ecosystem by correcting the project name in the support instructions.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.0.4 by updating the version string in the package initialization and setup files. It also adds Python 3.7 to the supported programming languages in the project metadata.

This commit adds a new "Building Extensions" section to the Flask documentation. It guides users who cannot find a suitable existing extension to read the extension development guide. The change is located in the extensions documentation file.

In `flask/testing.py`, the `make_test_environ_builder` function now accepts `json` as a keyword argument instead of a positional one. This change prevents potential conflicts when passing other arguments and ensures JSON data is correctly processed via the `kwargs` dictionary.

This commit updates the Read the Docs build environment configuration in the .readthedocs.yaml file. It changes the build operating system from Ubuntu 20.04 to 22.04 and upgrades the Python version from 3.10 to 3.12.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to clarify how blueprint template folders are prioritized and how to structure them for overriding. It also adds a new section explaining how to build URLs between pages. The changes primarily affect the `Flask` class documentation and the blueprints guide.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to use the standard `assert_false` method instead of the non-standard `assert_true` with negated logic. It adds the `assert_false` helper to the `FlaskTestCase` base class and applies it across various test modules for clearer assertions.
The Makefile now uses rsync instead of scp to upload documentation files to the server. This improves the upload process by allowing for more efficient file synchronization.

The `Flask.run` method now derives the default port from the `SERVER_NAME` configuration variable if it is set, rather than always defaulting to 5000. This change ensures the development server respects the port specified in the application's server name.
This commit adds the author name and email address to the project's metadata configuration. It updates the setup.cfg file to include these details for the package.
This commit corrects a typo in the testing tutorial documentation. It changes the phrase "not a good idea" to "not a bad idea" to accurately recommend adding automated tests.

This commit updates the project's contribution guidelines to include a link to the community Discord server. It also clarifies that style-related patches are not accepted, helping contributors focus on functional changes.

This commit fixes the error message raised by the `after_this_request` function in Flask's context module. Previously, using the decorator outside a request context caused a confusing error; now it raises a clear `RuntimeError` explaining that it must be used within a request context.
This commit removes an unused import from the Flask module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating a redundant reference to the threading local object, which has no impact on application behavior.
This commit corrects the documentation for Flask's redirect and abort functions in the quickstart guide. It removes incorrect syntax and simplifies the explanation to improve clarity for users.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Request.json` property in the Flask wrappers module. It clarifies that the property returns `None` if the request body is not valid JSON and specifies the Python version or library requirements for JSON parsing.

This commit updates the changelog to clarify that the type annotation fix applies to all teardown methods, not just teardown_request. It corrects the documentation in the CHANGES.rst file to accurately reflect the scope of the previous change.
This commit corrects a broken changelog link in the CHANGES file. It adds a missing reference definition to ensure the link to the release notes resolves properly for users.

This commit adds support for generic HTTPException handlers in Flask, allowing developers to define catch-all error handlers for both the application and individual blueprints. The `Flask._find_error_handler` method now resolves handlers in a specific priority order, checking for specific status codes before falling back to generic exception handlers.

This commit adds documentation to the Blueprints guide explaining how to register custom error handlers. It clarifies that the errorhandler decorator works on Blueprint objects, allowing developers to create specific error pages for their routes.
This commit corrects several typos in the design documentation. It fixes grammatical errors in the description of implicit application objects and explicit object behavior.

Nested blueprints now register with their dotted names, allowing same-named blueprints to exist at different locations. The `register_blueprint` method in the `Flask` class accepts a `name` option to assign unique names for URL generation.

This commit marks the `test_main_module_paths` test in `tests/test_instance_config.py` as expected to fail. It addresses a flaky test issue caused by a strange interaction with the tox testing environment.

This commit adds a new documentation page demonstrating how to subclass the Flask application class. It updates the main patterns index and the "becoming big" guide to link to this new example, helping users customize features like the Jinja2 environment.

The commit updates the test runner in `tests/flaskext_test.py` to accept a list of extensions as an argument to the `run_tests` function. It also enhances the HTML report template to include clickable links that navigate directly to specific test logs.

This commit introduces a custom FixedOffset class to replace the standard datetime.timezone, ensuring Python 2.x compatibility for timezone-aware datetime tests. It updates the TestJSON module to use this new class when verifying JSON serialization of aware datetimes.
This commit updates the Python dependency versions in the requirements files. It bumps pytest to 7.4.4, mypy to 1.8.0, and pre-commit to 3.6.0 to incorporate the latest bug fixes and features.

This commit finalizes the 0.12.3 release by updating the changelog to mark the version as released. It also refactors the make-release.py script, removing the module docstring and reorganizing imports for consistency.

This commit corrects several typos in the documentation files `becomingbig.rst` and `patterns.rst`. It fixes misspellings and clarifies wording regarding module organization and model definitions to improve readability.

This commit adds code coverage generation to the project's test suite by updating the tox configuration. It modifies the pytest command to include coverage flags for the flask module and adds the necessary pytest-cov dependency. Additionally, it updates the gitignore file to exclude generated coverage reports from version control.

This commit updates the test for `prepare_exec_for_file` in `tests/test_cli.py` to verify that the function correctly adds the parent directory of the input file to `sys.path`. It ensures the side effect of modifying the Python path is explicitly checked alongside the returned module name.

This commit updates the MethodView class in flask/views.py to collect HTTP method handlers from base classes using the method resolution order. It removes the previous logic that only checked for an explicitly set methods attribute, allowing inherited handlers to be recognized automatically.

This commit simplifies how Flask exposes the original exception within an InternalServerError. It removes the need for compatibility checks with older Werkzeug versions, allowing developers to access the original error directly without using getattr. The change affects the Flask class and its exception handling logic.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to explain how to define separate view functions for different HTTP methods on the same route. It introduces the use of method-specific decorators like `app.get` and `app.post` as an alternative to handling all methods within a single function.

This commit reverts a previous change that incorrectly closed HTML list item tags in the JavaScript example template. It restores the original markup in the base.html file to fix potential rendering issues in the example application.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.1.4 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It also marks the release date in the changelog and corrects a minor formatting inconsistency in the documentation.

This commit removes an accidental debug print statement from the Flask application class. It prevents unwanted console output during URL adapter creation, ensuring clean execution of the `create_url_adapter` method.

This documentation update replaces references to the deprecated TextField with StringField in the WTForms registration example. It ensures users see the current recommended field type for text inputs in the patterns guide.
This commit corrects minor grammatical errors in the Flask quickstart documentation. It updates example code snippets to include a comma in the "Hello, World" greeting for consistency.

This commit updates the development dependencies for the project's CI/CD workflows and pre-commit configuration. It bumps the versions of GitHub Actions such as checkout, setup-uv, setup-python, and cache to their latest releases. The changes ensure the build and test environments use the most recent tooling.

This commit updates several development dependencies to their latest versions, including pre-commit, tox, and virtualenv. It also bumps the versions of documentation and typing tools like Pygments and types-setuptools.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It fixes the misspelled environment variable name in the description of the `run` method, ensuring users see the correct `SERVER_NAME` reference.

This commit fixes the PDF documentation for Flask by ensuring page numbers are displayed correctly. It changes the page style in the `flaskstyle.sty` module from empty to plain, resolving an issue where page numbers were missing.

This commit improves the `Request.on_json_loading_failed` method in `src/flask/wrappers.py` to provide a more specific error message when JSON decoding fails in debug mode. It ensures that the original exception is preserved in the raised `BadRequest` error, allowing users to see the exact reason for the failure.

This commit updates the standalone WSGI deployment documentation to include instructions for using uWSGI. It explains how to run the uWSGI HTTP router and provides links to further configuration guides.
This commit updates the documentation for application factories to correct a minor wording error. It clarifies the phrasing regarding how to access the application instance within a request context.

This commit updates the pyupgrade pre-commit hook from version 3.7.0 to 3.8.0. It modifies the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to ensure the project uses the latest version of the tool for Python code modernization.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency from version 2.7.1 to 2.8.2 in the development requirements. It also adds the sphinx-tabs package and updates the pygments dependency to include sphinx-tabs as a source.

This commit streamlines the CI configuration by reducing the number of test environments and caching dependencies to speed up builds. It also enables branch coverage collection for both the Flask source and test code, and integrates Codecov for reporting.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to replace references to the standard library's unittest module with pytest. It clarifies testing terminology in the signals and testing guides, ensuring the documentation aligns with modern testing practices.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the .vscode directory from version control. This prevents local Visual Studio Code configuration files from being accidentally committed to the repository.

This commit fixes documentation build errors caused by lines exceeding the maximum length in several RST files. It adjusts the text wrapping in files like `advanced_foreword.rst` and `cli.rst` to ensure the documentation renders correctly.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.1.3 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It also marks the release date in the changelog, transitioning the status from unreleased to officially released.

This commit modifies the Flask class to raise an assertion error when a new URL rule attempts to override an existing endpoint function. This prevents silent overwrites of view functions, ensuring developers are immediately aware of conflicting route definitions.

The `shell_command` function in `flask/cli.py` now respects the `PYTHONSTARTUP` environment variable. This allows users to execute custom startup scripts when launching the Flask shell, matching standard Python interpreter behavior.

This commit removes the internal `_compat` module, which provided Python 2 and 3 compatibility shims. It updates the Flask application, CLI, and helper modules to rely on native Python 3 features instead of these legacy utilities.

This commit updates the development dependencies for the project's CI/CD workflows. It bumps the versions of the `setup-uv` and `actions/cache` actions in the GitHub workflow files and updates the `uv.lock` file to reflect these changes.

This commit fixes a bug where a catch-all error handler for HTTP exceptions incorrectly intercepted internal routing exceptions, such as those used for slash redirects. The change modifies the Flask class to exclude these internal errors from user-defined handlers, restoring expected behavior.

This change modifies the `RequestContext.push` method in `flask/ctx.py` to prevent opening a new session if the request context is already active. This ensures that `stream_with_context` generators access the same session as the containing view, rather than creating a separate one.

The documentation for upgrading Flask now instructs users to use the pip command with the --upgrade flag instead of the deprecated easy_install command. This change updates the installation guide in the upgrading.rst file to reflect modern Python package management practices.

This commit updates documentation files to use consistent RST formatting for code terms like "with", "for", and "self". It also corrects file references in the patterns guide. The changes affect the Flask application module and various documentation pages.

This commit moves the `_default_template_ctx_processor` function from the `flask.ctx` module to `flask.templating`. It updates the imports in `flask.app` to reflect this new location, ensuring the template context processor remains accessible for injecting request data.

This commit removes previously deprecated code from the Flask application, including the `FLASK_ENV` variable, legacy JSON configuration keys, and various `Flask` and `Blueprint` properties. Users relying on these removed features will encounter errors, as the `Flask` class and related modules no longer support them.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.0.1. It updates the project version in pyproject.toml to a development release and adds a new entry to the CHANGES.rst file to track upcoming changes.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask Blueprint class where registering a partial function as a view would fail because it lacks a name attribute. The add_url_rule method now checks for the presence of a name before processing the view function.

This commit updates the Flask class to support a default error handler for all HTTP exceptions. If a specific handler is not found, the system now checks for a generic handler registered for the base HTTPException class.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to include a cross-reference for users who only want to log errors and stack traces. It directs readers to the application-errors section within the Debug Mode area.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the extension development guidelines. It removes the redundant word "furthermore" from the documentation requirements in the extensiondev.rst file.

This commit simplifies Flask's logging configuration by removing the `LOGGER_NAME` and `LOGGER_HANDLER_POLICY` settings. The `Flask` application now always uses a logger named `flask.app`, sets the log level only on first access, and adds a handler only if none are already configured.
Adds a documentation label to the templating page in the docs module. This allows other parts of the documentation to link directly to the templates section.

This commit updates the `script_info_option` function in `flask/cli.py` to use the modern Click callback signature. It ensures the callback correctly accepts the `param` argument, preventing potential errors when the CLI option is processed.
This commit adds a new test project to the repository, including a Flask application and a template file. It provides a basic setup with modules and routes for testing purposes.
This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It corrects a duplicated word in the description of how key errors from request data are handled.

This commit updates the project's automated dependency and workflow configurations. It adjusts the Dependabot settings to target the 2.0.x branch and adds a new schedule for GitHub Actions updates. Additionally, it upgrades the lock-threads action to version 3 in the repository's lock workflow.

This commit updates the `_FakeSignal` class in `flask/signals.py` to better mimic the blinker API. It ensures that the `temporarily_connected_to` and `connected_to` attributes are both set to a failure handler when the real blinker library is unavailable.

This commit updates development dependencies and CI tooling to their latest versions. It bumps the PyPI publish action in the GitHub workflow and refreshes pinned versions in the requirements files and pre-commit configuration.

This commit updates the documentation link for the Quart project to reflect its move from GitLab to GitHub. The change ensures users are directed to the correct repository when referencing Quart in the async-await documentation.

This commit ensures that a "Vary: Cookie" header is added to HTTP responses whenever a session is accessed. This change allows caching proxies to correctly distinguish between different users' sessions, preventing them from serving cached content to the wrong person. The update primarily affects the `SecureCookieSession` and `SessionMixin` classes in `flask/sessions.py`.

This commit fixes LaTeX errors that occurred when generating the documentation PDF. It updates the flaskstyle module to replace an unsupported Unicode character with a non-breaking space and corrects a conditional check for PDF output.

This commit replaces the custom documentation theme with the standard pallets-sphinx-themes package. It removes the local theme submodule and updates the Sphinx configuration in docs/conf.py to use the new theme.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the Config class in flask/config.py. It clarifies the description of the silent parameter in the from_envvar and from_pyfile methods to accurately reflect the intended behavior.

This commit corrects a broken hyperlink in the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation file. It updates the URL for the "committing as you go" section to point to the correct domain, ensuring users can successfully access the referenced Git tutorial.

This commit updates the test suite for Flask's extended flashing functionality to ensure the test client explicitly checks response status codes. It also corrects the route definitions in the BasicFunctionalityTestCase to include trailing slashes, preventing silent failures during testing.

This commit optimizes URL generation by caching the blueprint path calculation. It replaces a manual loop in Flask's inject_url_defaults method with a call to the new _split_blueprint_path helper, improving performance when resolving URL defaults.

This documentation update fixes a startup error in the Celery tutorial where using the variable name `app` for the Flask instance caused a conflict with Celery's internal options. By renaming the variable to `flask_app` in the `celery.rst` guide, the worker now starts successfully without raising an attribute error.
This commit fixes a documentation typo in the Flask application class. It corrects the method name referenced in the `preprocess_request` docstring to accurately point to `url_value_preprocessor`.

This commit adds the `docs/_themes` directory as a tracked submodule. It ensures the documentation theme files are included in the repository, allowing the build system to access the custom styling assets.
This commit fixes a spelling error in the security documentation. It corrects the word "rememdy" to "remedy" within the description of cross-site scripting in the `docs/security.rst` file.

The Flask application and module classes now accept a package name during initialization. This change enables the framework to correctly locate and load resources from the directory where the module is defined.

This commit updates the WTForms documentation to replace deprecated validator references. It changes examples in the patterns guide to use the modern validator instead of the legacy one, ensuring users do not adopt code that will be removed in future versions.

This commit updates the test configuration in pyproject.toml to suppress a specific deprecation warning triggered by changes in Python 3.12 alpha. It prevents pytest from treating this internal warning as an error, ensuring test runs remain stable during the transition to the new Python version.

This commit cleans up the Flask module and its tests by fixing typos in docstrings and removing an unused import. It also adjusts line lengths to meet the 79-column limit, improving code readability without changing application behavior.
This commit prevents the Travis CI build from running on the website branch. It modifies the .travis.yml configuration to exclude that specific branch from the automated testing process.

This commit corrects minor spelling errors and formatting inconsistencies across various Flask documentation files. It improves the clarity of the user guide by fixing typos in sections covering configuration, deployment, and development patterns.

The documentation for the SQLAlchemy pattern in Flask now recommends using the `teardown_appcontext` hook instead of `teardown_request`. This change ensures database sessions are properly closed when the application context shuts down, not just at the end of a request.

This commit introduces a new ConfigAttribute class to the Flask module, enabling application attributes to automatically forward to the configuration dictionary. It also begins defining the debug flag on the Flask class to control debugging behavior.

In debug mode, Flask now raises a specific error when a POST request triggers a routing redirect, preventing silent data loss. This change modifies the Flask class to detect and report these problematic redirects, improving visibility into routing issues during development.
This commit fixes a typo in the Flask configuration documentation. It corrects a minor wording error in the description of the testing mode setting within the config module.

This commit allows developers to specify a custom endpoint name when using the route decorators on Flask applications and blueprints. Previously, the endpoint was automatically derived from the function name, but now it can be explicitly set via the endpoint option.
This commit adds a missing changelog entry to the CHANGES file. It documents the addition of support for configurations, ensuring the release notes accurately reflect the new feature.
This commit updates the formatting of the project's changelog file. It removes an empty line from the version 1.0 section to improve the document's structure.

The `jsonify` function in `flask/helpers.py` now serves JSONP responses with the `application/javascript` MIME type instead of `text/javascript`. This change aligns the response header with modern web standards for JavaScript content.
This commit fixes a typo in the installation documentation, changing the word "tricker" to "trickier" to improve clarity. The change is located in the `docs/installation.rst` file.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the Flaskr tutorial documentation. It changes the word "chose" to "choose" in the introduction section to improve clarity for users reading the guide.

This commit updates the changelog entry for the importlib.resources module. It clarifies that the command-line interface now uses importlib.metadata to load command entry points, replacing the previous undocumented dependency on setuptools.

This commit corrects two typos in the documentation strings within the Flask module. It fixes a misspelling in the Module class and updates a reference in the Flask class to point to the correct Request class.

Flask now supports asynchronous view functions, error handlers, and request lifecycle hooks. This feature is implemented in the Flask class and Scaffold module using the asgiref library to bridge async and sync contexts.

This commit updates comments in the Flask views module to improve grammar and consistency. It corrects capitalization and punctuation in the View, MethodView, and MethodViewType classes without changing any functional behavior.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.1.2. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a placeholder entry to the changelog for the upcoming release.

This commit introduces a pluggable JSON provider interface, allowing developers to replace the default JSON handling with a custom implementation. It deprecates the previous configuration options and custom encoder/decoder classes in favor of the new `JSONProvider` class.

This commit reorganizes the documentation by moving debugger details into a new "Debugging Application Errors" section within the error handling guide. It also updates the main title to "Logging Application Errors" to better reflect the content focus.

This commit refactors Flask's `make_response` method to improve clarity and error handling. It now raises `TypeError` instead of `ValueError` for invalid response types and provides more descriptive error messages. The changes also allow bytes for status values and Headers objects for headers.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the SQLAlchemy documentation examples. It updates the `users.insert` call to use the correct method signature, ensuring the code snippets in the `sqlalchemy.rst` file are valid and executable.

This commit updates the Flask application to use its own `url_for` method as a template global, avoiding an extra call through the helpers module. It also updates the changelog to document the relocation of `url_for` and `redirect` methods to the `Flask` class.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the Flask application class. It explicitly states that the return values from teardown_appcontext and teardown_request functions are ignored, preventing user confusion about their usage.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.0.0. It updates the version string in the `flask` module and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST configuration option. It updates the description in the config.rst file to properly state that sessions are refreshed, improving the clarity of the user-facing documentation.
This commit corrects the documentation for Flask's internal configuration values. It updates the rendering of the `None` value in the config reference to use proper double-backtick formatting.

This commit updates exception handling across several Flask modules to use explicit exception chaining, resolving a linting warning. It modifies functions in the app, CLI, and scaffold modules to properly link new exceptions to their causes.

This commit improves the type hints for the `errorhandler` decorator in Flask's `Scaffold` class. It ensures that type checkers correctly infer the exception type and return value for error handlers registered on applications and blueprints.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify that returning a 404 status code is required when rendering a custom error page. It explains that Flask defaults to a 200 status code, which incorrectly indicates success, and shows how to explicitly set the 404 status.

This commit updates the Flask class to pass the current AppContext explicitly to request dispatch methods, replacing the previous use of proxy objects. It introduces a deprecation warning for subclasses that override these methods with the old signature, ensuring backward compatibility during the transition.
Updates the GitHub Actions checkout dependency to version 3.5.0 in the publish and test workflows. This ensures the repository uses the latest minor release for checking out code during CI runs.

This commit updates the Flask example applications to use explicit string names instead of deriving them from module names. It modifies the app creation in the flaskr, minitwit, and largerapp examples to ensure consistent application identification.

This commit updates the contribution guidelines to instruct developers to include issue-closing keywords in their commit messages. It clarifies how to automatically close related issues when a pull request is merged.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask class explaining that in debug mode, request teardown is delayed after an exception to allow the interactive debugger to access the context. It notes that this behavior is controlled by the PRESERVE_CONTEXT_ON_EXCEPTION configuration variable.

This commit updates the changelog to remove a trailing space from the entry regarding the removal of deprecated code. It corrects a minor formatting inconsistency in the release notes for the 2022-08-01 version.

This commit ensures the `py` library is explicitly installed during test setup for the Flask extension tests. It resolves issues where extensions relying on `py.test` failed due to the default version being on an incorrect Python path.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `url_for` helper where forcing a specific URL scheme would permanently alter the application's state. It ensures the original scheme is restored after building the URL, preventing subsequent requests from using the wrong protocol.

Removes the deprecated `modules` property from the `Flask` class. This eliminates the deprecation warning previously shown when accessing this attribute, as it has been replaced by the `blueprints` property.

Flask's JSONEncoder now supports serializing dataclass objects, allowing them to be converted to JSON without manual conversion. This change updates the default method in the flask/json module to handle dataclasses, improving compatibility for users working with modern Python data structures.

The `get_version` function in `flask/cli.py` now reports the full Python version string instead of truncating it to the first three characters. This ensures the CLI version output displays the complete version details, including minor and micro releases.

This commit updates the README.md file to fix Markdown link syntax by removing unnecessary empty brackets from several references. It also removes two extra blank lines to improve the document's formatting consistency.
This commit updates the changelog to document a deprecation in version 1.0. It notes that the `request.json` attribute is now deprecated in favor of using the `request.get_json()` method.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the flashing pattern documentation. It corrects the introductory sentence for the code example in the `docs/patterns/flashing.rst` file.

This documentation update adds a note to the mod_wsgi deployment guide regarding access control configuration changes in Apache 2.4. It alerts users to potential differences in how permissions are handled compared to earlier versions.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to include instructions for sharing a local server using Localtunnel. It also adds clearer links to the tutorial setup section to improve navigation for new users.

The project now uses flit as its build backend instead of setuptools. This change updates the development environment setup and documentation to reflect the new packaging tool, removing unnecessary dependencies from the installation process.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the testing guide where a code example failed to run due to a missing import. It adds the necessary Flask module import to the example in the `docs/testing.rst` file.

This commit corrects a minor typo in a comment within the `MethodViewType` class in `flask/views.py`. It changes "baseclass" to "base class" in the `__new__` method, improving documentation clarity without altering any code behavior.

This commit adds a `--version` command-line option to the Flask CLI, allowing users to display the current Flask and Python versions. The change modifies the `FlaskGroup` class in `flask/cli.py` to include this new flag.

This commit fixes an issue where session cookies failed to work correctly in Chrome when using localhost. The `get_cookie_domain` method in the `SessionInterface` class now returns `None` instead of `.localhost` to ensure compatibility with the browser's cookie handling.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the error handling documentation. It changes the word "interchangable" to "interchangeable" in the file docs/errorhandling.rst.

This commit fixes broken cross-references in the testing documentation by correcting the module paths for Werkzeug classes. It updates the links for the test client and response data attribute to point to their correct locations within the Werkzeug library.

This commit updates the test environment configuration to run Flask tests against the latest master branch of Werkzeug instead of a specific sprint branch. The change modifies the dependency source in the tox configuration file to ensure compatibility with the most recent Werkzeug development version.

This commit corrects the docstring for the Flask class and its errorhandler method. It updates the example code to show that the page_not_found handler function now correctly accepts an error argument, reflecting the actual API behavior.

This commit resolves resource warnings in the Flask test suite by ensuring response objects are properly closed. It adds garbage collection to the deprecation warning fixture and explicitly closes responses in static path and sendfile tests.

This commit updates the documentation for the `send_from_directory` function in `flask.helpers`. It clarifies that the `directory` parameter must not be derived from client input to prevent security vulnerabilities.

This commit updates the deployment documentation to include OpenShift as a free hosting option for Flask applications. It adds a link to the relevant OpenShift guide in the hosted options section of the deploying index.

This commit updates the API documentation to note that the `provide_automatic_options` functionality was introduced in version 0.8. It clarifies the release history for users checking when this feature became available.

This commit modernizes exception handling syntax across the Flask codebase by replacing the deprecated comma syntax with the "as" keyword. It updates modules including app.py, config.py, and various test files to ensure compatibility with Python 3.
