This commit updates the project changelog to document the introduction of generic pluggable views. It records the addition of class-based views as a new feature in the release notes.

This commit updates the `ErrorHandlerCallable` type in `src/flask/typing.py` to correctly reflect that error handlers can be asynchronous. It allows the type to accept both synchronous and awaitable callables, matching the runtime behavior where invocations are wrapped in `ensure_sync`.
This commit corrects the Python version definitions in the Travis CI configuration file. It ensures that version numbers are properly quoted to prevent parsing errors during the build process.

This commit corrects the project changelog by moving a bugfix entry from the unreleased major release section to the unreleased bugfix release section. The entry describes a fix in the context management module that ensures `ctx.auto_pop` receives the exception object when a `BaseException` occurs.

This commit documents the new `category_filter` argument for the `get_flashed_messages` function in Flask. It allows developers to render flashed message categories in separate blocks, improving template flexibility. The changes update the changelog and expand the function's documentation.

This commit corrects minor spelling and formatting errors in the Flask documentation and source code. It updates the Flask class and related documentation files to fix typos like "unittesting" and "errorhandlers."

This commit updates the AUTHORS file to add Keyan Pishdadian to the list of contributors. It also reorganizes the entries to maintain alphabetical order, moving Edmond Burnett to the correct position.

This commit updates the pinned versions of development, documentation, and testing dependencies in the requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest compatible releases of libraries such as cryptography, mypy, and jinja2.

This commit removes the deprecated Module class and related functionality from the Flask application. Users can no longer register modules using the Flask.register_module method, as this feature has been replaced by Blueprints.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to explain the benefits of using URL building over hardcoding links. It highlights that this approach simplifies maintenance, handles character escaping, and correctly manages applications hosted in subdirectories.

This commit removes the Jinja2 autoescape and with extensions from the default configuration in the Flask class. Users will no longer have these specific template features enabled by default, requiring manual setup if needed.

This commit refactors the Flask CLI script system to support custom application creation logic. It renames the `load_callback` parameter to `create_app` within the `ScriptInfo` class, allowing special applications to define how their app instance is generated.

This commit improves type checking for view functions in Flask's routing system. It updates the `Scaffold` class and its subclasses to use specific `ViewCallable` types, ensuring that route decorators and view functions are correctly validated by static type checkers.

This commit enables Flask signal receivers to be asynchronous functions. It updates the Flask class and related context modules to pass an async wrapper when sending signals, allowing subscribers to handle events without blocking the main thread.

This commit improves the grammar and consistency of the flashing pattern documentation. It updates the text in docs/patterns/flashing.rst to clearly describe how the index and login templates inherit from the layout template.

This commit removes Python 2.5 from the continuous integration test matrix. It updates the Travis CI configuration to stop running tests on this deprecated version, ensuring the build only targets supported Python releases.

This commit corrects the documentation for the distribute module by removing the obsolete -R option from the egg_info configuration examples. It also fixes a formatting error in the "Tagging Builds" section to ensure the setup.cfg example renders correctly.

This commit updates tests and documentation to reflect that redirect responses now use relative URLs in the Location header by default, omitting the scheme and domain. It modifies the Response class in the wrappers module and adjusts assertions in tutorial and regression tests to expect paths like "/auth/login" instead of full URLs.

This commit adds test cases to the Flask test suite to verify the behavior of template filter registration methods. It covers both the `add_app_template_filter` method and the `app_template_filter` decorator within the `Blueprint` class. These tests ensure filters are correctly added to the application's Jinja environment.

This commit updates the package metadata in setup.py to explicitly declare support for Python versions 2.5, 2.6, and 2.7. This ensures that the project's compatibility is correctly displayed on package indexes and to users checking supported environments.
This commit adds a new documentation page describing how to integrate the MongoKit library with Flask applications. It also corrects a typo in the existing SQLAlchemy pattern documentation.

This commit corrects the documentation URL in the JavaScript example's pyproject.toml file. It updates the link to point to the correct Flask patterns page for JavaScript instead of the incorrect jQuery page.
This commit corrects a typo in the API documentation where "JSOn" was misspelled. It ensures the description of the JSON encoder delegation in the `docs/api.rst` file is accurate and professional.

This commit updates development dependencies and configuration files, including GitHub Actions workflows and pre-commit settings. It also modifies the `CertParamType` and `DefaultJSONProvider` classes within the Flask source code.

This commit clarifies the docstring for the `Flask.preprocess_request` method in `flask/app.py`. It explicitly documents that the method invokes two distinct sets of hook functions and explains how they are filtered before execution.

This commit updates documentation and code comments to use double backticks for Python literals like True, False, and None. It ensures consistent formatting across the Flask API, configuration, and tutorial guides.

This commit updates the project's CI pipelines to test against Python 3.8 instead of Python 3.7. It modifies the Azure Pipelines configuration, Tox settings, and contribution documentation to reflect this version change.

This commit updates the test suite to use identity checks instead of equality checks for type comparisons, resolving linting warnings. The changes affect the test_session_special_types and test_teardown_request_handler_error functions in the test_basic.py module.
This commit updates the changelog to document version 0.5.2, a bugfix release from July 2010. It notes a fix for an issue with loading templates from directories when modules were used.

This commit adds a new `from_file` method to the `Config` class in Flask, allowing developers to load application settings from text files like TOML or JSON. It also updates the documentation to describe this new configuration option.

This commit updates the Flaskr example to use the sqlite3.Row factory instead of manually converting database rows to dictionaries. This change simplifies the code in the get_db and show_entries functions by allowing direct access to column names. The documentation is also updated to reflect this preferred querying pattern.

This commit updates the Flask application to correctly pass the subdomain argument when binding the URL map to the environment. It clarifies that subdomain matching remains disabled by default and requires explicit configuration, while updating documentation and tests to reflect this behavior.

In the `Request` class, the `on_json_loading_failed` method now checks the application's debug setting before raising an error. This prevents detailed exception messages from being exposed to users in production environments, ensuring only a generic bad request response is sent when debugging is disabled.

This commit updates the Flask application factory documentation to soften the tone of a specific warning. It changes the phrasing in the `appfactories` module to be less direct when advising against a particular implementation pattern.

This commit removes the use of LocalStack for managing application and request contexts in Flask. It replaces the old stack-based approach with context variables, affecting core modules like `app.py`, `ctx.py`, and `helpers.py`. This change simplifies context handling and improves compatibility with modern Python concurrency models.

This commit clarifies that `Config.from_object` uses the provided object directly without instantiating it. It documents that users must manually instantiate configuration classes to access properties, preventing confusion about how the method handles class objects versus instances.

This commit adds a test fixture file to support the zipimporter instance path test in the Flask test suite. It ensures the test environment includes the necessary egg file for accurate import behavior verification.

This commit fixes a missing comma in the documentation for the templating module. It corrects the sentence describing how context processors inject variables into a template, ensuring the text is grammatically correct.

This commit updates the docstring for the `make_response` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies that the function can force a view function's return value into a response object, which is useful for modifying headers within view decorators.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the Flask API documentation. It corrects the phrasing in the `docs/api.rst` file to properly introduce the parameters for the `Flask.route` method.

This commit corrects a typo in the CLI documentation by fixing the filename reference from "comamnds.py" to "commands.py". It ensures the example setup instructions accurately reflect the correct module name for users.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to reflect that Python 3 is now a recommended choice for new projects. It removes outdated warnings about a small ecosystem and limited user base, acknowledging that most libraries now support Python 3.

Flask now supports generating non-ASCII encoded JSON to reduce network transmission size. This feature is controlled by the new `JSON_AS_ASCII` configuration option, which remains enabled by default to maintain backward compatibility. The changes primarily affect the `flask.json` module and the `Flask` application class.

This commit updates the Flask project's visual branding by replacing the existing logo files with a new design. It modifies the artwork directory and documentation static assets to reflect the updated imagery.

This commit updates the development dependencies for the project's CI/CD workflows. It bumps the `setup-uv` action to version 8.0.0 and the `actions/cache` action to version 5.0.4 across multiple workflow files.

This commit removes the `_blueprint_order` list from the Flask class, as Python dictionaries now maintain insertion order natively. It updates the `register_blueprint` and `iter_blueprints` methods to rely on the standard dictionary structure instead of a separate tracking list.

This commit adds documentation to the security guide regarding SSL/HTTPS implementation and security headers. It lists recommended Flask packages for enforcing HTTPS and managing Content Security Policy to enhance application security.

This commit removes the automatic mimetype guessing feature from the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py`. Users must now explicitly provide the mimetype when sending files, as the previous behavior is no longer supported.

The `flash` function in `flask/helpers.py` no longer assumes that modifying a list retrieved from the session automatically updates the session object. This fixes an issue where messages were not persisted when using session backends with external storage.

This commit fixes the `MethodView` class in `flask/views.py` to work correctly on Python 3. It replaces the deprecated `__metaclass__` attribute with the `with_metaclass` helper, ensuring the view's metaclass is applied properly across different Python versions.
This commit fixes the tutorial documentation by correcting the order of the `dbcon` entry in the index. Users will now see the tutorial steps presented in the intended sequence.

This commit fixes a bug where exceptions during teardown could leave application contexts lingering in the stack. It modifies the pop methods in flask/ctx.py to ensure the context is always removed from the stack, even if an error occurs during the teardown process.

This commit improves the error message when registering a custom exception handler in Flask that is not a subclass of Exception. The assertion in the Flask class now explicitly states that custom exceptions must be subclasses of Exception, making the failure reason clearer to developers.

The migration script now parses Python source code using the RedBaron AST library instead of manual parsing. This change improves the reliability of the import transformation logic in the `flaskext_migrate` module, though some import formats remain unimplemented.

This commit updates the greenlet dependency from version 0.4.16 to 0.4.17 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the greenlet library for its testing environment.

Flask now logs by default even when debug mode is disabled, ensuring error messages are visible in production environments. This change modifies the `create_logger` function in `flask/logging.py` and introduces a new `LOGGER_HANDLER_POLICY` configuration option to control logging behavior.

The file uploads documentation no longer specifically recommends the Flask-Uploads extension. Instead, it now refers generally to available Flask extensions for handling file uploads. This change removes a direct link to a specific third-party package.

This commit adds PyPy to the list of Python environments tested by the project's tox configuration. Users running the test suite will now see PyPy included alongside standard CPython versions. The change modifies the `tox.ini` file.

This commit updates Flask to use importlib instead of the deprecated pkgutil module, ensuring compatibility with Python 3.12. It modifies the get_root_path and _find_package_path functions to retrieve module loaders via importlib.util.find_spec.

The `routes_command` in Flask's CLI now displays the subdomain or host for each route when domain matching is enabled. This change allows users to see which specific domain a route is bound to in the command-line output.

The `load_dotenv` function in `flask.cli` no longer changes the current working directory to the location of the `.env` or `.flaskenv` file. This prevents the application's working directory from unexpectedly shifting, which could interfere with relative file paths or package imports.

This commit introduces a new implementation for preserving request context during debugging and testing in Flask. It ensures that context variables like `request` and `g` remain accessible in the interactive debugger and that teardown functions execute reliably. The changes primarily affect the `Flask` app, `RequestContext`, and `FlaskClient` classes.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in a comment within the `flash` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies the documentation regarding session synchronization without altering any code behavior.

This commit replaces the previous AppVeyor and Travis CI configurations with a new Azure Pipelines setup for the 1.0.x branch. It updates the project's continuous integration workflow to run tests on Ubuntu using Python 3.7, affecting the overall build and deployment process.

This commit fixes a broken relative import in the `DispatchingJinjaLoader` class within `flask/templating.py`. Previously, the import for `explain_template_loading_attempts` failed because it did not use the correct relative path syntax. This change ensures the debug helper loads correctly when template loading attempts are explained.

This commit enables intersphinx in the documentation configuration, allowing cross-references to external projects like Python and Werkzeug. Previously, these mappings were commented out, preventing the documentation from linking to external API references. The change updates the `intersphinx_mapping` in `docs/conf.py`.
This commit adds the project's license file, establishing the terms for redistribution and use. It clarifies the legal permissions and restrictions for the software.

This commit corrects documentation errors in the API reference and pattern guides. It adds a missing entry for the `current_app` object and fixes a broken cross-reference link in the distribute pattern.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the docstring for the `has_request_context` function in `flask/ctx.py`. It removes an extra "if" clause to clarify the example sentence, improving the readability of the documentation without changing any code behavior.

This commit corrects the Azure Pipelines configuration to properly mark a job as an allowed failure. It replaces a manual exit code override with the standard `--ignore-outcome` flag for the `tox` command, ensuring the build does not fail if the test suite encounters errors.

This commit adds a `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` configuration variable to the `Flask` class, allowing developers to explicitly control whether exceptions are propagated. Previously, this behavior was automatically tied to the `DEBUG` or `TESTING` settings, but now it can be independently enabled or disabled.

This commit corrects several spelling errors in the Flask documentation, including "debugger," "libraries," and "recommended." These changes improve the readability of the user guide without altering any application behavior or code logic.

Flask now uses Werkzeug's JSONMixin class for request and response JSON handling, replacing its internal implementation. This change requires Werkzeug version 0.15 or higher and drops support for Python 3.4.

This commit updates the documentation for the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It adds a note reminding developers to ensure the file pointer is positioned at the start of the data before calling the function.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the quickstart guide where the file upload example used an undefined variable name. It corrects the reference to use the proper variable, ensuring the code snippet accurately reflects the expected behavior for saving uploaded files.

This commit improves the user experience by displaying a helpful message when registering an error handler for an unrecognized HTTP status code. It also clarifies the documentation for error handling in the Flask application. The changes primarily affect the Flask class and its error handler registration methods.

This commit updates the documentation for the WSGI standalone deployment guide. It replaces outdated links to the greenlet library with current, working URLs to ensure users can access the correct resources.

This commit corrects a broken hyperlink and improves the wording in the ASGI deployment documentation. It ensures the reference to the WsgiToAsgi adapter renders correctly and clarifies the description of serving the application.

This commit updates the setup script to dynamically read the package version from the main module instead of using a hardcoded string. This prevents version information from being duplicated and ensures the installed package version always matches the source code.

This commit adds a new example application demonstrating how to use Flask Blueprints. It shows how to register a blueprint multiple times with different URL prefixes, allowing the same routes to be accessible at different paths. The example includes a simple page blueprint with basic routes and templates.

This commit deprecates the `total_seconds` helper function in Flask's `helpers` module, advising users to use the standard `timedelta.total_seconds` method instead. It updates the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` in `sessions.py` to stop importing the deprecated function, ensuring internal code no longer relies on it.

This commit fixes a failing test in the Flask test suite related to import hook error handling. It updates the `ExtImportHookTestCase` to correctly skip an additional stack frame introduced by the `reraise` function, ensuring the test accurately validates error propagation.

This documentation update clarifies that HTTP POST requests must only be used for non-idempotent actions, correcting a previous statement that suggested they might be. The change also adds context explaining that this behavior aligns with how HTML forms typically transmit data to servers.

This commit updates the project's branding by replacing the horizontal logo with a name-only variant in the README. It also removes the old horizontal SVG file and adds new icon and logo assets to the documentation static directory.

This commit adds the missing documentation file for file uploads to the project's patterns directory. It provides a guide on handling file uploads, covering form configuration and saving files to the filesystem.
This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the dist folder from version control. This prevents build artifacts from being accidentally committed to the repository.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now sets the response date header to the file's modification time when available. This ensures the server emits the correct date for conditional requests, rather than relying on the current time.

This commit restricts the Werkzeug dependency to versions below 1.0 in the project's setup configuration. This change ensures compatibility with the 0.12 release by preventing the installation of potentially incompatible newer Werkzeug versions.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask views guide explaining how to apply decorators to class-based views. It clarifies that users must decorate the result of `View.as_view` or use the `decorators` class attribute, as decorating the class itself is ineffective.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions for black and isort to ensure consistent code formatting and import sorting.

The Flask 0.7 upgrade script now avoids unnecessarily modifying `url_for` calls that do not require endpoint prefix changes. This prevents incorrect rewrites in Python files and templates, ensuring only relevant endpoints are updated during the migration.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to replace references to the deprecated Module class with the Blueprint class. It adds docstrings for the Blueprint and BlueprintSetupState classes and updates the API reference to reflect these changes.

This commit updates the type ignore comment in the `stream_with_context` function within `flask.helpers` to satisfy mypy. It addresses a static type checking error by explicitly ignoring both argument type and return value mismatches.
This commit fixes the indentation of a numbered list in the application context documentation. It ensures the list items are properly formatted for correct rendering in the Sphinx documentation.

This commit removes the internal `_missing` sentinel from the `JSONMixin` class in `flask/wrappers.py`. It also updates the documentation for the `is_json` property and `get_json` method to clarify their behavior and add version notes.
This commit updates the project's README to include a direct link to the license file. It improves documentation clarity by making the licensing terms easily accessible to users.

This commit renames the global test fixture `setup_path` to `test_apps` in the test configuration. It updates various test functions in the blueprint, extension, and templating modules to explicitly request this fixture, ensuring proper test isolation.

This commit ensures the `Vary: Cookie` header is consistently added to responses whenever a session is accessed, modified, or refreshed. It fixes potential caching issues by moving the header logic within the `SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session` method to cover all relevant session states.

This commit corrects the command-line syntax examples in the Waitress deployment documentation. It ensures the `--host` flag is placed before the application reference to match the correct argument order for the `waitress-serve` command.

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify that the application listens on an application root rather than an IRI. It also corrects the example user request to display a percent-encoded URI instead of a raw Unicode character.

This commit ensures the `Vary: Cookie` header is consistently added to responses whenever a session is accessed or modified. It fixes inconsistent caching behavior by moving the header logic within the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` class in `src/flask/sessions.py`.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the Flask quickstart documentation. It changes the phrase "looks something like that" to "looks something like this" in the `docs/quickstart.rst` file.

This commit fixes an issue where error handlers could not access key information from `BadRequestKeyError` in non-debug mode. The `Flask.handle_user_exception` method in `flask/app.py` is updated to preserve the exception arguments, ensuring the data remains available for custom error handling.

This commit updates the Flask package version from 0.7 to 0.7-dev in both the main module and setup configuration. It marks the codebase as a development build, preventing users from installing it as a stable release.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.3.0 by updating the version string in the `flask` module from a development build to the stable release. It also updates the changelog to mark the version as released on April 25, 2023.

This commit updates the Flask application to use a new helper function, `_select_autoescape`, which enables template autoescaping only for HTML and XML file types. It also exposes the `json` module in the main package namespace and adds tests for JSON handling.

This commit updates the `setupmethod` function in `flask.scaffold` to use a TypeVar, ensuring that the original function's signature is preserved for type checkers. It also adds a type cast to the `update_wrapper` call to handle signature mismatches between the wrapper and the original function.

This documentation update corrects the Mongokit pattern example to demonstrate the standard Flask method for configuring the database hostname and port. It replaces the previous generic module example with a Flask application setup that uses configuration objects to pass connection details.

This commit updates the documentation for the FLASK_ENV environment variable to clarify that Flask and extensions may enable behaviors based on the environment, rather than automatically enabling debug mode. It removes outdated references to automatic debug activation in the CLI, configuration, and quickstart guides.

This commit updates the error message in the `FormDataRoutingRedirect` class within `flask/debughelpers.py`. It clarifies that POST requests with form data cannot be redirected reliably or without user interaction, providing a more accurate explanation to developers.

This commit removes outdated documentation recommending the deprecated `flask.ext` namespace for importing extensions. It updates the extension development guide to stop suggesting this legacy import method, which is no longer the standard practice.

This commit modernizes the project's development environment and configuration files, including updating pre-commit hooks, upgrading pip, and simplifying the CI matrix. It also adjusts documentation settings to use Sphinx extlinks and renames the security documentation page to avoid conflicts.

This commit updates the Black code formatter from version 22.6.0 to 22.8.0 within the pre-commit configuration. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the tool for automated code style checks.

This commit fixes a reStructuredText syntax error in the API documentation. It corrects the formatting of the "stack" directive in the "Useful Internals" section of docs/api.rst to ensure the documentation renders correctly.

This commit updates the extension development documentation to encourage new contributors to discuss their project ideas on the mailing list. It advises developers to seek community input to avoid duplicate work and improve API design. The changes are located in the extensiondev documentation file.
This commit corrects a broken cross-reference in the Flask documentation. It updates the link in the patterns index to point to the deferred callbacks page instead of the cookies page.

The `_render` function in `flask/templating.py` now correctly handles multiple template overrides. If more than one override is provided, it raises a runtime error instead of silently ignoring the extras.

This commit updates the test environment configuration to include the itsdangerous library, which supports Python 3.x. The change modifies the tox.ini file to ensure the testing suite runs with the correct dependencies.

This commit ensures that garbage collection is always performed before running leak tests, removing a previous condition that skipped it when the system lacked a reference count function. The change modifies the `assert_no_leak` context manager in the regression test module to consistently call `gc.collect`.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask class where the CLI group was incorrectly initialized with the application object instead of its name. It also adds comprehensive CLI tests to verify the correct behavior of the command-line interface.

This commit adds a test case to verify that Flask subclasses can suppress exception logging by overriding the log_exception method. It ensures that custom Flask applications can control how errors are reported without affecting core functionality.

This commit updates the testing documentation to clarify that the fixture handles closing and removing the database file after tests. It also adds blank lines to improve the formatting of the code examples in the testing guide.

This documentation update adds the X-Forwarded-Proto header to the proxy configuration example in the WSGI standalone guide. This ensures Flask correctly detects HTTPS connections, preventing broken external links and issues with extensions like Flask-OAuthlib.

This commit relaxes the type annotations for error handler functions in Flask's Scaffold, Blueprint, and Flask classes. It allows users to define more precise types and decorate the same function multiple times without type conflicts.

This commit fixes the `test_request_context` method in the Flask class to correctly handle the `SERVER_NAME` configuration. It ensures that the test environment includes proper host and port details, preventing errors when the server name is defined without an explicit port.

This commit updates the installation documentation to clarify that Python 3 users do not need to install virtualenv, as Python 3 includes built-in virtual environment support. It also corrects a typo in the example directory name from "venv" to "virtenv" and adds a section header for creating virtual environments.

This commit reverts a previous change to the Flask class, specifically within the handle_http_exception method. It corrects the documentation string to properly refer to "an HTTP exception" instead of "a HTTP exception."

This commit removes the dependency on the development version of Werkzeug from the test configuration. It ensures the test suite uses the latest stable release, which now supports Python 3.3, simplifying the setup in the tox.ini file.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the "Lifecycle of the Context" heading within the application context documentation. It also fixes inconsistent cross-reference markup for the current app, request, session, and global data objects in the design documentation.

This commit restores the public API by re-exporting the Request and Response classes from the flask package. It ensures users can access these objects directly from the top-level module, maintaining backward compatibility after the internal refactoring.

This commit updates the Flasky documentation theme to use a softer, less flashy background color for highlighted sections. It modifies the CSS styling for target definitions and highlight divs to improve visual readability.

This commit fixes how Flask determines the instance path for namespace packages, ensuring it selects the directory closest to the imported submodule. The change modifies the `_find_package_path` function in `src/flask/scaffold.py` to correctly handle these package structures.
Flask's JSON encoder now supports decimal.Decimal objects by converting them to strings. This change prevents serialization errors when using jsonify or dumps with decimal values.

This commit updates the project's test suite to use PyPy 3.10 instead of PyPy 3.9. It modifies the GitHub Actions workflow and the tox configuration to reflect this version change, ensuring tests run against the newer interpreter.

This commit introduces a new Module class to support pluggable applications within the Flask framework. It allows developers to define routes and URL rules that are registered with the main application instance, improving code organization for larger projects.

This commit fixes a security vulnerability in Flask's module system that allowed users to access files outside the static directory by using absolute paths. The `send_static_file` method in the `_PackageBoundObject` class now rejects filenames starting with a forward slash, preventing unauthorized file access.
This commit adds a new `query` route decorator to the `Scaffold` class in Flask. It allows developers to easily define routes for the HTTP QUERY method without manually specifying the method list.

This commit marks top-level names in the Flask package as explicitly exported. This change helps type checkers correctly understand imports in user projects, resolving potential static analysis errors.

This commit removes the examples directory from the test exclusion list in setup.cfg. This change allows the test runner to include the examples folder in its search scope, potentially altering which files are processed during test execution.

This commit updates the minimum required version of the Werkzeug dependency in the project's setup configuration. It ensures the application uses at least version 2.2.0a1, potentially enabling newer features or fixes from that release.

This commit reorganizes the documentation by moving debugging instructions from the blueprints page to a dedicated debugging page. It clarifies that the built-in debugger should not be used in production environments and directs users to external error logging tools instead.

This commit updates the changelog to document the removal of several deprecated Flask attributes and methods. It clarifies that users must now use alternative properties like `create_jinja_environment` or `blueprint` instead of the removed legacy code.

This commit approves the Flask-Script extension for the PyPI ecosystem. It moves the package from the listed to the approved status in the extreview module, updating its metadata to reflect the new approval.
This commit corrects the indentation of the changelog list in CHANGES.rst. It ensures the list items are properly formatted for consistent display in the project's change history.

This commit updates the CHANGES file to document the upcoming version 0.6.1. It identifies this release as a bugfix with a date to be announced, ensuring the project's changelog reflects the new maintenance release.

This commit updates the CI configuration to use specific PyPy versions on Travis and removes Python 3.6 from AppVeyor. It also restructures the Travis matrix to separate documentation and development environments, aiming to reduce build times.
This commit fixes a documentation typo in the Flask configuration reference. It removes an extra backtick from the definition of the TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS setting in the config.rst file.

This commit adds a missing documentation anchor to the error pages guide. It ensures the section is correctly referenced within the documentation structure. The change affects the `docs/patterns/errorpages.rst` file.

This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the quickstart guide documentation. It removes an unnecessary word from a comment explaining request method handling, improving clarity for users reading the setup instructions.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to include instructions for setting up a development environment. It adds steps to clone the repository and install Flask as an editable package using pip.

This commit removes Codecov integration from the project's CI configuration. It deletes the codecov token from Azure Pipelines and strips the codecov dependency and upload command from the tox test environment.

This commit updates the server documentation to reflect the redesigned macOS settings interface. It clarifies how to disable the AirPlay Receiver service, which occupies port 5000, by searching for it in System Preferences rather than navigating through the Sharing pane.

This commit refactors the TaggedJSONSerializer class in flask/sessions.py by moving the object_hook logic out of the loads method. This change allows developers to extend and reuse the serializer class more easily without modifying its internal deserialization behavior.

This commit adds unit tests to verify the behavior of the Flask endpoint decorator. It ensures that view functions correctly bind to specific routing endpoints within submounts and modules. The changes are located in the test suite for Flask's basic functionality and module handling.

This commit adds a custom converter to the Flaskr tutorial's database module, `db.py`. It ensures that timestamp values retrieved from the SQLite database are automatically parsed into Python `datetime` objects, improving data handling for users.

This commit updates the SendfileTestCase in the Flask test suite to disable direct passthrough for the data attribute. This adjustment ensures compatibility with newer versions of Werkzeug, preventing potential issues when testing file sending functionality.
This commit fixes the documentation build process for Flask by updating the Sphinx configuration. It removes unused imports and helper functions from `docs/conf.py` to resolve build errors.
This commit configures the pre-commit framework to automatically update its hooks on a monthly schedule. It modifies the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to enable this recurring maintenance task.

This commit updates the test suite to use the response object's built-in header properties instead of manually parsing raw header strings. It simplifies assertions in test_blueprints.py and test_views.py by directly accessing cache control and set header attributes.

This documentation update clarifies how to use third-party debuggers like PyDev or IntelliJ with Flask applications. It advises users to disable the built-in debug mode to prevent the application from reloading and interrupting the external debugging session.

This commit standardizes deprecation messages across the Flask CLI, helpers, JSON, and scaffold modules to explicitly reference "Flask 2.1" instead of just "2.1". It ensures users see consistent version information when using functions like `send_file`, `dump`, or the `Scaffold` class.

This commit deprecates legacy JSON encoding options in Flask's `json` module to align with the standard library's `json` module. It removes internal helper functions for text wrapping and updates the `JSONEncoder` class, ensuring consistent behavior for users relying on Flask's JSON utilities.

This commit corrects the documentation for the template rendering upgrade in the upgrading guide. It clarifies that blueprints now use a general template searchpath, requiring a specific subfolder structure for template names.

This commit updates the uWSGI deployment documentation to recommend using the `--manage-script-name` and `--mount` directives instead of the `uwsgi_modifier1` setting. This change ensures that `SCRIPT_NAME` and `PATH_INFO` are correctly rewritten for applications hosted at specific paths.

This commit updates the jQuery example script to include the standard entry point for running the application. It ensures the web server starts correctly when the file is executed directly, fixing a missing initialization step.

This commit improves the error message in Flask's `make_response` method when a view function returns an unsupported type. Previously, returning a boolean caused a confusing traceback; now it raises a clear `TypeError` explaining the valid return types.

This commit ensures that standard environment variables are reset after each test to prevent state leakage between tests. It introduces helper functions in the test configuration module to manage and restore the operating system environment.

This commit updates the Flask extension tester to use a fixed, memorable temporary directory path instead of system-generated ones, which are problematic on OS X. It also simplifies the path construction for the Flask directory within the test module.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to prevent nightly Python builds from failing the overall test suite. It modifies the build matrix in the .travis.yml file to mark nightly runs as allowed failures.

This commit fixes test failures in the minitwit and flaskr examples by ensuring `open_resource` is called with the correct text mode, preventing Python 3 from returning bytes instead of strings. It also updates documentation to explicitly show the `mode` parameter and corrects test assertions to compare against bytes.

This commit corrects minor grammatical and phrasing errors in the Flask async-await documentation. It clarifies that extensions predating async support do not expect async views, improving the accuracy of the guidance for developers.

This commit removes outdated deployment instructions for dotCloud from the documentation, as the service is no longer available. It updates the hosted options section in the deploying guide to reflect current reality.

This commit adds a "Download Documentation" section to the sidebar of the Flask documentation. It provides users with direct links to download the docs as a PDF or a zipped HTML archive. The change is implemented in the `sidebarintro.html` template.

This commit renames the Flask method `_ensure_exc_class` to `_get_exc_class_and_code` and simplifies its logic for resolving exception classes. It updates internal calls within the `Flask` class to use the new method name, improving code clarity without changing user-facing behavior.
This commit corrects a typo in the extension development documentation. It updates the example code to use the correct class name, SQLite3, instead of the misspelled Sqlite3.

This commit adds a new test module containing a Flask application with various route handlers and a view class. It provides example code to verify the behavior of typing tools against different function signatures and return types.

This commit refactors the `TestSafeJoin` tests in `tests/test_helpers.py` to use pytest's parametrize decorator. It replaces manual loops with data-driven test cases for `flask.safe_join`, improving test readability and structure without changing the underlying behavior.

This commit modifies the Flask application's error handling to preserve the original traceback when a BuildError is re-raised. It ensures that debugging information remains intact for users encountering URL building failures. The change affects the Flask class and includes a new test case to verify this behavior.

This commit updates the Flaskr example README to clarify that manual database initialization is no longer required. It removes instructions to call `init_db()` in a Python shell, noting that the process now runs automatically before the application starts.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask test suite to verify that the `send_from_directory` function correctly serves files from a specified directory. It ensures the helper returns the expected file content when used within a test request context.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.12.1-dev in the `flask/__init__.py` module. It marks the start of a new development cycle following the 0.12 release.

Adds a test to verify that the `_AppCtxGlobals` class returns the correct string representation when printed. This ensures the `__repr__` method accurately displays the application name for debugging purposes.

This commit updates the Unicode documentation in the Flask project to improve readability. It corrects punctuation in the introductory sentence of the unicode.rst file, adding commas to clarify the comparison between Flask, Jinja2, and Werkzeug.

This commit relaxes the type annotation for `after_request` functions in the `flask.typing` module. It allows callbacks to accept any subclass of the Werkzeug `Response` class, such as Flask's own `Response`, preventing type checking errors for users who annotate their handlers with the specific Flask class.

This commit disables subdomain matching by default in the Flask application class. Users must now explicitly enable this feature by passing a specific parameter to the Flask constructor, as setting the server name no longer implicitly activates it.

This commit refactors the Flaskr example application to use a blueprint and an application factory pattern. It moves the main application logic into a new factory module and a dedicated blueprint, allowing for cleaner code organization and easier testing.

This commit fixes the documentation sidebar by adding the carbon ads template to the list of displayed sidebar components. The change is made in the `docs/conf.py` configuration file, ensuring the ad widget appears correctly in the generated documentation.

This commit updates the Flask extension development documentation to clarify how to use the request context stack for sharing data with view functions. It also fixes a minor bug in the example extension code and adjusts the surrounding text to match the corrected implementation.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 1.2.0. It modifies the version string in the main module and updates the changelog to reflect the new release.

This commit adds documentation to the testing guide explaining how to use the `test_request_context` method. It demonstrates how to temporarily activate a request context to access context-bound objects like `request`, `g`, and `session` during tests.

This commit fixes a build error in the documentation by removing an invalid reference in the mod_wsgi guide. It also adds a touch icon to the site configuration and updates the theme submodule to support this new feature.

This documentation update standardizes file upload examples to use the application configuration object instead of a global variable. It ensures the file upload pattern consistently references the upload folder via the app config, improving clarity for developers following the guide.

This commit updates the `find_module` method in the `ExtensionImporter` class within `scripts/flaskext_compat.py` to remove the optional `path` argument. This change ensures the method signature aligns with the expected interface for module importers, preventing potential compatibility issues during module resolution.

This commit updates the project's continuous integration configuration to test against Python 3.4. It removes separate Travis requirement files and modifies the build script to handle dependency installation differently.

This commit configures the CI workflow to skip code tests when only documentation files are modified. It also enables strict warning handling in the Read the Docs configuration to ensure documentation builds fail on errors.

This commit modernizes the test suite for Flask's configuration handling by replacing deprecated assertion methods with their current equivalents. It updates the ConfigTestCase to use standard failure and boolean checks when verifying that loading a missing environment variable behaves correctly.

This commit adds a test case to verify that Flask's test request context and client correctly default to "localhost" when SERVER_NAME and APPLICATION_ROOT are not configured. It ensures the request URL is properly constructed in these scenarios.

This commit moves the logic for converting session lifetime values into the ConfigAttribute class. It introduces a helper function to ensure values are treated as timedeltas, allowing the Flask app to automatically convert numeric configuration inputs into the correct time format.

This commit corrects a typo in the security documentation where "haders" was misspelled. It ensures the example code for setting the Strict-Transport-Security header is accurate for users reading the guide.

This commit reformats the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation file to improve readability and consistency. It updates the Discord invite link and adjusts the indentation of list items for better visual structure.

This commit resolves a type-checking error in the Flask CLI module by conditionally importing the metadata package. It uses a type-checking guard to satisfy the linter while avoiding a version-dependent error on Python 3.10 and later.

This commit adds documentation for Werkzeug's development server, `run_simple`, within the application dispatch guide. It clarifies that this function is intended for local development and testing, while directing users to the deployment section for production server configurations.

This commit fixes a typing issue in Flask where template global decorators were incorrectly required to accept functions with no arguments. It updates the type definitions in `src/flask/typing.py` to allow these decorators to accept functions with any number of arguments.

This commit updates the minimum required version of the Werkzeug dependency from 2.3.5 to 2.3.6. It modifies the project configuration in `pyproject.toml` and updates the changelog in `CHANGES.rst` to reflect this version bump.

This commit updates the project's linting configuration to suppress the B905 warning from flake8. This prevents false positives for the `zip(strict=True)` argument, which is only supported in Python 3.10 and later. The change is made in the `setup.cfg` file.

This commit cleans up the package distribution by excluding development artifacts like Git folders, compiled Python files, and built documentation from the release. It updates the MANIFEST.in file to define these exclusions, ensuring the final package contains only necessary source files.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the Flask documentation index. It changes the word "devided" to "divided" in the introductory text. No functional code or behavior is affected.

Replaces the deprecated assertEquals method with assert_equal in the SubdomainTestCase class within the Flask testing suite. This change standardizes the test assertions to use the current, consistent naming convention.

This commit corrects inaccurate documentation in the packages module regarding how to register modules with explicit shortnames. It clarifies that moving views to a new location requires defining a unique shortname to prevent internal naming conflicts.
This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to improve readability. It moves the reference to the Flask class documentation to the end of the paragraph explaining the `__main__` check.

This commit updates the documentation for context processors in the templating module. It clarifies that these processors can expose functions to templates, not just variables, and improves the wording to explain this capability more clearly.

This commit updates documentation and examples to reflect the migration from setup.py to pyproject.toml for project configuration. It also standardizes virtual environment naming from venv to .venv across guides and sample projects.

This commit fixes a memory leak in the Flask application class where instances with static folders were not freed by the garbage collector. It resolves the issue by replacing a strong reference in the static view function with a weak reference to the app instance.

This commit updates the security documentation in the Flask project to improve clarity and formatting. It replaces a brief introduction with a more detailed explanation of browser security headers and standardizes the section heading style for HTTP Strict Transport Security.

This commit fixes an operator precedence bug in the Flask class that caused incorrect exception handling behavior. It ensures the debug mode and bad request error settings are evaluated together before being used in the condition.

This commit updates the project's development dependencies and CI workflow actions to their latest versions. It bumps the GitHub Actions checkout and setup-python steps in the publish and test workflows, as well as the pre-commit configuration and requirements files.

This commit removes unused return values and variables in the Flask application, debug helpers, and JSON modules. This commit raises the minimum required versions for Werkzeug, ItsDangerous, and Blinker in the Flask project. It ensures the package relies on the latest feature releases of these dependencies, updating the configuration in pyproject.toml and related test requirements.

The `show_server_banner` function in `flask/cli.py` now accepts an `eager_loading` parameter. When lazy loading is enabled, the `flask run` command displays a "(lazy loading)" note in the startup banner to clarify the application's loading behavior.

This commit splits the documentation foreword into two separate files to better serve different audiences. It introduces a new advanced foreword for experienced programmers, covering topics like thread safety in Flask, while retaining a general foreword for typical users.

This commit adds the missing assertIn and assertNotIn methods to the FlaskTestCase class for Python 2.6 compatibility. It resolves an issue where these standard test assertions were unavailable on that specific version, preventing test execution.

This commit introduces a new import mechanism in the `flask.ext` module to support the transition from `flaskext` to `flask_` naming conventions. It allows users to import extensions using the new `flask.ext` syntax, which automatically redirects to the correct module format.

This commit updates a test in the Flask application context module to verify the correct string representation of the global object. It ensures the test properly checks the output of the `repr` function for the `flask.g` instance.

This commit updates the test suite to ensure all tests pass, likely by fixing compatibility issues or updating test logic. It modifies the core test infrastructure in `tests/__init__.py` and adjusts tests across various modules like `test_basic.py` and `test_appctx.py`.
This commit fixes a minor grammatical error in the Flask templating documentation. It corrects the phrasing in the `docs/templating.rst` file to properly describe Jinja2 as the template engine.

This commit updates the Flask extension development documentation to remove references to the abandoned Flask Extension Registry. It cleans up outdated links and descriptions in the extension development and extensions guides, ensuring users are not directed to defunct resources.

This commit applies an automated formatting fix to the `stream_with_context` function in `src/flask/helpers.py`. It corrects a missing comma in the type annotation for the `generator_or_function` parameter, ensuring the code adheres to standard style guidelines.

This commit ensures that Flask's 500 error handlers always receive an InternalServerError instance, even when triggered by unhandled exceptions. This commit improves the error message in Flask's `make_response` method to include the specific endpoint name when a view function returns an invalid response type. This commit updates the Flaskr tutorial to store the database in the application's root directory instead of the system temporary folder. This change resolves issues for Windows users who lack a standard /tmp path, ensuring the database location is consistent across operating systems.

This commit adds a `get_namespace` method to the `Config` class in `flask/config.py`. It allows users to easily retrieve a dictionary of configuration options that share a specific prefix, simplifying access to grouped settings.

This commit adds an explicit `debug` parameter to the `Flask.run` method, allowing users to directly enable or disable debug mode without passing it through generic options. It clarifies that this parameter is distinct from the options forwarded to the underlying server runner.

This commit updates the docstring for the `Flask.run` method in `flask/app.py` to include a cross-reference to the `debug` attribute. It improves documentation clarity by directing users to the relevant attribute for more detailed information on debug mode behavior.
This commit corrects minor grammatical typos in the Flask tutorial documentation. It improves the readability of the blog and database sections by fixing sentence structure in the prose.

This commit adds Python 3.13 to the project's test matrix. It updates the GitHub Actions workflow and the tox configuration to include the new version in the list of supported environments for running tests.

This commit fixes test failures in the Flask test suite by updating exception syntax and ensuring response objects are properly closed. It modifies test cases in basic.py, blueprints.py, and helpers.py to prevent resource leaks and compatibility errors.

This commit corrects a misplaced parenthesis in the docstring example for the `make_response` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It ensures the documentation accurately reflects the correct argument order for passing a template and a status code.
This commit adds a test for the `get_version` function in the Flask CLI module. It verifies that the function correctly outputs both the Flask and Python versions to standard output when invoked.

This commit updates the submodule URL in the .gitmodules file to use the HTTPS protocol instead of the Git protocol. This change ensures the repository can be cloned successfully on networks that block the Git protocol.

This commit renames the internal context variable `_cv_req` to `_cv_request` across the Flask codebase for improved clarity. The change affects the `Flask` application class, `RequestContext`, and related helper functions, ensuring consistent naming without altering user-facing behavior.
This commit adds Python 3.14 support to the project's test suite. It updates the CI workflow and project configuration to run tests on the new version, including the free-threaded build.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask CLI where the `AppGroup.command` method failed to pass the group instance to the underlying Click command decorator. This ensures that commands registered via the `AppGroup` class are correctly associated with the application group.

This commit relocates the `wsgi_app` method within the `Flask` class in `flask/app.py` to a more logical position. The change reorganizes the code structure without altering the application's behavior or fixing any specific bugs.

This commit updates the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation by replacing the tab directive with a simple list format. It ensures the virtual environment setup instructions for Linux, macOS, and Windows display correctly without relying on specific Sphinx extensions.

This commit removes a test that verified the request context could handle Unicode hostnames compliant with IDNA standards. The change affects the test suite in tests/test_reqctx.py by deleting the test_environ_for_valid_idna_completes function.

This commit adds a documentation anchor for class-based views in the Flask API reference. It allows users to link directly to that section of the documentation. The change is located in the `docs/api.rst` file.

This commit fixes a formatting error in the documentation string for the `on_json_loading_failed` method within the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py`. It removes an extra blank line that was breaking the ReST syntax, ensuring the documentation renders correctly.
This documentation update removes the obsolete type attribute from script tag examples in the API reference. It clarifies that modern browsers do not require this attribute to execute JavaScript.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the Jinja2 templating documentation. It changes the phrase "of you" to "for you" in the description of autoescaping within the templating module.
This commit fixes a minor typo in the documentation for the Flask signals module. It adds a missing period to the description of the fallback behavior, ensuring the text is grammatically correct.

This commit changes how Flask handles view functions that fail to return a response. Instead of issuing a warning and returning an empty string, the `Flask.make_response` method now raises a `ValueError` to properly signal the error.

This documentation update clarifies the recommended configuration format for integrating Celery with Flask. It replaces the previous method of passing individual settings with a single dictionary reference and notes that Celery 5.x deprecated uppercase configuration keys.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions test workflow to use the built-in pip caching feature of the setup-python action. It replaces the previous manual cache configuration, which relied on a separate cache action and custom key generation, with a simpler, integrated approach.

This commit fixes a documentation typo in the logging guide by removing an extra closing parenthesis from the RequestFormatter constructor example. Users viewing the documentation will now see the correct syntax for initializing the formatter.
This commit adds documentation for the `headers` attribute in the API reference. It clarifies that this attribute provides access to incoming request headers as a dictionary-like object.

This commit adds a `url_for` method to the `Flask` class, allowing users to generate URLs for specific endpoints within the application. It also updates the `url_for` helper in `helpers.py` to support this new functionality.

This commit fixes a typo in the Celery documentation where "factor" was incorrectly used instead of "factory." It clarifies the instructions for configuring a Celery application in the `docs/patterns/celery.rst` file.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the test_cli_name function within tests/test_cli.py. It changes a plain string into a proper docstring, ensuring the test description is correctly recognized by Python tools.
