This commit adds documentation for deploying applications using the distribute package and corrects a documentation bug in the installation guide. It also updates the flash function in the main flask module.

This commit documents the new subscription operator syntax for accessing attributes on the `g` object in Flask. It clarifies that using `g['key']` is equivalent to `getattr(g, 'key', None)` and highlights its utility for testing. The changes update the API and testing documentation and add a test case to verify this behavior.
This commit removes the unused Redbaron dependency from the project's test configuration. It cleans up the tox.ini file to prevent unnecessary package installations during testing.

This commit refactors the Flask CLI scripting interface, introducing new classes like AppGroup and FlaskGroup to manage command registration and application contexts. It updates the documentation to describe these new components and clarifies how commands interact with the application context.

This commit adds a new documentation page for Flask extensions and includes it in the main table of contents. It explains how to find and install extensions using package managers like pip. The changes affect the documentation structure and the new extensions module.

The `App.select_jinja_autoescape` method in Flask now uses case-insensitive comparison for file extensions. This ensures that files with uppercase extensions, such as `.HTML`, are correctly identified for autoescaping.

This commit updates the changelog to document a behavior change in Flask's `after_request` handlers. It clarifies that these handlers now execute even when a request fails with an exception and an error page is generated.

This commit documents how to set default values for CLI command options using environment variables. It explains that users can configure options like the port for the run command by setting variables following the FLASK_COMMAND_OPTION pattern.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Flask extensions guide. It updates the reference from the non-standard "requirements.rst" file to the standard "requirements.txt" file, ensuring users are directed to the correct dependency file.
This commit corrects the documentation for the Flask configuration file. It clarifies that the Debug setting defaults to True only when the environment is set to development, rather than production.

Simplifies the logic in the `find_best_app` function within the Flask CLI module. It removes the error raised when multiple potential applications are found, allowing the command to proceed if exactly one match is identified.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask's internal `_request_ctx_stack` module. It details the attributes available on each stack layer, such as the active application, request, and session objects. The change also includes an example demonstrating how to access the current session from the top of the stack.
This commit updates the Flask version number to 1.0.3.dev in the `flask/__init__.py` module. It also adds a new entry to the changelog to mark the start of the 1.0.3 development cycle.
This commit corrects minor spelling errors in the Flask documentation. It fixes typos in files such as becomingbig.rst and design.rst to improve the clarity of the written guides.

This commit pins the operating system and Python version for the Read the Docs build environment. It ensures the documentation builds consistently using Ubuntu 20.04 and Python 3.10, preventing unexpected failures from version drift.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.1.2 by updating the version string in the main package initialization. It also updates the changelog to mark the release date and modifies the manifest to exclude compiled Python files from the distribution.

This commit adds a unit test to verify the behavior of the `appcontext_tearing_down` signal in Flask. It ensures the signal fires with a `None` exception after a request completes, even if the view raised an error. The test is located in the `tests/test_signals.py` module.

This commit deprecates registering the same Blueprint instance with the same name multiple times, issuing a warning to users. The change modifies the `Blueprint.register` method in `src/flask/blueprints.py` to detect duplicate registrations.

This commit updates the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py` to ensure Python 3 compatibility. It replaces the deprecated multi-argument raise syntax with a standard exception re-raise that preserves the original traceback.

This commit fixes broken internal links in the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation. It corrects the anchor target for the "Run the tests" section to ensure the link resolves correctly for users navigating the guide.

This commit updates the package documentation to guide users to the largerapp example source code when they encounter difficulties. It adds a reference to the flask/examples/largerapp directory in the docs/patterns/packages.rst file.

This commit removes the deprecated `error_handlers` attribute from the `Flask` class, eliminating the associated getter and setter methods. It also updates the initialization of `error_handler_spec` to no longer reference the removed internal dictionary.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to explain how to use external debuggers like Eclipse or Aptana. It details the `debug`, `use_debugger`, and `use_reloader` configuration options, clarifying how to manage the debug process when using third-party tools.

Updates the actions/setup-python dependency from version 4.4.0 to 4.5.0 in the GitHub Actions workflows. This change affects the publish and tests workflow files to ensure the latest minor version is used for setting up the Python environment.

This commit refactors the `_get_static_url_path` method in the `_PackageBoundObject` class within `flask/helpers.py`. It simplifies the logic for determining the static URL path by using early returns, making the code easier to read without changing the application's behavior.

This commit updates the Flask application's response handling to correctly identify text and binary data. It replaces the previous type checks with more accurate ones, ensuring that `bytearray` objects are properly recognized as valid response types.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Flaskr example tests and documentation by adding a missing closing angle bracket to an HTML assertion. The change ensures the test correctly validates the rendered message content within the FlaskrTestCase class.

This commit updates the SQLAlchemy documentation to replace a placeholder with a detailed explanation of manual object relational mapping. It describes the trade-offs between manual and declarative approaches and provides a code example for setting up the database engine and metadata.

This commit updates the FastCGI deployment documentation to clarify that nginx and older lighttpd versions require an explicit socket path. It corrects the example code to properly initialize the WSGIServer within the main block.

This documentation update clarifies how to run applications using the factory pattern with the Flask CLI. It explains that the `flask` command automatically detects factory functions like `create_app` or `make_app` when the `FLASK_APP` environment variable is set.

This commit modifies `find_package` in `flask/helpers.py` to handle PEP 302 import hooks that lack an `is_package` method. Instead of failing silently or with a generic error, it now raises a descriptive `AttributeError` explaining that the method is required by Flask.

This commit exposes the method that generates default OPTIONS responses as a public API on the Flask class. Subclasses can now override this method to customize how the application handles OPTIONS requests.

This commit renames the GitHub issue and pull request template files from RST to Markdown extensions to accurately reflect their content format. The change affects the `.github` directory, ensuring the templates are correctly identified as Markdown documents.

This commit resolves a type-checking error reported by mypy in the Flask application class. It adds a type ignore comment to the `make_response` method to suppress a false positive regarding header updates.

This commit ensures that exceptions raised within Flask applications are correctly propagated to the Werkzeug development server instead of being blocked. It modifies the Flask class and the CLI run command to enable error passthrough by default.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to clarify how to set environment variables on Windows. It distinguishes between Command Prompt and PowerShell syntax, providing specific examples for each shell.

This commit adds a test to verify that the Blueprint endpoint decorator correctly associates a view function with a specific endpoint name. It ensures that requests to the mapped URL return the expected endpoint identifier while confirming that the blueprint's URL prefix does not create an unintended route.

This commit updates the documentation for the folders tutorial to fix a broken link to the Jinja2 library. It corrects the URL in the `docs/tutorial/folders.rst` file to point to the current official website, ensuring users can successfully access the external reference.

This commit updates development dependencies and removes an unnecessary type ignore comment in the Flask CLI module. It also refines the `CertParamType` class definition within `src/flask/cli.py` to align with updated Click library requirements.

This commit adds a workaround for a limitation in Python 3.3's namespace loader that could cause incorrect package detection. It introduces a helper function in `flask/helpers.py` to determine if a module is a package by checking the loader's capabilities, ensuring `find_package` behaves correctly.

This commit updates the Flask application class to clarify how error handlers interact with teardown functions. It also adjusts the test suite to ensure exceptions are properly propagated during teardown verification.

This commit documents how to customize routing converters in the Flask application class. It also corrects a documentation typo in the API reference and updates the default Jinja options to use an immutable dictionary.

This commit removes per-project contribution and code of conduct files to prevent synchronization issues, replacing them with a single global guide. It updates the README to explicitly link to the contributing guide, as GitHub's interface does not automatically display it.

This commit changes the Flask application's jinja_options attribute from an immutable dictionary to a standard dictionary, allowing users to modify configuration values more easily. It clarifies in the documentation that these changes must occur before the Jinja environment is created.

This commit adds support for third-party CLI plugins to the Flask command-line interface. It allows extensions to register new commands via setuptools entry points, making them available through the FlaskGroup class.

This commit updates the project's installation configuration to include Werkzeug and Jinja2 as required dependencies. Users will now automatically receive these libraries when installing the package, resolving previous setup issues where they had to be installed manually.

This commit updates documentation and configuration files to replace the deprecated "py.test" command with "pytest". It ensures users and developers use the correct, modern command name when running the test suite.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the Flaskr tutorial setup guide. It adds the missing `os` import to the code example in `docs/tutorial/setup.rst`, ensuring the provided instructions are complete and accurate for users.

The extension import mechanism in flask/ext/__init__.py no longer suppresses errors during module loading. This ensures that import failures are properly reported to the user instead of being silently ignored on certain Python versions.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the pyupgrade, black, and flake8 tools. It ensures the project's automated code checks run with the latest available releases.

This commit fixes a typo in the Jinja2 documentation where the `tojson` filter was misspelled as `tosjon` in an example. The correction ensures users copying the code from the `api.rst` file will use the correct filter name.

This commit renames the test module from `flask.testsuite` to `tests` and updates all internal imports accordingly. It also renames test files to follow the `test_` prefix convention, making them easier to identify and run by standard test discovery tools.

This commit introduces the `get_json` method to the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py`, replacing the previous `json` property. It updates the test suite to use the new method for parsing JSON request bodies.

This commit refactors the Flask CLI by introducing a new AppGroup class that automatically wraps commands with the application context. It updates FlaskGroup to inherit from this new class, simplifying command registration for developers using the Flask command-line interface.
The test workflow now triggers on pushes to the stable branch instead of versioned branches. It also consolidates the ignored file patterns into a more compact list format.
This commit fixes a grammatical error in the SQLAlchemy documentation. It corrects the phrasing in the `docs/patterns/sqlalchemy.rst` file to improve clarity regarding session management.

The `_render` function in `flask/templating.py` now allows the `before_render_template` signal to override the default template rendering. If exactly one signal receiver returns a non-None value, that value is returned directly instead of rendering the template.

This commit fixes a resource leak in the Flask test suite by ensuring a response object is properly closed. The change adds a close call to the `test_send_from_directory` method within the `SendfileTestCase` class, preventing file handle exhaustion during test execution.

This commit removes PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 from the test matrix in the GitHub Actions workflow and tox configuration. It also renames the remaining test jobs to remove the "Pallets" prefix, simplifying the CI setup.

This commit updates the changelog to document a change in Flask's application factory behavior. It clarifies that factory functions no longer require a `script_info` parameter to work with the `flask` command, as the object is passed automatically if the function accepts a single argument or one named `script_info`.

This commit fixes an import error that occurred when Flask extensions were only partially initialized during a redirect. It updates the `_ExtensionImporter` class to handle recursive imports by managing temporary module entries, preventing crashes in the extension loading process.
This commit adds a new job to the Azure Pipelines configuration to run the stylecheck environment via tox. It ensures code style validation is performed as part of the continuous integration process.

The `fix` function in `scripts/flaskext_migrate.py` now accepts an AST object directly instead of a file path. This change allows the migration logic to be tested programmatically without requiring shell execution or file I/O.

This commit corrects a minor grammatical error in the error handling documentation. It changes the word "Of" to "Or" in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file to improve clarity for users reading the guide.

This commit updates the test command in the tox configuration to use the Python test runner script directly instead of invoking make. This change resolves a warning regarding the test environment not being properly installed.

This commit optimizes template loading in Flask's DispatchingJinjaLoader by adding a fast path that skips detailed explanation logic when the EXPLAIN_TEMPLATE_LOADING configuration is disabled. This improves performance for standard template requests by avoiding unnecessary processing.

This commit deprecates the `before_first_request` feature in the Flask application class, advising developers to run setup code during application creation instead. The change updates the `Flask` and `Blueprint` classes to mark the related methods as deprecated for removal in the next major version.

This commit standardizes internal imports across several Flask modules, including app, config, and helpers, to use relative paths from the local _compat module. This change ensures consistent module resolution and prevents potential import errors when the package is installed or used in different environments.

The test suite for import migration now skips all tests if the redbaron package is not installed, preventing import errors. This change modifies the test_import_migration.py module to use pytest.importorskip for the dependency.

This commit ensures that JSON parsing failures return a response with the correct Content-Type header and a JSON object body. It modifies the `Request.on_json_loading_failed` method in `flask/wrappers.py` to handle this behavior, with tests added to verify the fix.

This commit updates the changelog to document recent changes in the Flask framework. It notes that the Flask class now avoids unnecessary imports for programmatic use and that Blueprints and Flask instances support new methods for adding application-wide template filters.
This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to remove unnecessary colons after setting names. It improves the formatting consistency in the config reference guide.

This commit documents the new `Config.from_json` method in the Flask 1.0 changelog. It also adds a version note to the `Config` class in `flask/config.py` to indicate when this feature was introduced.

This commit updates the docstring for the NoImportsTestCase class in the Flask test suite. It clarifies that avoiding the __import__ function allows tools to create Flask instances even when modules have import-time errors. This change improves the documentation for meta-programming scenarios by explaining the use of standard library modules for metadata retrieval.

This commit removes the local editable source configuration for the Werkzeug dependency in the project's build files. It switches the project to use the standard version 3.1.5 from the public package registry instead of a local development copy.

The `load_dotenv` function in `flask/cli.py` now outputs its warning message to standard error instead of standard output. This change ensures that diagnostic messages do not interfere with the application's standard output stream.

This commit adds external links to the official documentation for SQLAlchemy and WTForms. It updates the documentation files for these patterns to help users find more detailed information about the libraries.

This commit refactors the test environment builder from a factory function into a dedicated class named EnvironBuilder. It updates the Flask application's test request context method to instantiate this new class directly, replacing the previous function call.

This commit adds documentation for the Flask 0.7 upgrade script, explaining how it scans applications to generate safe diffs for backward-incompatible changes. It also begins documenting the `walk_path` function within the upgrade script module.

This commit updates the Flask package version from 0.10.2-dev to 0.11-dev. It modifies the version string in the `flask/__init__.py` module and the `setup.py` file to reflect the new development release.
This commit corrects a broken pull request link in the changelog. It updates the Unreleased section of CHANGES.rst to ensure the reference is valid.

This commit reorders the deployment options in the documentation index and updates cross-references in the FastCGI guide. It ensures the standalone WSGI option is correctly listed alongside other server configurations. The changes affect the `docs/deploying` module.

This commit updates the documentation configuration to add a missing link for the itsdangerous library and corrects a syntax error in the intersphinx mapping. It also fixes a broken text reference in the security documentation regarding session cookie expiration.

This commit updates development dependencies and GitHub Actions workflows to their latest versions. It refreshes the lock file and configuration for tools like pre-commit and uv, ensuring the project uses current, secure versions of its build and testing infrastructure.

This commit corrects the release date for version 0.7 in the CHANGES file. It updates the date from June 27th to June 28th, 2011, ensuring the project history accurately reflects when the Grappa release was actually published.

This commit adds a fallback mechanism to the documentation build configuration in `docs/conf.py`. If the Flask theme support module is missing, the build now proceeds with the default theme and displays a warning instead of failing.

This commit updates the changelog to document the new `provide_automatic_options` parameter in `Flask.add_url_rule`. It also reorganizes and renames related tests in `tests/test_basic.py` to improve clarity and consistency.

The `send_file` function in Flask's helpers module now raises a `ValueError` when passed a text-mode file object, such as `StringIO`. Previously, this input resulted in a successful response containing an empty file.

This commit updates the test suite to ensure that deprecation warnings are visible during test execution. It modifies the `catch_warnings` function in `tests/flask_tests.py` to explicitly enable these warnings, preventing them from being silently ignored.

This commit updates the installation documentation in the README to point to the current pip getting-started guide. It replaces an outdated link to the quickstart page, ensuring users are directed to the correct resource for installing and updating the package.

The `stream_with_context` helper in `flask.helpers` is refactored to support asynchronous views. This change ensures that streaming responses no longer fail when used within async endpoints, allowing request context access to persist correctly.

This commit updates the development dependency tox from version 3.19.0 to 3.20.0. It modifies the requirements/dev.txt file to reflect this version bump, ensuring the project uses the latest stable release of the testing tool.

This commit adds the missing documentation page for the Flask command line interface. It describes how to use the built-in `flask` script and `python -mflask` to access application commands. The changes are located in the `docs/cli.rst` file.
This commit corrects grammatical errors and clarifies wording in the security documentation. It improves the descriptions of HTTPS implementation and security headers in the `docs/security.rst` file.

This commit updates the project's development and documentation dependencies to newer versions. It replaces a specific git commit of Sphinx with the stable 4.0.2 release and bumps several other packages, including Jinja2 and MarkupSafe, to their latest minor releases.

This documentation update clarifies that Flask now requires Python 3.5 or later, removing the previous recommendation for Python 3.4. Users installing the framework should now ensure their environment meets this minimum version requirement.

This commit fixes the alignment of the logo in the Flask documentation. It removes the right-alignment setting from the image directive in the main documentation index, ensuring the logo displays correctly.

This commit removes an unnecessary type ignore comment from the `make_response` method in the `Flask` class. It resolves a static type checking warning reported by mypy, ensuring the codebase remains clean without altering runtime behavior.

This commit documents the addition of keyword argument support to the Flask test client. It updates the changelog and adds a version note to the `Flask.test_client` method in `flask/app.py` to reflect this new feature.

This commit updates the SLSA GitHub generator dependency in the publish workflow from version 1.7.0 to 1.9.0. It ensures the build process uses the newer generator version for SLSA level 3 provenance generation.
This commit updates the project version to 0.5.1 in the setup.py file. It prepares the codebase for a bugfix release by incrementing the version number.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `add_url_rule` method where lowercase HTTP method names, such as 'options', were not recognized correctly. It ensures that method names are converted to uppercase before processing, allowing users to define routes with lowercase method strings without breaking automatic OPTIONS handling.

This commit cleans up the Flask JSON module by replacing the deprecated unicode type with text_type in htmlsafe_dump. It also simplifies line breaks and string formatting in the jsonify function for better readability.

Updated the WSGI standalone deployment documentation to replace deprecated Werkzeug sample code. The example now uses the current proxy fix middleware import and includes explicit configuration parameters for protocol and host headers.

This commit removes an unused development server entry point from the Flask module. It eliminates the code that allowed running the application directly as a script, which is not part of the standard library usage.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `send_from_directory` function in Flask's helpers module. It specifies that the `directory` parameter is relative to the current application's root path, improving clarity for users configuring file serving.

This commit corrects documentation links in the Flask quickstart guide to properly reference the `flask.Request` class instead of the lowercase `flask.request` object. This ensures users are directed to the correct API documentation for request attributes like method and form data.

This commit adds a section to the documentation foreword warning against using Python 3 for web development. It explains that unresolved WSGI standardization issues make the language unsuitable for this purpose until the situation is resolved.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.0.3 by updating the version string in the `flask` module. It also standardizes the date format in the changelog to use ISO 8601 notation for consistency.

This commit fixes a bug where after_request handlers were incorrectly invoked twice in certain scenarios. It also improves the logging system by making the logger name configurable to better support unit testing, as standard library loggers are cached.
This commit corrects a typo in the extension development documentation. It updates the example code to use the correct class name, SQLite3, instead of the misspelled Sqlite3.

This commit updates the extension development documentation to clarify licensing requirements for the Flask Extension Registry. It specifies that extensions must use a BSD, MIT, or more liberal license to be listed. The changes are made in the extensiondev.rst file.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask Blueprint class where nested URL prefixes were not correctly applied during registration. It ensures that the url_prefix is properly set whether defined at construction or during the registration override.

This commit consolidates the project's linting rules into a new .flake8 file, removing the previous configuration from setup.cfg. It updates the codebase to comply with the new strictness settings, such as removing unnecessary import statements in example and test modules.

The `upgrade_python_file` function in `scripts/flask-07-upgrade.py` now detects and updates deprecated error handler registrations. This ensures that code using the old `error_handlers` dictionary syntax is correctly migrated to the new decorator-based approach during the upgrade process.

This commit updates the mod_wsgi deployment documentation to address the removal of the execfile function in Python 3. It provides the correct code snippet for activating a virtual environment in Python 3 .wsgi files.

Flask now supports regular Werkzeug routing rules added directly to the URL map, not just those created via the `add_url_rule` method. This change updates the `Flask` class to safely handle rules that may lack specific attributes, ensuring broader compatibility with external routing configurations.

This commit adds documentation to the testing guide explaining how to manually trigger post-request processing. It demonstrates using the `process_response` method within a test request context to apply `after_request` handlers to a response object.

This commit updates documentation files to correct the spelling of "App Engine" from "AppEngine" or "appengine." It ensures consistent terminology across the CGI deployment, caching, and lazy loading guides. No functional code changes are included.

This commit enables autoescaping by default for the `render_template_string` function in Flask. Users will now see HTML entities for special characters in template strings, preventing potential XSS vulnerabilities. The change updates the `Flask` class configuration and related documentation.

The Flask CLI now accepts --app, --env, --debug, and --env-file command-line options, allowing users to configure the application and environment directly without relying solely on environment variables. This change modifies the FlaskGroup and ScriptInfo classes in the cli module to parse these new arguments.

This commit updates the type hints for the `render_template` function in Flask's templating module. It allows the function to accept `Template` objects in addition to strings, ensuring the type declaration matches the actual implementation.

This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.2.1 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It also adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes for this release.

This commit updates the WSGI standalone deployment documentation to include a simple nginx proxy configuration example. It clarifies how to handle header rewriting for REMOTE_ADDR and HTTP_HOST when running the application behind an HTTP proxy.

This commit corrects a typo in the local environment setup instructions within the CONTRIBUTING.rst file. It updates the Windows virtual environment activation command to reference the correct .venv directory path.

This commit adds a test case to the BasicFunctionalityTestCase in tests/flask_tests.py to verify that the session permanent flag is correctly set to True. It ensures the application properly handles session expiration settings during requests.

This commit corrects a documentation example for class-based views in the extension development guide. It fixes the method signature to properly include the self parameter, ensuring the code snippet accurately reflects how to define a view method.

This commit updates the type hints for the `static_folder` parameter in the `Scaffold`, `Flask`, and `Blueprint` classes to accept `pathlib.Path` objects. This allows users to pass path objects directly instead of being restricted to string values.

The `_ExtensionImporter` class in `flask/ext/__init__.py` now distinguishes between recoverable and critical import errors. It re-raises exceptions if the traceback originates from an important module, preventing silent failures during extension loading.

This commit updates the WSGI standalone deployment documentation to improve clarity and formatting. It refines the explanation of proxy headers and corrects the syntax for code blocks in the nginx configuration examples.

This commit makes minor revisions to the Flask documentation, including updates to the application context, configuration, deployment, and tutorial pages. The changes primarily involve correcting punctuation and clarifying phrasing for better readability.
This documentation update clarifies the default locations for Flask instance folders. It explains where the instance directory is expected for both single-module and package application structures.

This commit fixes a broken test case in the Flask helpers module. It corrects the indentation of the Content-Length header assignment within the send_file function, ensuring the code executes correctly.

This commit updates tests in `tests/test_reqctx.py` to accurately reflect that Unicode host headers are valid, except for non-printable characters. It adds a test verifying that a non-printable character in the Host header correctly triggers a 400 Bad Request response.

This commit corrects the command-line syntax for running Flask applications in the application factory documentation. It updates the examples in the appfactories module to place the `--app` option before the `run` subcommand, ensuring users copy the correct usage.

The examples for Flask applications have been updated to use the command-line interface for initialization and execution. This change affects the minitwit, flaskr, and other sample projects, replacing direct script execution with standard Flask CLI commands.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's module registration where the subdomain for static file rules was incorrectly set. The `_register_module` function now uses the application state's subdomain instead of the module's, ensuring static assets are served under the correct domain.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the file upload pattern. It clarifies that the application should redirect users to the uploaded file page rather than the upload page after a successful upload.

This commit improves type annotations for decorators in Flask's `Scaffold`, `Flask`, and `Blueprint` classes. It ensures type checkers correctly recognize that these decorators return the same function signature as their input, resolving previous typing inaccuracies.

This commit updates the contribution documentation to improve the first-time setup instructions. It adds a link to the pre-commit framework guide and formats the installation command as a code block for clarity.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the Flask documentation and updates the pre-commit configuration. It fixes typos in the appcontext, quickstart, and templating guides and adjusts the codespell hook to automatically write changes.

This commit updates the API documentation for the flask.json.tag module by moving the description from the main API file into the module's docstring. It replaces explicit class references with an automodule directive to simplify the documentation structure.

This commit adds documentation for the application context and its teardown handlers in Flask. It clarifies that the `appcontext_tearing_down` signal now passes an exception argument, improving clarity for developers using the `Flask` class and `AppContext` module.

This commit updates the changelog to document a change in how environment files are processed. It notes that the default encoding for loading .env and .flaskenv files is now UTF-8, enabling the use of non-ASCII characters.
This commit removes an unused import from the Flask application module. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating dead code that had no effect on the application's behavior.

This commit updates the CLI documentation to accurately reflect the current FLASK_APP environment variable detection logic. It clarifies how the flask command-line interface is installed and used, removing outdated references to previous versions. The changes primarily affect the documentation files and the flask.cli module.

This commit optimizes the `prepare_import` function in `flask/cli.py` by caching the result of the file extension check. It prevents redundant calls to `os.path.splitext` when processing Python file paths, improving performance during CLI operations.

This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to clarify that the SERVER_NAME setting accepts a port number in addition to the server name. It corrects the example to show the combined format, helping users properly configure subdomain support.

This commit updates project metadata and documentation, including a new README and changes to the author list. It also modifies the Travis CI configuration to add macOS testing and separate the documentation build.

This commit corrects a broken documentation link in the changelog for the `Config` class. It updates the reference to use the officially documented shortcut package path instead of the incorrect internal path.
This commit fixes a broken documentation link in the API reference. It corrects the formatting of the IRI reference in the "Incoming Request Data" section of the API documentation.
This commit removes unnecessary print statements from the Mongokit pattern documentation. It cleans up the example code in the docs/patterns/mongokit.rst file to improve clarity.

This commit deprecates importing `escape` and `Markup` directly from the `flask` package. Users should now import these utilities from the `markupsafe` library instead. The change updates the `flask` module's attribute handling and documentation to reflect this shift.

This commit updates the Flask blueprints documentation to clarify that blueprint template folders have lower priority than the application's template folder. It also corrects a typo in the static files section and improves the overall phrasing of the text.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to demonstrate proper HTML escaping for user-provided data. It modifies the example return statements for username and subpath variables to use the escape function, preventing potential security vulnerabilities in the displayed output.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the views guide where the `register_api` function was shown with an incorrect parameter name. It updates the example to use `name` instead of `url`, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the actual API signature.
This commit corrects a typo in the Eventlet deployment documentation. It fixes the formatting of the `wsgi.server` reference in the `docs/deploying/eventlet.rst` file to ensure proper rendering.

Flask now requires the blinker library, making signals always available to users. The `signals_available` attribute is deprecated, and the `Namespace` class in `src/flask/signals.py` is updated to reflect this change.
This documentation update reorganizes the SQLAlchemy import statements in the patterns guide. It moves the Table import to a separate code block to clarify usage contexts.

This commit enhances the test suite for Flask's test client by adding checks for session persistence during redirects. It updates the TestToolsTestCase class to verify that session data is correctly maintained or cleared across requests, improving coverage of the testing module's behavior.

This commit expands the test suite for Flask's extension import hook to cover new package naming conventions. It updates the import logic in the ExtImportHookTestCase to recognize modules starting with flask_ and flaskext., ensuring correct resolution for both old and new extension styles.

The server now listens on the loopback address 127.0.0.1 by default instead of all interfaces. This change resolves compatibility issues with Chrome browsers. The update is documented in the CHANGES file for version 0.2.
This commit corrects a typo in the FastCGI deployment documentation. It adds a missing closing parenthesis to the lighttpd configuration example, ensuring the code snippet is syntactically valid.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask application where after-request functions were not executed when an error handler was triggered. The `Flask` class now uses a new `finalize_request` method to ensure these postprocessing steps run for both standard requests and error responses.

The migration script now correctly handles import statements wrapped in parentheses, preventing malformed output during code conversion. This fix updates the `fix_from_imports` function to use a new helper, `_get_modules`, for proper string formatting. A new test case verifies this edge case.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the BlueprintSetupState class within the Flask blueprints module. It fixes the misspelling of "blueprint" in the docstring for the __init__ method, ensuring accurate documentation for users.

This commit finalizes the 1.0 release by updating the changelog with the release date and correcting the project links in setup.py. It changes the code and issue tracker URLs from the Pallets Sphinx themes repository to the main Flask repository.

This commit corrects several typos in the CHANGES.rst file, including fixing the spelling of "implicitly" and correcting a grammatical error regarding the test client's ability to preserve request context. These changes improve the accuracy and readability of the project's release notes.

This commit adds a new documentation page explaining the lazy loading pattern for views and updates the tutorial with explicit chapter links. It also adjusts the documentation configuration to hide the module index and Sphinx branding. The changes primarily affect the docs module and the minitwit example.

This commit corrects a documentation typo in the testing guide, changing "close the function" to "close the file." It also reverts a previous change in the main Flask module that added an unnecessary blank line.

This commit updates various development and testing dependencies to their latest versions, including security patches for cryptography and charset-normalizer. It also bumps the pre-commit hook versions and makes a minor adjustment to the `get_root_path` function in `src/flask/helpers.py`.

This commit updates the documentation to describe the new error handler system introduced in version 1.0. It explains how developers can register custom views to display user-friendly error pages for specific exceptions. The changes affect the error handling, quickstart, and upgrading documentation files.

This commit introduces a migration script to convert legacy Flask extension imports to the modern namespace format. The `migrate` function in `scripts/flaskext_migrate.py` rewrites import statements to replace the old `flask.ext` prefix with the new `flask_` style.
This commit fixes a spelling error in the debugging documentation. It corrects the word "controled" to "controlled" in the file docs/debugging.rst.

This commit updates the documentation for the application context teardown function to reflect that it now accepts an exception argument. The change clarifies the expected signature for the `teardown_db` example in the `appcontext` module.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for the Flask class. It fixes a typo in the module name referenced within a docstring, ensuring the text accurately describes how SQL queries are picked up.

This commit expands the documentation for application factories by explaining how to initialize extensions like Flask-SQLAlchemy. It clarifies that extension objects are not bound to a single app, allowing one instance to serve multiple applications.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask quickstart guide explaining how the framework handles URL redirects and trailing slashes. It clarifies that routes defined with a trailing slash behave like folders, ensuring unique and canonical URLs for users.

The lock workflow now explicitly requests write permissions for issues and pull requests, ensuring it can function correctly under stricter security defaults. It also adds a concurrency group to prevent overlapping executions.
This commit corrects minor typos in the favicon documentation. It capitalizes "Flask" and changes "webserver" to the standard "web server" in the docs/patterns/favicon.rst file.

This commit updates the versions of pyupgrade, reorder_python_imports, and black in the pre-commit configuration. It ensures the project uses the latest stable releases of these code formatting and linting tools.

This commit makes the Flask documentation build reproducible by using the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH environment variable to determine the copyright year. It modifies the docs/conf.py module to replace the current system time with a fixed timestamp, ensuring consistent output across builds.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that the current development versions of Jinja2 and Werkzeug are required. It also adds a section directing users to the official website for prebuilt documentation or the local docs folder for source files.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask testing suite to verify that session data persists correctly after a redirect. It ensures the test client maintains session state across requests, addressing a potential bug where sessions might be lost during redirects.

This commit introduces documentation files to track the approval status of Flask extensions. It records details such as approval dates, versions, and licenses for packages like Flask-Babel and Flask-SQLAlchemy. The changes aim to improve transparency in the extension review process.

This commit updates the documentation for Flask's JSONEncoder to clarify that Decimal types are serialized as strings. It adds this missing detail to the API reference and the class docstring to improve clarity for users.

Updates the GitHub Actions lock workflow to use the correct option names for version 3. This change ensures the workflow correctly configures the inactivity periods for locking issues and pull requests.

This commit prevents the extension importer from setting dotted attribute names on the flask.ext module, which could cause unexpected namespace pollution. The change modifies the _ExtensionImporter class to only set attributes for simple module names. A new test case verifies that no dotted keys remain in the module dictionary after imports.
This commit adds the greenlet package to the project's test dependencies. It ensures the library is available when running tests via tox, supporting features that require greenlet.
This commit fixes a documentation error in the Flask application class. It corrects the reference to the Werkzeug test utility from a function to a class within the test request context method.

This commit updates the Read the Docs configuration to explicitly pin the Python version to 3.10. It ensures the documentation build uses a consistent Python environment, preventing potential build failures due to version ambiguity.

This commit removes the deprecated `g` property from the `RequestContext` class in Flask. Users who previously accessed `g` through the request context will now encounter an error, as they must use the application context instead.

This commit renames the documentation changelog file to "changes" and updates the documentation index to reflect the new name. It also clarifies the license section title to specify the BSD-3-Clause license.

This commit fixes the JSON availability test in the Flask module by conditionally importing the `json` helper only when it is available. This prevents import errors in environments where the JSON library is missing, ensuring the application loads correctly.

This commit modifies the `DispatchingApp` class in `flask/cli.py` to load the application in a background thread during development. This change speeds up initial requests by preventing the server from blocking while the application is imported.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.0.3 to 3.0.4. It modifies the pinned dependency versions in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the latest patch release.

This commit resolves static type checking errors reported by Pyright across the Flask codebase. It updates type annotations in modules like `app.py`, `blueprints.py`, and `cli.py` to satisfy the type checker, ensuring the project passes strict type validation.

This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the `render_template_string` function in `flask/templating.py`. It updates the parameter name from `template_name` to `source` to accurately reflect the function's argument.
The test suite in `tests/flask_tests.py` now includes example application tests for Flaskr and MiniTwit. It also conditionally skips JSON-related tests if the required JSON library is not available.
This commit initializes the changelog for version 1.0.1 by adding a new section to the CHANGES.rst file. It marks the release as unreleased, preparing the documentation for upcoming changes.

This commit fixes several typos in the documentation files, including correcting "een" to "been" and "undoubtably" to "undoubtedly" in the HTML FAQ. It also adjusts spacing in a code example within the quickstart guide.

This commit adds support for the Partitioned cookie attribute, allowing third-party cookies in iframes to persist across different sites. It introduces the `SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED` configuration option to the `Flask` app and updates the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` to apply this attribute when saving sessions.

The CLI loader now correctly passes keyword arguments to the `create_app` function. This fixes an issue where the app factory would fail if it expected `**kwargs`. The change is implemented in the `call_factory` function within the Flask CLI module.

The `send_from_directory` function in `flask/helpers.py` now raises a `BadRequest` error instead of crashing when an invalid file name is provided. This change ensures that malformed file path inputs are handled gracefully with a proper HTTP response.

This documentation update demonstrates how to register multiple URL rules for a single function endpoint. It modifies the example in the lazy loading patterns guide to show a helper function that iterates through a list of URL rules.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions checkout step in the test workflow from version 2 to version 3. It ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest major release of the checkout action for compatibility and security improvements.

This commit fixes a cross-site scripting vulnerability in Flask's JSON serialization by ensuring all forward slashes are escaped. The `_tojson_filter` function now checks if the underlying JSON library already escapes slashes and applies manual escaping if necessary to prevent script injection.

This commit moves the `_PackageBoundObject` class and related helper functions from `flask.helpers` to `flask.scaffold`, renaming the class to `Scaffold`. It consolidates package path resolution logic within the scaffold module, simplifying imports for the `Flask` application class.

This commit corrects the documentation for the FlaskClient class in flask/testing.py. It ensures that the word "with" is properly formatted as inline code in the docstrings for the class and the session_transaction method.

This commit resolves type-checking errors by configuring mypy to ignore missing imports for the cryptography module. It also updates the test environment to automatically install required type stubs during execution.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to use the new assert_in and assert_not_in helper methods instead of manual string checks. It adds these helpers to the FlaskTestCase class to simplify assertions across various test modules.

This commit updates the pip-compile-multi pre-commit hook from version 2.4.6 to 2.5.0. It modifies the .pre-commit-config.yaml file to ensure the project uses the latest stable release of this dependency management tool.

This commit updates the minimum required Werkzeug version to 2.3.7. It modifies the `get_version` function in `flask.cli` and the `FlaskClient` class in `flask.testing` to retrieve version information using `importlib.metadata` instead of direct module imports.
The package version in the setup configuration is updated from 0.1 to 0.2. This change reflects the new release version for the head module.
This commit corrects a minor grammatical typo in the quickstart documentation. It changes the article before the HTTP status code in the description of how string return values are handled.

This commit adds support for template context processors in the Flask application class, allowing developers to inject custom data into templates. It introduces a default processor that automatically provides request, session, and g objects to the template context.

This commit fixes the project layout diagram in the tutorial documentation by replacing non-breaking space characters with standard spaces. This ensures the file tree renders correctly in the user's browser without misaligned characters.

This commit removes the static `importerror.py` test application and updates the `TestNoImports` class in `test_helpers.py`. The test now dynamically creates the necessary file within a temporary directory, making the test suite more self-contained and reducing reliance on external test fixtures.

This commit adds a test case to verify that application-wide error handlers registered via a Blueprint work correctly. It ensures the handler catches 403 errors triggered from both the main Flask app and other registered Blueprints. The changes are located in the test_blueprints.py module.

This commit removes outdated documentation files, including the advanced foreword and various pattern guides. It cleans up the project's documentation structure by deleting obsolete content related to Flask's internal design and configuration.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions for black and isort to ensure consistent code formatting and import sorting.

This commit introduces blueprint-based template loading by adding a new DispatchingJinjaLoader and Environment class to the templating module. It updates the Flask application to manage blueprints and pass the app instance to the Jinja environment, enabling templates to be resolved from registered blueprints.

This commit removes a legacy fallback in the Flask class that handled older Werkzeug versions lacking the allowed_methods method. It simplifies the make_default_options_response function by directly calling the modern API, eliminating unnecessary exception handling and outdated code.

This commit refactors the test discovery logic in the Flask test suite by consolidating the separate functions for finding tests and their names into a single `find_all_tests` function. It also removes the unused `common_prefix` variable and updates the `BetterLoader` class to support this streamlined approach.

This commit fixes a documentation build failure caused by a missing CONTRIBUTING.rst file. It updates the MANIFEST.in file to include this file in the distribution, ensuring the documentation can be built successfully.

This commit removes the six dependency from the Flask codebase, replacing its utility functions with native Python 3 equivalents or internal compatibility shims. It updates modules like helpers, json, and templating to ensure the application runs without requiring the external six library.

The `get_version` function in `flask/cli.py` now outputs a simplified Python version string and moves the Werkzeug import inside the function. This change cleans up the version display logic for the `flask --version` command.

This commit reorganizes the test suite by moving all JSON-related tests from the general helpers module into a dedicated test file. This change improves code organization and maintainability without altering any application behavior or fixing bugs.

This commit updates the tox configuration to include specific dependency versions for testing. It adds the lowest supported version of Click and the development versions of both Click and MarkupSafe to the test environment dependencies.

This commit fixes an infinite redirect loop that occurred when using blueprints with empty URL defaults. It modifies the `Flask.add_url_rule` method to ensure empty default dictionaries are converted to `None`, working around a known Werkzeug bug.

This commit updates the changelog to document a new feature in the `add_url_rule` method. It notes that users can now disable automatic OPTIONS handling for non-class view functions by passing a specific keyword argument.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in a comment within the `RequestContext` class in `flask/ctx.py`. It changes the phrasing to accurately describe the removal of deprecated functionality, improving code readability without altering behavior.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask class clarifying that server errors are suppressed by a generic error page unless debug mode is enabled. It explains that enabling the interactive debugger without debug mode will not catch exceptions, guiding users on how to configure the run method correctly.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask where an empty static folder path resulted in an invalid default static URL route. The `_get_static_url_path` method in `flask/helpers.py` now returns an empty string instead of a leading slash when the folder name is empty, ensuring the application initializes correctly.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.0.1 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number, ensuring the library reports the correct version to users.

This commit fixes a test suite failure on Python 2.5 by adding a future import for the with statement. The change ensures the view tests in flask/testsuite/views.py run correctly on older Python versions.
This commit updates development dependencies to their latest versions. It bumps the setup-uv and actions/cache actions in the GitHub workflow files and refreshes the uv.lock file.

The CI test workflow now uses version 2 of the GitHub Actions cache step instead of version 1. This update ensures the build process utilizes the latest supported caching functionality for dependencies.

This commit removes a trailing blank line from the test file for request context handling. It applies automated formatting fixes to the test suite, specifically targeting the dynamic cookie name test. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit updates the project's README to replace the first-person singular pronoun "I" with the first-person plural "We." This change ensures the documentation's tone is consistent with the rest of the file.

This commit updates the Flask tutorial documentation to clarify how to start the application. It adds the specific command to run the script and describes the expected startup message, improving the setup instructions for new users.

This commit adds support for the SameSite attribute on session cookies, allowing developers to restrict cross-site cookie transmission for improved security. The feature is implemented in the SecureCookieSessionInterface class within the sessions module and controlled via the new SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE configuration option.

This commit corrects minor typographical errors and formatting inconsistencies across several documentation files, including the API reference, deployment guides, and tutorials. It improves the clarity and professionalism of the project's written documentation without altering any functional code.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the API documentation for the JSON module. It fixes the typo "ahve" to "have" in the description of method serialization behavior.

This commit prevents the greenlet package from being installed on Python 3.11 by adding a version constraint to the development and test requirements. This change ensures that greenlet-dependent tests are excluded on that Python version, avoiding potential compatibility issues.

This commit adds Python version compatibility metadata to the package configuration. It ensures PyPI correctly displays which Python versions are supported, preventing users from attempting to install the package on unsupported versions like Python 3.0 through 3.3.

This commit adds a documentation note to the API reference explaining that Werkzeug simplifies redirect URLs containing default values using a 301 status code. It clarifies the underlying behavior for users configuring URL rules.

This commit updates the change log to clarify that the `provide_automatic_options` parameter is now supported directly in the `add_url_rule` method. It corrects the documentation to remove the incorrect reference to `**kwargs` for this feature.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the Flask quickstart guide where the unescaped character was incorrectly displayed as a backslash sequence. It corrects the example output for the `striptags` method to show the proper right-pointing double angle quotation mark.

This commit updates the project's README file to correct the placement of the documentation link. It moves the reference to the Flask documentation within the links section to ensure proper formatting.

This commit fixes a bug in the `_matching_loader_thinks_module_is_package` function within `flask/helpers.py` where namespace packages were not correctly identified. It updates the loader type check to use class attributes instead of instance attributes, ensuring accurate detection of frozen importlib loaders.

This commit documents that HTTP headers must be set before a streaming response begins, as they cannot be modified once the body is sent. It clarifies this requirement in the streaming and templating documentation, noting that accessing the session inside a generator may prevent necessary headers from being set.

This commit fixes several typos in the comments within the ExtensionImporter class in scripts/flaskext_compat.py. It corrects misspelled words and missing punctuation to improve the clarity of the documentation.

This commit updates the pinned versions of several development, documentation, and testing dependencies. It bumps packages such as filelock, pre-commit, and tox to their latest releases across the requirements files.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` no longer raises an error when it cannot infer a MIME type from a file name. Instead, it defaults to a generic binary type, allowing file downloads to proceed successfully.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the Flask documentation for deferred callbacks. It changes the instruction to call "then" to "them" when referring to callback functions attached to the `flask.g` object.
Updates the Jinja2 template documentation link in the quickstart guide to use HTTPS instead of HTTP. This ensures the documentation reference uses a secure connection.

This commit clarifies the documentation for Flask's `url_for` helper and the `SCRIPT_NAME` configuration value. It specifies that `APPLICATION_ROOT` and `SERVER_NAME` settings only apply when generating URLs outside of an active request context.

This commit removes several tests from the test_reqctx.py module that verified how Flask handles invalid or IDNA-encoded host headers. These tests were likely dependent on Werkzeug's specific behavior for validating hostnames, which is no longer relevant.

This commit improves the test request context in the Flask application class by correctly handling server names with ports instead of blindly appending them. It also updates the testing client to build a proper initial environment based on the application's configuration.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the upgrading documentation. It changes the word "cought" to "caught" in the description of exception handling behavior. The change is located in the docs/upgrading.rst file.

This commit removes the development version of the blinker library from the test requirements to prevent test failures caused by broken Python 3 compatibility. It ensures the test suite uses a stable version of the dependency instead of the unstable development branch.

This commit resolves a type-checking error in the Flask Request class caused by updated Werkzeug endpoint types. It suppresses the specific mypy warning on the endpoint property to ensure the code passes static analysis without altering runtime behavior.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.12.1 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.

This commit adds support for loading Jinja2 templates from Flask modules, allowing templates to be discovered in module folders alongside the main application. It introduces a new dispatching loader class to handle template resolution across these locations.

The tutorial documentation and the Flaskr example application were updated to reflect the new Flask script structure. This change modifies how the database initialization function is defined and invoked within the example code.

This commit fixes a bug where exceptions raised before entering a request or app context were incorrectly passed to teardown handlers. It updates the push methods in the AppContext and RequestContext classes to clear previous exceptions, ensuring teardown functions receive the correct error state.

This commit adds documentation to the quickstart guide explaining how to wrap the internal WSGI application with middlewares. It also introduces a new method, `create_url_adapter`, to the `Flask` class for generating URL adapters during request processing.

This commit fixes a bug where template paths starting with "./" failed to load in module-based Flask applications. The `_DispatchingJinjaLoader` class now normalizes template paths using `posixpath.normpath` before attempting to load them, ensuring consistent path resolution.

This commit updates the documentation for the new Flask CLI, specifically adding guidance on how to use factory functions. The changes primarily affect the CLI documentation and the `prepare_exec_for_file` function in `flask/cli.py`.

This commit updates the `get_root_path` function in `flask/helpers.py` to correctly handle interactive sessions and zip-imported modules. It prevents errors when the import name is `__main__` or when the loader lacks a `get_filename` method, ensuring the root path is resolved reliably.

This commit standardizes documentation and code comments to use American English spelling, changing "behaviour" to "behavior." It updates the Flask class, jsonify, and send_file functions, along with various documentation files, to ensure consistent terminology across the project.

This commit refactors the Flask library by moving template rendering functions and the Jinja loader class into a new dedicated module. This commit updates the documentation for the templated view decorator to clarify that non-dictionary return values are passed through unchanged. This allows users to return redirects or simple strings directly from the decorated function.

This commit restores the behavior where pushing an application context automatically opens the session. It modifies the `AppContext` class in `src/flask/ctx.py` to ensure the session is available when the context is pushed, rather than only when explicitly accessed.

This commit standardizes the error handling for setup methods in Flask's Scaffold, Blueprint, and Flask classes. It replaces the previous boolean check with a new `_check_setup_finished` method that raises an assertion error if a setup method is called after the first request, preventing inconsistent application state.
Fixes a typo in the testing documentation where "Ify ou" was corrected to "If you." This improves the readability of the guide for accessing test client sessions.

This commit clarifies that Flask's teardown_appcontext method only receives unhandled exceptions, not those caught by error handlers. It updates the documentation in the Flask class and adds regression tests to verify this specific behavior.

This commit updates the Flask README to clarify that the development version requires Jinja 2.4 and Werkzeug 0.6.1. It replaces outdated information about refactoring with specific version numbers and installation instructions using easy_install.

This commit removes the TestBasicFunctionality class from the test suite in tests/test_basic.py. It eliminates the associated test methods that verify core Flask application behaviors, such as request handling and error management.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the docstring for the `preprocess_request` method within the `Flask` class. It clarifies that the method calls each `before_request` function without arguments, improving the accuracy of the documentation.

This commit fixes an issue where registering a Flask Blueprint with a new name failed to apply certain request hooks. The `Blueprint.register` method now distinguishes between the first instance registration and the first name registration, ensuring hooks trigger correctly for both old and new names.

Updates the GitHub Actions workflows to use newer versions of the lock-threads and PyPI publish actions. This ensures the repository's automated locking and publishing processes run with the latest available features and security patches.

This commit removes outdated documentation for the `UpgradeSecureCookieSession` and `UpgradeSecureCookieSessionInterface` classes from the API reference. It also deletes the corresponding section in the upgrading guide that explained how to use these classes for session migration.

This commit updates the test configuration to prevent running older Werkzeug versions against Python 3. It modifies the tox.ini file to restrict Python 3 test environments to only the release and development dependency sets, excluding the lowest version set.

This commit updates the testing documentation to remove the word "trivially" from a description of overriding a user. The change clarifies that the process is not necessarily simple, correcting a potentially misleading statement in the docs/testing.rst file.

This commit fixes an issue where using the `json` argument with Flask's test client incorrectly pushed and popped an extra application context. The change modifies the `flask.json` module to accept an optional app parameter, preventing unnecessary context management during testing.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the view decorators guide. It removes unnecessary single quotes from the example template name string, ensuring the code snippet accurately reflects the intended behavior.

This commit corrects the Apache configuration example in the deployment documentation by replacing the incorrect ScriptName directive with the proper ScriptAlias directive. This ensures users configure their web server correctly to map the application path.

This commit begins the development cycle for Flask version 2.1.3 by updating the version string in the main package initialization. It also documents a change to inline optional imports that are only required for specific CLI commands.

This commit adds documentation for running Flask applications with the Gunicorn WSGI server. It explains how to use Gunicorn with eventlet and greenlet support, providing a simple command example for deployment.

This commit adds a changelog entry documenting a fix for unprintable Unicode characters in the Host header. It notes that using the built-in RequestContext now returns an HTTP 400 response instead of an HTTP 500 error.

This commit updates the contributing guide to clarify that the issue tracker is exclusively for Flask bugs and feature requests, not general support questions. It also removes the outdated reference to the IRC channel and refines the Stack Overflow search tip.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the error message raised by the MethodView class in flask/views.py. It changes the assertion text from "Not implemented method" to "Unimplemented method" for better clarity when a request method is not supported.
This commit adds a missing test template file to the nested directory. It ensures the test suite has the required resource for validating nested template rendering.

This commit adds a `session_transaction` method to the `FlaskClient` class in `flask/testing.py`. It allows developers to easily modify session data directly within test environments without making full requests.

This commit corrects a documentation typo in the `Response` class within `flask.py`. It updates the attribute reference from `request_class` to `response_class`, ensuring the documentation accurately describes how to customize the response type.

This commit updates the Python 3 documentation by removing outdated section headers and clarifying version requirements. It specifies that Flask 0.10 and Werkzeug 0.9 were the first releases to support Python 3, helping users identify compatible library versions.

This commit moves the core application, blueprint, and scaffold modules into a new sansio directory. It prepares the codebase for a refactor that separates framework-agnostic logic from Flask-specific implementations, following the structure used by Werkzeug.

This commit updates the lock-threads GitHub Action from version 2 to version 3 in the repository's workflow configuration. The change ensures the automated thread locking process uses the latest major release of the tool.

This commit adds tests to verify the request processing hooks of the Flask Blueprint class. It ensures that before and after request handlers execute correctly for both blueprint-specific and application-wide requests.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to improve cross-references and clarify the development server section. It modifies the quickstart guide to use direct document links and rewrites the server documentation to better explain the `run` command.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the static file tutorial where the localhost URL was missing the default port number. This commit simplifies the `Request.json` property in `flask/wrappers.py` by removing an unnecessary intermediate variable. It directly returns the parsed JSON data, streamlining the code without changing the user-facing behavior.

This commit adds documentation explaining the lifecycle of a Flask application and individual requests. It introduces a new guide detailing application setup and request handling to help users understand the framework's internal structure.

This commit corrects minor grammatical and spelling errors in the Flask CLI documentation. It fixes typos such as "instanciate" and improves phrasing in the `docs/cli.rst` file for better readability.

This commit fixes a bug in the FlaskClient class where nested request contexts were not fully cleaned up when using the test client as a context manager. It ensures that all preserved contexts are popped upon exiting the block, preventing resource leaks.

This commit fixes the Flask command-line help text to correctly display the required file extension for the FLASK_APP environment variable. Previously, the example suggested using "hello" instead of "hello.py," which would cause the command to fail on Windows. The change updates the documentation string in flask/cli.py.

This commit adds documentation for a new templating decorator pattern. It explains how this decorator allows view functions to return a dictionary of values, which are then automatically passed to a specified template for rendering.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `View.as_view` method in Flask's `views` module. It specifies that the `name` argument is not forwarded to the view class constructor, correcting a previous ambiguity in the docstring.
This commit updates the pip-tools dependency from version 5.2.0 to 5.2.1 in the development requirements. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the package management tool.

This commit adds coverage exclusion markers to `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks across multiple Flask modules, including `app.py` and `blueprints.py`. This prevents code coverage tools from reporting these type-only imports as untested, ensuring accurate coverage metrics without changing runtime behavior.

This commit replaces the static image logo with a scalable vector graphic for the Flask project. It updates the README and documentation configuration to display the new SVG logo, removing the previous PNG files.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the API reference where the default converter was incorrectly named "unicode" instead of "string." It updates the description in the API documentation to accurately reflect the available converter names.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flaskr testing documentation where the example code incorrectly deleted the production database instead of the test database.
