This commit clarifies the documentation for changing the row factory in SQLite3 to improve tutorial readability. It explains how to use dictionaries or Row objects for query results within the get_db function.

This commit refactors several tests in tests/test_blueprints.py to utilize the shared app and client fixtures. It removes redundant manual setup code for creating Flask applications and test clients, streamlining the test suite.

This commit updates the documentation for the Flask module support. It adds a new section to the API reference for Module objects and expands the docstring for the Module class to explain its role in organizing larger applications.

This commit improves the documentation by adding a cross-reference from the foreword to the design principles section. It also clarifies in the design document that extensions may depend on Jinja, even if users choose a different templating language.
This commit adds a shebang line to the `run-tests.py` script. This change allows the file to be executed directly as a command-line program without explicitly invoking the Python interpreter.

This commit updates the documentation for SQLAlchemy patterns to reflect a change in the official documentation URL structure. It corrects the link to the declarative extension guide in the `docs/patterns/sqlalchemy.rst` file, ensuring users are directed to the correct page.

This commit updates the Flask CLI documentation to improve wording and formatting, and replaces a screenshot with a smaller, optimized version. It also corrects the build directory configuration in the tox setup to fix build issues.

This commit ensures that Flask processes blueprints in the exact order they were registered, specifically for template loading. It introduces a new `iter_blueprints` method to the `Flask` class and updates the `DispatchingJinjaLoader` to respect this sequence.

This commit updates the asgiref dependency from version 3.4.0 to 3.4.1 in the development and test requirements files. It is a patch-level update that likely includes minor bug fixes or improvements to the asynchronous support library.

This commit marks the official release of version 3.0.3 by updating the project's changelog. It changes the status from "Unreleased" to "Released" with the date April 7, 2024, in the CHANGES.rst file.

This commit ensures that the session is marked as accessed when checking for key existence or length, preventing unnecessary session updates. It modifies the `RequestContext` class to track these operations and updates the `Flask` app to use the internal session reference.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flask documentation for the views module. It clarifies that HTTP methods map to class methods rather than functions, ensuring the description of MethodView is accurate.

This commit updates the Black code formatter from version 22.12.0 to 23.1.0 in the pre-commit configuration. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the tool for consistent code formatting.

This commit updates the extension development documentation to clarify that the class-based approach provides a manager object for handling database connections. It also corrects the example code to use the request context stack instead of the global object for accessing the database.

This commit updates the extension development documentation to clarify maintenance requirements for approved Flask extensions. It specifies that projects must secure a new maintainer with full hosting and PyPI access if the original author steps away, defaulting to the Flask core team if none is found.

This commit adds a new `tox-test` target to the Makefile, allowing developers to run the Flask test suite via tox. It also introduces a `tox.ini` configuration file to define the Python environments and test commands, and updates `.gitignore` to exclude the `.tox` directory.

This commit updates the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` to use the `unicodedata` module directly for filename normalization, replacing the previous import. It also adds documentation noting support for UTF-8 filenames and refactors tests to verify that the `filename*` parameter is omitted for ASCII headers.

This commit adds a new CONTRIBUTING.rst file to the Flask project. It provides guidelines for users on how to report issues and where to seek support, improving the project's documentation for new contributors.

Flask no longer sets the session cookie domain by default, preventing modern browsers from treating it as a subdomain match. The `SessionInterface` class no longer falls back to `SERVER_NAME` for the domain, and warnings for localhost or IP addresses are removed.

This commit adds a hint to the Flask tutorial documentation explaining where to place new code. It guides users to group module-level functions together, such as request handlers, below the database initialization function. The change is located in the database connection tutorial section.

This commit improves error handling in the Flask CLI when a factory function is called with incorrect arguments. It prevents the CLI from incorrectly treating a TypeError as a missing application, ensuring the original error is raised instead. The changes affect the `find_best_app` and `find_app_by_string` functions in `flask/cli.py`.

This commit updates the project configuration to include the typing test directory in the static type checking process. It ensures that type annotations within the test suite are validated alongside the main Flask source code.
This commit corrects a grammatical error in the package documentation. It clarifies that modules with decorators must be imported within the `__init__.py` file, rather than "when in" it.

This commit updates the application dispatch documentation to reflect a change in the default backend interface path. The example now shows the backend running on `/backend` instead of `/admin`, aligning the docs with the new naming convention.

This commit merges the request context into the app context, making the former a deprecated alias. This simplifies internal context tracking in the Flask application and changes how contexts are managed during request dispatch.

This commit updates the contributing documentation to include explicit git commands for creating branches, checking them out, and committing changes. It clarifies the workflow for new contributors by providing specific terminal instructions for these common tasks.
This commit introduces a mini blogging application named Flaskr to serve as a tutorial example. It adds the main application logic, database schema, templates, and tests to the examples directory.
The JSONEncoder in flask/json.py now supports serializing UUID objects. Previously, attempting to encode a UUID would raise an error, but it is now converted to a string.

This commit updates the greenlet dependency from version 0.4.15 to 0.4.16 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the greenlet library for its testing environment.

This commit updates the Flaskr and Minitwit examples to use modern SQLite connection patterns, replacing older methods with context-based resource management. It also adds a new section to the application context documentation explaining how to cache and deallocate resources like database connections per request.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's Blueprint class that prevented registering the same blueprint multiple times with different names. It allows users to register a blueprint with a custom name via the register method, enabling distinct URL prefixes for identical blueprint objects.
This commit updates the Windows installation documentation to improve clarity and structure. It refines the instructions for adding the Python Scripts folder to the system PATH environment variable.

This commit removes deprecated parameter names from Flask's file sending utilities. Users must now use the new names, such as `download_name` instead of `attachment_filename`, when calling `send_file` or `send_from_directory`. The changes affect the `helpers` module.
This commit adds David Lord to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's attribution records to include his name under the "Patches and Suggestions" section.
This commit corrects grammatical errors in the file upload documentation. It updates the fileuploads.rst file to fix typos in the description of payload limits.

This commit adds documentation for the `send_from_directory` helper function in Flask. It includes a performance note recommending the use of `X-Sendfile` or webserver configuration to serve files directly, improving efficiency.

This commit adds documentation for Flask's signal system, which allows decoupled communication between the framework and extensions. It introduces a new signals page and updates the API reference and table of contents to include this new section.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, and testing dependencies to their latest versions. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revisions for flake8 and isort in the configuration file.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's CLI where Windows file paths containing a colon followed by a slash caused app import failures. The `ScriptInfo.load_app` method now ignores such colons when splitting the import path, allowing valid Windows paths to be loaded correctly.

This commit updates the test suite for the sendfile helper to handle a behavior change in Python 3.8. The test for sending a directory now expects a NotFound error instead of a BadRequest error on newer Python versions. This ensures the test passes correctly across different Python releases.

This commit renames the `get_package_path` function to `get_root_path` in `flask/helpers.py` to clarify its purpose and prevent confusion with other path utilities. The update also adjusts the internal call within the `_PackageBoundObject` class to use the new name.

This commit removes an unused variable from the FastCGI deployment documentation example. It clarifies the script name stripping logic by eliminating a redundant attribute that was not utilized in the provided code snippet.

This commit adds a warning to the SecureCookieSessionInterface when a session cookie domain is set to an IP address. It introduces a new is_ip helper function in flask/helpers.py to detect IP addresses, which is used by the save_session method to trigger the warning.

This commit removes the conditional logic that checked for the availability of a JSON library, assuming it is always present. It simplifies the imports in the main Flask module and eliminates the internal assertion and fallback mechanisms in the helpers module.

This commit rewrites the Flask tutorial documentation and updates the corresponding example application. It modernizes the codebase to use blueprints and a factory pattern, improving the structure of the tutorial project.

This commit fixes the Fabric deployment documentation to ensure the local command returns a string. It explicitly sets the capture parameter to true, as the default behavior changed in Fabric 1.0. The update is located in the fabric.rst file.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the Django documentation for error pages. It fixes the typo "uncought" to "uncaught" in the description of how internal server error handlers process exceptions.

This commit finalizes the release of version 2.1.1 by updating the project's changelog. It changes the status from unreleased to a specific release date, marking the version as officially available to users.

The Flask test client now supports a `json` parameter in `make_test_environ_builder`, allowing users to easily send JSON payloads in test requests. This feature automatically serializes the data and sets the appropriate content type, while preventing conflicts if both `json` and `data` arguments are provided.

This commit updates the documentation link for the Flask-Uploads extension in the file uploads pattern guide. It replaces the outdated PythonHosted URL with the current Read the Docs address, ensuring users are directed to the correct project documentation.

Flask now uses the standard library's json module exclusively, removing the dependency on simplejson. This change eliminates the need for custom encoding detection and simplifies string translation logic within the JSON handling functions.

This commit updates the installation documentation to improve the flow of instructions. It modifies the text in the `docs/installation.rst` file to guide users more smoothly toward activating Flask in their shell.

This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to clarify that setting `app.debug` or `app.config['DEBUG']` does not work with the `flask` command-line script. It instructs users to export the `FLASK_DEBUG` environment variable instead to enable debug mode when running the development server.

This commit removes the Flask-Genshi entry from the list of extensions considered for unlisting. It corrects the status of the package in the extreview documentation, ensuring it is no longer flagged for removal.

This commit updates the installation tutorial documentation to provide more comprehensive resources for understanding project packaging. It replaces a single link with two distinct references, directing users to both a packaging tutorial and a detailed guide on distributing packages.

This commit fixes an issue where the Flask command-line interface failed when running with an external debugger on Windows. It updates the main function in the CLI module to explicitly pass command-line arguments, ensuring the tool works correctly in that environment.

This commit removes redundant hyperlinks from the security documentation, leaving only the plain text names for headers like Content Security Policy and HSTS. The change affects the `docs/security.rst` file to simplify the display of these security header descriptions.

This commit updates the name and description of the GitHub workflow responsible for locking inactive closed issues. It clarifies that the process targets only closed issues to encourage fresh discussions on new topics.

This commit updates various development and build dependencies to their latest versions, including replacing pep517 with pyproject-hooks. It also adjusts the Flask class in src/flask/app.py to ensure compatibility with the updated testing utilities.

This commit updates the test suite to use identity checks instead of equality checks for type comparisons, resolving linting warnings. The changes affect the test_session_special_types and test_teardown_request_handler_error functions in the test_basic.py module.

This commit introduces a new Config class to Flask, allowing users to load application settings from Python files or modules. It updates the Flask application initialization to support this new configuration mechanism and adds corresponding documentation and tests.

This commit updates Flask to use Python's standard urllib.parse module instead of the removed werkzeug.urls utilities, ensuring compatibility with Werkzeug 2.3. It modifies the Flask.url_for method and EnvironBuilder class to handle URL quoting and splitting using the new standard library functions.

This commit stops the Flask development server from automatically passing exceptions to the debugger unless explicitly configured to do so. It removes the default behavior in the `Flask.run` method and `run_command` function that linked the `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` setting to the `passthrough_errors` option.

The `tojson` filter in Flask now escapes exclamation marks following less-than signs to prevent script block injection in HTML5 parsers. This change modifies the `_tojson_filter` function to ensure safer JSON output within web pages.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flaskr example documentation. It updates the README to properly identify the application as "Flaskr" instead of "Flask," ensuring the project name is displayed accurately to users.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the FastCGI deployment documentation. It changes the word "incomming" to "incoming" in the description of how requests are handled.

This commit updates the sphinx-tabs dependency from version 1.3.0 to 2.0.0 in the development and documentation requirements files. This change ensures the project uses the latest version of the Sphinx extension for tabbed content.

This commit fixes a ValueError that occurred when processing certain invalid Range requests. The fix modifies the send_file function in flask/helpers.py to safely handle cases where the file object is None.

The `tojson` filter in Flask now escapes single quotes to prevent breaking HTML attributes when the filter is used within single-quoted tags. This change improves compatibility with frameworks like Angular.js by ensuring the generated JSON is safe for broader HTML contexts.

This commit restructures the Flask package to establish a working import layout for the module. It moves core imports out of the main initialization file into specific submodules like app, helpers, and wrappers. This change ensures that the Flask application and its components load correctly without circular dependency issues.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the CGI deployment guide. It fixes a typo in the `docs/deploying/cgi.rst` file that incorrectly referenced `sys.stdin` instead of `sys.stdout` when describing environment overrides.

This commit updates the pytest configuration in setup.cfg to use the modern `[tool:pytest]` section header instead of the deprecated `[pytest]` format. This change ensures the project's test configuration remains compatible with current tooling standards.

This commit fixes a rendering bug in the Flaskr example where unclosed list item tags caused subsequent content to inherit incorrect styling. It adds the missing closing tags to the show_entries.html template to ensure proper HTML structure.

This commit updates the request context documentation to replace the term "development mode" with "debug mode." It clarifies how exceptions are handled and how context is preserved based on the application's debug setting.

This commit fixes a typo in the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation by removing an incorrect code block directive. It also updates the example commands to include the standard shell prompt prefix for clarity.

This commit corrects version markers in the Flask documentation and source code, changing references from version 1.0 to 0.11. It ensures that features like the CLI, configuration options, and error handling are accurately attributed to the correct release version.

This commit updates the pytest dependency from version 6.2.4 to 6.2.5 in the development and test requirements files. It is a routine patch-level version bump that does not change application behavior or fix specific user-facing bugs.
This commit updates the CHANGES.rst file to add an "Unreleased" section under the Version 3.1.0 heading. It prepares the changelog for new entries by inserting a placeholder for upcoming changes.

This commit updates the file upload documentation to use a set literal instead of the set method for defining allowed extensions. It improves code readability in the fileuploads module without changing application behavior.

This commit updates the pytest dependency from version 6.0.2 to 6.1.1 in the development and test requirements files. It removes the now-unneeded more-itertools package, which was previously required by the older pytest version.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the API documentation. It fixes the typo "JSOn" to "JSON" in the description of the JSON encoder delegation behavior.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask test suite to verify that the application correctly handles URL parameters when a custom character encoding, such as EUC-KR, is configured. It ensures that non-ASCII characters in query strings are properly decoded and returned as UTF-8.
This commit adds the PATCH method to the list of supported HTTP methods in the flask.views module. It allows the MethodView class to handle PATCH requests, which were previously ignored.

This commit updates the documentation for packaging patterns to clarify that the `url_prefix` argument must be explicitly provided when registering modules. It explains that Flask cannot infer URL prefixes from package names, preventing routing errors for users setting up application modules.

Fixes an import error in the Flask test suite by correcting the source of the `reload_module` function. The change updates the import in `flask/testsuite/ext.py` to use the `six.moves` namespace, ensuring compatibility with the `six` library.

Context preservation on exceptions is now handled directly by Flask's RequestContext instead of the test client. This change moves the logic into the core framework to reduce the risk of runaway request contexts during unit tests.

This commit improves the Flask JSON module's behavior when no application context is active. It ensures that default settings for key sorting and encoder/decoder classes are applied in the `_dump_arg_defaults` and `_load_arg_defaults` functions.

This commit updates the Dependabot configuration to target the 2.0.x maintenance branch for dependency updates. It also changes the update schedule to run monthly on Mondays at 16:00 UTC and restricts updates to lockfile-only changes.
This commit corrects the title in the module docstring for the Flask CLI. It changes the reference from "flask.run" to "flask.cli" to accurately reflect the module's purpose.

This commit moves URL matching in Flask's RequestContext to occur after the request context is pushed, rather than during creation. This change allows custom URL converters to access the application and request contexts, enabling features like database lookups during routing.

This commit restructures the Flask deployment documentation by splitting the single `deploying.rst` file into separate, topic-specific pages. It creates new files for CGI, FastCGI, mod_wsgi, and other deployment options, improving navigation and organization for users seeking specific server configurations.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Eventlet deployment documentation. It corrects the placement of a closing parenthesis in the example code for starting a WSGI server, ensuring the command is valid.

This commit removes unused unittest imports from several Flask test modules, including test_appctx, test_blueprints, and test_reqctx. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating redundant dependencies without altering any application behavior or test logic.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the docstring for the `errorhandler` method within the `Flask` class. It fixes the phrasing to accurately describe how the decorator registers a function for a specific error type.

This commit adds a workaround for App Engine environments by explicitly importing the werkzeug module in flask.py. This ensures the dependency is loaded correctly in zip-based setups, preventing potential import errors.

This commit corrects the example usage of the PathDispatcher class in the application dispatch documentation. It removes an incorrect domain argument from the constructor call, ensuring the code snippet accurately reflects the expected interface.

This commit updates the CLI documentation to clarify IDE integration instructions for PyCharm. It distinguishes between the Professional and Community editions, noting that the latter requires manual configuration of the Flask run command. The changes are located in the `docs/cli.rst` file.

The `run_async` function in `flask.helpers` now raises a runtime error if it detects that Werkzeug's fallback ContextVar implementation is being used. This prevents subtle bugs that occur when running async code on Python versions below 3.7, where the fallback does not work correctly across asyncio tasks.

This commit corrects the example Fabric file in the documentation to improve clarity and accuracy. It updates the directory creation command to use an absolute path and fixes the indentation of the installation step.

This commit standardizes the capitalization of metadata field names in the extension review documentation. It updates the approved and unlisted extension lists to use consistent title case for version and license labels.

This commit adds a MANIFEST.in file to ensure the package includes the Makefile, changelog, license, authors, tests, and documentation when building source distributions. It explicitly prunes the documentation build directory to keep the distribution clean.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.1.1 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the lighttpd FastCGI configuration example within the deployment documentation. It changes the incorrect arrow operator to the proper equals-greater-than symbol, ensuring users copy a valid configuration.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the feature request issue template. It ensures the guidance text properly instructs users to include links to relevant specifications or previous discussions.

This commit updates the CLI documentation to clarify how the ScriptInfo object is passed to application factories. It specifies that the object is sent as a keyword argument if the parameter is named script_info, or as a positional argument if the factory accepts a single parameter without explicit parentheses.

This commit fixes a bug in the `_ExtensionImporter` class within the Flask extension module, ensuring that imports from the legacy `flaskext` namespace correctly resolve to the newer `flask_` package format. It also adds a comprehensive test suite to verify that the import hook handles both simple modules and complex package structures accurately.

This commit deprecates the `should_ignore_error` method in the Flask and App classes. Users will now see a warning if they rely on this method to suppress error handling during request dispatch. The change encourages handling errors in teardown handlers instead.

This commit updates the Python version used to generate pip-compile requirements from 3.8 to 3.12. It removes dependencies that are no longer needed for the newer Python version, such as importlib-metadata and exceptiongroup, across multiple requirement files.

This commit updates the Flask documentation foreword by adjusting line wrapping and rephrasing a few sentences for clarity. It modifies the text in the `docs/foreword.rst` file to improve readability without changing the core meaning.

This commit allows developers to customize request size limits per request via the Request class, rather than relying solely on global configuration. It introduces new settings for form memory and part limits, and updates the documentation to explain these resource constraints.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the pyupgrade and reorder_python_imports tools. It ensures the project's automated code checks run with the latest available releases.

This commit adds a `json_dumps` method to the `EnvironBuilder` class in `flask/testing.py`. It allows the builder to serialize JSON data directly, supporting the deprecation of the older `make_test_environ_builder` function.

This commit adds a return type annotation to the `App.__init__` method in the `flask.sansio.app` module. It clarifies that the constructor returns `None`, improving static type checking for users of the Flask application class.
This commit corrects a typo in the testing documentation. It fixes a misspelled word in the description of how after_request functions behave within a test request context.

This documentation update corrects the WSGI server import example in the standalone deployment guide. It replaces the deprecated gevent.wsgi module with gevent.pywsgi to ensure users utilize the current API.

This commit corrects a typo in the styleguide documentation, fixing the phrase "whitespace is absent" to "no whitespace" for clarity. The change updates the general whitespace rules in the docs/styleguide.rst file.

This commit updates the `log` and `main` functions in `scripts/flaskext_tester.py` to use Python 3-compatible print syntax. It ensures the script runs correctly on both Python 2 and Python 3 environments by replacing legacy print statements with function calls.

This commit adds the `APPLICATION_ROOT` configuration variable to the Flask application class. This commit fixes a grammatical error in the documentation for the signals module. It corrects a missing word in the instructions for choosing a signal sender, improving the clarity of the user guide.

The `FlaskClient.session_transaction` method in `flask/testing.py` now raises an error if cookies are not enabled, preventing silent failures during session testing. This change ensures that session transactions explicitly require a valid cookie jar to function correctly.

This commit rewrites the `with_metaclass` helper in `flask/_compat.py` to simplify class creation logic. It removes the previous workaround involving a temporary metaclass subclass, replacing it with a more direct approach.

This commit removes version constraints for Sphinx and sphinx-tabs in the documentation requirements. It allows the build to use newer versions of these packages, resolving previous compatibility issues with docutils.

The `_AppCtxGlobals` class in `flask/ctx.py` is updated to behave like a standard object while adding support for the `in` operator and iteration. A new `get` method allows retrieving attributes without raising errors if they are missing.

This commit cleans up the codebase by removing unused imports and fixing variable naming inconsistencies in the test suite. It also adds a new audit target to the Makefile to support running setup.py audit.

This commit deprecates the `g` property on the `RequestContext` class in Flask. Users accessing `g` through the request context will now receive a warning, as the attribute is scheduled for removal in version 2.2. The change directs developers to access `g` directly or via the application context instead.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to verify that sessions persist when following redirects, a feature previously unsupported by the Werkzeug test client. It modifies the `test_redirect_keep_session` method in `TestToolsTestCase` to conditionally assert session data only when the new `redirect_client` capability is available.
This commit updates the blueprint documentation to include the command for listing URL rules. It clarifies how to inspect the application's URL map by adding the appropriate command to the examples.
This documentation update clarifies how to define a favicon route in Flask. It adds an explicit endpoint name to the example in the favicon pattern guide, ensuring the route is properly identified.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the pyupgrade and black tools. It ensures the project's automated code checks run with the latest available releases of these formatters.

This commit reverts a previous change that attempted to handle BaseExceptions like KeyboardInterrupt in Flask request handlers. It removes the specific error handling logic from the Flask.wsgi_app method and deletes the associated test case, restoring the previous behavior for these exceptions.

The flaskext_migrate.py script now supports converting "import flask.ext.foo" statements to the new "import flask_foo" format. However, it does not update function calls elsewhere in the source code, which may require manual correction.

This commit consolidates the documentation for flashed message examples into a single location within the flashing patterns guide. It updates the template snippet to use a more modern alert style and corrects a variable name inconsistency in the loop.

This commit updates the minimum version of Werkzeug required for the test environment from 2.3.0 to 2.3.3. It modifies the dependency specifications in the Pallets test requirements files to ensure compatibility with the newer Werkzeug release.

This commit updates the python-dotenv dependency from version 0.17.1 to 0.18.0 in the development and test requirements files. It is a routine minor version bump that does not change application behavior or fix specific bugs.

This commit fixes a typo in the Flask quickstart documentation. It corrects the phrase "result object" to "response object" when describing how to modify a response using the `make_response` function.

This commit updates the changelog to document the addition of `template_test` methods. It notes that these new methods complement the existing `template_filter` family, providing users with a new way to define template tests.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 1.0.2.dev in the main module. It marks the start of the next development cycle following the 1.0.1 release.

This commit fixes a bug in the `DispatchingJinjaLoader` class where the `list_templates` method returned incorrect template names when blueprints or modules were used. The change ensures that module-based blueprints are properly handled during the template listing process.

Calling `app.run()` when the application is started via the Flask CLI development server now does nothing instead of starting a second server. This prevents confusing behavior for new users. The change modifies the `Flask.run` method in `flask/app.py`.

This commit stops Flask from intercepting 307 and 308 routing redirects in debug mode, as these statuses preserve the request body. The change updates the `Flask.raise_routing_exception` method and removes the `FormDataRoutingRedirect` helper, preventing unnecessary error messages for valid redirects.

This commit adds upgrade notes to the documentation explaining the transition from Flask Modules to Blueprints. It clarifies that Blueprints require explicit names, unlike the previous automatic naming scheme, and notes that the automatic upgrade script may fail in some cases.

This change ensures that an application context is automatically active for custom CLI commands added to the app or blueprint, removing the need for the `with_appcontext` decorator. The `FlaskGroup` class in `src/flask/cli.py` is updated to handle this context management, simplifying the setup for developers.

This commit adds a new HTML FAQ document to the project documentation. It clarifies the use of HTML5 in Flask examples and addresses common confusion regarding XHTML. The new file is integrated into the main documentation index.

This commit restructures the Flask project by moving the main package into a `src` directory. It updates the build configuration in `setup.py` and `setup.cfg` to correctly locate and install the code from the new path.

This commit refactors JSON handling in Flask by introducing a new JSONMixin class in flask/wrappers.py. It consolidates shared logic for checking JSON content types and parsing data, allowing both Request and Response objects to reuse these capabilities instead of duplicating code.

This commit updates the project's dependency versions across development, documentation, and example environments. It bumps packages such as Flask, Werkzeug, and Redis to newer releases, ensuring compatibility with Python 3.11.

This refactoring updates the JSONTag class in flask/json/tag.py to store the serializer instance during initialization rather than passing it to every method. It also separates the handling of tagged dictionaries and passthrough objects into distinct cases and adds docstrings to clarify the behavior of the serialization methods.

This commit enables static file serving directly within the Flask WSGI application, rather than relying solely on the development server. It modifies the Flask class to wrap the WSGI app with SharedDataMiddleware, ensuring static assets are accessible in all deployment contexts.

Flask's response handling now accepts lists as return values, automatically converting them to JSON responses. Previously, returning a list from a view function would raise an error, but it now works seamlessly alongside dictionaries. This change updates the Flask class and its type definitions to support the new behavior.

This commit adds JSON response handling to the Flask wrappers module, enabling the Response class to parse and expose JSON data. It also introduces a helper function to standardize JSON mimetype detection for both requests and responses.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use version 3.4.0 of the tool. It ensures the project uses the latest available release for its automated code checks.
This commit adds a placeholder entry to the changelog for Flask version 0.12.1. It marks the upcoming release as a bugfix version that has not yet been published.

This commit fixes a typo in the streaming documentation by correcting the word "Now" to "Note." It clarifies the explanation of how yield expressions are sent to the browser in the streaming patterns guide.

The `run_async` function in `flask.helpers` no longer copies the current request context before executing the wrapped coroutine. This change removes unnecessary overhead because modern Python context variables automatically persist across threads, making the previous manual copying step redundant.

This commit changes how Flask handles subdomains for nested blueprints, ensuring a child blueprint's subdomain prefixes the parent's to form a complete domain chain. This behavior in the Blueprint class now mirrors URL prefixing logic, making nested subdomains more intuitive for users.

This commit fixes a typo in a comment within the Flask JSON module. It corrects the capitalization of the word "Figure" in the documentation for the simplejson import fallback. No functional behavior is changed.

Updates the pre-commit configuration to target the 2.2.x release branch for automatic dependency updates. This ensures the project's pre-commit hooks are synchronized with the latest stable release line.
This commit adds Frozen-Flask to the list of approved extensions in the extreview module. It records the approval details, including the version, license, and review date, for the project.

This commit updates the docstring for the `errorhandler` method in the `Flask` class. It clarifies that the parameter accepts either an integer error code or an arbitrary exception class, improving documentation accuracy for users.

This commit fixes an issue in the `RequestContext` class where exceptions were not properly propagated during context cleanup. By explicitly passing the exception to the inner application context's `pop` method, the `RequestContext.pop` function now ensures correct error handling behavior.
This commit updates the project's author list to include Ali Afshar. It modifies the AUTHORS file to credit this individual for patches and suggestions.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the Flask application context documentation. It corrects the phrasing in the `appcontext.rst` file to properly describe the use of the `flask.g` object for storing application-specific information.
This commit corrects a typo in the HTML FAQ documentation. It updates the list of supported closing tags to include the definition term tag instead of the incorrect tag previously listed.

This commit updates documentation links to resolve broken references, specifically changing the Discord invite URL and renaming the "minimal, complete, and verifiable example" link to "minimal reproducible example." This commit improves the LaTeX output of the Flask documentation by enabling the use of parts in the configuration. It restructures the table of contents and updates the main Flask class to support these formatting changes.

This commit updates the Flask configuration documentation to clarify the fallback order for secret keys. It notes that while order is not strictly required, the default implementation tests the last key first, suggesting users list keys from oldest to newest.

This commit updates the README to correct the example log output for a simple Flask application. It changes the code block type to text and replaces the old startup message with the current Flask log format, including the app name and local IP address.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the `Flask.handle_exception` method. It changes the article "an" to "a" before the number 500, ensuring the text reads naturally for users reviewing the error handling behavior.

This commit updates the type hint for the response object in the Flask typing module to use the sansio version from Werkzeug. This change allows Quart to more easily extend Flask classes by aligning their type definitions, even though the standard Flask response is technically different.

This commit updates the `select_jinja_autoescape` method in the `Flask` class to enable autoescaping for `.svg` files. This change ensures that SVG content is treated as XML and properly escaped to prevent potential security vulnerabilities.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to clarify how to instantiate the application. It removes redundant explanations about module naming conventions and simplifies the description of passing the module name to the Flask class.

This commit adds troubleshooting warnings to the Flask deployment documentation for CGI, FastCGI, and mod_wsgi. It advises users to ensure their application's development server is not started during deployment to prevent conflicts.
This commit corrects a typo in the CLI documentation, changing "One Flask" to "Once Flask" to improve clarity. The fix is located in the `docs/cli.rst` file.

This commit updates the database schema definitions in the Flaskr and Minitwit examples to use the `text` data type instead of `string`. This change ensures the SQL syntax is valid for SQLite, preventing errors when users run the tutorial scripts.
This commit fixes a typo in the application factories documentation by removing an incorrect comma. The change corrects the sentence structure in the `appfactories` module to improve readability.

This commit fixes the documentation example for creating a custom test client in the Flask class. It corrects the initialization method to properly handle the authentication argument and call the parent class constructor, ensuring the example code is accurate.

This commit removes an unused import of the Range class from the werkzeug datastructures module in flask/helpers.py. It cleans up the codebase by eliminating unnecessary dependencies without altering any application behavior.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to remove redundant empty action attributes from HTML form examples. It clarifies that forms default to submitting to the current URL, improving the accuracy of the file upload, flashing, and WTForms pattern guides.

Refactors the test for the `get_debug_flag` function in `tests/test_helpers.py` to use parameterization. This simplifies the test code by replacing multiple manual environment variable checks with a data-driven approach.

This commit updates the documentation for the "becoming big" section and the foreword. It clarifies how Flask extensions provide reusable functionality through hooks and signals, and expands on the challenges of forking the framework.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `on_json_loading_failed` method in the `Request` class. It updates the parameter type to accept an optional `ValueError`, accurately reflecting that the exception argument can be `None`.

Fixes a documentation error in the Windows installation guide where the virtual environment activation path used the incorrect lowercase directory name. The corrected path now properly references the "Scripts" folder, ensuring users can successfully activate their environment.

This commit updates the Flask migration script to correctly handle attribute access in function calls and standard imports. It fixes a bug where the script failed to properly extract package names and format function call parameters, ensuring accurate code transformation.

This commit updates the Flask and MiniTwit examples to use the new application context requirement for database initialization. It renames the initdb function to init_db and adds a CLI command wrapper, ensuring tests properly push the app context before running setup.

This commit changes the default application name for console-based Flask apps from "unknown" to "__main__". The change affects the `Flask.name` property in `flask/app.py`, ensuring the name correctly reflects the entry point for scripts run directly.

This commit updates documentation and source code to use consistent formatting for file extensions and code references. It standardizes the use of double backticks for inline code and the `:file:` role for filenames across various Flask documentation pages and helper modules.

This commit updates the templating documentation to explain how context processors can inject variable functions into templates. It clarifies that these functions are evaluated during rendering, allowing for dynamic data injection, unlike static variables created at startup.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to reflect the transition from modules to blueprints. It replaces references to registering modules with instructions for registering blueprints in the configuration and application factory guides.

This commit removes deprecated code from the Flask package that was scheduled for deletion in version 1.0. It eliminates the backward-compatible alias for the session class and the obsolete availability flag, cleaning up the module's public interface.

This commit replaces a custom warning-capture fixture with pytest's built-in recwarn fixture across the test suite. It ensures that no unexpected warnings remain after tests complete, improving the reliability of deprecation checks in modules like test_basic and test_deprecations.

This documentation update clarifies that developers can define custom URL converters for Flask routes. It adds a note to the API reference indicating that this is done via the application's URL map attribute.

This commit updates documentation and examples to ensure teardown handlers do not fail when a before-request handler was skipped or errored. It modifies the teardown_request functions in the Flaskr and Minitwit examples to check for the database object before closing it.

This commit fixes a bug where a trailing slash in the static folder path caused the static route to incorrectly catch all URLs. The `_PackageBoundObject` class now strips the ending slash from the static URL path to prevent this behavior.

This commit fixes a bug where aware, non-UTC datetime objects were incorrectly encoded in JSON responses. The `JSONEncoder.default` method in `flask/json/__init__.py` now properly converts these datetimes to UTC before processing.

This commit modifies the documentation configuration to display original function signatures in the generated API docs. It patches Sphinx's inspection utilities to unwrap decorators, ensuring that decorated functions show their underlying argument specifications rather than the wrapper's.

This commit deprecates the legacy `flask.ext` namespace package system for Flask extensions. It introduces a new `ExtDeprecationWarning` and updates the `ExtensionImporter` in `flask/exthook.py` to emit clear warnings when users attempt to import extensions using the old format. Documentation is also updated to reflect this change.

This commit reduces the size of JSON responses generated by Flask's `jsonify` function when pretty-printing is disabled. It achieves this by removing unnecessary whitespace after separators, resulting in more compact output.

This commit adds a custom `assertIsInstance` method to the `FlaskTestCase` class to support Python 2.6, which lacks this assertion in its standard library. It resolves a failure in the `ConfigTestCase` where the missing method caused an error during test execution.

This commit fixes a documentation syntax error in the `stream_with_context` function within `flask/helpers.py`. It corrects the reStructuredText formatting for the generator usage example, ensuring the documentation renders correctly for users.
This commit fixes a typo in the signals documentation by removing an accidental double period. The change corrects the text in the `docs/signals.rst` file to improve readability.

The Flask application now uses a custom logger subclass that automatically enables debug-level logging when the application is in debug mode. This change modifies the Flask class to ensure debug messages are visible without manual configuration.

This commit modifies the test_extension function in tests/flaskext_test.py to prevent py.test from incorrectly calculating terminal widths during test execution. It also adds logic to remove any existing tox.ini file from the checkout directory to avoid conflicts with the test environment.

This commit relaxes the type hint for the `send_file` function in Flask's helpers module. It allows passing any bytes IO object, not just binary IO, improving compatibility for users sending file data.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask test client where teardown handlers were not executed when the client was used in a with statement. The FlaskClient class now correctly pops response contexts on exit, ensuring proper cleanup behavior for users relying on context management.

This documentation update clarifies that attempting to register an error handler on an existing instance now raises a ValueError. It informs users of this change in behavior during the upgrade process.
This commit updates the package list in setup.py to include the flask.ext module. This ensures the extension package is properly installed and available to users.

This commit corrects the import path for the BaseConverter class in the Flask application documentation. It updates the example in the Flask class initialization to reference werkzeug.routing instead of the incorrect werkzeug module.

The `run_audit` command in `setup.py` is updated to simplify its directory scanning logic. It now uses a static tuple of top-level directories and `os.walk` to traverse subdirectories, replacing the previous manual list construction and file iteration.

This commit modifies the mypy command in the tox configuration to remove the automatic type stub installation flags. It ensures that type checking relies on the stubs already defined in the typing requirements file rather than attempting to install them during the test run.

This commit adds a `root_path` parameter to the `Flask` and `Blueprint` classes to allow manual specification of the application's root directory. This resolves issues where Python 3.3 namespace packages prevent automatic path detection, ensuring the application can locate its resources correctly.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to use the Sphinx mimetype role for content types like application/json and text/html. It affects the docs for the jsonify function and Request class methods, ensuring consistent formatting in the user guide.

This commit fixes a minor grammatical error in a comment within the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It removes a redundant word to improve the clarity of the documentation. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit restores the `register_error_handler` method to the `Blueprint` class, allowing developers to attach specific error handlers to individual blueprints. It also re-adds the corresponding test case to verify that these blueprint-specific handlers function correctly.

This commit fixes a typo in the SQLAlchemy documentation example. It corrects the `__repr__` method in the `User` model to display only the name, removing the erroneous reference to the email attribute.

This commit updates pinned dependency versions across development, documentation, and testing environments. It also bumps the pre-commit hook revision to v2.32.1. These changes ensure the project uses the latest stable releases of its supporting tools.

This commit adds a new `before_render_template` signal to Flask, allowing developers to execute custom logic immediately before a template is rendered. The signal is defined in `flask/signals.py` and triggered within the `_render` function in `flask/templating.py`.

This commit introduces the `stream_with_context` helper in `flask.helpers`, allowing developers to keep the request context active while streaming data. It also fixes a bug where pushing application contexts multiple times caused unexpected behavior.

This commit allows the `SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT` configuration variable to accept a `datetime.timedelta` object in addition to an integer representing seconds. It updates the `Flask` class and related helper functions to handle this new type for file caching durations.
This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use a newer version of the tool. It changes the pinned revision from v2.7.4 to v2.9.0 in the .pre-commit-config.yaml file.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now checks if the normalized filename is valid ASCII before deciding how to encode it. If the filename is pure ASCII, it uses only the standard filename parameter, avoiding unnecessary UTF-8 encoding. This ensures simpler headers for common filenames while maintaining compatibility for non-ASCII names.

This commit corrects a syntax error in the blueprint nesting example within the documentation. It fixes a missing closing quote in the child blueprint's URL prefix, ensuring the code snippet is valid and copy-paste ready for users.

Flask now manages application and request contexts using Python context variables instead of Werkzeug's LocalStack, improving performance and memory usage. This change affects the AppContext and RequestContext classes in the ctx module, while the globals module retains a deprecated _FakeStack for backward compatibility.
This commit updates the Celery documentation to clarify when to use a task queue and explains an example task. It also removes a deprecated abstract attribute from the Celery integration.

This commit updates the package manifest and setup configuration to include the Flask test suite in distributed releases. It ensures that test applications, static files, and templates are properly packaged alongside the main library.

This commit improves the type hints for the `send_file` and `send_from_directory` functions in Flask's helpers module. It also updates the `get_send_file_max_age` method in the `Scaffold` class to provide more accurate type information for developers.

This commit corrects two intersphinx references in the Flask class documentation. It updates the link for the development server to point to the correct Werkzeug serving module and fixes the test request context reference to use the proper EnvironBuilder class.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.8 by updating the version string from a development build to the stable release. It modifies the version identifiers in the main package initialization and the project setup configuration.

This commit updates the `find_best_app` function in `flask/cli.py` to use `itervalues` instead of `iteritems` when scanning a module for Flask instances. This change aligns the code with Python 3 conventions, where dictionary iteration methods have been renamed.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 1.0.1.dev in the main module. It marks the start of a new development cycle following the 1.0 release.

This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the `teardown_request` method within the `Flask` class. It changes the word "if" to "it" to accurately describe how the application context is kept alive.

This commit refactors the host and port resolution logic in the Flask.run method to use explicit if-else blocks instead of complex expressions. It simplifies how default values are assigned when running the development server, making the code easier to read and maintain.

This commit updates the API documentation to accurately reflect the current code structure. It adds descriptions for the response status string and the status code attribute within the Response Objects section.

This commit clarifies the correct working directory for running the Flask application in the tutorial documentation. It specifies that users must remain in the top-level project directory rather than the package folder when executing the development server.

This commit updates the test configuration to suppress a new deprecation warning related to the ast module in Python 3.12. It modifies the filterwarnings setting in pyproject.toml to prevent this specific warning from appearing during test runs.

This commit adds documentation for Flask's URL processors, a feature introduced in version 0.7. It explains how to handle common URL segments, such as language codes, automatically without manual processing in every view function. The new guide is integrated into the main patterns index.

This commit changes Flask's response processing to save the session after request callbacks execute. This allows developers to modify session data within after-request callbacks, ensuring those changes are persisted. The change affects the `Flask.process_response` method.

This commit removes the deprecated `static_path` argument from the `Flask` class constructor. Users who previously passed this argument will no longer receive a deprecation warning, as the parameter has been fully removed.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Flask tutorial's database connection guide. It updates the description of request lifecycle hooks to accurately reference the `after_request` method instead of the incorrect `teardown_request` method.

This commit adds a test case to verify that Flask modules correctly serve templates and static files from their respective directories. It updates the Module class in flask/module.py to pass the static path during registration, ensuring proper file resolution for nested applications.

This commit simplifies the tox configuration by removing redundant package build settings from specific test environments. It allows these environments to inherit the base test environment configuration, streamlining the project's testing setup.

This commit updates the TestJSON class in tests/test_helpers.py to ensure compatibility with Python 3 by changing string assertions to bytes. It also corrects typos in two test method names to improve clarity and consistency.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions test workflow to replace the deprecated `set-env` command with the standard environment file approach. This ensures the Python version hash is correctly exported to the job environment without triggering deprecation warnings.

This commit ensures the tox.ini file is included in the source distribution. It updates the MANIFEST.in file to list tox.ini alongside other standard project files, making it available to users who install the package from source.

This commit fixes a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It corrects a malformed reference to the `g` object in the docstrings for `request_context` and `test_request_context`, ensuring the text renders correctly for users.

This commit updates the documentation to use correct double-backtick formatting for the `script` tag in several reStructuredText files. It ensures the tag is rendered as inline code rather than plain text in the generated API and pattern guides.

This commit adds a new configuration option, `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS`, to the Flask application. It allows users to disable the automatic generation of responses for OPTIONS requests, which lists valid HTTP methods. This change is implemented in the `Flask` and `App` classes.

This commit updates the development dependency tox from version 3.15.2 to 3.16.0. The change is recorded in the requirements/dev.txt file to ensure the project uses the newer version of the testing tool.
This commit updates the Flasky documentation theme to ensure footnote tables span the full width of the page. It modifies the CSS styling for the footnote table element to improve layout consistency.

This commit updates the documentation for the `jsonify` function in `flask/json.py` to accurately reflect the current conditions for pretty-printing responses. It clarifies that output is formatted for readability when the `JSONIFY_PRETTYPRINT_REGULAR` setting is enabled or the application is in debug mode, removing outdated references to specific request headers.

This commit adds unit tests to verify that Flask's JSON encoder correctly converts aware datetime objects to GMT across various timezones. It addresses a bug where encoding failed for non-UTC timezones by introducing a new test case in the TestJSON class. The change also updates the test environment configuration to include the required pytz dependency.

This commit corrects a duplicated word in the Flask issue template. It removes the redundant "any" from the instruction to provide extra information, ensuring the text is clear for users reporting bugs.

This commit updates the development dependencies in the tox configuration to use HTTPS URLs instead of the git protocol. This change ensures that dependency installation works correctly on networks that block the git protocol.

This commit reorders the self-hosted deployment options in the documentation, moving the WSGI-Standalone entry above mod_wsgi. The change affects the `docs/deploying/index.rst` file to adjust the presentation order of deployment methods.

This commit fixes subdomain inheritance for nested blueprints in Flask. It ensures that child blueprints correctly inherit the subdomain from their parent blueprint when no explicit subdomain is provided. The change modifies the Blueprint.register method to handle this logic.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the Flask error handling documentation. It corrects a typo in the sentence describing the ability to raise HTTP exceptions. The change is limited to the docs/errorhandling.rst file.

This commit standardizes the naming of the template engine from "Jinja2" to "Jinja" across documentation and source code. It updates references in the App and Environment classes to ensure consistent terminology for users.

This commit updates the documentation for view function return values in the quickstart guide. It clarifies the valid tuple formats by adding the `(response, status)` option and improving the overall wording for clarity.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for error handling. It fixes the misspelled class name "InsuffcientStorage" to "InsufficientStorage" in the example code within the errorhandling.rst file.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `Config.from_object` method in Flask. It explains that the method only loads uppercase attributes from modules or classes, noting that dictionaries are not supported.

This commit corrects line breaks in the Flask documentation foreword to improve readability. It adjusts the text wrapping in the `docs/foreword.rst` file, ensuring sentences flow naturally without awkward splits.

This commit adds test coverage for the Blueprint class's teardown_request and teardown_app_request methods. It verifies that these teardown functions execute correctly during request processing, increasing the test coverage of the blueprint module.

This commit reverts a previous change to the WTForms documentation, restoring the original HTML examples in the `docs/patterns/wtforms.rst` file. It removes the added closing tags and the form action attribute that were introduced in the prior update.

This commit fixes a minor typo in the Flask tutorial documentation by adding a missing period to a sentence in the setup guide. The change ensures the text in the setup.rst file is grammatically complete.

This commit corrects a typo in the release codename for version 0.9, changing "Camapri" to "Campari." The change updates the CHANGES file to ensure the project's release notes display the correct name.

This commit updates the documentation for the `_get_exc_class_and_code` method in the `Flask` class. It clarifies the expected type for the `exc_class_or_code` parameter, specifying that it accepts either an exception class or an integer error code.

This commit normalizes whitespace in the `safe_join` function within `flask/helpers.py` and adds a blank line to the test suite. It does not change any user-facing behavior or fix a bug, serving only as a minor code formatting cleanup.
This commit corrects a documentation example in the Fabric patterns guide. It updates the file path from "sdist" to "dist" to match the standard output directory for Python source distributions.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask test suite to verify the behavior of the `jsonify` function when the `padded` argument is set to `False`. It ensures that the JSON output correctly omits padding in this specific scenario.

This commit adds a test case to the JSONTestCase class in tests/flask_tests.py to verify that Flask correctly handles JSON request bodies with non-UTF-8 character encodings. It ensures that data sent with a specific charset, such as iso-8859-15, is properly decoded and returned as UTF-8.

This commit reverts a previous change in the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` class within `flask/sessions.py`. It restores the logic where `save_cookie` is called for all non-empty sessions, as it already handles the necessary cookie management. This ensures consistent session persistence behavior.

This commit updates the pinned versions of development, documentation, testing, and typing dependencies in the requirements files. It refreshes packages such as asgiref, certifi, and mypy to newer releases, ensuring the project uses current library versions.

This commit updates the Werkzeug dependency in setup.py to require version 0.14 or higher, removing the previous upper limit. It also cleans up the changelog entry for version 0.12.5 by standardizing the release date format and removing obsolete references.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the views module where a function argument was mislabeled. It updates the example signature for the register_api function to use the correct parameter name, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the expected code structure.

This commit cleans up error messages in the Flask command-line interface by hiding internal traceback frames. Users will see more concise error reports when the CLI fails to locate or load an application. The changes affect the `DispatchingApp` and `ScriptInfo` classes in `flask/cli.py`.

The `jsonify` function in `flask/json.py` now appends a newline character to the end of JSON responses. This change ensures compatibility with clients that expect UNIX text files to end with a newline, preventing potential parsing issues.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.10.2-dev in preparation for a potential release. It modifies the version string in the main package initialization and the setup configuration file.

This commit corrects the documentation for the views module, fixing incorrect examples for registering class-based views. It updates the code snippets to properly use the `as_view` method for `DetailView`, `ItemAPI`, and `GroupAPI` classes.

This commit exposes the maximum age for static files as a configurable value, allowing developers to customize cache headers for static content. It introduces a new hook in the Flask class and helper functions to support this configuration, including within Blueprints.

This commit updates the testing documentation to show the correct way to use the Flask test client with a teardown context. It clarifies that the client should be instantiated within a context manager to ensure proper resource cleanup.

This commit corrects a missing space in the changelog documentation. It ensures the text properly separates the phrase "the" from the configuration variable name. The change is limited to the CHANGES file.

This commit reverts a previous change to the CLI test suite, specifically within the TestRoutes class. It restores the original logic for filtering route endpoints and updates the assertion to check for a specific method string in the output.

This commit fixes a documentation rendering issue where a backtick was missing, causing the text to display incorrectly. It updates the configuration guide to properly separate the command option from the following sentence.
This commit updates the CI configuration to allow Flask to run on Python 3.3 with release requirements. It removes the previous exclusion that prevented this specific combination from being tested.
This commit corrects minor typos in the Flask documentation. It fixes spelling errors in the configuration, error handling, extension development, security, and style guide pages.

This commit updates the documentation for the flashing pattern to warn that excessively large messages cause silent failures. It explains that browser and server cookie size limits prevent session cookies from storing very long flash messages.

This commit updates development dependencies and CI workflow actions to their latest versions. It also modifies the `SessionMixin` class in `src/flask/sessions.py` to adjust the behavior of the `permanent` attribute.

The publish workflow now references a specific version tag for the SLSA generator instead of a commit hash. This change ensures the build process uses a stable, identifiable release of the security tooling.

This commit updates the test environment configuration to install Werkzeug from a specific development branch instead of a stable release. It modifies the `tox.ini` file to ensure tests run against the latest changes in the Werkzeug codebase.

This commit ensures the session cookie respects the configured server name by setting the appropriate domain attribute. It modifies the `Flask.save_session` method in `flask/app.py` to derive the domain from the `SERVER_NAME` configuration. A new test verifies this behavior for sessions using a server name.

This change ensures that running the Flask command with only the help flag loads the application first, matching the behavior of running the command with no arguments. Previously, custom commands were missing from the help output when the help flag was used. The fix updates the FlaskGroup class to handle this case correctly.

This commit updates the pytest dependency from version 6.1.2 to 6.2.1 in the development and test requirements files. It ensures the project uses the newer test runner version for its development and testing environments.

This commit removes the OpenID example application from the repository. The functionality is now provided by the flaskext.openid extension, making the local example redundant. The deletion includes the main application script, helper modules, and associated templates.

The `jsonify` function in `flask/json.py` now supports serializing top-level arrays to JSON. This change allows users to return lists directly, though it introduces a security risk in ancient browsers.

This commit allows users to specify a subdomain and URL scheme when creating a test request context in Flask. It updates the `Flask.test_request_context` method and the `make_test_environ_builder` function to accept these new parameters, enabling more accurate testing of blueprint routes and different protocols.

This commit allows the `template_filter`, `template_test`, and `template_global` decorators in Flask's `App` and `Blueprint` classes to be used without parentheses. Users can now apply these decorators directly to functions, simplifying the registration of custom template utilities.

This documentation update clarifies testing examples by replacing the ambiguous `self.assert_equal` call with a standard `assert` statement. This change prevents beginners from mistakenly copying invalid code that relies on a non-existent method.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to clarify that JSON parsing is triggered by the `is_json` property rather than strictly the `application/json` mimetype. It corrects the descriptions for the `json` property and `get_json` method to reflect this broader acceptance of mimetypes.

This commit removes version restrictions for the upload and download artifact actions in the Dependabot configuration. It allows the project to automatically update these dependencies to version 4 and later, removing the previous block that kept them on version 3.

This commit updates the docstrings in the Request class within flask/wrappers.py to use consistent capitalization at the start of sentences. It corrects minor grammatical inconsistencies in the documentation for URL matching attributes. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit fixes an incorrect import statement in the Flask documentation for the `@templated` decorator. It ensures the example code correctly imports `render_template` alongside `request`, preventing copy-paste errors for users implementing this pattern.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to correct the formatting of external resource links. It ensures that the IRC channel and Stack Overflow are properly referenced for users seeking help with questions rather than bugs.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask application where the `preprocess_request` hook incorrectly passed `request.values` instead of `request.view_args` to the callback function. This ensures that view-specific arguments are correctly available during request preprocessing.

This commit adds a GitHub Actions workflow to run pre-commit checks on pull requests and pushes to main or version branches. It ensures code style and linting rules are enforced automatically before merging.

This commit prevents Flask from failing at import time on FIPS-compliant systems where SHA-1 is unavailable. It introduces a lazy wrapper in the sessions module to defer accessing the default hash function until runtime, allowing developers to configure an alternative before use.

This commit updates the minimum required version of Werkzeug to 0.14 in the project's test configuration. This change ensures the application supports the SameSite cookie attribute, which is necessary for modern browser security features.

This commit updates the .gitignore file to exclude the .idea/ directory from version control. This prevents PyCharm-specific project configuration files from being tracked, keeping the repository clean of local IDE settings.

The `load_dotenv` function in `flask/cli.py` now consistently returns `False` instead of `None` when python-dotenv is missing or the specified path is not a file. This change aligns the function's behavior with its documented return type.
This commit updates the changelog to document the removal of unused code from the Flask module. It clarifies the contents of the bugfix release by adding a specific entry for this cleanup.

This commit fixes documentation rendering errors in the Flask configuration and file upload guides. It corrects the syntax for the version added directive in the config module and updates the formatting of the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH setting in the file uploads pattern.

This commit updates the upgrading documentation to warn users that per-module template folders are no longer automatically resolved. It explains that templates must now be manually reorganized to include the blueprint name in their path, as the upgrade tool does not handle this migration.

This commit adds a test case to the BasicFunctionalityTestCase in flask/testsuite/basic.py to verify response creation from a Response instance and status tuple. It also standardizes string quoting in the test file for consistency.
This commit updates the changelog to document a fix in version 0.12. It notes that the dev server now returns an Internal Server Error instead of crashing, reverting a previous behavior change.

The flash function in flask.py now uses setdefault to ensure the session is marked as modified when a message is added. This fixes a bug where the session modification flag was not set correctly, potentially preventing flash messages from persisting.

This commit fixes test failures caused by new server name mismatch warnings by removing a custom warning-catching fixture. It replaces the fixture with the standard `-Werror` option, which also speeds up the test suite by approximately three times.

Adds a security policy file to the repository to guide users on reporting vulnerabilities. This corrects a previous configuration error where GitHub incorrectly referenced a documentation file for security information.

This commit updates the type annotation for the `select_jinja_autoescape` method in the `App` class to accept `None` in addition to strings. This change accurately reflects that the method can handle filenames that are not provided, improving type safety for developers using the Flask application object.

This commit removes the union merge attribute for the CHANGES.rst file from the repository's .gitattributes configuration. This change alters how version control handles conflicts in the changelog, likely to prevent automatic merging of entries.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the MethodView class in flask/views.py. It clarifies that defining a get method causes the view to respond to GET requests, fixing a confusing sentence in the docstring.

This commit updates the documentation for blueprints by removing outdated module references and adding new sections. It explains how to register blueprints at different URL locations and notes that registering them multiple times depends on the specific implementation.

This commit adds a `required_methods` attribute to view functions in the Flask application. When set, the `Flask.add_url_rule` method ensures these HTTP methods are always included in the route registration, even if they were explicitly excluded in the route decorator.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask application where the default OPTIONS response failed to list all valid HTTP methods in the Allow header. The change modifies the Flask class to use a new helper method that correctly aggregates allowed methods from multiple routing rules.

This commit updates the documentation foreword to clarify that a microframework is defined by its lack of opinionated decisions for the user, rather than just its small size. It removes defensive language about sacrificing features for larger applications.

Flask's `send_file` and `send_from_directory` functions now wrap Werkzeug implementations, changing default caching behavior to use conditional requests instead of a 12-hour timeout. The `cache_timeout` parameter is renamed to `max_age`, and `attachment_filename` becomes `download_name`.

This commit fixes incorrect validator usage in the WTForms documentation example. It moves the password confirmation validation to the password field and removes the invalid self-reference from the confirm field.

This commit adds documentation for using async and await in Flask views and updates related source files. It clarifies that routes and handlers can be coroutines when the async extra is installed, explaining the performance implications for WSGI applications.
This commit corrects a duplicated word in the Flask documentation tutorial. It removes the redundant "to" in the description of how forms are configured to submit to the `add_entry` view function.
