This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 3.1.1. It updates the project version in pyproject.toml to a development release and adds a new entry to the changelog.

This commit updates the documentation for Celery background tasks, renaming the section to "Background Tasks with Celery" and refining the introductory text. It clarifies that a task queue allows long-running operations to execute in the background, ensuring requests return immediately.

This commit updates the Flask helpers, sessions, and test suite modules to replace direct calls to the next() method with six.advance_iterator(). This change ensures compatibility with Python 3, where the next() method was removed from iterators.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.8.7 to 1.8.8. This patch-level dependency update ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for publishing packages.

Updates the actions/checkout dependency in the publish and tests GitHub workflows from version 3.5.0 to 3.5.2. This patch update ensures the repository uses the latest stable release of the checkout action for its CI/CD pipelines.

This commit updates the intersphinx mapping in the documentation configuration to point to the latest Blinker documentation version. It resolves a stale reference that previously pointed to an older release, ensuring cross-references in the docs resolve correctly.

This commit introduces class-based views to the Flask framework, allowing developers to define views using classes like View and MethodView instead of standalone functions. It updates the Flask class to automatically detect HTTP methods from these view classes and improves error messages for blueprint registration conflicts.

This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It fixes the misspelling of "subdomain" in the parameter description for the route method, ensuring accurate documentation for users.

This commit modernizes the signal tests in tests/test_signals.py by switching from unittest to pytest. It adds a conditional skip marker to ensure tests only run when the blinker library is available, preventing import errors.

This commit updates the API documentation for the `abort` function in the `docs/api.rst` file. It replaces the manual description with an automatic reference to the Werkzeug library's documentation, ensuring the function details remain accurate and synchronized with the upstream source.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the version 0.10.1 changelog entry. It changes the word "were" to "where" in the description regarding duplicate method registration for an endpoint.

This commit fixes a broken test in the Flask test suite by replacing a threading condition variable with a simple sleep in the `test_before_first_request_functions_concurrent` method. This change resolves a synchronization issue in the `BasicFunctionalityTestCase` that was causing the test to fail.

This commit introduces a new test module, flask_tests.py, containing the ContextTestCase class. It adds basic unit tests to verify core Flask behaviors, including request context binding, URL dispatching, and session management.

This commit updates the minimum Werkzeug dependency to version 2.2.2 to incorporate fixes for the router, header parsing, and development server. It also removes the redundant development server warning message from the `show_server_banner` function in the Flask CLI module.

This commit updates the minimum required version of Jinja2 in the setup.py file to 2.10.1. This change ensures Flask users receive a critical security fix, preventing the use of an older, insecure version of the dependency.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `get_json` method in the `Request` class. It explicitly states that the method returns `None` when the request mimetype is not `application/json`, unless the `force` parameter is used.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for the blueprints module. It clarifies the explanation regarding the inability to unregister a blueprint after an application has been created.

This commit simplifies the error handler lookup in Flask's `Flask` class by removing unnecessary logic that checked for circular MROs and re-added superclass MROs. It replaces a complex queue-based traversal with a direct iteration over the exception class's MRO, as Python guarantees MROs are acyclic and complete.

This commit updates the Flask version string to use a PEP 440-compatible format, changing it from a hyphenated style to a dot-separated development release. This ensures the package version is correctly recognized by standard Python packaging tools. The change affects the version definitions in the main package initialization and setup files.

This commit corrects the import path for the secure_filename function in the file upload documentation. It updates the example to import from werkzeug.utils instead of the top-level werkzeug package, ensuring users copy the correct code.

This commit corrects the documentation for error handling by updating the description of Sentry. It clarifies that Sentry is a source-available project rather than open source, ensuring accurate terminology in the user guide.

This commit corrects two typos in the shell documentation file. It fixes a grammatical error in the description of importing modules and clarifies the syntax for importing from a module like `shelltools`.

This commit adds a `total_seconds` helper function to `flask/sessions.py` to calculate the duration of a timedelta object. It replaces the native `total_seconds()` method call within `SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session` to ensure compatibility with Python versions prior to 2.7.

This commit adds Python 3.7 support to the project's continuous integration pipelines. It updates the configuration files for AppVeyor, Travis CI, and tox to include the new version in the test matrix.

This commit refines the wording in the Flask quickstart documentation for clarity and conciseness. It updates the introductory text and the instructions for running a minimal application within the docs/quickstart.rst file.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's testing client where session transactions failed for IPv6 addresses. The `FlaskClient.session_transaction` method now correctly parses the host using URL splitting instead of simple string partitioning.

This commit corrects the documented version for the SessionInterface class in Flask. It updates the version added note from 0.7 to 0.8 in both the API documentation and the source code to accurately reflect when the feature was introduced.

This commit fixes an issue where the Flask command-line interface failed when running with an external debugger on Windows. It updates the main function in the CLI module to explicitly pass command-line arguments, ensuring the tool works correctly in that environment.
Fixes a failing test in the JavaScript example by updating the expected template name. The test now correctly references the fetch.html template instead of the outdated xhr.html file.

This commit moves the FlaskClient testing class from the main application module into a dedicated testing module. It refactors the test client implementation to improve code organization and separation of concerns.

This commit adds a new section to the API documentation explaining the three methods for defining URL routes in Flask. It clarifies how to use the route decorator, the add_url_rule function, and the underlying url_map attribute. The changes primarily affect the documentation file and reference the Flask class.

The CI configuration now runs the test suite via the Makefile instead of directly invoking the Python setup script. This change updates the Travis build process to use the project's standard test command.

This commit updates the test suite to use monkeypatching for system path modifications, improving test isolation in the TestInstance class. It also adds Python 3.4 with lowest requirements to the CI matrix.

The Flask.logger property now uses the application's name instead of the hardcoded "flask.app" string. This change allows multiple Flask applications in the same process to have distinct loggers, reverting a behavior introduced in version 1.0.

This commit corrects typos and formatting errors in the documentation for the `run_simple` function. It fixes a missing colon in the code block directive and corrects the spelling of "enabled" to improve the clarity of the debugging instructions.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to explain how to stop the server and enable debug mode. It details how to configure the Flask application to automatically reload on code changes and provide a debugger, improving the user experience for local development.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `after_request` method in the `Flask` class. It corrects the description to specify that the callback function expects an instance of the response class, rather than the class itself.

This commit updates the documentation for standalone WSGI servers, clarifying that they typically include HTTP capabilities. It advises users to consider running these servers behind a dedicated HTTP server like Apache or Nginx for better deployment.

This commit adds a troubleshooting note to the Flask quickstart documentation regarding cookie-based sessions. It advises users to check cookie size limits if session values fail to persist across requests without a clear error message.

This commit improves the clarity and concision of the Routing section in the Flask quickstart documentation. It rewrites sentences to reduce ambiguity, adds a code sample demonstrating path converter types, and removes the HTTP method overview to keep the guide focused.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in an assertion message within the Blueprint class. It updates the error text in the add_url_rule method to properly state that endpoints should not contain dots.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.0.2 by updating the version string in the main package initialization file. It changes the version identifier from a development build to the stable release number, ensuring the library reports the correct version to users.

This commit updates the Flask documentation and example applications to reflect the new configuration system. It adds an upgrading guide and modifies the flaskr and minitwit examples to use the updated setup.

This commit updates the Pallets-Sphinx-Themes dependency to version 2.0.0rc1 across development and documentation requirements. It removes the separate packaging requirement from the docs configuration and adds asgiref to the development environment.

This commit updates the type annotation for the `stream_with_context` function in `flask.helpers`. It removes an unnecessary return-value type ignore, resolving a static analysis finding without changing runtime behavior.

This commit removes an unused import from the Flask module and updates the test suite to expect a ValueError instead of a warning when a view function fails to return a response. The changes ensure the test correctly validates the new error behavior in the BasicFunctionalityTestCase.

The `create_logger` function in `flask/logging.py` now disables logger propagation by default. This prevents application log messages from being duplicated by parent loggers, ensuring cleaner output for users.

This commit updates the Flask documentation for patterns, snippets, and extensions. It corrects cross-reference links in the application context and extension development guides to ensure they point to the correct pages.

This commit adds basic support for modules in the Flask application, allowing routes to be organized under specific module names. It introduces a `module` property to the `Request` class and updates the `url_for` function to automatically prefix endpoints with the current module name when not explicitly specified.

Adds a test to verify that the `jsonify` function in the Flask module raises a `TypeError` when both positional and keyword arguments are provided. This ensures the function correctly rejects ambiguous input and includes a specific error message indicating undefined behavior.

This commit updates the deprecation version for the `Config.from_json` method in the Flask `Config` class. It corrects the documentation to indicate that the method was deprecated in version 2.0 rather than 1.2.

This commit reorganizes test setup in tests/test_basic.py to prevent late initialization issues. It moves the session clearing route definition earlier in the test_session_using_session_settings function and refactors the bad request key error test into a parameterized test named test_trap_bad_request_key_error.
The installation documentation now uses the dot command instead of the source keyword to activate virtual environments. This change improves shell portability across different operating systems.

This commit improves support for composable command-line interfaces in the Flask CLI module. It renames the FlaskClickGroup class to FlaskGroup and updates the ScriptInfo class to accept configuration parameters directly during initialization.

This commit adds optional signal support to the Flask application, allowing extensions to hook into request and template rendering events. It introduces a new signals module and updates the Flask class to emit these signals, requiring the blinker package for functionality.

This commit updates the ExtImportHookTestCase in the Flask test suite to handle Python 3 traceback structures. It ensures the test correctly navigates traceback frames on Python 3, preventing assertion failures during test execution.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to include the missing `any` and `uuid` URL converters. It ensures the API and quickstart guides accurately list all available Werkzeug builtin converters for users.

This documentation update corrects the installation instructions to recommend using `pip` instead of `easy_install` for root-level installations. It ensures the guide reflects current best practices for package management.

Removes the obsolete `flask-07-upgrade` script, which previously automated code migrations for Flask 0.7. This cleanup eliminates outdated tooling that is no longer needed for modern application upgrades.

The `RequestContext.copy` method now includes the current session object in the copied context. This ensures that `flask.session` remains valid and up-to-date when using `copy_current_request_context` in background tasks.

The `main` function in `flask/cli.py` is simplified to remove manual argument manipulation for module execution. This change leverages improved reloader support in Werkzeug 0.15, which now correctly detects `python -m` commands without requiring custom workarounds.

This commit updates the project's README file to replace a previous tagline with a new one focused on web development. The change alters the descriptive text displayed to users but does not affect any functional code or behavior.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect the removal of the internal request context stack in favor of a direct proxy. It clarifies that accessing the current request context now raises an error if no request is active, affecting the Flask application and context modules.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for the packages module. It changes the word "Similiarly" to "Similarly" in the instructions for providing the application directory path.
This commit corrects a grammatical typo in the request context documentation. It changes the word "of" to "or" in the description of using the test client within a with statement.

This commit updates five Python dependencies in the requirements files to their latest patch versions. It bumps cryptography, mypy, pyright, pytest, and tox to ensure the project uses the most recent stable releases for development and testing.

This commit adds support for secret key rotation in Flask by introducing the `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` configuration option. It allows the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` to verify sessions using a list of previous keys, preventing active sessions from being invalidated when the primary key changes.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask test suite to verify URL generation between an application and a registered blueprint. It ensures that routes defined directly on the app can correctly reference blueprint endpoints using dotted names. The new test is added to the BlueprintTestCase class.

This commit adds initial test cases for the Blueprint class in Flask, specifically verifying URL rule definitions. It also updates the BlueprintSetupState to properly handle and merge URL defaults during rule registration.

This commit updates the documentation for the Config class in Flask to clarify the return values of its configuration loading methods. It specifies that methods like from_file and from_envvar return True on success, while from_mapping always returns True.

This commit adds an `--extra-files` option to the `flask run` CLI command, allowing users to specify additional files that trigger the development reloader. It introduces the `SeparatedPathType` class in `flask/cli.py` to parse multiple paths separated by colons or semicolons.
This commit fixes a missing closing parenthesis in the uWSGI deployment documentation. It corrects a typo in the example code snippet within the `docs/deploying/uwsgi.rst` file.

This commit updates the Werkzeug dependency to version 2.3.3 to incorporate recent bug fixes. It simplifies the `FlaskClient` class in the testing module by removing compatibility code for older Werkzeug versions, ensuring the session cookie correctly sets the `Vary: Cookie` header.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask development server where setting the port to 0 was incorrectly overridden by the default value. The `Flask.run` method now explicitly checks for `None` instead of relying on boolean evaluation, allowing the operating system to select an available port.

This commit updates the Flask application and its test suite to support Python 3.3 by removing obsolete future imports and fixing compatibility issues. It specifically removes the `init_jinja_globals` hack from the `Flask` class, which previously failed to work correctly on Python 3.3.
This commit removes the redundant license file from the documentation directory. The documentation license is already covered by the project's main license file, so the separate file was unnecessary.
This commit initiates the development cycle for Flask version 2.0.2. It updates the version string in the main package module and adds a new entry to the changelog to track upcoming changes.

This commit removes the deprecated `script_info` argument from the Flask CLI's app factory invocation. The `ScriptInfo` class and related helper functions in `src/flask/cli.py` no longer pass this object to application factory functions, simplifying the interface.

This commit corrects several typos in the docstrings and comments within the flask/run.py module. It improves the clarity of documentation for functions like find_best_app and the DispatchingApp class without altering any code behavior.

This commit updates the Flaskr example to use the application factory pattern for the CLI. It removes the dedicated `_cliapp.py` module and updates the README to point the `FLASK_APP` environment variable directly to the `create_app` factory function.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 2.0.0rc2. It modifies the `__version__` variable in the `flask` module to reflect the new release candidate.

This commit adds a new AppVeyor configuration file to set up continuous integration for the project. It configures the build environment to run tests using Tox on Python 2.7 and 3.6 for the master and maintenance branches.

This commit configures the Travis CI build to suppress unnecessary Slack notifications. It disables join messages and enables notice messages to reduce channel spam. The changes are applied to the project's Travis configuration file.
This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to improve clarity. It corrects the terminology in the response object description by changing "200 error code" to "200 status code."

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify that the object now supports the `in` operator for checking attribute existence and yields all keys when iterated. The change is limited to the `docs/api.rst` file.

This commit improves the readability of the development server warning message in Flask's CLI. It updates the text displayed by the `show_server_banner` function to clearly state that the server is for development only and should not be used in production deployments.

This commit updates the changelog to correct a typo in the description of a test client bug. It clarifies that the issue occurred when using the "with" statement, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the specific syntax involved.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the Flask documentation for blueprints. It fixes the typo "Paremeters" to "Parameters" in the description of how URL prefix arguments are handled.

This commit corrects the documentation for the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It replaces references to a non-existent `build_error_handler` property with the correct `url_build_error_handlers` attribute, ensuring the docs accurately describe how URL build errors are handled.

This commit updates the `reset_logging` fixture in `tests/test_logging.py` to ensure tests pass on pytest versions greater than 3.3.0. It explicitly unregisters and re-registers the logging plugin to properly reset logging handlers between test runs.

This commit corrects a formatting error in the docstring for the `stream_with_context` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It adds the missing double colon required for proper documentation rendering, ensuring the example code displays correctly.

This commit fixes a string formatting error in the documentation for the views module. It corrects a code example that was missing a required argument, ensuring the URL rule generation snippet is syntactically valid.

This commit fixes the `Flask.auto_find_instance_path` method to correctly identify the base directory when a module is installed in a standard library prefix. It ensures the instance path is resolved properly for packages located within a `lib` directory structure.

Updates the actions/checkout dependency from version 4.1.4 to 4.1.6 in the GitHub Actions workflows. This patch update applies to the publish and tests workflow files to ensure the repository uses the latest stable release of the checkout action.
This commit updates the Flask testing documentation to include the `g` object in a code example. It ensures the import list is complete for users referencing the `appcontext_pushed` signal.

The documentation for returning API errors as JSON now correctly specifies including the error's status code in the response. This ensures the example code properly conveys the HTTP status to the client.

This commit fixes a grammatical typo in the help text for the shell command in the Flask CLI. It corrects the phrase "manually configuring" to "manually configure" within the `shell_command` function in `flask/cli.py`.

Fixes a typo in the extension development documentation where the database cursor variable was incorrectly named. This corrects the example in the `docs/extensiondev.rst` file to use the proper `sqlite3_db` attribute.
This commit updates the copyright year in the project's license file from 2012 to 2013. It ensures the legal documentation reflects the current year of maintenance.

The shell command in Flask's CLI no longer displays the application's environment variable in the startup banner. This change removes the environment label from the output shown when users launch the interactive shell.

This commit removes the recommendation to use Tornado as a WSGI server in the Flask deployment documentation. It clarifies that Tornado is less scalable for this purpose and only suitable for specific mixed-application scenarios, addressing common user confusion.

This commit adds Flask-Creole to the list of approved extensions in the extreview module. It records the initial approval date, version 0.4.4, and BSD license. The entry also notes that Flask-Creole should share an API with Flask-Markdown.

This commit adds a test to verify that Flask correctly handles requests exceeding the configured maximum content length. It ensures that when a POST request is too large, the application triggers a 413 error and returns the custom response defined in the error handler. The test is located in the BasicFunctionalityTestCase class within the Flask test suite.
This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It fixes the parameter label in the `request_context` method, changing "params" to "param" for accuracy.
This commit fixes several grammatical errors in the Flask configuration documentation. It corrects phrasing in the `docs/config.rst` file to improve clarity and readability for users.

This commit removes redundant empty lines from the test configuration and signal test modules to comply with PEP8 formatting standards. It ensures that functions are separated by exactly two blank lines instead of three, improving code consistency.

This commit updates the changelog to document a behavior change in Flask's environment file loading. It clarifies that Flask no longer changes the current working directory when loading `.env` or `.flaskenv` files from the top-level directory, preventing potential confusion.

This commit removes a placeholder variable from the user_timeline function in the Minitwit example application. It resolves a regression that was introduced in a previous change, restoring the function to its correct state.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the extension development documentation. It changes the phrasing in the `docs/extensiondev.rst` file to improve clarity for users reading about extension structure.

This commit corrects a parameter name in the `json_dumps` method of the `EnvironBuilder` class within `flask/testing.py`. It changes the variable from `args` to `kwargs` to accurately reflect that it holds keyword arguments, ensuring consistent naming conventions.

The documentation for deploying Flask on Google App Engine now directs users to the official Google Cloud guide instead of an unmaintained third-party template. This change ensures the deployment instructions are current and authoritative.
This commit disables the helpful tips in the GitHub issue template by extending the HTML comment markers. Users will no longer see the guidance text when creating new issues in the Flask repository.

This commit adds a new example application to the repository, demonstrating how to structure a larger Flask project. It includes the necessary package setup, view definitions, and template files for the "yourapplication" module.

This commit updates the Sphinx documentation generator from version 3.2.1 to 3.4.1. It modifies the pinned dependency versions in the development and documentation requirements files to ensure the project uses the newer release.

The `flask.run` module now accepts a thread flag to enable multithreading in the local development server. This change allows users to handle multiple requests concurrently when running the application via the `flask run` command.

This commit updates the `make_diff` function in `flask-07-upgrade.py` and the `fail` and `info` functions in `make-release.py` to use Python 3-compatible print syntax. It ensures these scripts run correctly in Python 3 environments by replacing legacy print statements with function calls.

This commit resolves a deprecation warning triggered by importing MutableMapping directly from the collections module. It updates the SessionMixin class in flask/sessions.py to use a compatibility alias from flask/_compat.py, ensuring the code works correctly across different Python versions.

This commit removes trailing whitespace from several lines in the Flask application module. It cleans up the source code for the Flask class and its exception handling methods without altering any functional behavior.

This documentation update corrects the attribute name used to access the application instance directory. It replaces the outdated `instance_root` reference with `instance_path` in the configuration examples. This ensures users follow the current API for locating files within the instance folder.
This commit fixes missing commas after introductory phrases in the project documentation. It updates the main index file to improve grammatical correctness in the introductory text.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask class explaining how to disable code execution in the interactive debugger while keeping the traceback screen active. It clarifies that users can pass the use_evalex parameter to the run method to achieve this specific behavior.

This commit adds a test to verify that `flask.url_for` correctly passes special values like `_external` and `_anchor` to registered URL build error handlers. It ensures these parameters are available when a custom handler processes a build error.

This commit refactors the Flask test suite initialization by renaming the path setup function to `setup_path` and adding validation to ensure directories exist before being added to the system path. It also adds docstrings to helper functions like `iter_suites` and `find_all_tests` to clarify their roles in the test runner.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to prevent HTML injection in example code snippets. It modifies the sample view functions to properly escape user-provided input before rendering it in responses.

This commit adds a docstring to the FlaskClient class in flask/testing.py. It clarifies that the class behaves like a standard Werkzeug test client but defers request context cleanup until the end of a with statement.

This commit updates the signal tests in `tests/test_signals.py` to use explicit connect and disconnect calls instead of a context manager. It ensures the `before_render_template` signal is properly cleaned up after each test case.

This commit corrects a typo in the Flask documentation for the signals module. It updates the reference for the `appcontext_popped` signal to properly include the `flask` namespace, ensuring the documentation accurately reflects the correct symbol name.

This commit updates the CHANGES file to mark version 0.10.1 as a released bugfix. It replaces the pending status with the specific release date of June 14th, 2013, clarifying the project's release history.

Flask now accepts custom JSON mimetypes for incoming data, allowing requests with non-standard content types to be parsed correctly. This change updates the Request class in flask/wrappers.py to recognize these variations in the is_json property and get_json method.
This commit removes support for Python 3.6 from the Flask project. It updates the CI configuration, documentation, and test suite to reflect the new minimum version requirement.

This commit fixes an issue where static folder paths with Windows-style backslashes were not handled correctly. It updates the `_PackageBoundObject` class in `flask.helpers` to strip both forward and backward slashes from the `static_folder` value, ensuring consistent behavior across operating systems.
This commit corrects a duplicated word in the project's changelog. It updates the CHANGES.rst file to remove the redundant "even" from the description of template auto-reloading behavior.
This commit corrects a typo in the version 0.10.2 changelog entry. It clarifies that the etags bug fix applies to file streams with a name, rather than files without a name.

This commit updates the CONTRIBUTING.rst documentation to clarify branch creation procedures for contributors. It specifies that bug and documentation fixes should branch from the latest stable release, while feature additions should branch from master.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the docstring for the `handle_http_exception` method within the `Flask` class. It changes the phrasing from "an HTTP exception" to "a HTTP exception" to improve documentation accuracy.

This commit standardizes the license and copyright notices across the Flask codebase. It removes the separate AUTHORS file and consolidates licensing information into a single LICENSE file, updating references in documentation and source files.

This commit restores the full traceback for import errors in the Flask CLI, preventing the `locate_app` function from hiding the original exception details. Users will now see the complete error message when an application fails to import, rather than a generic notification.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask views guide, specifically introducing a section on using MethodView for building web APIs. It explains how to map different HTTP verbs to a single view class and provides a table illustrating URL routing for user management endpoints.

This commit updates the GitHub issue template to direct users to the Pallets Discord server instead of the retired IRC channel for general questions. It modifies the guidance text in the issue template file to reflect the new community support channel.

This commit updates the documentation for loading jQuery in the `docs/patterns/jquery.rst` file. It recommends placing the script tag at the bottom of the body and introduces a fallback mechanism that loads a local copy if the Google CDN fails.

This commit updates various development and documentation dependencies to their latest versions. It bumps the pre-commit configuration and updates packages such as cachetools, identify, and tox in the requirements files.

This documentation update corrects the uWSGI socket path in the deployment guide to match the application name. It ensures the example command uses a consistent socket location, preventing confusion for users setting up their Flask application.

This commit updates the Flaskr tutorial documentation to improve clarity and accuracy for the installable app pattern. It corrects section titles, fixes environment variable references, and generalizes packaging guidance by removing specific emphasis on setuptools.

This commit updates the changelog to document the increased minimum version requirements for several Pallets dependencies, including Werkzeug, Jinja2, and Click. It alerts users to check the respective change logs for these projects to understand the implications of the version bumps.

This commit introduces a new request dispatching mechanism in the Flask application class, refactoring how requests are processed and contexts are managed. It updates the `Flask` and `RequestContext` classes to handle request lifecycle events, though the associated unit tests have not yet been updated to reflect these changes.

This commit updates the configuration documentation to clarify that Windows environment variables are always uppercase, affecting how nested keys are formatted. It also adds a test case to verify the correct handling of these uppercase prefixed environment variables.

This commit fixes a broken code example in the quickstart documentation. It updates the session example to properly initialize a Flask application and include the necessary request import, ensuring the snippet is valid and runnable.

This commit fixes a typo in the quickstart documentation by removing a duplicated word in the description of URL converters. It clarifies the explanation for how the system handles missing trailing slashes.

This commit fixes broken cross-references in the deployment documentation for FastCGI, uWSGI, and standalone WSGI. It replaces invalid reference tags with correct document tags to ensure links work properly.

This commit fixes a missing import in the Flask context module, which would have caused a runtime error when the application attempted to re-raise exceptions. The change adds the necessary symbol to the compatibility imports in `flask/ctx.py`.

This commit corrects the parameter order in the documentation for the `safe_join` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It ensures the docstring accurately reflects the function's signature, preventing confusion for developers reading the API reference.

This commit refactors the test suite in tests/test_views.py by removing the TestView class and converting its methods into standalone test functions. This change simplifies the test structure and aligns it with standard testing practices.
This commit updates the version string in the Flask package's main module to include the ".dev" suffix. It corrects the reported version number to accurately reflect a development build.

This commit fixes a typo in the jQuery pattern documentation by correcting the phrase "kindly enough" to "kind enough." The change improves the clarity of the explanation regarding the `tojson` filter's behavior within script blocks.

This commit adds documentation to the Flask class explaining example use cases for the request_globals_class parameter. It clarifies how developers can customize the request context to store attributes, manage database connections, or control attribute access behavior.

This commit adds a clarifying comment to the `_ExtensionImporter` class in the Flask extension module. It explains the logic for preventing duplicate import hooks when the module is reloaded, ensuring the system correctly identifies and removes stale instances by class name.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's test client where query parameters were stripped from requests using absolute URLs. The `make_test_environ_builder` function in `flask/testing.py` now correctly appends the query string to the path.

The Flask application now configures a logging handler to record request handling exceptions when not in debug mode. This change allows developers to receive notifications, such as emails, for server errors. The main Flask class was updated to support this new logging behavior.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's SecureCookieSessionInterface where setting a session cookie would overwrite any existing Vary header values. The new _patch_vary_cookie_header method now appends "Cookie" to the header only if it is not already present, preserving other entries.

The test client and test request context now share internal logic for creating the environment, ensuring consistent behavior. This change makes the test client properly respect the APPLICATION_ROOT and SERVER_NAME configuration variables as defaults.

This commit introduces a new ConfigAttribute class to the Flask module, enabling application attributes to automatically forward to the configuration dictionary. It also begins defining the debug flag on the Flask class to control debugging behavior.

This commit clarifies documentation in the packages module regarding endpoint behavior. It explains that a specific routing condition applies to all endpoints, not just static folders, noting that static folders are more commonly affected in typical applications.

This commit fixes the `App.add_url_rule` method so that explicitly setting `provide_automatic_options=True` correctly enables automatic OPTIONS handling, even when the global configuration disables it. Previously, only the ability to disable this feature worked, causing inconsistent behavior for users trying to force-enable it.

This commit updates documentation links to point to the new pythonhosted.org domain instead of the deprecated packages.python.org. It ensures that references to extensions like Flask-OAuth and Flask-SQLAlchemy in the docs remain accessible.

This commit corrects a typo in the upgrading documentation, changing "In generally" to "In general." It improves the clarity of the text regarding custom error handlers without altering any functional behavior.

This commit updates the Azure Pipelines configuration and tox settings to include test output and add a build run against the Python release candidate. These changes ensure the project's continuous integration tests verify compatibility with the upcoming Python version.
This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It changes the word "actually" to "actual" in the description of the `preprocess_request` method to improve clarity.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.12.5.dev in the `__init__.py` file. It marks the start of the next development cycle following the 0.12.4 release.

This commit removes the deprecated `request_globals_class` property from the `Flask` class in `flask/app.py`. It eliminates the backward-compatibility methods that previously issued a warning and redirected access to the new `app_ctx_globals_class` attribute.

This commit fixes the `Blueprint.register` method in Flask to correctly combine URL prefixes when nesting blueprints that were created with a `url_prefix` value. Previously, the nested blueprint's prefix might not be properly appended to the parent's prefix, leading to incorrect routing.
Updates the documentation to point to the new domain for the Dive Into HTML5 resource. This ensures users are directed to the correct website when accessing the external link.

This commit adds the flaskext_compat module to restore support for the legacy flask.ext import syntax in Flask versions 0.7 and earlier. It introduces the _ExtensionImporter class to redirect these imports to the correct extension modules, ensuring compatibility for users relying on the old naming convention.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to install the development version of Werkzeug from its Git repository before installing the project. This ensures the test environment uses the latest Werkzeug features or fixes during continuous integration runs.

This commit updates the versions of several pre-commit hooks, including pyupgrade, reorder_python_imports, black, and pre-commit-hooks, in the .pre-commit-config.yaml file. It ensures the project uses the latest stable releases of these tools for code formatting and linting.

This commit refactors JSON handling into a shared mixin for request and response objects, adding `is_json` and `get_json` methods to responses to simplify testing. It also updates the test client to support a `json` keyword argument for sending JSON data directly.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to reflect the new Click-based command-line interface. It replaces instructions for running the app with `app.run()` in favor of the `flask` command or `python -m flask`. The changes affect the quickstart guide and add new sections for CLI and server usage.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the database initialization tutorial documentation. It clarifies the instructions for adding imports to the Flask application file, improving readability for users following the guide.

This commit adds a new documentation chapter on handling application errors and logging. It updates the Flask documentation structure to include this new section and adjusts the version display logic in the configuration file.

This commit updates the API documentation to clarify how Flask handles JSON key sorting. It explains that the `JSON_SORT_KEYS` configuration variable controls this behavior, noting that keys are sorted by default and outside of the application context.

This commit corrects a typo in the logging format string within the error handling documentation. It fixes a broken example that would have caused a logging error due to an invalid key. The change is located in the docs/errorhandling.rst file.
This commit corrects a typo in the file header of the `flask/json.py` module. It updates the module name from `flask.jsonimpl` to `flask.json` to accurately reflect the file's identity.

This commit fixes a test failure in the test_signals module by correcting the expected data type for the response body. It updates the assertion to expect bytes instead of a string, ensuring the test correctly validates the output of the before_render_template signal.

This commit updates documentation in the quickstart guide and the Config class to clarify how debuggers interact with Flask's reloader. It corrects the description of how object variables are handled in the Config.from_object method, removing an inaccurate note about lowercasing.
This commit corrects two spelling errors in the project's README file. It fixes the misspelling of "developed" and "prebuilt" to improve the documentation's accuracy.

This commit fixes the `Request.blueprint` property in `flask/wrappers.py` to correctly identify the blueprint name when it contains dots. It changes the string splitting logic to ensure the correct prefix is returned for dotted blueprint names. A new test verifies this behavior for both frontend and backend blueprints.

This commit improves Flask's exception handling by introducing a new ExceptionHandlerDict class that simplifies how error handlers are stored and retrieved. It also adds a helper function to extract HTTP status codes from exceptions, making the process more intuitive and robust.

This commit fixes broken syntax highlighting in the Flask quickstart documentation. It converts the example script output in the URL Building section into comments within the code block. The change is made in the docs/quickstart.rst file.

This commit updates the README files for the Flaskr and Minitwit examples to use standard Markdown syntax for file references. It removes the Sphinx-specific `:file:` role, ensuring the documentation renders correctly in standard Markdown viewers.

This commit fixes an import error in the `flask.json` module caused by a name change in the `itsdangerous` library. It ensures compatibility by attempting to import the JSON module under both its old and new names.

The blueprint example previously failed to start because it lacked an entry point to launch the server. This commit adds the necessary execution block to the main script, allowing the application to run correctly.

This commit fixes a documentation example in the `TaggedJSONSerializer` class within `flask/json/tag.py`. It corrects the `register` method call to use the `index` keyword argument, ensuring the example properly demonstrates inserting a tag with higher precedence rather than accidentally setting the `force` flag.

This commit resolves a type-checking error in the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` class within the Flask sessions module. It refines the type ignore comment in the `save_session` method to specifically address a potential union attribute issue, ensuring the code passes static analysis without altering runtime behavior.

This commit suppresses specific pytest warnings related to unraisable and unhandled thread exceptions in the test suite. It modifies the `test_exception_propagation` function in `tests/test_basic.py` to prevent these warnings from appearing during test execution.

This commit ensures that using Blueprint setup methods after registration always triggers a warning, removing the previous conditional flag. It modifies the Blueprint class to enforce this behavior consistently, preparing for a future version where such actions will raise an error.

This commit simplifies the exception handling logic in Flask's `handle_user_exception` method. It removes legacy code that manually formatted error messages for older Werkzeug versions, streamlining how `BadRequestKeyError` is processed during debugging or when trapping bad request errors.

This documentation update clarifies that while Flask works well with Python 3, libraries like Werkzeug and Flask may still have stability issues. It warns users that they might encounter bugs, which are typically related to encoding problems.

This commit resolves resource warnings in the Flask test suite by ensuring response objects are properly closed after tests. It updates test cases in the basic, blueprints, and helpers modules to explicitly close responses, preventing unclosed file handle errors.

This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the Flask class's initialization method. It updates the reference from the before_request decorator to the correct after_request decorator, ensuring the documentation accurately describes the available hooks.

This commit adds an `aborter` object to the Flask application, allowing developers to customize how HTTP aborts are handled, including support for custom status codes. The `flask.abort` function now delegates to this new app attribute instead of using the default Werkzeug implementation.

This commit refactors the test suite in `tests/flask_tests.py` by splitting a single test into two distinct cases. It separates the verification of explicit instance paths from the checks for uninstalled module paths within the `InstanceTestCase` class.

This commit updates the development dependency tox from version 3.17.1 to 3.18.0. It modifies the requirements/dev.txt file to reflect this version bump, ensuring the project uses the latest stable release of the testing tool.

This commit updates the documentation for the Request class in flask/wrappers.py. It clarifies a sentence that became outdated following changes to the request object documentation. The change ensures the description accurately reflects the class's relationship to Werkzeug.

This commit reverts a previous change to use pytz for timezone handling in tests, as the standard library alternative is incompatible with Python 2. It updates the TestJSON class in tests/test_helpers.py to utilize pytz timezones for verifying aware datetime serialization.
This commit removes an unused datetime import from the Flask application module. It cleans up the code in flask/app.py without altering any application behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.

This commit improves the English phrasing in the quickstart documentation. It corrects a grammatical error in the introductory sentence for a template rendering example within the docs/quickstart.rst file.

This commit standardizes the terminology in documentation and code comments by replacing "testsuite" with "test suite." It updates the `RequestContext` class in `flask/ctx.py` and several documentation files to ensure consistent naming throughout the project.

This commit adds a missing newline to the end of the `_assert_have_json` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It ensures the file ends with a proper line break, which is a standard convention for text files.

This commit adds documentation to the CLI guide explaining how to integrate Flask with virtual environments. It provides specific instructions for editing activation scripts in Unix Bash and Windows CMD to set the application name automatically.

This commit adds documentation to the async-await guide warning users about a Python 3.8 bug on Windows. It explains that encountering a specific thread-related error requires upgrading to Python 3.9.

This commit adds the ability to register Click CLI commands directly onto Flask blueprints. When a blueprint is registered with the application, its commands become available under the main flask command, typically nested within a group named after the blueprint.

This commit fixes a bug where handled exceptions were incorrectly treated as missing during context teardown. It replaces the default `None` value with a dedicated sentinel in `Flask.do_teardown_request` and `Flask.do_teardown_appcontext` to distinguish between no exception and a handled one.

This commit removes the `_os_alt_seps` variable from the `flask.helpers` module. It eliminates a list of operating system path separators that was previously used to prevent directory traversal attacks in the `send_from_directory` function.

This commit fixes an invalid cross-reference in the Python 3 documentation. It corrects the anchor label in the `docs/python3.rst` file to ensure links to the Python 3 support section resolve correctly.

This commit fixes a PEP 8 style violation by ensuring inline comments are preceded by at least two spaces. It updates the Flask class, safe_join function, and test_iterable_loader test to correct the spacing.
This commit updates the project's test configuration to use pytest instead of the custom run-tests.py script. It adds pytest to the dependencies and changes the test command in the tox.ini file.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.8.4 to 1.8.5. This patch-level dependency update ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for deploying packages.

This commit adds a `config_class` attribute to the Flask application class, allowing developers to specify a custom class for managing application configuration. The `make_config` method now uses this attribute to instantiate the configuration object, enabling features like attribute-based access to settings.

The `redirect` helper in Flask now returns a 303 status code by default instead of 302. This ensures clients always switch to GET requests after a redirect, which is more correct for frontend libraries like HTMX.

This commit corrects a broken class reference in the error handling documentation. It updates the description of the asctime format specifier to properly link to the LogRecord class, ensuring users can navigate to the correct API documentation.
This commit adds Martijn Pieters to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It acknowledges his contribution of patches and suggestions to the project.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the application context documentation. It corrects a sentence in the `appcontext.rst` file to properly state that extensions should store their additional information.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `jinja_loader` property in the `Scaffold` class. It changes the return type from `FileSystemLoader` to the more general `BaseLoader`, ensuring the annotation accurately reflects the possible loader types.

This commit updates the documentation for the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py`. It clarifies that the `SERVER_NAME` configuration variable controls the server address used when generating absolute URLs, defaulting to `localhost`.

This commit clarifies the documentation for the `before_request` method in the `Flask` class. It explicitly states that these functions take no arguments and that returning a non-None value stops further request handling by treating the return value as the response.
This commit adds Flask-Mail to the list of approved extensions in the extreview module. It records the initial approval date, version 0.3.4, and BSD license for the package.

This commit adds a test to verify that the CLI correctly displays a full traceback when an exception occurs during app creation. The test ensures that error messages and stack traces are visible to users, confirming the behavior of the FlaskGroup class in the test_cli.py module.

This commit ensures Flask always registers URL rules for static files, even if the static folder does not exist. This change supports Google App Engine environments where static folders may be removed during deployment. The modification affects the Flask class initialization and helper functions.
This commit updates the CHANGES file to add a missing reference link for a specific pull request. It ensures the changelog correctly links to the relevant issue for the unreleased major version.

This commit fixes minor documentation typos in the installation and quickstart guides. It corrects a missing closing parenthesis in the shell instructions and a grammatical error in the debugger description.

The `SessionInterface.get_expiration_time` method in Flask's sessions module now returns a timezone-aware UTC datetime instead of a naive one. This ensures session expiration times are correctly interpreted across different time zones.

This commit corrects minor spelling and capitalization errors in the project's changelog and documentation files. It updates the CHANGES file and documentation pages to ensure consistent terminology and proper grammar.

This commit removes obsolete code from the DispatchingJinjaLoader class in the flask/templating module that attempted to handle legacy module-based template loaders. It eliminates a workaround for old-style blueprints, cleaning up the template loading process.

This commit fixes a security vulnerability in the `send_from_directory` function within `flask/helpers.py` that allowed users to download arbitrary files on Windows systems. It now blocks requests containing OS-specific path separators, preventing access to files outside the intended directory.

This commit updates the minimum required version of the Werkzeug dependency from 2.3.3 to 2.3.5. It modifies the project configuration and test requirements to ensure compatibility with the newer release.

This commit fixes an issue where setting an empty static folder required explicitly defining an empty static URL path. It updates the Flask and Blueprint classes to automatically strip trailing slashes from the static URL path during assignment.

This commit fixes a crash in Flask's RequestContext when the URL adapter fails to initialize due to invalid request headers. Instead of propagating the error, it now treats the failure as a standard routing exception, resulting in a proper HTTP error response.

This commit refactors the command loading logic in the Flask CLI module to properly inherit from the new ContextGroupMixin. It removes the redundant initialization and command handling code from the FlaskGroup class, simplifying the structure. Users will notice no change in behavior, as this is an internal code cleanup.

This commit corrects a typo in the docstring for the DispatchingApp class in flask/cli.py. It changes the word "applicationt" to "application," ensuring the documentation is accurate and free of spelling errors.

This commit modifies the `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` to remove the "flask" prefix from generated ETags. This change obscures the underlying server technology from clients, preventing them from easily identifying the web framework in use.
This commit simplifies the MongoEngine documentation page and redirects the legacy Mongokit page to it. It updates the title and introductory text in the MongoEngine pattern file to improve clarity.

This commit updates the templating documentation to cover filters, tests, and globals, and cleans up type hints for the related decorators. It affects the App and Blueprint classes in the sansio modules.

This commit updates the changelog to include a reference link to the documentation for pluggable views. It clarifies the description of the new class-based views feature for users reviewing the release notes.
This commit adds a new section to the project's changelog file for version 0.10. It introduces a placeholder entry indicating that the release date is yet to be determined.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency from version 2.5.0 to 2.5.1 in the development requirements file. It ensures the project uses the latest patch release of the pre-commit tool for running git hooks.

This commit removes the entire flask.py module, eliminating the core Flask application framework. Users will no longer be able to create or run Flask applications, as all essential classes and functions are deleted.
This commit adds a new guide for Flask extension developers to the documentation. It introduces the extensiondev.rst file and updates the documentation index to include the new page.
This commit updates the CHANGES file to finalize the release details for version 0.9. It sets the release date to July 1st, 2012, and assigns the codename Camapri.

This commit corrects grammatical errors in the error handling documentation. It fixes phrasing in the introductory text and clarifies the explanation regarding log message visibility in production mode.
This commit ensures the simplejson library is installed when running tests for Python 2.5. It adds a specific test environment configuration to the tox.ini file to handle this dependency.

This commit updates the security documentation to recommend only the flask-talisman package for configuring HTTPS and security headers. It removes the previous list of multiple alternative packages and simplifies the guidance for users setting up secure connections.
This commit adds a new line art logo file to the project's artwork directory. It introduces the SVG asset for use in documentation or branding materials.

This commit corrects the documentation for deferred callbacks by adding a missing return statement to the example code. It ensures the example properly demonstrates how to return a response object within a before_request callback.

This commit switches the project to use pip-compile for managing development, documentation, and test dependencies. It updates the setup instructions and build configuration to reference the new pinned requirements files, ensuring consistent and reproducible environments for contributors.

This commit adds a speculative comment to the `is_important_traceback` method in the `_ExtensionImporter` class. It explains why global variables remain accessible during import failures, noting that Python removes the module from `sys.modules` without nulling its globals.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2010 to 2011 in the header comments of several Flask modules. It affects files such as app.py, config.py, and helpers.py, ensuring the metadata reflects the current year. No functional code changes are included.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `loads` function in Flask's JSON module. It now accurately indicates that the function accepts both string and byte inputs, resolving a mismatch between the declared type and actual behavior.

This commit adds interactive Python documentation and fixes part styling. It enables manual context binding for console use without requiring the with statement. The request context is now accessible within the with statement, allowing further push or pop operations.

This commit adds a `decorators` attribute to the `flask.views.View` class, allowing developers to apply decorators to class-based views directly within the class definition. This simplifies the process of adding functionality like authentication to pluggable views without manually wrapping the view function.
Removes an unused import from the Minitwit test suite. This cleanup simplifies the test module without altering any application behavior or fixing a user-facing bug.

This commit updates the README to reflect the migration from the custom `run-tests.py` script to the `py.test` testing tool. It clarifies that tests are now located in the `tests/` directory and simplifies the instructions for running the test suite.

This commit updates the Flask documentation to explain how to make a development server accessible from other devices on a network. It clarifies that the server is restricted to localhost by default for security reasons and shows how to change the host setting in the `Flask.run` method to allow external connections.

This commit updates outdated project URLs in the Flask documentation, examples, and source code to point to the new Pallets Projects domain. It ensures that links to Jinja and other resources resolve correctly for users. The changes affect the debug helpers and template testing modules.

This commit removes the redundant `_register_error_handler` method from the `Scaffold` class in `src/flask/scaffold.py`. It simplifies the error handling logic by having `errorhandler` call `register_error_handler` directly, eliminating an unnecessary intermediate step.

The `tojson` filter in Flask templates is now safe by default, removing the need for the `|safe` modifier to prevent double-escaping. This change updates the escaping logic in `flask/json.py` and adjusts documentation to reflect that JSON output is automatically handled for safe inclusion in HTML.

This commit updates the project's development and typing dependencies to their latest versions. It bumps the pre-commit hook revision, along with the identify, cryptography, and mypy packages, ensuring the tooling remains current.

This commit refines several test cases in the test suite to improve assertion precision and fix context handling. It updates tests in test_appctx.py, test_basic.py, test_cli.py, and test_config.py to use more specific error matching and proper client context managers.
This commit removes the `view_func` parameter from the documentation of the `Flask.route` method in `flask/app.py`. It corrects the API reference to accurately reflect the current function signature.

This commit corrects a documentation typo in the testing guide, changing "close the function" to "close the file." It also reverts a previous change in the main Flask module that added an unnecessary blank line.

This commit deprecates the FLASK_ENV environment variable and the app.env attribute, removing the distinction between development and debug modes. Users should now control debug mode directly using the --debug option or app.run(debug=True). The changes primarily affect the Flask class and CLI helpers.

This commit updates the Python 3 documentation in the Flask project to reflect that most users still rely on Python 2. It removes outdated statistics regarding PyPI download numbers and clarifies the current state of ecosystem support.

This commit updates the documentation for the configuration module to provide more practical examples for the DATABASE_URI setting. It replaces a simple in-memory database example with a demonstration of how to construct a file-based SQLite path using the operating system's path utilities.

This commit expands the test matrix to verify the project's behavior with and without the simplejson dependency. It updates the Travis CI configuration and tox environment list to include new test environments that explicitly install simplejson.

This commit adds a new decorator, `template_test`, to the Flask application and Blueprint classes. It allows developers to register custom Jinja2 tests, mirroring the existing functionality for template filters.

This commit updates the session lifetime test in the Flask test suite to use the `seconds` attribute instead of the `total_seconds` method. This change ensures compatibility with Python 2.6 and earlier versions, which do not support the `total_seconds` method on timedelta objects.
This commit fixes a bug where request contexts were leaking during test execution. It adds a check to the FlaskTestCase tearDown method to ensure the request context stack is empty after each test.

This commit updates the CLI tip message in the `load_dotenv` function within `flask/cli.py`. It now informs users that both `.env` and `.flaskenv` files are recognized, clarifying which configuration files can be used.

This commit updates development dependencies, including bumping the setup-uv action version in GitHub workflows. It also applies minor code adjustments to several Flask modules, such as the App, Scaffold, and testing classes, to align with the updated tooling.

This commit updates external links in the documentation and contribution guides to use HTTPS instead of HTTP. It ensures that references to external resources, such as Stack Overflow and Sphinx, are secure. The changes affect multiple files, including the issue template and various documentation pages.

This commit corrects a broken cross-reference in the Flask signals documentation. It updates the link to point to the correct request context section, ensuring users can navigate to the relevant information about context-local variables.

This commit updates the changelog to document a fix preventing exception details from leaking into context teardown handlers. It clarifies that information from already caught exceptions is no longer exposed during the teardown process.

This commit corrects the documentation for Flask extension development to reflect the proper import order. It updates the guidance in the extensiondev module to recommend importing from flask_foo first, rather than the previously suggested flask.ext.foo.

In the persona example, the login handler now uses the response's built-in JSON method to parse verification data instead of manually decoding the raw content. This simplifies the code in the login_handler function.

This commit adds `is_json` and `get_json` methods to the `Response` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to simplify testing JSON responses. It also updates the testing documentation to reflect these new methods and corrects minor wording.

This commit replaces the global `_get_data` helper with a `_get_data_for_json` method on the `JSONMixin` and `Response` classes. It allows the `get_json` method to pass a cache flag to the request's data getter, improving response caching behavior.

This commit fixes an issue in Flask's BlueprintSetupState where a blueprint with an empty string prefix was incorrectly ignored. It changes the logic in the add_url_rule method to allow empty prefixes and routes without a leading slash.
This commit adds tests to the TestJSON class in tests/test_helpers.py. It verifies that flask.json.dump correctly writes data to a file and that jsonify properly converts UUID objects.

The `url_for` function in `flask.py` now appends any unknown keyword arguments to the generated URL as query parameters. The quickstart documentation is updated to explain this behavior and provide an example of using it.

This commit fixes a missing import in the Flask quickstart documentation. It adds the necessary line to import the request object in the HTTP methods example, ensuring the code snippet runs correctly for users.

This commit corrects a typo in the server documentation, changing "got to" to "go to" when describing how to disable a conflicting service on MacOS. The change is located in the `docs/server.rst` file.

This commit removes outdated external links to the project website and Twitter account from the documentation and configuration files. It updates the README, Sphinx configuration, and project metadata to reflect the removal of these social media and web presence references.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask application where proxy exceptions could trigger incorrect error handlers. The `handle_user_exception` method now explicitly checks for a null error code to ensure these exceptions are always trapped and filtered out.
This commit cleans up the SVG files used for the Flask documentation branding. It updates the horizontal, vertical, and icon assets to improve their structure and rendering quality.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Flask CLI that prevented the code from running on Python 3. It updates the `DispatchingApp` class to use the `reraise` helper instead of the deprecated Python 2 exception raising syntax.

This commit fixes a bug preventing proper subdomain support by allowing the server name to be specified. It introduces a new `SERVER_NAME` configuration key in the `Flask` application to enable this functionality.

This commit improves the reliability of Flask's teardown system when exceptions are handled during error processing. It introduces a new `should_ignore_error` method to the `Flask` class and updates `RequestContext` to ensure teardown handlers receive accurate exception information.

This commit refactors the JSON dump tests in the TestJSON class to use in-memory string buffers instead of writing to temporary files. It removes the dependency on the PY2 compatibility flag and updates the test data to use a more descriptive example.

This commit updates the test suite for the `find_best_app` function in the CLI module. It adds a new test case to verify behavior when a module does not contain a Flask application and renames internal test classes for clarity.

This commit adds documentation for the `static_path` parameter in the `Flask` and `Module` classes. It clarifies that this option, introduced in version 0.5, allows users to specify a custom web path for static files without changing the underlying file directory.

This documentation update clarifies how to serve uploaded files in a Flask application. It removes the manual URL rule configuration and explains using the SharedDataMiddleware to handle file serving automatically.

This commit prevents Flask from registering empty CLI groups when a Blueprint is added to an application. It modifies the Blueprint class to skip registration if no commands are defined, ensuring that invoking such a group results in an error rather than a confusing empty help message.

This commit removes unused module docstrings from various Flask source and test files. It also simplifies the `__main__.py` entry point by removing redundant conditional logic. No user-facing behavior changes.

This commit adds a backwards compatibility import in the `flask` package to ensure the `Session` class remains accessible from the top-level namespace. It also updates the upgrading documentation to explain the separation of the session module and object in version 0.8.

This commit adds a comprehensive test suite for the MiniTwit example application, verifying core features like user registration, login, and message posting. It also fixes a typo in the password mismatch error message within the register function.

This commit updates the pre-commit configuration to use newer versions of the pyupgrade, reorder_python_imports, and black tools. It ensures the project's automated code checks and formatting align with the latest releases of these utilities.

This commit adds TODO comments to the Azure Pipelines configuration file. It notes that a codecov token needs to be added and that JUnit test results should be emitted. No functional behavior is changed.

This commit adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow to automatically lock inactive issues and pull requests. The new lock.yaml file triggers every ten minutes to close threads that have been inactive for fourteen days, helping maintain repository organization.

This commit updates the BetterLoader class in run-tests.py to recognize fully qualified test names. It allows the test runner to correctly load tests when the name starts with the module prefix, fixing cases where such tests were previously ignored.
This commit updates the Flask package version to 0.12.3-dev in the `flask/__init__.py` module. It marks the start of a new development cycle following the 0.12.2 release.
This commit adds Thomas Schranz to the list of contributors in the AUTHORS file. It updates the project's credit list to acknowledge his patches and suggestions.

Removes the MANIFEST.in file, which previously defined which non-Python files to include in source distributions. This change likely reflects a migration to a modern build system that handles file inclusion automatically.

This commit allows templates to be rendered without an active request context, meaning request, session, and g objects are unavailable. It also makes the config object a true global, ensuring it is accessible in imported templates. These changes affect the Flask application and templating modules.

This documentation update modifies the SQLAlchemy pattern examples to enable Unicode support by adding the convert_unicode flag to the engine creation calls. It ensures that the documented database configuration properly handles Unicode data for users following the guide.

This commit updates the Flask quickstart documentation to accurately list the objects and functions available inside templates. It adds references to the application config and the URL generation function, while also correcting the grammar of the surrounding text.

This commit switches the Flask project's build backend from setuptools to flit_core. It updates the project configuration to use flit for versioning and source distribution packaging, ensuring the build process aligns with the new backend requirements.
The project logo displayed in the PDF documentation has been updated. This change refreshes the visual branding in the generated documentation files.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.3.2 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the release date in the changelog. It transitions the package from a development state to a stable release.

This commit fixes a missing backtick in the docstring for the `get_cookie_path` method within the `SessionInterface` class in `flask/sessions.py`. The change corrects the documentation formatting for the `SESSION_COOKIE_PATH` configuration variable.

This commit adds initial type checking support to the Flask project by integrating mypy into the CI workflow and marking the package as typed. It configures the type checker in setup.cfg and includes the necessary dependencies and metadata files.

This commit updates the DebugFilesKeyError class in flask/debughelpers.py to encode its error message as UTF-8 bytes. It also adds a test case to verify this debug behavior when accessing missing file uploads.

This commit improves the clarity and flow of the Flask documentation's introductory sections. It rewrites the description of the User's Guide in the table of contents and refines the foreword to better explain the project's purpose.

This commit fixes an unbound error in the Flask application by correcting a method call within the ListConverter class. The change ensures the parent class's to_url method is properly invoked, resolving a potential runtime failure during URL generation.

This commit reorganizes the documentation structure by swapping the order of the "API Reference" and "Additional Notes" sections. It moves the API reference to appear immediately after the main content, while shifting design notes, license, and changelog information to the end.

This commit corrects a grammatical error in the Django tutorial documentation. It updates the description of the register view function in the views module to use the correct article before "validation error."

This commit adds a new test module to automatically verify the compatibility of Flask extensions. It fetches the list of available extensions and runs their test suites using tox to ensure they work correctly with the current Flask version.

This commit updates the copyright year from 2010 to 2012 in the project's license file and documentation configuration. It ensures the legal attribution and metadata in the docs reflect the current year.

This commit updates the session classes in Flask to use generic type parameters for better type checking. It modifies `SessionMixin` and `SecureCookieSession` to explicitly define their key and value types, removing previous type ignore comments.
This commit adds a new `run_audit` command to the `setup.py` module. It allows users to audit their source code for undefined or redefined names using PyFlakes.

This commit fixes a bash syntax error in the Flask application factory documentation by adding quotes around the app factory argument. It also corrects the application name from "myapp" to "hello" to match the example code.

This commit adds a new section to the CLI documentation explaining how to configure PyCharm to work with the Flask CLI. It includes a screenshot of the run configuration settings to guide users through the necessary IDE tweaks.

The `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py` now accepts a `_method` parameter to explicitly generate URLs for specific HTTP methods. This allows developers to create links that target particular request types, such as POST, rather than relying on default behavior.
