This commit corrects a grammatical error in the documentation for circular imports. It updates the description in the patterns module to accurately state that two modules depend on each other.

This commit updates the Python dependencies in the requirements files to their latest patch versions. It bumps pyright, pytest, and pre-commit to ensure the project uses the most recent stable releases for development and testing tools.

This commit updates the Flask API documentation to warn users that disabling JSON key sorting may cause issues with content-based HTTP caches and Python's hash randomization. The change clarifies the potential side effects of setting the `JSON_SORT_KEYS` configuration variable to false.

This commit corrects awkward phrasing and clarifies the introduction of the testing documentation. It improves the readability of the text in the `docs/testing.rst` file, specifically regarding the origin of a quote and the benefits of automated testing.

This commit corrects minor grammatical and typographical errors in the Flask documentation and source code comments. It updates phrasing in the configuration, style guide, and upgrading guides, as well as comments within the Flask application class.
This commit corrects a typo in the CLI documentation by updating the reference from `data.info` to `info.data`. It ensures the docs accurately describe the structure of the data dictionary for users.

This commit updates the mod_wsgi deployment documentation to include instructions for using virtual environments. It explains how to modify the .wsgi file to activate a specific virtual environment, ensuring dependencies are isolated from the system-wide installation.

This commit makes the endpoint parameter optional for modules, allowing Flask to automatically derive the endpoint name from the view function's name. It introduces a new helper function, `_endpoint_from_view_func`, in `flask/helpers.py` to handle this logic, which is then used by both the `Flask` and `Module` classes when registering URL rules.

This commit fixes a typo in the docstring for the `get_cookie_path` method within the `SessionInterface` class in `flask/sessions.py`. It corrects the formatting of the `SESSION_COOKIE_PATH` reference to properly display as a code element.

This commit updates the installation guide in the documentation module. It removes introductory text about installation methods and WSGI definitions, streamlining the description of Flask's external dependencies.

This commit introduces a new TESTING configuration flag to the Flask class. It allows developers to enable testing mode, which activates unittest helpers and other features with additional runtime costs that are disabled by default.

This commit fixes an unexpected CI failure by excluding example tests from the test suite. It modifies the `tox.ini` configuration to run only the main test directory, preventing the example tests from executing.

Updates the development requirements to fetch the blinker dependency from its new GitHub location instead of Bitbucket. This ensures the build system can successfully install the package after the repository migration.

This commit enables blueprints to define specific error handlers that take precedence over global application settings. It modifies the Flask class to manage these blueprint-specific handlers during request processing. Users can now customize error responses for individual blueprints rather than relying solely on app-wide defaults.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 3.0.1 by updating the project metadata. It changes the version string in the configuration file from a development build to the stable release and marks the changelog entry as released.

Updates the lock-threads GitHub Action from version 4.0.0 to 4.0.1 in the lock.yaml workflow. This patch release applies minor fixes to the automated thread locking process without changing its core behavior.
This commit fixes a typo in the package documentation. It corrects a sentence in the `docs/patterns/packages.rst` file to accurately describe redirecting to a different function rather than a module.

This commit corrects several spelling errors in the Flask API documentation. It fixes typos in the `docs/api.rst` file, ensuring terms like "library," "signaling," and "overridden" are spelled correctly for users reading the manual.

This commit updates the project's changelog to document a new feature. It notes that the system now supports per-package template and static-file directories, allowing developers to organize assets more granularly.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Flask class. It updates the docstring for the `create_global_jinja_loader` method to accurately reference the `jinja_loader` function instead of the incorrect `create_jinja_loader` name.

This commit adds documentation for deploying Flask applications using the Twisted Web server. It explains how to use the `twistd` utility to run a WSGI application, providing examples for standard and foreground execution.

This commit corrects grammatical errors in the Python 3 documentation file. It changes "complicated" to "complicates" and "effect" to "affect" to accurately describe how encoding issues impact users. The text is also rewrapped for better readability.

This commit fixes a documentation error in the testing guide where a code example was missing the necessary `os` import. It ensures the example correctly imports both `os` and `unittest` to prevent confusion for users following the instructions.

Updates the Flask CLI to support the newer Click 2.0 library. It adjusts the `set_debug_value` and `set_app_value` functions to accept the required `param` argument, ensuring compatibility with the updated dependency.

The `fix_from_imports` function in `flaskext_migrate.py` now correctly skips imports that should remain unchanged, preventing unintended modifications. This fix ensures that valid import statements are preserved during the migration process.

This commit updates the pre-commit dependency from version 2.4.0 to 2.5.0 in the development requirements file. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the pre-commit framework for running code checks.
Flask now raises an error when attempting to register a new function on an already used endpoint. This change clarifies the behavior for users who mistakenly try to reuse an existing endpoint name.
This commit adds a link to the official documentation in the project's README file. Users can now easily access the Flask documentation directly from the project's main description page.
This commit updates the pre-commit development dependency from version 2.14.0 to 2.14.1. It modifies the requirements/dev.txt file to reflect this patch-level version bump.

This commit corrects the example values for the `url` and `base_url` fields in the API documentation. It ensures the examples accurately reflect that `base_url` excludes query parameters while `url` includes them.

This commit adds documentation explaining that Flask async views cannot spawn background tasks because the event loop stops when the view completes. It advises using a task queue or an ASGI server with the asgiref adapter to handle background work. The changes update the async-await and ASGI deployment guides.
This commit introduces the initial HTML structure and logo for the Flask project website. It establishes the basic layout, styling, and branding elements for the new web presence.

This commit refactors session cookie domain logic in Flask's `SecureCookieSessionInterface` to allow IP addresses as exact domains. It adds warnings when the domain is a bare hostname or IP, which may cause issues in browsers like Chrome.

This commit updates tests in the test_helpers module to verify that the Content-Disposition header correctly handles UTF-8 filenames. It ensures the header parsing logic properly identifies the last parsed value for the filename option.

The Makefile now uploads Flask documentation to a new server, flow.srv.pocoo.org, instead of the previous host. This change updates the rsync destinations for the HTML, PDF, ZIP, and EPUB files to the new path.

This fix ensures that Flask's `process_response` method correctly applies all registered after-request functions, including those from the application context, when Blueprints are present. Previously, the method would discard these functions, causing them to be skipped during the response phase.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's `jsonify` function where the JSON response body was incorrectly formatted as a tuple instead of a string. Users would have noticed the output included extra parentheses and quotes around the JSON data. The change ensures the newline is properly appended to the serialized JSON string.

This commit fixes a bug in Flask's BlueprintSetupState where registering a route with an empty string failed to correctly apply the blueprint's URL prefix. The add_url_rule method now properly handles empty rules by assigning the prefix directly, ensuring routes like the root path resolve correctly.
This commit updates the changelog to mark version 0.12.1 as officially released on March 31st, 2017. It clarifies the release status for users checking the project's history.

This commit corrects the type annotation for the `TeardownCallable` in the `flask.typing` module. It changes the expected return type from a response object to `None`, accurately reflecting that teardown functions do not return a value.
The publish workflow now uses OIDC authentication for PyPI uploads instead of static tokens. This change removes the need to store and manage secret tokens for the publishing process.

This commit fixes a bug in the `safe_join` function within `flask/helpers.py` where the function incorrectly used POSIX path separators on Windows. This change ensures that path validation correctly handles Windows-specific separators, preventing potential security issues or errors when joining paths on that platform.

This commit updates the sphinx-tabs dependency in the documentation requirements from version 1.1.13 to 1.3.0. It also removes several transitive dependencies that are no longer required by the new version.

This commit prevents duplicate registration of blueprint components like routes and error handlers when a blueprint is attached to multiple applications. It introduces a first_registration flag in the Blueprint class to ensure setup logic runs only once per blueprint instance.

This commit adds test cases to the ExtImportHookTestCase class to verify the import behavior of legacy Flask extension packages. It ensures that both simple and package-based old-style extensions are correctly resolved by the import hook.

This commit removes the dependency on the pytz library for handling time zones in the test suite. It updates the `test_jsonify_aware_datetimes` function in `tests/test_helpers.py` to use standard timezone offsets instead of pytz time zones.
This commit corrects grammar and typos in the Flask extension development documentation. It improves the clarity of instructions regarding licensing requirements and class design for shared objects.

This commit removes IRC notification settings from the Travis CI configuration. Users will no longer receive build status updates in the Freenode chat channel. The change affects the .travis.yml file.

This commit fixes a documentation example in the quickstart guide that caused a ValueError because the view function did not return a response. It updates the code snippet to properly return the result of the login functions.

This commit adds a security warning to the `send_file` function in `flask.py`. It advises developers to validate user-provided filenames to prevent path traversal vulnerabilities, suggesting a check for directory traversal characters.

This commit corrects a capitalization error in the documentation headline for the jQuery AJAX pattern. It changes the title from "AJAX With jQuery" to "AJAX with jQuery" in the `docs/patterns/jquery.rst` file.

This commit refactors the test suite in tests/test_testing.py by removing class-based test structures. It converts the TestTestTools and TestSubdomain classes into standalone functions to simplify the test organization.

This commit fixes a broken test case in the Flask signals test suite that failed when the blinker library was missing. It updates the test environment configuration files to ensure blinker is installed during testing. The changes primarily affect the SignalsTestCase class in the signals test module.

This commit changes the default behavior of the `TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD` configuration in the Flask application class. Previously, templates were always reloaded on request; now, they are only reloaded when the application is running in debug mode. This adjustment improves performance by avoiding unnecessary disk I/O in production environments.

This update allows Flask view functions to return lists, which are automatically converted to JSON responses just like dictionaries. The change modifies the `Flask.make_response` method to handle this new return type and updates the documentation to reflect the expanded behavior.

This commit removes the deprecated `total_seconds` helper function from the `flask.helpers` module. Users should now use the standard `timedelta.total_seconds` method instead to calculate the total seconds from a time delta object.

This commit fixes a test failure on Windows where the `os.path.samefile` function is unavailable. It updates the `add_to_path` function in the Flask test suite to handle the missing attribute gracefully, preventing crashes during test setup.

This commit fixes a bug in the Blueprint class where the app_url_value_preprocessor method failed to register functions correctly. It corrects the internal attribute name and key used to store these preprocessors, ensuring they are properly applied to URL routing.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.0.0 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the release date in the changelog. It transitions the package from a release candidate to the stable version.

This commit updates the project's development, documentation, and testing dependencies to their latest versions. It also adds the typing requirements file to the development dependencies, ensuring type checking tools are available during development.
This commit corrects a typo in the error handling documentation by changing "changes are" to "chances are." The fix improves the clarity of the text in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file.

This commit adds tests for the new application context stack behavior in Flask. It updates the `url_for` function in `flask/helpers.py` to raise specific errors when the application context is missing or a URL adapter cannot be created.

This commit adds documentation to the configuration guide explaining how the SERVER_NAME setting affects subdomain support and session cookies. It clarifies that browsers may block cross-subdomain cookies when the server name lacks dots, such as localhost.

This commit removes the automatic monthly update schedule for pre-commit hooks. It modifies the pre-commit configuration file to stop the continuous integration system from automatically updating the hook versions.

This documentation update removes the instruction to run the example script with the Python interpreter. It clarifies that users should simply save the file, while retaining the warning against naming the application flask.py to avoid conflicts.

This commit adds support for nesting blueprints within other blueprints, a long-requested feature. It introduces a new `register_blueprint` method on the `Blueprint` class to allow this hierarchical structure. The `Flask` app now handles these nested structures by resolving endpoint names and URL prefixes from parent to child.
This commit updates the versions of pyupgrade, black, and pre-commit-hooks in the pre-commit configuration. It ensures the project uses the latest stable releases of these code quality tools.

This commit updates the documentation build process in the tox configuration to ensure a clean build for every test run. By adding the environment flag to the Sphinx command, it prevents stale artifacts from interfering with the output.

This commit corrects the test file names referenced in the Flaskr and Minitwit example READMEs. It updates the documentation to point to the actual test files, preventing users from attempting to run non-existent scripts.

This commit adds a new "Requirements" section to the Python 3 documentation. It clarifies that Flask requires Python 3.3 or higher and mandates the latest versions of its core dependencies, including itsdangerous, Jinja2, and Werkzeug.

This commit fixes a data type mismatch in the Flask test suite's request processing tests. It corrects the `after_request` handler in `BasicFunctionalityTestCase` to properly handle byte strings, ensuring the test accurately validates response data modifications.
This commit removes the Python 3.4 test job from the Azure Pipelines configuration. It stops the continuous integration system from running builds on this unsupported Python version.

This commit corrects version references in the Flask documentation, changing mentions of version 1.0 to 0.11. It ensures that features like CLI integration and error logging are accurately attributed to the correct release in the API, CLI, and error handling guides.

This commit adds documentation explaining how to implement custom API error handlers in Flask. It guides developers on creating expressive exception types to replace default HTML error responses for RESTful APIs.

The `get_flashed_messages` function in `flask/helpers.py` now accepts a `category_filter` argument. This allows developers to retrieve only specific message categories, enabling them to render different types of flash messages in separate HTML blocks.

This commit updates the Flask tutorial documentation to clarify password storage practices. It replaces a simple text note with a formal security admonition in the views module, warning users against storing plain text passwords in production systems.

This commit fixes an import error in the Flaskr example that occurred when using Python 2. It updates the `flaskr/__init__.py` module to use a relative import, ensuring compatibility with both Python 2 and 3. The documentation and configuration files are also updated to reflect this change.

This commit updates the documentation for error handling to fix a broken link to Sentry's Flask-specific guide. The change corrects the URL in the `docs/errorhandling.rst` file to point to the current, valid location for the resource.

The `main` function in `flask/cli.py` now only appends `.cli` to the reloader command on Python 2.6. This prevents an import warning from appearing when running the CLI on Python 2.7 or later versions.

This commit adds a test to verify that the `from_pyfile` method in `flask/config.py` correctly handles missing files when the `silent` flag is enabled. It also fixes a test failure by importing the `errno` module and updating an assertion in `tests/flask_tests.py`.

This commit fixes a syntax error in the Flask CLI that prevented the command-line interface from functioning. It modifies the FlaskGroup class to ensure built-in commands are loaded first, allowing the script to remain functional even if the application fails to load.

This commit changes the behavior of Flask's request local proxies so that accessing unbound objects raises a RuntimeError instead of an AttributeError. The change is implemented in the `_lookup_object` function within the `flask/globals` module.

This commit updates the Python version requirements in setup.py to explicitly exclude Python 3.3. Users attempting to install the package on Python 3.3 will now be prevented from doing so, ensuring compatibility with supported versions only.

This commit updates the documentation for the `Flask` application class and the `redirect` helper function. It clarifies that `flask.redirect` now delegates to the `app.redirect` method, allowing developers to customize redirect behavior.

This commit updates the Cherokee project links in the FastCGI and uWSGI deployment documentation to use HTTPS instead of HTTP. This ensures users are directed to the secure version of the website when following the setup instructions.

This commit corrects the type annotations for the `__exit__` methods in `AppContext`, `RequestContext`, and `FlaskClient` to allow optional values. This improves compatibility with Python's `ExitStack` utility by accurately reflecting that exception arguments may be null.

This commit adds a test case to the Flask test suite verifying that before-request hooks execute correctly when a routing error occurs. It ensures that the 404 error handler can access data attached to the application context by these hooks.

This commit updates the FastCGI deployment documentation to clarify how to hide the .fcgi file from application URLs. It refines the explanation of using the ScriptAlias directive in Apache to achieve cleaner URL structures.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 0.7 by updating the version string from a development build to the stable release. It modifies the version identifiers in the main package initialization and the project setup configuration.

This commit fixes the instance path detection in the Flask class to correctly handle applications installed as Python eggs. It ensures the path resolution skips the egg wrapper folder, allowing the application to locate its instance directory properly.
This commit updates the SQLAlchemy documentation example to include the `Table` class in the import statement. It ensures the code snippet is complete and functional for users following the pattern.

This commit updates the packaging dependency from version 20.8 to 20.9 across development, documentation, and test requirements. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the library for version parsing and comparison.

This commit renames the Flask application's request lifecycle hooks from `request_init` and `request_shutdown` to `before_request` and `after_request`. The change updates the `Flask` class, documentation, and examples to reflect the new, clearer naming convention for these decorators.

This commit fixes the ordering of signing keys in the `SecureCookieSessionInterface` to ensure the active key is correctly identified during rotation. It resolves an issue where fallback keys were not prioritized as expected by the serializer.
This commit removes trailing whitespace from a docstring in the Flask class within flask/app.py. It is a cosmetic change that does not alter the application's behavior or functionality.

This commit converts the project's README file from plain text to Markdown format. It removes the old ASCII art layout and replaces it with standard Markdown syntax for better readability and compatibility with modern documentation platforms.

This commit updates the sendfile test helper to use the older response data attribute, ensuring compatibility with older Werkzeug versions. It modifies the SendfileTestCase class to prevent test failures when running against legacy dependencies.

This commit updates the Flask CLI to allow the FLASK_APP environment variable to point to local packages without requiring a .py extension. It modifies the ScriptInfo class and related functions in flask/cli.py to support loading nested packages and local modules.

This commit updates the README to clarify that installing Flask via pip automatically handles all dependencies. It removes the previous mention of easy_install to improve accuracy. The change simplifies the installation instructions for users.

This commit ensures that all teardown callbacks in Flask are executed even if one of them raises an error, preventing subsequent cleanup steps from being skipped. The change modifies the `Flask` class and introduces a helper to collect and handle exceptions during the teardown process.

This commit adds the `has_request_context` function to the Flask module, allowing developers to check if a request context is currently active. It enables code to safely access request information without raising errors when no request is present.

This commit fixes a bug in the Flask testsuite where directory names containing dots caused test failures. It corrects file path handling in the ConfigTestCase and LoggingTestCase classes by limiting string splits to the final extension.

This commit fixes a grammatical error in the API documentation for the Flask framework. It corrects the phrasing in the `docs/api.rst` file to accurately describe how the application checks view functions for method definitions.

Calling setup methods on a Flask Blueprint after it has been registered now raises an error instead of issuing a warning. This change in the Blueprint class ensures that configuration changes are not silently ignored, preventing inconsistent application of blueprint settings.
This commit corrects a capitalization typo in the Flaskr tutorial documentation. It updates the application name from lowercase to "Flaskr" in the introduction section to ensure consistent branding.

This commit corrects a spelling error in the documentation for Flask's JSON serialization and request handling. It updates the docstrings for the `dumps` function in `flask/json.py` and the `Request` class in `flask/wrappers.py` to properly spell "overridden."

This commit fixes a broken hyperlink in the upgrading documentation. It corrects the reference to the Flask-OldSessions extension in the docs/upgrading.rst file to ensure users can properly access the linked resource.

This commit fixes a bug in the TaggedJSONSerializer class where registering a new tag with the default index prevented inserting it as the penultimate item in the order list. The default index for the register method is changed from -1 to None to allow correct positioning.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to replace bare assert statements with the self.assert_ method. This change ensures that test failures are properly reported by the testing framework rather than raising unhandled exceptions. The modifications affect multiple test modules, including basic functionality, blueprints, and templating tests.

Updates the PyPI publishing GitHub Action in the publish workflow from version 1.8.5 to 1.8.6. This patch-level dependency update ensures the CI pipeline uses the latest stable release of the action for publishing packages.
This commit fixes a typo in the error handling documentation. It corrects the spelling of "appropriate" in the configuration example within the docs/errorhandling.rst file.
This commit adds a README file to the Flaskr example, providing instructions for setup and usage. It also removes an unnecessary import from the flaskr.py module.

This commit restores the `filename` parameter to the `send_from_directory` function in Flask's helpers module. It allows users to continue using the old parameter name while issuing a deprecation warning to encourage migration to the new `path` argument.
This commit fixes a documentation error in the fileuploads guide by removing an unnecessary HTML paragraph tag. The change ensures the example form code displays correctly without extra markup.

This commit clarifies the documentation for application factories in the Flask patterns guide. It restructures the section on extensions to better explain how they interact with app factories, improving readability for developers.
This commit corrects a spelling error in the Python 3 documentation. It changes the word "untilization" to "utilization" in the API Stability section of the python3.rst file.

This commit adds a new JavaScript AJAX example application to the repository, demonstrating jQuery, XMLHttpRequest, and fetch usage. It updates the documentation to reference this new example and removes outdated links to the MiniTwit test suite.

This commit updates the Flask security documentation to improve consistency and readability. It standardizes the capitalization of technical terms like HTTP, HTTPS, and URLs, and corrects the phrasing of security header descriptions.

This commit updates the mod_wsgi deployment documentation to clarify the syntax change for directory permissions between Apache 2.2 and 2.4. It adds a specific example showing the transition from the older "Order allow,deny" directive to the new "Require all granted" format.

This commit adds a stub for the `connect_via` method to the `_FakeSignal` class in `flask/signals.py`. It ensures that signaling support remains functional when the Blinker library is not installed, preventing errors when this method is called.

This commit deprecates passing the script_info object to application factory functions in Flask's CLI, as this behavior was not portable outside the flask command. Users should now access this data via the Click context if needed. The change affects the call_factory and find_app_by_string functions in the cli module.

This commit adds a dedicated test-requirements.txt file to manage testing dependencies. It updates the Makefile to automatically install these requirements before running tests, ensuring pytest is available for the test suite.

This documentation update clarifies that Flask requires Python 2.5 or higher and does not support Python 3.x. It explains that the WSGI specification was not yet finalized for Python 3 at the time of writing.
This commit corrects a typo in the documentation for the Flask class. It changes the description of the testing attribute from "flask" to "flag" to accurately reflect its purpose.
This commit updates the pip-tools dependency from version 5.1.2 to 5.2.0 in the development requirements. It ensures the project uses the latest stable release of the package management tool.

This commit refactors Flask's internal data structures to use defaultdicts, simplifying code in the Flask, Blueprint, and Scaffold classes. It removes redundant checks for missing keys, making the intent clearer without changing user-facing behavior.

This commit adds test coverage for the flask.json.tag module, verifying that custom tags correctly serialize and deserialize data. It also updates existing session tests to ensure special types are handled properly during storage and retrieval.

The test suite for helper functions now uses the monkeypatch fixture to manage environment variables instead of manually modifying and restoring them. This change improves test isolation and reliability for the TestHelpers class.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to accommodate changes in how Werkzeug formats cookie headers. It corrects assertions in the BasicFunctionalityTestCase to ensure session expiration tests pass reliably.

This commit removes the ExceptionHandlerDict class from the Flask application module. It simplifies how error handlers are stored and looked up by eliminating this custom mapping structure. The change updates the internal logic for registering and finding exception handlers within the Flask class.

This commit updates the Flaskr tutorial setup documentation to address a path issue on Windows systems. It adds a note advising users to replace the default `/tmp` database path with a writable location of their choice to ensure the application runs correctly.

This commit updates the changelog to document that `flask.render_template` now accepts an iterable of template names in addition to a single name. When given an iterable, the function renders the first template it finds.

This commit removes the JSONMixin class from the Flask wrappers module, simplifying the Request and Response classes by eliminating redundant JSON handling logic. It also updates the API documentation to automatically list inherited members instead of manually specifying them.

This commit updates the Flask test suite to verify instance path resolution for various module types, including main modules and installed packages. It adds new test cases to the InstanceTestCase class to ensure correct behavior when applications are run from different directory structures.

This commit adds a `redirect` method to the `Flask` class, allowing applications to customize how redirect responses are generated. The global `flask.redirect` helper now delegates to this new method, enabling apps to override the default redirect behavior.

The `send_file` function in `flask/helpers.py` now issues deprecation warnings when generating etags or guessing mimetypes from file-like objects. This change addresses previous unreliability in these features, prompting users to pass filenames or manually specify metadata instead.

This commit adds documentation for the blueprint parameter in the Flask class's register_blueprint method. It clarifies the expected input for users registering a blueprint, improving the clarity of the API reference.

This commit adjusts the line height settings in the Flasky documentation theme and the main website to improve text readability. It modifies the CSS for paragraphs and list items in the docs, and adds specific line height rules for paragraphs and code blocks on the homepage.

This commit corrects a documentation error in the Flask testing guide where the `client` fixture was incorrectly shown accepting a `request` argument. It updates the example in `docs/testing.rst` and the corresponding code in `examples/flaskr/tests/test_flaskr.py` to reflect that the fixture takes no arguments.

This commit updates the Travis CI configuration to run tests against the standard Python environment instead of the release-specific one. It changes the tox environment variable in the build matrix to ensure the project is tested with the default Python interpreter.

This commit updates the design documentation to clarify that Flask does not include a database layer or form library. It also notes that the logger switches to debug mode when debugging is enabled and highlights the utility of application factory functions for testing.

The documentation for the `allowed_file` function in the file uploads pattern is updated to handle case-insensitive file extensions. This change ensures that files with uppercase extensions are correctly recognized against the allowed list, preventing valid uploads from being rejected.

This commit updates the build requirements in pyproject.toml to mandate flit_core version 3.11 or higher. It prevents a build error that occurred when using an SPDX license expression, which older versions of flit_core did not support.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 2.0.1 by updating the version string in the `flask` module and marking the changelog as released. It changes the package version from a development build to the stable release.

This commit updates the documentation for the `before_first_request` decorator in the `Flask` class. It clarifies that decorated functions must accept no arguments and that their return values are ignored.

This commit updates the project's tagline in the README to clarify that a pocket knife is not always sufficient. It replaces the previous wording with a more concise statement about the limitations of a single tool.

This commit updates the GitHub Actions test workflow to use the full Python version hash for the pre-commit cache key. This ensures the cache correctly invalidates when the specific Python build changes, preventing stale cache hits.

This commit adds documentation to the appdispatch patterns guide explaining how to enable the interactive debugger. It clarifies that debugging must be activated on both the Flask application and the Werkzeug server when using run_simple.

This commit corrects the API documentation to clarify that `request` is an object attribute rather than a class definition. It updates the Sphinx directive in the `docs/api.rst` file to properly reflect that the actual class name is `Request`.

This commit updates the itsdangerous dependency to version 0.17 and refactors the SecureCookieSessionInterface and TaggedJSONSerializer classes in flask/sessions.py. It adjusts the internal serialization tags to align with the new library version, ensuring session data is correctly encoded and decoded.

This commit fixes a logic error in the `prepare_exec_for_file` function within `flask/cli.py` where an `__init__.py` file was incorrectly stripped of its extension. The change ensures the function correctly identifies and handles initialization files before processing standard Python scripts.

This change allows users to pass additional keyword arguments to the `test_client` method, which are forwarded to the client class constructor. This enables customization of the test client instance beyond the default cookie settings.
Updates the copyright year in the documentation configuration from 2012 to 2013. This change ensures the generated documentation displays the correct current year for the Flask project.

This commit removes the use of the pkg_resources library to simplify template loading in Flask. The Flask class now always uses a file system loader for templates, which temporarily drops support for running applications from zip files.

This commit corrects several grammatical typos in the Flask documentation. It updates phrasing in multiple guides, including the extension development and quickstart pages, to improve clarity and readability for users.

This commit adds a missing docstring to the `prepare_exec_for_file` function in `flask/cli.py`. It also simplifies the file path validation logic within the `FlaskClickGroup` class by removing redundant checks for path separators.

This commit removes unused imports from the Flask application and helper modules. It cleans up the codebase by deleting unnecessary references to the `os` module, the `NotFound` exception, and the `wraps` function.

This commit updates the Flask CLI to parse the FLASK_APP environment variable using the ast module, allowing users to pass keyword arguments to application factory functions. The ScriptInfo class and related helper functions in src/flask/cli.py are modified to support this new syntax for defining applications.

This commit updates the documentation link for Flask-Talisman in the web security guide. It corrects the URL to point to the project's current GitHub repository, ensuring users are directed to the correct source.

This commit updates the project's README to clarify that the framework is designed for rapid prototyping rather than small-scale applications. It also adds a link to the community resources page for further guidance.

This commit updates project dependencies and configuration files, including GitHub Actions workflows and pre-commit settings. It also refreshes the lock file and example project definitions to ensure compatibility with the new versions.

This commit fixes a typo in the API documentation where the term "roule" was incorrectly used instead of "rule." It corrects the description for the `rule` parameter in the `docs/api.rst` file to ensure accurate terminology.

This commit optimizes several static image files within the documentation directory to reduce their file sizes. The changes affect assets like the Flask logo and tutorial screenshots, resulting in faster page load times for users viewing the project documentation.

This commit finalizes the release of Flask version 1.1.1 by updating the version string in the main package. It also corrects project documentation and website URLs to use secure HTTPS links across the repository.

This commit fixes a Windows-specific issue where temporary database files were not being removed after tests, causing subsequent test runs to fail. It moves the file cleanup logic from the client fixture into the app fixture to ensure the file is closed and deleted immediately after creation.
This commit improves the grammar and readability of the documentation for the signals module. It corrects minor phrasing errors in the description of signal subscriptions and helper context managers.

This documentation update adds the missing `import os` statement to the Flaskr tutorial setup. It ensures users can correctly use `os.path.join()` when defining the database location in their application.

This commit ensures that request objects are properly closed when the request context is popped, preventing potential resource leaks. It modifies the `RequestContext.pop` method in `flask/ctx.py` to check for and call a `close` method if available on the request object.
